NFL Fines Two Cardinals After Rams Game
full_text:
ARIZONA — Two different Arizona Cardinals were fined after their Week 6 upset victory over the Los Angeles Rams.
OLB Eku Leota was fined over $6,000 for a blindside block during a punt return while TE Teagan Quitoriano was also fined nearly $7,000 for a leg-whip block.
2 #AZCardinals were fined from Week 6. Eku Leota ($6,361 for a blindside block) Teagan Quitoriano ($6,750 for a leg whip) pic.twitter.com/kwgKxckstY
These aren't the first Cardinals to be fined this season:
The Cardinals, collectively, have seen their players fined over $50,000 this season.
The NFL has fined players on 166 of 15,203 plays this regular season.
Week 6 was a massive upset victory for the Cardinals, who emerged to 2-4 on the season after winning their second game at SoFi Stadium.
Arizona, according to head coach Mike LaFleur, has shown tremendous growth since Week 1.
“That’s a good question. I do think in some aspects our run game has grown from a variation standpoint in terms of what we’re doing schematically and then how those guys are executing, but there are still aspects of our run game we need to improve," he told reporters this week.
"I think the operation’s the one that is the biggest. There's no yards that go with operation in terms of what you guys can see, but we know that when we’re operating at the level that we’re capable of it does lead to yards, which leads to points, which leads to obviously the result that we’re all hunting up, so I'd say those two aspects. I think we’ve, for the most part all year, have done a good job of keeping the ball in play in terms of getting our completions and all that.
"I think there’s a lot of room for us still to continue with our YAC in terms of our drop steps and our transitions and all that. As long as we’re here that standard’s never going to change. We’re always going to be hunting to be number one in the league at stuff like that. It does take talent to be good at that. I’m not going to say that that stuff takes no talent, but it’s definitely a skill set that we can continue to work on.”
The Cardinals hope to keep that momentum going against the Denver Broncos in Week 7.

title: Breaking Down Cardinals' Flurry of Roster Moves Before Broncos Game
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have announced four roster moves ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the Denver Broncos, including a release and signing to the active roster alongside two practice squad elevations before Sunday.
Williams had been filling in for a depleted Cardinals safety room hampered by injuries, though a mix of guys returning to full health and poor play from Williams — who was picked on by opposing offenses when on the field —led to Williams' dismissal from the active roster.
“Just the time on task from the week before. (Then) making sure that ‘Rabbit’ (Dadrion Taylor-Demerson) felt as good as we thought he was going to feel and (then) kind of ease him back in there," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said on starting Williams over Dadrion Taylor-Demerson.
Now, Taylor-Demerson is back and Kitan Crawford is healthy again too. Though Andrew Wingard has already been ruled out, Budda Baker is questionable and now looks likely to play with Williams' release.
Hull is filling in RB3 duties for the Cardinals as Jeremiyah Love is set to miss another week due to his ankle injury. Hull will play behind Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier against the Broncos, and after his preseason performance, fans at State Farm Stadium will be pleased to see him suit up once again.
Hull was also made active last week when Love missed his first game of the season. The move to sign him to the active roster instead of simply elevating him from the practice squad is an interesting one, which may indicate he could be sticking around more than just this weekend.
The Cardinals are down several offensive linemen entering this game, as Arizona is effectively down to their fourth-string right guard in Hayden Conner alongside a rookie seventh-round pick (Jayden Williams) at left tackle. Eguakun fills the void of depth in that regard.
Meanwhile, Arizona ruled out Walter Nolen III ahead of Sunday while Darius Robinson is questionable along the defensive line. They'll need more bodies in the trenches ahead of Week 7, which explains the Harrison-Hunte elevation. This could be a sign that Robinson isn't playing against Denver.

title: Cardinals Mailbag: What's Going on With Carson Beck?
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are hoping to steal a win against the Denver Broncos this week, and with all eyes on Larry Fitzgerald and his Ring of Honor induction, the Cardinals are hoping to do their part and keep fans in the seats of State Farm Stadium past halftime.
This week's mailbag is lighter than usual, thanks for all of the questions!
Same, Joel. I've been pounding the table for the Cardinals to be more aggressive when it comes to blitzing. After allowing four straight 30-point games, Rallis put the pedal to the metal and had his highest blitz rate of the season in their upset win over the Rams.
Whether that carries over is one of the biggest talking points of the week. You'd think the Cardinals would want to put pressure on a struggling Bo Nix, but I'm just a guy with a laptop.
Mike LaFleur promised changes that came to the defensive side of the ball. He followed through, and so did Rallis.
Their more aggressive approach in defensive play-calling wasn't the sole reason they won in Los Angeles, though there's certainly something there for the Cardinals to build on.
I appreciate the weekly question, AngryCardsFan. Still no major updates from Mike LaFleur on either player.
It does feel like Reiman will be back at some point this season, but it doesn't feel like he's close to playing. Conner did get an update from Monti Ossenfort on his appearance with Arizona Sports:
“James is really close to a return,” Ossenfort said . “He’s going to continue to work and be ready to go. There are some roster construction considerations that go into that, but James is doing great. As always, he’s been a positive influence on the team, and he’s progressing well in his rehab.”
Who knows what the future holds for either. The Cardinals are very much keeping it under wraps.
Bryan, I'm not paying the ambulance bill, that's for damn sure. I assure you journalism money isn't all that great!
I'd love for them to actually look at my hamstrings, which have been jello after turning 30. I've got a big Turkey Bowl coming up where I need to repeat my MVP performance.
I'm letting them treat me, for sure, I haven't seen any electrical substations nearby.
Terry, I understand how it feels like that from the outside.
Beck's injury history has been... interesting. He played in the Hall of Fame Game, practiced the week after and suddenly had rib injuries so bad he was ruled out for the rest of preseason play — which was a blow for the Cardinals.
However, this injury — his back now — is different from his preseason injury. This just popped this week.
Beck hasn't played because he's been inactive as the emergency quartertback, not because he's hurt. This week is the first time all regular season he could miss a game due to injury alone.

title: Cardinals GM Sends Clear Message After Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals' trade with the Houston Texans for Marvin Harrison Jr. is officially in the rearview mirror.
Though outside of a short statement in the team's press release, we've yet to hear from general manager Monti Ossenfort.
Ossenfort appeared on Arizona Sports' 98.7 FM on Friday and wasn't shy about moving on from Harrison.
"Those decisions are always hard. I think the world of Marv, and he's going to have a bright future in this league," said Ossenfort. "For us it was just an opportunity to that presented itself. A team stepped up with a trade opportunity that we thought was a significant pick.
"You're trying to do right by the player. Us communicating that timeline to Marvin Saturday morning, it's never a smooth process. It's always difficult timing but always want to be transparent when we can ... We're not looking back."
The Cardinals dealt Harrison to the Texans for a trade package that ultimately netted them a second-round pick, a solid deal for a player who only had five receptions on the season.
There were rumblings Harrison wasn't happy in the desert — though it doesn't sound like the Cardinals were too happy with their former fourth overall pick, either.
“My role is always to do what’s best for the team,” Ossenfort continued. “It’s always to do what’s best for the team in terms of the information that we have at that specific time. That’s what I’ve always done. That’s what I will always continue to do, what the right move is for the team.
"It may be different as weeks go by, but at that time, we believe that was the best move for the team. And that’s what we did.”
The Cardinals move forward with Trey McBride and Michael Wilson as their top two weapons with Kendrick Bourne filling in for Harrison. Houston, meanwhile, added Harrison to their receiver's room of  Nico Collins, Tank Dell and Jaylin Noel.

title: Final Cardinals-Broncos Injury Report Revealed
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Denver Broncos have revealed their final Week 7 injury report.
The Cardinals have ruled out all of Jeremiyah Love (ankle), Andrew Wingard (knee), Walter Nolen III (ankle) and Jon Gaines (knee) ahead of Sunday's clash at State Farm Stadium.
That marks four starters Arizona is already down entering the weekend, with more potentially on the way.
Budda Baker (groin/illness), Carson Beck (back), Max Melton (knee) and Darius Robinson (back) are officially listed as questionable.
In Denver, three players in Tyler Badie (thumb), Jonah Eliss (ankle) and Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) are out while Jonah Coleman (ankle) and Pat Surtain II (ankle) are questionable for the Broncos.
Both teams are able to make up to two standard practice squad elevations on Saturday, which could tip who is probable to play or not play depending on which positions are activated. Official game inactives are due on Sunday at 11:35 AM while kickoff is at 1:05 PM in the desert.
The Cardinals are desperately looking to play spoiler once again, though some massive injuries in the likes of Nolen and Love will make things tough. With Gaines out, Arizona will start Hayden Conner at right guard against a Broncos defense that has already generated 60 pressures this season.
Arizona is confident Baker is trending in the right direction while Robinson and Melton are still up in the air.
With four established players out and possibly more on the way, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur knows there's a tall task ahead with a staunch Denver defense.
"They’re very smart. They’re very well coached. I have as much respect for ‘VJ’ (Broncos Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph) as anyone in this league," he said to reporters earlier this week.
"They do it their own way. I don’t want to say they’re not with the times — whatever that means but it’s got an old-school approach to it in terms of some of their coverage and that’s a credit to them. You can tell ‘VJ’ and those guys believe in what they believe in and they’re unapologetic with it.
"They play really hard. I see 11 guys working in unison. It’s a challenge. Yes, it’s the last two weeks, but it’s really been all year, and it’s been for a few years now. We have our hands full with this group, for sure.”
Arizona is 2-4 on the season while the Broncos are 4-2.

title: Larry Fitzgerald Shares Emotional Message to Cardinals Fans Ahead of Ring of Honor Ceremony
full_text:
It's Larry Fitzgerald's weekend in the desert, and the Arizona Cardinals' legend couldn't be more thankful for the Red Sea as he prepares to enter the team's Ring of Honor.
“Just how much I appreciate them. What it meant to be able to don that Cardinals helmet, the memories that we've been able to share out there in Glendale. I still remember 2006 like it was yesterday," Fitzgerald told reporters this weekend when asked about Arizona fans.
"We had that preseason opener with the stadium patch against the Steelers. Just the electricity driving up to the stadium, first time pulling in the A lot and seeing all the people up on top of the stands cheering and just the energy that I received all those times coming into that place and the love that I receive still to this day going around in the community. I just want to be able to reiterate how much that has meant to me and my family and something that I'll never forget.”
Fitzgerald, after being inducted into the NFL Hall of Fame earlier this year, will go into the Cardinals' Ring of Honor as the team plays host to the Denver Broncos in Week 7.
Reflecting in a press conference with reporters, Fitzgerald said he doesn't take seeing the flurry of No. 11 jerseys lightly.
"I felt like the responsibility was a lot more when I was playing," Fitzgerald continued on being asked about emerging as an Arizona sports icon.
"I'm washed now and the kids are like, 'Hey, you're Larry Fitzgerald.' I say, 'Yeah, yeah.' They're like, 'My dad used to really like you. My dad used to really like you.' So it's kind of moved on, but I always remember driving to the stadium and (I'd be) looking out in the stands and looking out into the people walking around and I'm like, 'Man, there's a lot 11 jerseys there.' I'm saying (to myself) most of those kids I know didn't have the money to buy them and being a parent now, I'm not going to buy my kid a jersey of a player that I don't respect if they don't play hard or they're not active in their community.
"There's a criteria that we all would have as a parent to be OK with our son wearing or our daughter wearing their jersey, so that responsibility was never lost on me. I still think to a certain degree that I have it, but it's not like I'm in the spotlight like (TE) Trey (McBride) is or how (S) Budda (Baker) is or 'J Love' (RB Jeremiyah Love) is. They're in the fight every single day, so I think the onus is a little bit higher with them.”

title: Jeremiyah Love, Walter Nolen III Get Final Injury Call For Cardinals-Broncos
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are going to be down some serious star power against the Denver Broncos.
Head coach Mike LaFleur has ruled out Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Walter Nolen III (ankle) among a few others for Week 7, which includes Andrew Wingard (knee) and Jon Gaines (knee).
"All right, just to get this through. So Jeremiyah, Walt, and Dewey will all be out for Sunday, and then unfortunately, Jon Gaines had a practice injury yesterday, so he'll be out as well," LaFleur said.
The Cardinals' coach also confirmed Carson Beck and Darius Robinson's injuries weren't serious. Budda Baker is also being monitored, but the team feels good about him according to LaFleur.
The #AZCardinals are ruling out RB Jeremiyah Love, S Andrew Wingard, OL Jon Gaines and DL Walter Nolen III for Week 7’s battle against the Denver Broncos. Carson Beck dealing with back spasms. Not long term. No conversations to put Love on IR. Feels good about Budda Baker.
Arizona isn't expected to place Love or Nolen on injured reserve. Love will miss his second consecutive game while Nolen will be out for the first time in 2026.
This will massively hamper the Cardinals' chances to pull off another upset, this time coming against the Broncos — who are playing some of the toughest defense in the league.
"I don't care what scheme you run on defense, as long as you have conviction in it, which they do. There's clarity with the players, which they do. You have good players that matches the scheme that they're trying to run, which they do. Like they're all on the same page," LaFleur said of Denver's defense.
"Cover two, cover three, quarters, I mean, everyone has everything. It's how you're coaching it and how you're mixing and matching it, and what you know VJ [Vance Joseph] is thinking that he thinks is going to be best vs. us. We're going to get a little bit of everything. I'm assuming. I mean, that's usually what ends up happening.
"And then there's specific areas where you're anticipating maybe a little bit more of this than that, based on who we have compared to maybe based on some other teams. You never really know exactly what you're going to see. You just go off of what you saw on tape, some of your past experiences. But as we know, this defense has been playing really well for a few years, and it's going to be a challenge not only because of the scheme, but because of the players that are actually running the scheme."
The Cardinals will release their final practice reports for today, though Arizona clearly will be down some massive names.

title: Why Larry Fitzgerald Chose Now For Cardinals Ring of Honor Moment
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals move into this weekend with one player in mind: Larry Fitzgerald.
The Hall of Fame receiver is set to be inducted into the Cardinals' Ring of Honor in Arizona's Week 7 home battle against the Denver Broncos, a long awaited weekend that's sure to have State Farm Stadium packed with loyal fans who witnessed one of the best careers in Arizona sports history.
Fitzgerald, speaking with reporters this week, says the moment was actually supposed to happen years ago.
“Fortunately, I have a great relationship with (Owner) Michael (Bidwill) and the family, so this has been something we've talked about since the time I left. Actually, about three years ago, we decided on a date, and I had something family-wise come up shortly after we had agreed on it," he said.
"And Michael was like, 'hey, if it feels right.' We've always been in constant communication and that's one of the best things about being in the same place for such a long time. You build really strong relationships. As I said, he's like an uncle to me. We felt like this was the right time and we thought it was cool to be able to do it in October, which is Breast Cancer Awareness Month.
"The Cardinals have been great about early detection and really being proactive in the community amongst so many other things. We just felt like it was the right time. (Senior Vice President, Fan Engagement and Operations) Lisa Manning was very important in getting us across the finish line as well.”
Fitzgerald's mother passed due to breast cancer back in 2003, which has since led the perennial All-Star receiver to be heavily involved in raising awareness through his foundation alongside millions donated to the cause.
Week 7 fit Fitzgerald's calendar for a handful of reasons, which includes his son Devin — who plays football at Notre Dame. The Fighting Irish have a bye week this weekend.
"I mean, life is full. Chasing the kids around. Devin has the bye week. One of the reasons I picked this week is because Notre Dame is on the bye. (To) be able to have him here and to be able to be with Apollo and Milo, to be able to do it together, that's something that was really important," Fitzgerald continued. "Business is going well. Life is good. I feel like I've built a nice off ramp for myself."

title: Walter Nolen, Jeremiyah Love and More Cardinals Stars Miss Practice
full_text:
TEMPE — Things are not looking good for the Arizona Cardinals in the health department.
The likes of Walter Nolen III, Jeremiyah Love and Budda Baker were the biggest names absent from the Cardinals' Thursday practice. Arizona plays host to the Denver Broncos in Week 7.
Nolen (ankle), Love (ankle) and Baker (groin/illness) all have not practiced for two consecutive days now in the build-up to Sunday. Also not spotted at practice today was Andrew Wingard (knee) and Max Melton (knee) — Wingard was a DNP yesterday while Melton was limited on Wednesday.
Earlier today, CBS Sports reported that Love is not expected to play, which would mark a second consecutive game missed for the third overall pick. His current ankle injury has been managed the last few weeks and is different from the one that saw him miss the end of preseason play.
It's looking as if the Cardinals will again rely on Bam Knight, Tyler Allgeier and Evan Hull against a stout Broncos defense.
Nolen's absence would be massive in the trenches, as the second-year defensive lineman was starting to come into his own, playing a big part in helping Arizona control the line of scrimmage and get after the quarterback.
In terms of ceiling and potential, Nolen's is by far the highest out of anybody along the Cardinals' defensive line. Missing him against a struggling Broncos offense would be huge.
Baker's absence would leave an obvious hole in the team's secondary in terms of both talent and game-planning. After a rough start, Baker's quickly turned the corner and has pieced together a strong overall 2026 campaign.
"There's just certain things where if you can try to get him to the point of attack on each play, like you got to do it, just because he makes those plays," Cardinals defensive coordinator Nick Rallis told reporters on Baker.
"He puts people in negatives. He creates negative plays, that's a thing week to week is like where can we get Budda around the ball without being obvious?"
The Cardinals, sitting at 2-4, are hoping to string together consecutive wins for the first time all season when Denver comes to State Farm Stadium.
The official practice report will drop later today, but from a health perspective, things do not look good for Arizona.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur will meet with reporters on Friday morning, where he'll likely verify who is in and out for the weekend.

title: FalconsSI Predictions Falcons vs. 49ers Week 7: Can Atlanta Finally Win at Home?
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons face a difficult challenge in Week 7 as they welcome the undefeated San Francisco 49ers to Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sunday.
Atlanta is searching for its first home win of the season, but San Francisco presents a major test for a team still trying to find consistency on both sides of the ball.
Despite the 49ers dealing with injuries, the Falcons will need a complete performance to pull off the upset. Here is how our staff sees Sunday’s matchup playing out.
The Falcons are winless at home this season, and they will need to pass a difficult test Sunday to change that trend. The undefeated 49ers have established themselves as one of the league’s top teams, and Atlanta enters the matchup with defensive holes to fill and an offense still searching for consistency.
If Michael Penix Jr. can stay clean in the pocket, the Falcons will have a legitimate chance to compete. However, slowing down George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey will be especially difficult without linebacker Divine Deablo.
San Francisco’s offensive weapons could prove too much for Atlanta’s defense, leading to another disappointing home result for the Falcons.
Prediction : 49ers 28, Falcons 17
At first glance, the betting line makes this matchup appear favorable for Atlanta. A 6-0 San Francisco team might be expected to be a bigger favorite, but the 49ers’ extensive injury concerns could be keeping the matchup closer than anticipated.
The Falcons have enough talent to beat any team when they put everything together. The problem is finding that consistency against quality opponents. Atlanta must figure out how to handle opposing pressure, or the 49ers could overwhelm Penix with aggressive blitz packages.
San Francisco is vulnerable because of its injuries, giving Atlanta a puncher’s chance. However, until the Falcons prove they can consistently perform against strong competition, picking them to pull off an upset remains difficult.
Prediction :  49ers 31, Falcons 23
After Bears fans took over Mercedes-Benz Stadium last week, I expect another takeover from 49ers fans on Sunday. Atlanta should deliver a much better performance, but I still have concerns about whether the offense can do enough to secure a victory.
San Francisco’s injuries will have an impact, but Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey will ultimately be too much for Atlanta’s defense. Meanwhile, the 49ers’ pass rush could make life difficult for Penix, particularly if the Falcons struggle to protect their young quarterback.
I expect Atlanta to keep the game competitive and give its home crowd something to cheer about. However, until the Falcons demonstrate they can finish against a quality opponent, I cannot pick them to get over the hump.
San Francisco escapes with a narrow victory, leaving Atlanta with another frustrating home loss.
Prediction : 49ers 28, Falcons 24
The 49ers are currently the best team in football in my opinion which makes this a tough matchup for the Falcons.
This would be a lopsided matchup if the 49ers were healthy, but that’s not the case. The 49ers have been led by arguably the best passing attack in the league, but they’ll be without Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel . Stopping Georgie Kittle and McCaffrey will still be a tall order, however.
The Falcons offense matches up well against the 49ers defense on paper, especially given that Nick Bosa will be out. The key will be can the Falcons o-line deal with all of the twists and stunts that the 49ers will throw at them, and can they keep Fred Warner from taking over the game.
I have the 49ers winning, but I think the Falcons will keep it close.

title: Why Bijan Robinson Is ‘Fired Up’ for Falcons’ Showdown With Undefeated 49ers
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have a golden opportunity this Sunday.
They can end their two-game losing streak while earning a statement win over one of the NFL’s final three unbeaten teams, the San Francisco 49ers.
“That’s why you love this game,” said Falcons running back Bijan Robinson .
“They’re a very good team, and there’s the underdog story and everything. We’re really just focused on ourselves and what we need to do. But these are the games that you love to play for.”
The other two undefeated NFL teams are the Kansas City Chiefs and the Minnesota Vikings, squads that the Falcons will meet in the four games after facing the 49ers.
The Falcons entered the 2026 season with one of the hardest schedules across the league, and the coming weeks are unrelenting.
After a 0-2 start while in quarterback purgatory, the Falcons (2-4) strung together two consecutive wins, but then lost two straight. Atlanta’s last outing was a failed comeback loss to the Chicago Bears, 31-23, last Sunday, Oct. 18.
As for the 49ers (6-0), they defeated the Washington Commanders 23-17 on Oct. 19’s Monday Night Football on Oct. 19 to remain perfect on the season.
San Fran boasts the ninth-best total offense out of the NFL’s 32 teams, with quarterback Brock Purdy leading the way with his pocket presence and opportunistic running . Behind Purdy is one of the league’s top running backs, Christian McCaffrey, the 2025 NFL Comeback Player of the Year.
Their offense is second in total EPA and No. 1 in passing EPA, according to Sumer Sports. However, they're missing several key weapons .
Defensively, the 49ers are fifth in the NFL total defense. Former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris is the defense coordinator. Robinson said he and Morris spoke “a couple of weeks ago.”
Additionally, the Niners have star linebacker Fred Warner, whom Robinson deems “the best in the game.”
“It’s all the little things that are going to require us to win this game,” Robinson said. “This is a great opponent coming in. Just that alone, I’m fired up. I can’t wait. I’m juiced up, I know the other guys are too. It comes with the competitiveness that we have to bring. We have to come in here and make sure we’re on top of what we’re supposed to do to win this game.”
Falcons-49ers kickoff at 1 p.m. on Sunday at Atlanta’s Mercedes-Benz Stadium. FOX will televise the NFL Week 7 matchup.
The teams met a season ago, when San Francisco hosted and won the Sunday Night Football meeting 20-10 last October.

title: Falcons Make A.J. Terrell Decision, Plus Several Roster Moves
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons announced several roster moves Saturday ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, including activating cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. from injured reserve, signing defensive end Drake Jackson, and placing offensive tackle Michael Jerrell on injured reserve for a bicep injury.
Terrell has missed the last four weeks with a groin injury suffered in Week 2. The veteran cornerback practiced throughout the week after opening his 21-day return window Wednesday. With his activation to the active roster, Terrell will not carry an injury designation and is expected to play Sunday.
Atlanta also added Jackson to the active roster, adding depth to its defensive line ahead of a matchup against a San Francisco offense ranked No. 3 in scoring and No. 9 in total offense. Jackson gives the Falcons another option along the defensive front as they look to pressure the quarterback and slow down the 49ers' passing attack.
The Falcons placed Jerrell on injured reserve with a biceps injury, adding to an offensive line already dealing with personnel concerns. Atlanta also ruled out wide receiver Beaux Collins, who is recovering from a hip injury, and offensive tackle Cameron Williams, who has an ankle injury.
Meanwhile, Atlanta used standard practice squad elevations on running back Khalil Herbert and linebacker Brian Asamoah.
Herbert's elevation adds running back depth as the Falcons manage injuries after losing Brian Robinson Jr. to a hamstring ailment that will keep him out Sunday. Asamoah's elevation gives Atlanta another linebacker option as the team prepares for San Francisco without Divine Deablo.
Defensive back Avieon Terrell is also dealing with a back injury and an illness. His status remains questionable for Sunday's game, leaving the Falcons waiting for further clarity on his availability.
The roster adjustments come as Atlanta looks to improve on both sides of the ball against a difficult opponent. The Falcons rank 28th in the NFL in passing yards allowed, surrendering 252 yards per game, making the older Terrell's return particularly valuable for the secondary.
While Terrell's activation is the headline move, Atlanta will also rely on its newly available depth pieces to help navigate injuries and prepare for a critical Week 7 matchup. The Falcons will look to make the most of their roster changes when they host the 49ers on Sunday.

title: Raheem Morris Has a Message for Falcons Before Return to Atlanta
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are set for a Week 7 homecoming with former head coach Raheem Morris coming to Mercedes-Benz Stadium for the first time since the two parted ways in January.
Morris, who is now the defensive coordinator for the San Francisco 49ers, spent the last two seasons with the Falcons. While he ultimately missed the playoffs in both years, he laid the groundwork for this 2026 team’s makeup. His first year at the helm was marked by signing Kirk Cousins to a lucrative free-agent deal, then drafting Michael Penix Jr. with the eighth overall pick just a few months later.
That strategy didn't go as planned, and it marked an inauspicious start to two roller-coaster seasons in Atlanta before he was fired in January alongside general manager Terry Fontenot.
Some floated the idea that Morris could hold on for one more season after he rallied the Falcons to four straight (albeit meaningless) wins to end the year. Instead, he finished 16-18 overall, and Arthur Blank took the organization in a new direction.
The NFL is a business, and the 49ers will be looking to go about their business this Sunday, but could there be a little added motivation for San Francisco? Not likely, says 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan when he was asked this week about the defense’s desire to “win this game” for their defensive coordinator.
“I don’t think they can be more motivated,” Shanahan said. “I think our guys are as motivated as they can get each week. I don’t think they get too caught up in that stuff, but I know they care about Raheem a lot and definitely would want to do that for him, but I don’t think we’re looking at too much of a personal game like that.”
All-Pro linebacker Fred Warner echoed Shanahan's perspective, emphasizing that the 49ers approach every game with the same level of urgency.
“I feel like we treat every week as if it is the biggest week of our lives,” Warner said. “To play with even more emotion than what we play with already would be – I’m not even sure about what that would look like at this point, right? But every week has its own challenges. I’m sure Raheem wants this one in a big way because he was the former head coach there. We want it in the biggest way, as the 49ers, because this is the next one.”
The former Falcons head coach wasn't directly asked about his feelings on returning to Atlanta for the first time since being fired, but he said it is “helpful” to understand the makeup of the players in that locker room.
But in typical Morris fashion, he did pour out a lot of love for his former players.
“Love the kid, you know, love everything about him: the personality, who he was, the thrower,” Morris said about Penix. “He's back healthy, and he's everything that you thought and hoped for. As far as being a play-action passer, he can push the ball down the field and can make all the throws, and go through the whole process. He’s just one of those guys that I have a lot of appreciation for and love for.”
As for running back Bijan Robinson, whom he called “the best player in football” last season, the praise remained.
“I talked about Bijan last year – I talked about him being the best player in the NFL, and he certainly is, arguably, the best player in the National Football League,” Morris said. “He's special. He's one of those guys. He's as special a talent that we see in this league and can do everything.”
It appears to be business as usual for Morris and the 49ers. The former head coach may be on the opposite sideline Sunday, but his appreciation for the players he coached in Atlanta hasn't changed. Whether that familiarity gives San Francisco an edge remains to be seen.
Shanahan and Warner made it clear that the 49ers plan to approach this matchup the same way they do every other week. On Sunday, Morris will find out if that appreciation translates to a defensive game plan that can stop his former team.

title: Falcons Face Wounded 49ers Team Missing Key Weapons
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons (2-4) take on the San Francisco 49ers (6-0) this week at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Neither team has had a bye this season, and the injuries are starting to pile up.
The Falcons had 11 players listed as questionable on Friday's injury report , and they already ruled out linebacker Divine Deablo and nickel Billy Bowman Jr.
The 49ers are coming off a short week after their win over the San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football, and they'll be without key offensive weapons against the Falcons .
San Francisco ruled out a pair of starting wide receivers in long-time Falcons nemesis Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel.
Evans leads the team with 420 receiving yards. Samuel is third on the team with 206 yards, and he's added 78 rushing yards on just nine carries.
Evans spent 12 years with the NFC South rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and he's had more than his share of success against the Falcons. In 21 games, he has 1,652 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns. He's only had more yards against the Carolina Panthers (1,760), but he's faced the Panthers 23 times. His per-game average against the Falcons is higher at 78.7 vs. 76.5.
He may be 33 years old, but he still went for six catches for 132 yards against the Falcons in December. It was the second-best game of his career against the Falcons, with his top game coming way back in 2016 when he had 150 yards and two touchdowns in a Buccaneers loss in Tampa.
With the Falcons having injuries at linebacker and nickel, missing Samuel comes as maybe even a bigger break. While he's listed as a wide receiver, he's built like a running back. He specializes in catching short passes and turning them into longer gains. He puts a lot of stress on the linebackers and nickelbacks of defenses.
The 49ers also list wide receiver Christian Kirk as questionable. With Brock Purdy playing the way he is, the 49ers still have Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle, who leads the team with five touchdown receptions. The running back and tight end are still players who will stress the linebackers and nickelbacks of the Falcons.
Brandin Cooks is next on the depth chart behind Evans, but the 49ers may rely on more two-tight end sets on Sunday.
On the other side of the ball, starting safety Marques Sigle has been ruled out. He's only played in four of the team's six games, and he's still the fifth-leading tackler. The 49ers will rely even more heavily on All-World linebacker Fred Warner to try to contain Falcons' running back Bijan Robinson.
The game kicks off at Mercedes-Benz Stadium at 1:00 p.m. EST and will be televised on FOX.

title: Roddy White Stresses What Falcons Need from Michael Penix Jr. to Be Great
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. has played like a franchise quarterback for large portions of this season. There's just one problem -- Penix hasn't been on the field enough.
That's what former Falcons wide receiver Roddy White argued when he discussed the status of the organization, especially, the team's quarterback position.
Penix is in his third season with the Falcons. Yet, he's started just 16 games. Penix missed 10 contests in 2025 and the beginning of this season because of a knee injury.
"As far as where our franchise is right now, we do need him to be available each and every week," said White while speaking to SI on Falcons at the the Chase for Business’ Make Your Move Summit in Atlanta this week. "It's been tough to deal with when he's not in there because the game plan, and the team, changes so much.
"Everyone in that locker room trusts and believes in him, and he gives us the best opportunity to win. We love it when he's out there, but he has to be out there to help us win and get some of these W's in these close games that we've been playing up to this point."
Penix's injury past was a storyline for the quarterback before he came to Atlanta. The signal-caller went through multiple knee and shoulder injuries during his extensive college career.
Then, during his first full year as an NFL starter, Penix partially tore his left ACL. The injury sidelined him until Week 3 of this season.
He's started every game since then. So on one hand, the Penix critics about his injury past should be more silent. But in Week 5 against the Baltimore Ravens, Penix exited late in the fourth quarter with a rib injury. Penix missed overtime, which ended in a loss for Atlanta.
"Those are the times that you need your quarterback to come through and make plays for you so you can win those," added White.
The former Falcons wideout used Drake London as an example for how different the Falcons offense is with and without Penix.
When Penix has started this season, London, who White called one of the best receivers in the league, has averaged 40 receiving yards per game. When Penix starts, London is posting 117.5 receiving yards per contest.
White spoke with media while partnering with Chase Bank to help entrepreneurs in the Southeast this past week. At the summit from Oct. 20-22, small-business owners from the Atlanta area and the surrounding states gathered to network and learn from Chase Bank the best practices for beginning a small business.
The former Falcons receiver is a small business owner himself. He owns a construction company that focuses on building single-family houses, small developments and commercial real estate. The company primarily works in Atlanta but also sometimes in North and South Carolina.
"A lot of us just out here communicating, doing business with each other,  learning from each other, helping each other along the way.," said White at the summit. "Chase helps us navigate through the business space, as far as what directions to go in, what people you need to talk to for banking situations and how you can build your business on a week to week, month to month, year to year basis.
"This is an opportunity to also come in and learn from each other and also just communicate within the structure of a business and have fun with each other and learn from each other."
More than 1,000 small-business owners gathered at the summit. All types of different industries were represented.
White started his business after 11 seasons with the Falcons from 2005-15. The receiver registered six consecutive 1,100-yard campaigns from 2007-12. He also earned four straight trips to the Pro Bowl from 2008-11 and made first-team All-Pro in 2010.
White remains the all-time Falcons leader in receiving touchdowns. White is also second on the team's receptions and receiving yards list behind only Julio Jones.

title: Falcons' Lengthy Injury Report Raises Questions Before 49ers Game
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons will enter Sunday's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers with a lot of questions surrounding their roster availability, as four players have been ruled out and 10 others are listed as questionable.
Running back Brian Robinson Jr., linebacker Divine Deablo, defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. and offensive tackle Michael Jerrell will miss Sunday's contest.
The extensive injury report could force Atlanta to make adjustments on both sides of the ball as it prepares for a challenging matchup.
Robinson's absence was one of the more notable developments on Atlanta's final injury report. The running back was limited during Wednesday's practice before missing Thursday and Friday, ultimately being ruled out for Sunday's game.
With Robinson unavailable, the Falcons will need additional contributions from their remaining running backs. Stefanski confirmed that Khalil Herbert, who is currently on the practice squad, will serve as the backup.
Atlanta will likely elevate Herbert from the practice squad for the 49ers matchup. Robinson's absence could also affect how the Falcons distribute carries and handle passing downs against San Francisco's defense.
Deablo's absence could create another challenge for Atlanta's defense, particularly with rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels also dealing with an injury.
Daniels offered an encouraging update on his condition , saying he "feels good." His availability remains important as the Falcons determine their linebacker rotation and who will handle defensive communication duties.
If Daniels is active, he could be a candidate to wear the green dot which he has done in games this season. Harold Perkins Jr. and Josh Woods are other potential options if Daniels cannot play.
Whoever assumes that responsibility will need to help keep Atlanta organized against a San Francisco offense that uses motion and varied personnel groupings to create favorable matchups.
The Falcons also received a positive update regarding cornerback A.J. Terrell, who is working his way back from a groin injury.
Stefanski said he thought Terrell "looks better," suggesting the cornerback has made progress during the week. Terrell's potential return would provide a boost to a secondary that will be without Bowman and could have other defensive backs unavailable.
Terrell's status is especially important against San Francisco, given the uncertainty surrounding Atlanta's cornerback depth.
Several other players remain questionable, including defensive linemen Samson Ebukam and Za'Darius Smith, defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. and defensive backs C.J. Henderson and Avieon Terrell. Their availability could influence Atlanta's defensive rotations and personnel packages.
Stefanski noted that San Francisco is dealing with similar week to week challenges, making preparation and roster flexibility important components of Sunday's matchup.
The Falcons must now wait for the final availability decisions before determining their game day personnel. Robinson's absence is confirmed, while Terrell's potential return and Daniels' status remain important storylines to monitor.
Atlanta will look to overcome those personnel challenges when it hosts San Francisco on Sunday, with the outcome potentially hinting on how effectively its available players handle expanded responsibilities.

title: Kyle Pitts Sr. Showing Why Atlanta Falcons Must Get Him More Involved
full_text:
Kyle Pitts Sr.’s volatile usage in the Atlanta Falcons offense has been a recurring topic since the franchise invested the 2021 fourth overall NFL Draft pick in the tight end out of Florida.
“We want to get him the ball,” Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. said of the 6-foot-6, 250-pound target. “He’s one of our best players on the team.”
Through six games, Pitts has 15 catches for 169 yards and three touchdowns. According to Pro Football Focus , he is also second in the NFL in yards after catch per reception, averaging 7.5
“I think he’s at his best when he has the ball in his hands in open space,” Falcons offensive coordinator Tommy Rees discussed Pitts. “Kyle’s shown that throughout his entire career, he’s certainly shown that over the last few weeks. It’s our job to put him in a position to have those plays.”
He had his best game of the season as Atlanta turned to him when its offense was spiraling in its 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears .
“For us to reach out full potential, he’s got to be a big part of that,” Rees said.
The Falcons’ potent rushing attack, led by Bijan Robinson , was neutralized, and the pass game wasn’t picking up much traction either.
Trailing 31-7, the Falcons attempted to make a fourth-quarter comeback.
The unit began finding a rhythm. Pitts was at the forefront, finishing with a team-high five receptions and two touchdowns on a 60-yard output.
“Just going out there and trying to play as fast as I can, and be an asset to this offense any way I can,” Pitts told reporters after the game. “And being there for Mike and the rest of this offense.
During the offseason, Atlanta made the 26-year-old Pitts the third-highest-paid NFL tight end , inking a three-year, $54 million extension with $36 million guaranteed .
However, his performance hasn’t matched his play at times. But it’s not all Pitts’ fault.
Through the first three weeks of the season, the opening two of those being quarterbacked by the now-cut Cooper Rush , Pitts had just three targets.
Since Week 4, Pitts’ opportunities have increased. He has 13 receptions on 16 targets.
And Penix wants to remind people that Atlanta’s pass attack isn’t a one-trick pony, “ Drake London’s somewhere down there somewhere” type of attack.
“Whenever KP is open, I’m not just looking past him,” Penix said. “So that whole narrative is crazy, especially with him being the person I’ve spent the most time with since I’ve been here. So for people to say I don’t think about Kyle, I only think about Drake, it’s like this is somebody I was with every day in the offseason.”
The Falcons (2-4) next host the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers (6-0) at Mercedes-Benz Stadium this Sunday. Kickoff is at 1 p.m. on FOX.
Atlanta looks for a statement that would end a two-game skid and keep them in striking distance of the NFC South divisional race.

title: Recently Cut Atlanta Falcons 3rd-Round Pick Puts Raheem Morris, 49ers on Alert
full_text:
Former Atlanta Falcons edge rusher Bralen Trice is exploring his next opportunity after visiting the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, less than a week after appearing on Atlanta's active roster.
The 49ers hosted Trice for a visit after the Falcons released him on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The former third-round pick is looking for a new home after finally making his NFL regular-season debut in 2026, following two injury-plagued seasons in Atlanta.
San Francisco's defensive staff includes former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, now the 49ers' defensive coordinator. Although Morris coached Atlanta in 2024 and 2025, Trice never played under him in a regular-season game. Trice spent his first two NFL seasons sidelined by injuries while Morris led the Falcons.
If Trice joins the 49ers, he would be the second former Falcon Morris has brought to San Francisco. The 49ers signed edge rusher Khalid Kareem from the Falcons' Practice Squad before the season opener.
Atlanta selected Trice with the 74th overall pick in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Washington, hoping he could develop into a productive pass rusher. However, his professional career got off to a difficult start when he tore his ACL during his first preseason game as a rookie.
Trice missed the entire 2024 season before suffering another setback with the same knee during the 2025 campaign. Those injuries kept him out of a regular-season game during his first two years with the organization.
The 25-year-old entered training camp healthy in 2026 but did not make Atlanta's initial 53-man roster. After clearing waivers, he returned to the Falcons' practice squad in early September.
Atlanta gave Trice three weeks of practice squad elevations to prove himself. His Week 3 performance against the Green Bay Packers stood out, as he recorded four quarterback hurries while helping Atlanta's defensive front generate pressure.
The Falcons eventually signed Trice to their active roster on Oct. 17 after using all three of his standard practice squad elevations. However, his time back on the 53-man roster was brief, as Atlanta released him three days later after the Falcons signed Charles Snowden from the Washington Commanders Practice Squad .
Trice appeared in four games for Atlanta this season, recording two total tackles and one pass defended, according to the Falcons' official release announcement and NFL statistics. He also showed flashes as a pass rusher, particularly with his four quarterback hurries against Green Bay.
For San Francisco, the visit offers a chance to evaluate a young defender who has faced significant adversity but is finally getting meaningful NFL playing time. His experience working along the defensive front could give the 49ers another option as they assess their depth at linebacker and edge defender.
Morris' presence adds an interesting connection between Trice's former team and his potential next destination, even without a previous on-field relationship between the two.
Trice has yet to establish himself as a consistent NFL contributor, but his healthy return in 2026 gave him his first chance to show the ability that earned him a third-round selection. Whether that opportunity continues in San Francisco remains to be seen.

title: 3 Critical Adjustments The Ravens Offense Must Make For QB Snoop Huntley
full_text:
The Ravens offense has been carrying the defense for the most part through the first six games of the Jesse Minter era. That’s got to change.
This will be a third-straight week with Snoop Huntley at quarterback instead of Lamar Jackson, who is dealing what he called an incredible painful high-ankle sprain that prevented him from really trying to run for two weeks but which the team insists on calling “day-to-day.” That’s problematic on many levels and the Bengals are the best team they have faced without the two-time MVP this season.
If this becomes a scenario where Huntley has to try to keep pace with a big day from Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, then it’s fair to expect the Ravens will be sitting at 4-3 come Sunday night with successive setbacks in the AFC North. This is going to require highly complimentary football. It mandates a significant contribution from Baltimore’s run game – and beyond just Derrick Henry, trust me – to keep Burrow off the field, shorten this game and give the ball-control and high-percentage approach required by Huntley’s limitations in the downfield passing game to make this a ballgame.
If this is another record day for Bengals receiver Ja’Marr chase – and he has done things to Baltimore’s defense that no pass catcher has ever done to any defense – it’s hard to see, say, Huntley doing the same sort of things with Zay Flowers throwing nothing but short and underneath passes. So, what can we expect from Huntley, realistically?
Well, here’s what Doyle is going to have to help him concoct if the offense is going to sustain more than what we’ve seen in the first two games – almost nothing against the Falcons until the final two drives and almost nothing in their final nine drives after a great start against the Browns.
Catching like eight balls for 60 yards or six for 66 isn’t going to work. Not against this opponent, Even if the Ravens had an excellent game on defense we’re still talking about holding the Bengals to 24-27 points; the Ravens aren’t getting there without Flowers getting loose.
It doesn’t have to be on a long ball, but it needs to do explosive yards after the catch and Doyle is going to have to get even more creative with Flowers than he’s been (and former head coach and player caller Todd Haley, who isn’t easily impressed, was gushing about Doyle’s use of Flowers to me on “The Daily Flock” ). Probably going to have to deploy him in the backfield more. Might need to see more targets at or behind the line of scrimmage.
The Bengals do not have a very good run defense against outside runs, but the Browns were terrible against them and depleted by injury and they shut Henry down. Doyle needs to sell the threat or hint of Huntley running more than he has to this point. It needs to be a staple or quasi-staple.
It’s likely going to take more Justice Hill in the pistol with Huntley. Probably needs to be more RPO looks than anything close to how the game plans have functioned the past two weeks. Have a hard time seeing the Ravens win this game without Huntley running for 3-5 first downs himself and several of them for more than just a handful of yards.
This is yet another new offensive line for the Ravens. Stop me if you’ve heard that one before.
Five guys up front who have never played together before. A center who was probably going to get benched as a guard for the Eagles, just coming off a concussion in a new offense he’s still learning (Cam Jurgens), lining up against one of the dominant defensive tackles in the NFL with arguably the deepest group of DTs with him .
Huntley is going to get pressured, for sure, and the Bengals are generating a 50% pressure rate in the fourth quarter this season, and in his career, well, he’s been quite bad under pressure: 49% completions, just 5.0 yards per attempt and a 66.3 passer rating.
There need to be answers in the screen game and answers with hots and answers with a pass protection plan, that, again, might require more of Hill, their best pass protecting back at a time their best blocking tight end is already lost for the season. This QB needs to have as much of an incubator as possible, and some quick answers to what are likely to be probing questions from the Bengals defensive front.
There is YAC waiting to happen with rookie tight end Matthew Hibner. It needs to be an emphasis Sunday.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Four Storylines For Ravens' Divisional Matchup vs. Bengals
full_text:
After two weeks away, the Baltimore Ravens will be back at home in Week 7 for their second straight game against an AFC North opponent when they take on the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday afternoon at M&T Bank Stadium.
Coming off an ugly loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6 on the road, in which they blew another double-digit lead, the Ravens are currently tied for the best record in the division at 4-2, but are no longer in first place.
There are several intriguing storylines surrounding this divisional matchup between these two rival teams. Here are the top four.
After only managing 40 points and four touchdowns in the 10 quarters since the two-time league MVP-winning quarterback went down with what he revealed to be a high ankle sprain, the Ravens are going to have to find a way to prevail without him for the third week in a row. Jackson returned to practice this week but was a limited participant on all three days and went from being listed as questionable on the final injury report Friday to being downgraded to out on Saturday .
QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) has been downgraded to “out” for tomorrow’s game vs. Cincinnati.
Both Jackson and Pro Bowl backup Tyler Huntley, who went 1-1 starting in his absence, spoke to the media on Friday, and neither tipped their hand on who'd be under center for this game. Now that the cat is out of the bag, the Ravens will need Huntley and the offense as a whole to rebound from a woeful final three quarters that led to them blowing a double-digit lead to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6 .
"Just like every week, I just prepare to play, and once we get to Sunday, we're going to see," Huntley said.
If it weren't for the uncertainty surrounding the Ravens' starting quarterback situation, this storyline would be headlining this list heading into this game. The four-time Pro Bowler downplayed the significance of going up against his former team, whom he spent the last five years with and enjoyed the most successful stretch of his career with during his media availability earlier this week.
However, the acrimonious end to his tenure in Cincinnati is well-documented and while he denies that there's any bad blood between him and the franchise that refused to compensate him for elite production, his Ravens teammates believe he's going to feast off that extra motivation. With current sack leader Tavius Robinson out for the rest of the season with a pectoral injury, he'll be counted on even more to carry the pass rush .
"I am excited to see him against his former team," inside linebacker Trenton Simpson said. "The things he [does] in practice, the way he rushes the passer and just how he gets off the ball, I believe that this game for him is about to be like one of those ones, like [a] multiple-sack game. I'm calling it, [and] I'm excited to see the celebration he does."
After trotting out makeshift blocking units over the last three weeks, featuring their second- and third-string right guards and moving their stud first-round rookie guard, Vega Ioane, to center, the Ravens are set to have a league-high fifth different configuration on Sunday. With two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens, whom they acquired in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles, the Ravens could have their best configuration yet by a wide margin.
The Ravens' new-look interior offensive line will have quite the tough first test in this game, going up against a revamped Bengals interior defensive line that features a pair of multi-time Pro Bowl imports in Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen, who each have three sacks through their team's first five games, which ties edge rusher Boye Mafe for the team lead.
While the Cincinnati defense has been susceptible to runs to the outside, which lean toward the strength of the Ravens' outside zone-centric rushing attack, the trio of Jurgens, Ioane and veteran left guard John Simpson will still have to hold up in pass protection and when offensive coordinator Declan Doyle dials inside run concepts like trap and power.
Prior to last week, when they held the Cleveland Browns' leading wideout, Denzel Boston, to one catch for 15 yards on five targets, the Ravens' secondary had struggled to keep the top receivers of opposing teams under control, as the defense as a whole has been rounding into shape. They'll be facing arguably their toughest challenge of the season, and at least since they face the Dallas Cowboys in Week 3, when they go up against the Bengals' lethal duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on Sunday.
Chase, in particular, has been a nagging thorn in the Ravens' side ever since he entered the league. The five-time Pro Bowler has had his most prolific outings against Baltimore, with averages of just under 10 receptions and 125 receiving yards per game and has scored five touchdowns in his last five games in this rivalry series. Higgins leads the Bengals this season with 423 receiving yards and is tied with Chase for the team lead in receptions with 27. The Ravens' outside cornerback duo of Nate Wiggins and four-time Pro Bowl veteran Marlon Humphrey will have their hands full anytime Joe Burrow drops back to pass.

title: Ravens Make Final Decision On Lamar Jackson's Status For Sunday
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens opted not to drag out Lamar Jackson’s medical situation through the weekend.
After head coach Jesse Mitner said on Friday the team was willing to take any decision with Jackson down to the wire if need be, and Jackson signaled how “very, very painful” the high ankle sprain was, the two-time MVP’s status ended up clarified well before kickoff. Baltimore ruled him out Saturday afternoon, making the messaging about this being a day-to-day injury for three weeks seem even more baffling.
Where twice before they ruled out Jackson on Friday, this time the team and player took it until Saturday. It was the same result, despite very different practice weeks,Jackson spoke about the severity of the injury and its limitations on him as anything but a daily complication, while Ravens head coach Jesse Minter has stuck with that messaging, which probably hasn't served the player, the team or its fans well.
Jackson was always quite likely to miss at least two games with the injury as we originally reported and in fact he will miss at least three including Sunday's key divisional game with the Bengals. While Minter has been calling Jackson “day-to-day” for three weeks the reality couldn’t be further from the truth as even after three limited practice sessions Jackson was not cleared for Week 7 after suffering the injury at the end of the first half in Week 4.
At this point it’s fair to expect that Jackson will have to practice fully a time or two in order for he and the Ravens to be comfortable with his return. Minter reiterated through the week that any final decision would include all parties being aligned that it was the right time for Jackson to return. Jackson is also the rarest of truly elite quarterback who has no future guarantees on his contract beyond this season and he has as much leverage as any NFL player ever has for 2027 with an $85M cap hit, a no-trade clause and a no-franchise tag clause. Which makes any injury with him the focus of increased attention.
“Again, between Lamar, our staff and us, it's going to be a decision based on him, how he feels and how effective [we] feel like it could be,” Minter said Friday after practice.
On Friday Jackson explained what it would take to be able to help the team enough to play:
“I don't feel like I have to be 100%,” Jackson said. “If I can just be out there and tolerate the pain in my ankle, that's it. If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play. But I'm restricted and I can't do what I do, I'm not helping. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that's not helping my team at all.”
Jackson also said on Friday: "I started feeling better, like I said, Sunday. Monday (entering Week 7). We came out and tried to run a little bit. I did better than I did the week prior, because I couldn't run at all the week prior. It was just crazy. It was hurting bad.."
Veteran Snoop Huntley gets the start instead. Huntley is a significantly limited passer, the entire scope of the passing game falters with him out and rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle better do a significantly better job of leaning into the screen game and multiplicity in the run game with Jackson out. He also better design more runs for Huntley, who can still move, and dabble with more RPOs.
The Bengals have a lethal interior pass rush led by offseason acquisition Dexter Lawrence – they are the best fourth-quarter pass rush in the NFL by a mile – and the Ravens are starting new center Cam Jurgens, who was struggling mightily for the Eagles at guard , and will field their fifth offensive line in seven weeks.
Doyle also better find ways to get role players into bigger roles with the potential for yards after the catch (especially two of these potential contributors ). Jackson has an 11-2 record against the Bengals (7-2 against Joe Burrow) and has run for 837 yards against them, the most any QB has amassed against any team in the history of the NFL.
Baltimore’s offense was a mess for three quarters against Atlanta with Huntley at the helm and for the final nine drives against the Browns, which produced no points.

title: Ravens Stock Report: 3 Role Players Who Can Provide A Boost Vs Bengals
full_text:
There will be no shortage of starpower on the field at M&T Bank Stadium Sunday.
Whether two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, still iffy with an ankle injury, plays or no t.
Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase have enjoyed historic games at Baltimore’s expense and Ravens $30M pass rusher Trey Hendrickson faces his former team for the first time, one he left with plenty of acrimony but a revenge spot he’s mostly tried to downplay. The AFC North battle is rich with subplots and drama, but could be decided by some lesser discussed players do things they don’t always do.
In particular, there are three role players who could be in position to make a pivotal play or two to shift this game in Baltimore’s favor. Given their issues holding leads and winning games at home, and considering how messy the secondary has been and what might still be to come at the trade deadline, and with the Bengals coming off a bye, the Ravens are going to need more than just their highest-paid players to step up and these three could be standouts if given the opportunity:
Rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle was pretty hard on  for the offense for their debacle in Week 6, back-up QB or not, and for good reason. He didn’t experiment nearly enough with multiplicity  in the run game and didn’t get enough people involved and didn’t attack the perimeter enough with others than Derrick Henry.
“I would say that what we put on tape wasn't up to our standard,” Doyle said.
The Bengals will not allow inside runs with tackle Dexter Lawrence anchoring and no one is really trying it. When Cincy allows nine yards a pop off left end and six off right end, while not go there? And pistol looks with Hill should work better the some of the stuff with Henry. Not sure how much under center runs should be a point of emphasis but designed screens for Hill and some pony package looks with Henry better be.
Thankfully, his hand injury only put him out one week. Without him, Baltimore’s tight end issues – top blocker Durham Smythe is out for the season and veteran Mark Andrews (one catch for four yards) is washed despite his top-10 compensation at his position. So getting Hibner back and off the injury report entirely is a big deal.
He has caught all five of his targets and made little plays into big gains. He can win on a double move in the slot or win after the catch and 9.0 yards of YAC per reception (Andrews is at 2.0 over the last two years) should have Declan Doyle seeking ways to activate him more and subjugate Andrews. Fellow rookie right end Josh Cuevas is doing more each week too. Hibner catching a ball out of the backfield feels inevitable and bet he is in motion quite a bit in this game.
Losing edge defender Tavius Robinson for the year is a big deal . A really big deal. He excels setting the edge, plays with real power and was coming along as a pass rusher and had a toolkit to naturally play opposite Hendrickson. The Ravens know that Hendrickson and Green both feel at their best rushing against the left tackle and it’s time for Jesse Minter to get creative about how to get him and Hendrickson on the field together.
I’ve liked what I’ve seen from Green when he twists inside and attacks the A Gap some. They could use a NASCAR package where Green starts in the wide position, almost a Wide 9, and loops inside with the pass rush like Hendrickson does.
Not that the Bengals will run much, or run well, but that’s not either of these guy’s fortes, Still, finding a way to keep Hendrickson healthy and effective for all four quarters is a must, and he has waned through games with his hand issue a concern.
He’s supposed to be the “closer” but has no sack and just four pressures in the fourth-quarter all season – Baltimore is among the dregs in pressure and sacks in that quarter – yet the Bengals are tops in the NFL in those metrics this season without him in the fourth. Having Green and Hendrickson try to impact the quarterback together needs to be a thing.
“Trey definitely feels more comfortable on the right,” defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said, “and … Mike seems pretty indifferent to it. So, both of those guys I think can eat regardless of where they're aligned.”

title: Top Four Reasons The Bengals Could Beat The Ravens Sunday
full_text:
The Ravens used to be one of the best home teams in the NFL.
Sunday will be a difficult test for rookie head coach Jesse Minter, who is once again juggling unusual personnel situations and tricky injury situations including starting quarterback Lamar Jackson, who is questionable with an ankle injury and made progress this week but perhaps not enough to play. The Bengals are fresh off a bye and in considerably better health. Jackson has owned them with an 11-2 record while averaging 29 points per game, but the Bengals offense has also had some legendary days at Baltimore’s expense and Minter’s defense was quite shaky in critical areas through the first third of the season.
These are the top four reasons the Bengals could win Sunday and push the Ravens down in the AFC North standings:
Even if Jackson plays, he has barely practiced for three weeks since suffering the injury, he has never worked much at all with new center Cam Jurgens at all (more on that in a minute) and his legs have been a huge part of his success against Cincy. Jackson has 837 rushing yards against them; most of any QB against any NFL team, but how much of that will be in the cards even if Jackson does suit up?
Rookie play caller Declan Doyle, coming off his worst performance as an offensive coordinator, has been hesitant to lean into designed runs and RPOs and Jackson’s legs have not been as much of a weapon since 2024, honestly. The Bengals also fortified their defensive line in a major way, they are holding opposing passers to the same rating Baltimore’s vaunted secondary is (87.0) and it certainly looks like this will be a situation where Jackson will have to feel out his ankle though the game.
That’s enough to sway the margins with two teams this well matched.
“I don't feel like I have to be 100%,” Jackson said on Friday about being able to play. “If I can just be out there and tolerate the pain in my ankle, that's it. If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play. But (if) I'm restricted and I can't do what I do, I'm not helping. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that's not helping my team at all.”
The Bengals have arguably the deepest and most impactful rotation of defensive tackles in the NFL right now and it goes way beyond just offseason-acquisition Dexter Lawrence . They are leading the NFL in sacks and pressures from that position and Jurgens has only had really two full workdays on the job in practice and that was somewhat split between two QBS.
Jurgens has not played center with any consistency in quite some time, moving to guard with the Eagles, he was playing poorly for Philadelphia and may have been on the cusp of being benched before the trade, he barely knows the offense and his teammates and he just came out of concussion protocol. If that seems like a lot, that’s because it is.
This will be the Ravens fifth offensive line combination in seven weeks and there is little interior cohesion and it’s been a problem all season. Not sure Jurgens fixes it right away against Sexy Dexy and this bunch and Lawrence knows him well from his time with the Giants battling Jurgens in the NFC East.
The Ravens are a joke in the fourth quarter, and they continue to set records for choking away double-digits leads and have blown three already this season and lost two of those games. With 16 losses in games where they lead by 10 or more since 2019, and having just done it again last week in Cleveland, this might be the Bengals catching them in a vulnerable moment.
None of the Ravens’ corners has been any good in the second half of games and top receivers have gutted them to the point it might need to be addressed before the trade deadline and its left hybrid safety Kyle Hamilton exacerbated by it all. Minter has tried to explain it away at times (I know a corner I would be trying to trade away ) but their late-game mental breakdowns are real and this team lacks the clutch gene and Joe Burrow has it and it might come down to the final possession. (Oh, and Bengals receiver Ja’Marr Chase has done things to the Ravens no WR has done to any other team in league history).
Former Bengal Trey Hendrickson may need to take this game over in a revenge spot; Baltimore is bottom seven in the NFL in fourth-quarter pressure rate and sack rate, while the Bengals are number one and it’s not even close with a 50% pressure rate and sublime 18.5% sack rate in the final quarter.
Baltimore’s choking is most acute at home. The Ravens recently had a five-game losing streak at home and they snapped it Week 4 against the Titans, but again failed to score in the second half of that game after Jackson went down and allowed Tennessee to hang around.
Kicker Tyer Loop hasn’t been great anywhere but has really struggled at home since the preseason and now he has competition back in the building. The Ravens seem incapable of putting forth a pure, focused four-quarter game at home and that might be what it takes to beat a talented Bengals squad.
Burrow is just 2-4 at Baltimore, so the Ravens do have that going for them, but he won at M&T Bank Stadium last year and two of those losses came when mastermind Mike Macdonald was running the Baltimore defense.

title: Ravens Final Week 7 Injury Report Reveals Major Change for Lamar Jackson
full_text:
After taking the practice field for the first time since suffering what he revealed was a high ankle sprain during his Friday media availability, Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was one of five players given a designation on the team's final injury report .
Fortunately for them, he joined defensive tackle Broderick Washington in being listed as questionable to play against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday in a massively important Week 7 AFC North showdown.
Game status vs. Bengals pic.twitter.com/bJIL9hngwi
"Right now, I'm headed in the right direction," Jackson said. "If it feels better tomorrow, we'll know tomorrow. So I can't call it. I just have a grace period until Sunday."
While seeing the two-time league MVP on the practice field all week was a welcome sight, it was still on a limited basis. However, head coach Jesse Minter shared that Jackson "was able to get a pretty good amount of work in" Friday's practice session.
"Between Lamar and our staff and us [coaches], it's going to be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective and things like that it can be," Minter said. "He's had a good couple days, but we'll see how it goes over the next 48 hours.
Minter had already ruled out veteran safety Jaylinn Hawkins with a knee injury that will keep him sidelined for multiple games, and he also ruled out fourth-year outside linebacker Tavius Robinson with what he revealed was a season-ending pectoral injury. This leaves the Ravens without one of their three starting safeties and their sack leader through the first six weeks with 3.5 .
The only other player given a final designation was third-year cornerback T.J. Tampa, who is listed as doubtful to play with a knee injury, as remains on injured reserve but returned to practice for the first time this week in a limited capacity.
The team's media podium might as well have been a ballroom floor with all the dancing around the question of whether Jackson or primary backup Tyler Huntley would be starting against the Bengals this week.
Usually, only the head coach and starting quarterback step to the podium to address the media on the Friday before upcoming games, which had been Huntley the previous two weeks and Jackson the four weeks before.
This time around, the Ravens had both quarterbacks speak after practice, and neither confirmed or denied who would and wouldn't start on Sunday, although Huntley expressed that he'd be ready to make his third straight start and 19th of his career if called upon.
"I just got to be ready to play Sunday if that's the case," Huntley said. Once we get to Sunday, we'll see."
The Ravens have posted 116 points, 14 touchdowns, 967 passing yards and 1,464 total yards in the 14 quarters with Jackson under center, and barely managed a third of those figures in the 10 quarters without him with 40 points, four touchdowns, 429 passing yards and 742 total yards.
While having the best dual-threat quarterback of all time back in the lineup would be a major boost not only for overall morale but also for the production and efficiency of the offense, Jackson doesn't want to be selfish by rushing back on the field if he can't be his usual dynamic and elusive self.
"I'm just trying to move how I move," Jackson said. "If I can't do that, I can't help my team. I can't put my team in a situation like that. I feel like I'm doing a disservice then."
The Bengals coaches were likely going to prepare to face either quarterback anyway. By having Jackson listed as questionable, which essentially equates to probable, and having him speak to the media in surprising depth about the nature and severity of his injury, they're giving their rivals a worst-case scenario for them to seriously consider coming to fruition on Saturday. Jackson as an 11-3 career record against the Bengals as a starter and was playing at an MVP level prior to suffering his injury.
"I don't feel like I have to be 100%.," Jackson said. "If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play. But I'm restricted. Like, I can't do what I do. I'm not helping nobody. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and get hit, [there's] no positives in that. That's not helping my team at all. I feel like I'm being selfish because it's about me at that point, you know, getting out there and be hurt. That's dumb."
