title: Ravens Head Coach Explains Lamar Jackson's Status For Week 7
full_text:
Ravens head coach Jesse Minter did not make an announcements about quarterback Lamar Jackson’s status for Sunday’s critical game against the Bengals, but left the door open that he could return from an ankle injury.
Minter would not commit to how Jackson’s status would be reflected on the final injury report – questionable would seem to be the most likely designation – and said the next 48 hours will play a role in whether back-up Snoop Huntley makes his third straight start of if Jackson is able to start the game with Baltimore trying to avoid consecutive losses in the AFC North.
“He was able to get in the work he needed to get in to potentially have a shot to play,” Minter said of Jackson’s three straight days of limited work in practice but not full participation. Minter also revealed that emerging edge talent Tavius Robinson was lost for the season with a pectoral injury and veteran safety Jaylinn Hawkins will not play Sunday as he deals with an injury.
The Ravens continue to put clips of Jackson at practice on their social media; make of that what you will. Huntley and Jackson both met with the media Friday and Jackson revealed that he is dealing with a high-ankle sprain, which generally carry a longer recovery time. He was wearing a wrap on the ankle as he spoke for the first time since suffering the injury, calling it "very, very painful."
"I'm headed on the right direction, but I can't call it right now," Jackson said of his status.
Jackson was unable to take the practice field at all the last two weeks and made definite strides this week. Minter had referred to Jackson’s status as “day to day” for weeks but also ruled him out on the past two Fridays. This meeting with the media was quite different. Minter reiterated that the decision will be made in consultation with the doctors and the quarterback himself; Jackson is in the final guaranteed year of his contract and has more leverage over this franchise than any player in the league arguably has over any franchise.
“We’ll see how it goes in the next 48 hours,” Minter said, adding as to the timetable of a final determination on his playing status could “go as long as it needs to take.”
Minter was hesitant to speak at length on what Jackson was and was knot able to do during the three sessions he took part in, though video of the portions open to the media appeared to indicate him being less encumbered on Thursday than he had been on Wednesday. Minter said Jackson put in “a pretty good amount of work” on Friday.
Jackson has not played since the first half of Week 4’s victory over the Titans. He was in MVP form at the time but was caught from behind stepping up in the pocket and trying to scramble and has yet to take the field in a game since then. Huntley said he is operating as if he could be called on again Sunday.
“You just prepare to play and when it comes down to Sunday we’ll see,” Huntley said.
The Bengals are coming off a bye and have revamped their defensive front , and will provide a strong challenge. Newly acquired center Cam Jurgens will be making his debut with Baltimore after missing two games in the concussion protocol.
Baltimore's secondary was already struggling - again blowing 10 point leads and with one of the worst fourth-quarter defenses in the NFL- prior to Hawkins being ruled out. Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase has already set NFL records against the Ravens and Minter had better be ready to make some changes to his cornerback usage, especially if his defense will have to operate with a limited back-up QB.

title: Trenton Simpson Details Key To Breakout Campaign With Ravens
full_text:
In the modern NFL, a position with one of the steepest learning curves for players making the transition from college to the professional level is at off-ball linebacker.
Given the complexities and illusions thereof that offenses look to portray and display on a down-to-down basis with pre-snap motions and an emphasis on targeting the middle of the field in the passing game, becoming just a serviceable inside linebacker, let alone a good-to-above-average one, is harder than ever and takes time.
More often than not, it may take multiple seasons and some tough growing pains and learning lessons for a full maturation to take place and for a talented player at the position to begin realizing their full potential.
That was the career arc for Baltimore Ravens 2020 first-rounder Patrick Queen, who broke out in a big way in his fourth season, earning Pro Bowl and Second Team All Pro honors in 2023 before he departed for greener pastures in free agency the following offseason.
Three years later, his successor appears to be following in his footsteps. Through the first third of the final year of his rookie contract, 2023 third-rounder Trenton Simpson has had quite an impressive start to his breakout campaign .
Through six games, he is one of only two NFL defenders who have recorded 40-plus tackles, five-plus tackles for loss and an interception this season. The only other player to have reached such a notable feat is his teammate, three-time All Pro Kyle Hamilton.
Only two NFL defenders have each recorded 40+ tackles, 5+ TFL and an INT this season. Both play for the @Ravens : Kyle Hamilton and Trenton Simpson. pic.twitter.com/rGcFayw0iW
After opening each of the last two seasons at the starting WILL spot next to four-time Pro Bowl veteran Roquan Smith , only to get benched and replaced in the lineup, Simpson pointed to the different approach he took to his contract year as the primary reason for his breakout and why the game is finally starting to slow down for him.
"I come in every morning at 6 o'clock, [and] I meet with my linebacker coach," Simpson said. "[Also], my mentality [and] the way I'm playing is just no fear, one play at a time, [give] everything I've got [and] focus on my one key. When the ball is snapped, if I see something, trust it, go and just play like a Raven, hit anything that moves."
While most of the Ravens coaching staff was overhauled when former head coach John Harbaugh was fired after a massively disappointing 2025 season, one of the few holdovers that first-year head coach Jesse Minter retained was inside linebackers coach Tyler Santucci. This meant that Simpson would have the same position coach in back-to-back seasons for the first time in his career, which is clearly paying major dividends given all his success.
"Coming in early allows [me] to get extra two hours on film, taking care of my body [and] getting an extra lift a week," Simpson said. "I'd say [I'm focusing on] nutrition, getting massages now [and] becoming a real pro.
"All the linebackers come in early, but I think that's allowed all of us to play well together. It allows us to all see the things on the same page. Everybody's playing at a high level in that room. I think it's really working."
In addition to Santucci playing a major role, Simpson also credits the incredible example that Smith sets day in and day out as another invaluable asset in his continued development and maturation as a player.
"He showed me the way," Simpson said. "He's been an All-Pro player [and] he's one of the best at it. [I've been] seeing what he's done over these last four years and [I'm] trying to translate it to my game because I've noticed playing beside him [that] he's so ahead before the ball even snaps.
"I think this year that's what coming in and watching more film has allowed me to do. If I see a formation, it's like, 'It's only going to be one or two things.' Then, once you see it, you just go."
Given Simpson's age, having just turned 25 this past summer, and the upward trajectory that he is currently on, he's a prime candidate for an in-season early contract extension . In the past, as recently as last year with nose tackle Travis Jones, the Ravens have had no problem locking in young rising stars in the midst of or heading toward breakouts.
Of the three remaining members of the team's 2023 NFL Draft class playing in the final year of their rookie deals, both Simpson and fourth-round edge rusher Tavius Robinson have shown that they're worthy of being extended. However, Simpson is more likely to agree to an early deal, since Robinson leads the team in sacks and plays a premium position that teams across the league would pay much more for if he reaches, or even comes close to, double-digit sacks this year.
Simpson has expressed that he wants to remain with the Ravens for the long haul on numerous occasions, including most recently on an episode of 'The Lounge' podcast earlier this week.
"I want to send a message to this organization like, y'all drafted me four years ago, and I want to prove to y'all that I want to be here and be a Raven for the rest of my career," Simpson said. "I know going out to practice every day and playing with my hair on fire in games, that'll make that happen."
Since Minter's variation of the Ravens scheme has helped unlock his full potential, Simpson might be compelled to want to stick around that much more at a reasonable price, if it means he can keep playing alongside Smith, whose play and impact were negatively affected following Queen's departure. By not letting this homegrown ascending talent walk, they could very well wind up having the best off-ball linebacker tandem once again.
Josh is a writer for Baltimore Ravens On SI focusing primarily on original content and reporting. He provides analysis, breakdowns, profiles, and reports on important news and transactions from and about the Ravens. His professional resume as a sports reporter includes covering local events, teams, and athletes in his hometown of Anchorage, Alaska for Anchorage Daily News. His coverage on the Ravens and other NFL teams has been featured on Heavy.com/sports, Maryland Sports Blog and most recently Baltimore Beatdown from 2021 until 2025.

title: The Ravens Must Explore These 3 Options To Fix Their Cornerback Problem
full_text:
The Ravens’ secondary is a primary concern.
Rookie head coach Jesse Minter can try to downplay it at times, and talk around it, but the fact that he is flooding the field with more defensive backs than anyone in the AFC  (in dime coverage 33% of the time, nearly twice as much as anyone in his conference) with not much to show for it has to be grating on him. Hybrid defender Kyle Hamilton, playing more linebacker now, has been the voice of reason, calling out this group for not playing to its standard, and this better get cleaned up quickly.
The Ravens get Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow off a bye on Sunday then it’s Josh Allen off a bye in Buffalo and Trevor Lawrence, Bryce Young and CJ Stroud are all in good form and looming. The schedule is about to get very real, and the Ravens need to get more out of their cornerbacks in particular. And Minter knows it.
“I think every week we're chasing certain things,” Minter said on Wednesday. “Really, after the Dallas game, I didn't think we – as much as their weapons were what they were – I really didn't think we played the run that well and played blocks and played really physically. I thought going into that next game we really improved in that area. Then it was obviously third down, and we're chasing improvement in that area.
“So, I think there's a lot of things that the guys are getting more in tune with each other, with how we play, physicality, being able to stop the run and the different coverages that we try to play. But there's always a million things that we're chasing, and it's no different this week. But I do see – I've told the defense now for a few weeks in a row, you see improvement. We're not anywhere where we want to be, but I see us getting better. And to Kyle's point, let's just keep chasing improvement every single day."
Minter needs to consider these measures to try to fix his secondary and especially to cull more impact from his corners , which has been a specialty of his throughout his career. This should be the progression:
Ravens GM Eric DeCosta has been whispering about his good this kid is for years and bragging to the local media – barely covertly, I guess – about how other teams covet him and want him in trade . Well, your team’s corners are allowing a bottom-10 passer rating and have combined for a handful of pass breakups and no picks despite being thrown on more in the fourth quarter than anyone else.
So now that Tampa is coming back from his latest injury setback, let’s get him on the field and give him a real runway. Not just a handful of dime snaps, but real stuff. Like starting outside corner stuff, because you need to fix your slot in the worst way possible , and Marlon Humphrey needs to try to earn his $19M there.
Young corners Keyon Martin and Chandler Rivers are allowing a passer rating of 119 in the slot and overall the numbers in the slot are brutal: 117.7 passer rating (27th) and 510 yards (27th). These elite QBs will shred them there and that’s where Humphrey needs to be (and if that doesn’t work just keep reading).
Minter doesn’t want to play veteran Chidobe Awuzie and hasn’t ever seemed to favor him, and it’s hard to see that changing with Tampa working back to the lineup. I like corner Amani Oruwariye and he has the long levers and body type that worked so well for Minter running his zone stuff with the Chargers.
He’s played in the league and played okay at times and has a skillset that would seem to lend itself to this scheme. This dude is 6-foot-2, 200 pounds. Probably worthy of a look-see if this team keeps blowing leads and getting torched by competent wide receivers. The Ravens also haven’t been tested by tight ends really yet but the propensity for that is increasing as soon as Sunday .
One could argue despite all the money and resources and former first-round picks at this position it is both the most underachieving and/or the biggest position of need on the roster. Yoi have to give to get and moving out Humphrey’s salary to create wiggle room to add wouldn’t be crazy.
The Ravens have the least cap space in the NFL, with limited options to restructure to add in a meaningful way, and addition by subtraction could be in order. The Chargers are a miserable 0-6, Minter knows their defensive backs incredibly well, and the Ravens and Chargers made a trade a year ago in which Minter turned benched first-round pick Odafe Oweh into a stud in LA.
Maybe he could do it again on Baltimore’s side this year, but it might require moving salary to create space, and specifically create space at corner.  I wouldn’t discount the idea and as longtime NFL personnel guy Pat Kirwan pointed out to me before the season the Ravens should be able to run a cheaper secondary with the scheme the star and not carrying bloated $20M contracts for allegedly top man-coverage guys who don’t pick the ball off.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Grading Ravens Defensive Position Groups Through Six Weeks
full_text:
With Week 6 in the rearview and Week 7 on the horizon, the 2026 NFL regular season is a third of the way in the books. The Baltimore Ravens currently find themselves in a three-way tie for the best record in the AFC North at 4-2, and the defense has been a work in progress while still contributing to the team's overall success.
Under new head coach and defensive play-caller Jesse Minter, they came into the season expected to be one of the best units in the league, and while they've dominated entire halves and sometimes three quarters of games, they've yet to put together a full four quarters of excellence.
The talent that general manager Eric DeCosta amassed on the defensive side of the ball has shown flashes of dominance and could round into a strength for this year's team as the offense continues to get healthy and keep being explosive . Here's how each position group has graded out thus far.
Gradual ramp-ups in training camp and delayed regular-season debuts prevented this talented bunch from hitting the ground running. However, over the past two games, they've begun to play up to their immense potential collectively instead of as individuals in spurts. The trio of multi-time Pro Bowlers Nnamdi Madubuike and Calais Campbell and budding star Travis Jones gives the Ravens one of the best interiors in the league.
In the four games since Madubuike returned from a serious neck injury that cut his 2025 season short, he looks more and more like his game-wrecking pre-injury form. Campbell remains the ageless wonder and has looked great the past two weeks and Jones as been a stud from the start of the season when it comes to making plays against the run at and behind the line of scrimmage. Behind them, veterans John Jenkins, Broderick Washington and third-year pro Aeneas Peebles have provided solid depth but haven't really stood out in a noticeable or consistent way.
This group has been the most pleasant surprise of the entire defense thus far this season, with how consistently disruptive they've been down in and down out each week, especially at the top of the depth chart. After a down year in 2025 that still saw him get voted to his fourth straight Pro Bowl, veteran Roquan Smith is back to playing at an All Pro level, leading the team with 47 total tackles, tying for the second-most sacks with two and making plays on the ball with an interception, forced fumble and two pass breakups.
At the WILL spot, fourth-year pro Trenton Simpson, is finally putting it all together in a contract year and has been enjoying quite the breakout campaign. He's recorded the third-most total tackles on the team with 41, including tying for the most tackles for loss with six, and he also has an interception to go along with a fumble recovery and a pass breakup. Second-year pros Teddye Buchanan and Jay Higgins have predominantly played special teams, with Buchanan seeing some limited snaps on defense in base personnel packages.
This is another group that has been hindered by health to a degree, with four-time Pro Bowl veteran and prized free agent acquisition Trey Hendrickson sustaining a finger injury that required surgery and caused him to miss two games. Yet in four games, he has still managed to record a pair of sacks, four quarterback hits and a 22.7% pressure rate, the highest rate among defenders with at least 25 pressures this season, according to NextGenStats .
Leading the Ravens with 3.5 sacks through six games is Tavius Robinson, another fourth-year pro making the most of his extended playing time in the final season of his rookie deal. He also leads the team with eight quarterback hits, batted down two passes and forced a fumble. Second-year pro Mike Green is tied with Hendrickson for the second-most sacks on the team with a pair and stepped up in a big way during the two games he was out. He ranks second on the team with six quarterback hits and has been playing the run well with four tackles for loss.
The Ravens also have a pair of rookies who have been playing regularly , with second-rounder Zion Young's snaps coming on defense during early downs while undrafted free agent Ethan Burke has primarily played on special teams but was the first of the two to record a sack.
The Ravens have gotten a mixed bag of results from this position group, with some impressive plays and missed opportunities to make more impactful ones despite constantly being in good position in coverage. They've been playing third-year pro Nate Wiggins and four-time Pro Bowl veteran Marlon Humphrey on the perimeter and deploying both second-year pro Keyon Martin and fifth-round rookie Chandler Rivers at nickel for stretches.
As a group, they've struggled to contain No. 1 wide receivers from both inconsistent and highly efficient passing offenses and haven't been making enough plays on the ball, with no interceptions and just nine pass breakups between them. Wiggins has been the best of the bunch, allowing just a 51.7 % completion rate and an opposing passer rating of 65.7. Neither he nor Humphrey has given up a touchdown this year yet and will need to raise their game even more during the next third of the season with tougher opponents yet to come.
The saving grace keeping this grade from being flat-out 'D' or 'C-' at best is the fact that three-time All Pro Kyle Hamilton is playing like a well-deserving Defensive Player of the Year candidate right now, and second-year pro Malaki Starks has shown signs of improvement over the past couple of weeks. What was being billed as potentially the best trio in the league all summer has fallen well short of expectations to start the season.
Collectively, they have not only failed to consistently come up with big plays in key moments but have also been the main culprits in some very detrimental breakdowns in coverage late in games and on third downs, especially.
Starks appears to be turning a corner, making plays both in coverage and as a forceful player against the run. However, the same can not be said about veteran free agent acquisition Jaylinn Hawkins, who has disappointed thus far. He has no pass breakups, interceptions, tackles for loss or plays on the ball of any kind. He'll need to start turning it around before the Ravens' coaches are forced to find a configuration that works better without him, possibly one that utilizes second-year undrafted gem and special teams ace Keondre Jackson.
Coming into the regular season after a disastrous end to his rookie year and a discouraging performance in the preseason, a lot of eyes were on and remain on second-year placekicker Tyler Loop. He's drilled some impressive kicks in high-leverage situations, including the walk-off winner in Rio de Janeiro in Week 3 to beat the Dallas Cowboys in a thriller and setting a new home-field record for the longest successful attempt. However, he's still struggled with consistency when it comes to making clutch kicks in the second half of games. Both of the Ravens' losses have featured missed kicks by Loop from under 50 yards, and this year, he's 10-of-13 on field goals, with one blocked attempt and two bad misses. The Ravens signed veteran kicker Jake Moody to the practice squad at the onset of the season to give Loop some competition and recently brought him back earlier this week in the wake of his recent struggles.
Rookie punter Ryan Eckley has been the field-flipping weapon that the Ravens envisioned they were getting when they selected him in the sixth round of this year's draft. Half of his punts have pinned the opposing team's offense inside its own 20-yard line; he's averaging 46.9 yards per punt and his longest has been 62 yards. As far as the return game goes, the Ravens haven't gotten much juice from second-year pro LaJohntay Wester, who's returned 10 punts for 91 yards with a long of 24. He's one of three players who have returned kicks, and none have broken one longer than 42 yards (Chris Moore in the season opener.
Josh is a writer for Baltimore Ravens On SI…

title: Bills' Best Asset Not Enough NFL Experts Are Talking About Responsible for 5-1 Start
full_text:
It's a sometimes forgotten aspect of the game that was emphasized by Buffalo Bills ' Hall-of-Fame head coach Marv Levy.
For as good as the Bills' offense has been through the first six games of the 2026 season, the special teams have been nearly flawless. Buffalo currently ranks second overall in the DVOA metric measuring special teams production and efficiency.
In fact, Buffalo has been so brilliant in that one-third of the game that special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers earned Bills' Assistant Coach of the Year honors in On SI's bye week superlatives .
Making the production even more impressive, it's not only one or two areas where the Bills' specialists are thriving during the team's 5-1 season start. Buffalo has enjoyed efficient across the board from kicking, punting, returning, covering kicks and winning the field position battle in key spots.
"Loving the way, the confidence that our special teams is playing with and the standard that they kind of showed and have to keep going," said head coach Joe Brady in the aftermath of the Week 6 road win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
Of note, Ray Davis leads the NFL in kickoff return average (31.0) and Tyler Bass has made all 13 field goal tries .
Realistically, the Bills' special teams can claim credit for turning the tide in three of the five victories. Their special teams play was clearly superior on the road in Weeks 5 and 6.
The Bills went on the road and pulled out a season-opening victory with plenty of help from the kicking game. In his first game in more than one year, Tyler Bass hit all three field goals in his return. Meanwhile, seventh-round rookie punter Tommy Doman netted  54.5 yards per punt on two boots.
Ray Davis opened the primetime affair by returning the Rams' kickoff 70 yards, setting up an early Bills' field goal. Then, in overtime, Greg Rousseau blocked a 48-yard game-winning field goal attempt by the Rams to give the Bills new life on Monday Night Football. On the ensuing possession, Bass ended the marathon by nailing a 45-yard field goal coming out of the two-minute warning.
Bass made all four of his field goal attempts in the road win over the Raiders. His first three-pointer, which capped Buffalo's opening possession, was set up by a 40-yard kickoff return by Davis. Doman punted twice during the victory, forcing two fair catches by Las Vegas.

title: Who Should Bills' Fans Root For during Week 7 Bye?
full_text:
Following back-to-back narrow victories on the road over the past two weeks out West against the Los Angeles Rams and Las Vegas Raiders, the Buffalo Bills have recently had a few days of rest during a seemingly much-needed bye week .
However, although the players and coaches in Western New York might be taking things a little easier this week , that doesn’t mean there isn’t still some business to attend to before next week’s preparations begin for an enticing AFC matchup against the Baltimore Ravens in Orchard Park at the new Highmark Stadium on November 1 at 1 p.m. ET.
Bills ON SI recently highlighted some critical changes that must be made despite the team’s 5-1 record, including some possible trades that could be processed by Bills’ general manager Brandon Beane before the NFL’s trade deadline of November 10 at 4:00 p.m. ET.
And, with that said, there’s some work for Bills Mafia to do this weekend, as well, as the fanbase will be tasked with the ever important job of scoreboard watching around the league on Sunday afternoon and evening.
As of now, the Bills hold a slight lead over the New England Patriots in the AFC East after quarterback Drake Maye and Co.’s disappointing primetime loss to the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on Amazon Prime’s Thursday Night Football just the other day, and there’s a chance that other teams nipping at Buffalo’s heels could—hopefully—suffer a similar fate this weekend.
With that in mind, here are seven crucial games for Bills’ fans to keep tabs on during this upcoming slate of NFL games in Week 7.
Despite starting the 2026 campaign with a 2-2 record to begin the fall, Pittsburgh has since reeled off two consecutive victories to even things up with the Cleveland Browns and Baltimore Ravens in the AFC North Standings.
The Steelers are seemingly finding their stride right now behind longtime NFL quarterback Aaron Rodgers and running back Jaylen Warren, so it’d be a nice gesture by the Saints if they could somehow slow Pittsburgh’s roll at the current moment.
An international loss by the Steelers is what Bills’ fans should be rooting for on Sunday morning this weekend.
Ultimately, neither Miami nor New York seem to be too much of a threat to the Bills in the AFC standings or the divisional standings this fall , but that still doesn’t matter.
Given that the Jets have two wins on the season and the Dolphins have zero to their name yet, it’d be a good idea for Bills’ fans to root for Miami and first-year head coach Jeff Hafley to get off the schneid to end October.
It’ll be a tough task on the road at MetLife Stadium, though, especially after the Jets just held tough with the Patriots in Week 6 during a 26-19 loss at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts.
The upcoming meeting between the Bengals and the Ravens is intriguing for a multitude of reasons, but for Bills’ fans it’ll be interesting for at least two specific points of discussion.
First, is quarterback Lamar Jackson playing against Cincinnati? If he isn’t, which could certainly be the case given that he’s missed the last two weeks with an ankle injury, then it’ll be longtime backup quarterback Tyler Huntley running the show once again.
And, if that does end up being the situation for Baltimore, then it’ll also mean that Jackson has another week of rest and preparation to get ready for a crucial AFC matchup against the Bills at Highmark Stadium next week.
The second reason it’s important?
Well, both the Bengals and Ravens possess a winning record at the moment, so it’ll be important to have the game end in a loss for one of Buffalo’s AFC counterparts instead of ending in a tie like the Washington Commanders and New York Giants did over in the NFC in bizarre fashion just two weeks ago.
For momentum purposes, it might be a good idea to have Baltimore top Cincinnati in the game on Sunday so that Jackson and Co. aren’t looking for even more revenge next week at Highmark Stadium following two straight losses to the Bills over the past few seasons.
In the end, this game probably won’t wind up being much of a contest given how surprisingly well the Cleveland Browns have started off the season, but it’ll still be important for fans to root for the Tennessee Titans in an upset at Nissan Stadium on Sunday afternoon.
Cleveland currently sits atop the AFC North through six weeks of the season under first-year head coach Todd Monken, and it’s been one of the biggest shockers of the 2026 season thus far.
The sooner that some teams can start knocking the Browns down a peg in the AFC standings, then the better it’ll be for Buffalo’s playoff chances later on this season . . . particularly when it pertains to possibly getting the No. 1 seed in the conference.
That was always the goal under former Bills’ head coach Sean McDermott over the past nine years, but unfortunately it never happened .
At this point of the season, things are looking a little bleak for the Denver Broncos despite their 4-2 record.
Quarterback Bo Nix has been receiving criticism for practically being a shell of himself on the field through the first six weeks of the season, and it’s a bit hard to fathom that this is the same squad that dismissed the Bills and quarterback Josh Allen from the AFC divisional round playoffs this past January.
The Cardinals are coming off a big win against the reeling Rams this past week, so it’ll be interesting to see how they stack up against Denver on Sunday.
It’d be a big boost for Buffalo if Arizona was somehow able to come away with an intraconference victory at State Farm Stadium.
Bills’ fans should be rooting for the continued downfall of head coach Sean Payton’s Broncos the rest of the season, especially considering the two teams will meet up later this season on Christmas night for a big matchup that will be broadcast on Netflix .
Although Buffalo managed to defeat both of these teams in back-to-back weeks following a dismal divisional loss to the Patriots at home, it’s still an important game to watch for Bills’ fans.
Well, the hope is that Los Angeles will be able to right the ship after two straight losses and knock the reeling Raiders down another peg heading into November.
Las Vegas looked like a sneaky AFC contender to start September, but now they’re sitting at 3-3. So, if Los Angeles can serve the AFC West squad another loss for a fourth straight week, then it’ll only mean positive things for Buffalo moving forward.
The less possible playoff competition the Bills have to worry about later on this season, the better.
This is the big one, Bills’ fans.
Sitting at a perfect 5-0 following a bye of their own a couple weeks ago in Week 5, the Chiefs are the only remaining undefeated squad in the AFC at this point in time.
Buffalo is right behind Kansas City in the standings, though, so it’ll be crucial for the Seahawks to give quarterback Patrick Mahomes, head coach Andy Reid, and the rest of the Chiefs’ team their first loss of the 2026 campaign.
For years, the Bills have been desperately trying to obtain the No. 1 seed in the playoffs ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs, and it’s yet to happen during former 2024 MVP quarterback Josh Allen’s first eight years in the league.
If it’s going to happen in Year 9, then the Chiefs are going to have to start piling up some losses sooner than later.
This game certainly seems like the first possible one.
Bills Mafia must put all of their cheering efforts into joining Seattle’s 12th-man on NBC ’s Sunday Night Football to end this weekend.
A loss by the Chiefs on Sunday evening would only make Buffalo’s meeting with Kansas City at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park on Thanksgiving night all the more exciting.
Let’s hope it happens, folks.

title: One NFL Trade Deadline Move Bills Must Make
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline approaching, Buffalo Bills general manager Brandon Beane should be working the phones in an attempt to shore up his team's defense. The Bills currently have two major needs, with cornerback and safety being problematic through their first six games.
Buffalo brought back Tre'Davious White , who started 16 games in 2025. White is currently on the practice squad, but the Bills will be working to get him up to speed as soon as possible.
While his addition will help, the Bills are still without a game-changing safety and C.J. Gardner-Johnson reminded them that he shouldn't be relied upon after getting ejected in Week 6, and eventually suspended for Week 8 , for spitting at Brock Bowers.
The good news for Beane is that there are several names rumored to be available , with the biggest name being Budda Baker of the Arizona Cardinals. As good as Baker is, he shouldn't be the top priority. Instead, Beane should be calling the Tennessee Titans about Amani Hooker.
Baker is a true playmaker at the position, but he's better in the box rather than as a deep cover safety. In Buffalo, it's far more urgent for them to address their coverage woes.
The Bills enter their bye week ranked 31st in defensive passing yards, and much of that has fallen on the performance of the safeties. Six games into the season, their highest-rated safety in coverage has been Gardner-Johnson, who has a 62.7 grade from PFF . Fellow starter Cole Bishop has a coverage grade of 47.5, while Damar Hamlin is sitting at 56.1.
Baker's coverage grade is lower than all three of those safeties, with a 47.1 entering Week 7 . It'sd a completely different story with Hooker, however, who has a 71.7 coverage grade , which is the 16th-highest at the position.
What makes Hooker even more intriguing, though, is that he's been even better against the run. The veteran currently has an 88.5 against the run, which helped him earn an 81.1 overall, which is currently the eighth-highest score at safety.
Tennessee is just 1-5 and they're expected to be sellers at the deadline. The Bills are on the other end of the spectrum, sitting at 5-1 and are one of the favorites to contend for a Super Bowl. To help increase their odds of finally winning a title, they need to shore up their primary weakness and Hooker is the perfect addition to do exactly that.

title: Bills Face Major Test After Bye With One of NFL’s Toughest Schedules
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are one of the hottest teams in the NFL right now. First-year head coach Joe Brady has them off to a 5-1 start as they enter their Week 7 bye.
Buffalo's only loss thus far came to the New England Patriots , their top AFC East rival, but the Pats recent loss dropped them to 4-3, giving the Bills some cushion.
Meanwhile, franchise quarterback Josh Allen is expecting the team to play its "best football" coming out of the Week 7 bye. That's vital because Buffalo will face a huge test right off the bat.
The Bills will host the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8, followed by visiting the Minnesota Vikings in Week 9. Those two opponents will be tough to handle, but it doesn't get much better after that with the Bills facing the fourth-toughest remaining schedule in the league.
Remaining Strength of Schedule 1. MIN --- hardest --- 2. ATL 3. MIA ... 30. DAL 31. TB 32. JAX --- easiest ---- pic.twitter.com/3ZNbIcafwe
In addition to playing the Ravens and Vikings, the Bills will see some of the top teams in the league, including the Kansas City Cheifs, Green Bay Packers, Chicago Bears, and the Patriots. They also have a Christmas Day game against the Denver Broncos , the team that knocked them out of the playoffs last season.
Brady and the Bills know their offense will be up to the challenge, but rookie defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard has to find a way to get more out of the defense. Buffalo is currently 31st in defensive yardage and 28th in points . Compare that to an offense that's sixth in yardage and first in points, and it's easy to see where the focus needs to be during the bye week.

He's met the challenge so far and if they can get through this schedule with enough wins to take the division, Brady and company will go into the postseason full of confidence.

title: Bills Brought Tre'Davious White Back, So What's Next Move to Boost Subpar Defense?
full_text:
It's no secret that the Buffalo Bills ' defense needs to improve at multiple positions.
The Bills, who are allowing 28.5 points per game, ranks next to last amongst their NFL peers in pass defense (285.8).
After keeping only three true outside cornerbacks on its 53-man roster, Buffalo finally reinforced its depth there by bringing  veteran Tre'Davious White back into the building this past week.
While there's an argument to be made that the Bills must seek more cornerback help on the trade market prior to the November 10 deadline, the reality is they likely won't be able to add anyone more capable than White at this point.
Buffalo has only $4.5 million in salary cap space available (per Spotrac), and there are needs for upgrades at safety and inside linebacker, too. In all likelihood, however, any changes at those two positions will come from within.
In the wake of a suspension and poor performance, one has to think Chauncey Gardner-Johnson is in danger of losing his starting status . The Bills simply need more from their safeties in former NFL safety Jim Leonhard's defense.
Unfortunately, former All-Pro Jordan Poyer isn't walking through that door this time. It also doesn't appear realistic for the Bills to add a true difference-maker like Budda Baker due to cap constraints.
While veteran Damar Hamlin can be serviceable in a starting role, Buffalo has two other options to explore.
One line of thinking says fifth-round rookie Jalon Kilgore, the fourth safety on the roster,  should get a chance to learn on the job. Kilgore made his defensive debut against the Las Vegas Raiders following Gardner-Johnson's ejection.
Kilgore totaled 11 snaps as an extra safety. He made a key third-down pass breakup, and he also allowed a touchdown.
The other option is to sign veteran Geno Stone off the practice squad . Stone, who has game experience at both strong and free safety, made 34 consecutive starts for the Cincinnati Bengals prior to signing with the Bills this past March.
In 2023, Stone led all NFL safeties with seven interceptions for the Baltimore Ravens. He has seemingly struggled since then, and it's a bit concerning that he didn't show enough during training camp to not earn a roster spot.
Although head coach Joe Brady has publicly expressed his satisfaction with the Bills' linebacking corps, there's the potential to provide a boost by making an internal change.
"I think you're not a fan of the way our linebackers are playing, based off some of the questions, but I have no issues with the way our linebackers our playing right now," said Brady prior to the Week 6 road game.
Whether it's taking away coverage snaps from either Terrel Bernard or Dorian Williams, it seems like a good time to activate veteran Shaq Thompson off the practice squad . Not re-joining the Bills until after training camp, the former first-round draft pick has presumably spent the season's first six weeks ramping up into playing shape.
If it's not Thompson, then there likely won't be any in-season change to the linebacking corps.
In fact, I'm not even sure there's an impactful enough trade to be made by general manager Brandon Beane, whose best deadline move in recent years is likely securing cornerback Rasul Douglas for the 2023 stretch run.
The Bills are going to have to bank on players continuing to grow into the defense, and Leonhard's ability to maximize the talent available.

title: Bills Paired With Eagles For Trade That Would Fix Defensive Problem for Buffalo
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills' defense has been a major problem during the 2026 season and general manager Brandon Beane needs to be aggressive to help that side of the ball out.
In the first year under new defenisve coordinator Jim Leonhard, the Bills sport one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Buffalo has been especially bad against the pass, with the Bills ranking 31st.
One major cause of their struggles against the pass has been the Bills' cornerbacks room, which has seen lackluster play from both Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun, with the former getting benched recently. Things have been so bad that the Bills brought Tre'Davious White back in the hopes he can help improve things.
The Bills still have a few more weeks before the trade deadline to assess where they stand, but if things keep going the way they have been, a cornerback trade is needed.
With the Philadelphia Eagles in rough shape following a 2-4 start and the loss of Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season, general manager Howie Roseman could start selling at the deadline.
One player The Athletic's Daniel Popper believes could be for sale is cornerback Riq Woolen, and he thinks the Bills could be a fit.
"Woolen won a Super Bowl with the Seahawks last season. He then hit free agency and, rather surprisingly, a market did not materialize for him. Woolen ended up signing a one-year deal with the Eagles. Although he has given up two touchdowns, Woolen has played well in coverage down-to-down for Philadelphia. He was in tight coverage on the Parker Washington one-handed touchdown in the Eagles’ loss to the Jaguars in Week 5. The combination of size and speed will always make Woolen an intriguing piece," Popper said.
"Best fits: Lions, Steelers, Bills, Jaguars," he added.
The Eagles signed Woolen to a one-year , $12 million contract, which means he could leave in free agency in 2027 for nothing. With Philly going nowhere fast, it makes sense to unload him to make sure that doesn't happen.
According to Pro Football Focus , Woolen's coverage grade in 2026 is a healthy 68.3, which ranks 25th at the position.
That mark ranks higher than both Igbinosun's (48.2) and Hairston's (36.4), and even No. 1 cornerback Christian Benford's (53.6).
While Woolen's raw coverage numbers haven't been great (53.3% completion rate, 108.5 passer rating), he is still doing better than all three of the Bills' top-three cornerbacks in completion rate allowed, and he has a superior passer rating permitted than Benford and Hairston.
Another plus with Woolen is his experience, something he has more of than Hairston and Igbinosun combined. He also has a Super Bowl ring, which is particularly intriguing for a Bills team gunning for that exact thing in 2026.
While we'd love for the Bills to swing a bit higher in their pursuit of a cornerback addition, the elite of the elite rarely become available.
Woolen would be a fine consolation prize who will come at the reasonable price of a Day 3 pick.

title: Bills Could Be Destined for Record-Breaking Season in Many Ways
full_text:
It’s already been a good week for the first-place team in the AFC East, and that club won’t be taking the field until a week from this Sunday.
On Thursday evening at Soldier Field, the Chicago Bears cooled off the New England Patriots. Ben Johnson’s team came away with a 30-24 triumph in a contest which saw New England’s Drake Maye and Chicago’s Caleb Williams both throw for 300-plus yards.
That means Joe Brady’s 5-1 Buffalo Bills have extended their lead in the division as the Pats dropped to 4-3. Of course, there’s still a lot of football remaining in the league’s 107th campaign.
Buffalo's drives this season: #1 of 32 in points per drive (3.13) #1 in drives ending in a score (57%) #1 in EPA per drive (1.15) #1 in series conversion rate (80.2%) punts on 19% of drives, the lowest in the NFL
Six weeks and one game into the 2026 NFL season and one thing is abundantly clear: Putting 30-plus points on the board is becoming more of a common occurrence. Last night’s performance by the Bears marked the 55th time a team reached that figure this season.
How did Josh Allen make this TD pass to Keon Coleman? BUFvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CNLw6KW2tC
Such is the case with Brady’s Bills. An offensive unit led by the tag team duo of quarterback Josh Allen and running back James Cook has already produced 23 touchdowns in six contests. Buffalo leads the NFL in average points per contest (32.8) and has reached the 30-point mark in four games.
That’s the good news. When it comes to the other side of the football, new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard is still looking for answers. The Bills are giving up 28.5 points per contest and only the Detroit Lions are allowing more total yards and passing yards per contest. Leonhard’s unit has surrendered 21 offensive TD—15 of those through the air. In the four games that Buffalo has reached at least 30 points, they have also permitted 30-plus points.
So where are we headed with this? There’s still 11 games remaining on the Bills’ schedule, and who they play doesn’t seem to matter these days. Allen and company are finding their way to the end zone, and so are their opponents.
It was just two years ago that the Bills set a team record for points scored (525) in a season. That happened to be the year that Allen was named the league’s MVP. Now ponder this. The franchise mark for the most points allowed in a season is a brisk 454 (28.4 points per game), which came in a 16-game campaign in 1984.
That club finished 2-14 under head coach Kay Stephenson, but that was bad enough for the team to earn the first overall pick in the ’85 NFL draft— selecting future Hall of Fame defensive end Bruce Smith.
The average Buffalo Bills’ game this season averages 61.3 points. That adds up to a lot of entertaining football. But if this club has any kind of aspirations of reaching and then winning Super Bowl LXI, Leonhard needs to come up with some solutions on his side of the football.

title: Bills' Jim Leonhard Getting Hot Seat Buzz Amid Buffalo's Defensive Struggles
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are 5-1 as they enter the bye this week, but that does not mean their season hasn't been without issues.
The biggest issue, by far, is the performance of the defense, which has been woefully disappointing over the first six games , leading to no shortage of scrutiny for new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard.
In per-game averages, the Bills rank 31st in total yards and passing yards, and 28th in points.
As a result of Buffalo's rough start, USA TODAY's Michael Middlehurts-Schwartz thinks Leonhard is one of the NFL's coordinators who is under the most pressure .
"Unlike some others on this list, Leonhard probably isn't facing questions of job security as he oversees a fairly significant shift in adapting former coach Sean McDermott's defense to a radically different scheme. But with Buffalo otherwise looking capable of competing for its first title, he's hardly off the hook," he said.
While there is no doubt plenty of pressure on Leonhard to turn things around, especially given the Bills' status as a Super Bowl contender, we just don't see his job being in any real danger.
It isn't easy to change schemes and have success in the first year, and making that harder is the fact that the Bills had to work in multiple new starters.
It also doesn't help that the Bills have seen lackluster play at multiple position groups, including linebacker, cornerback and safety, so part of the blame rests on general manager Brandon Beane swinging and missing on players at those positions.
The Bills have shown remarkable patience with coaches, and even with Beane himself, so there's a good chance Leonhard won't be shown the door, even if the defense's issues continue.
To his credit, Leonhard hasn't minced words about the performance of the defense.
“It’s time to start being good at something, right? I mean . . . that’s our struggles right now. It’s too inconsistent to pretend that we’re building, and working, and making improvements," he said.
When it comes to where the issues lie, Leonhard has pointed the finger at the secondary more than the defensive front.
“Significantly more on the back seven than there is on the front,” he said.
The safety pairing of C.J. Gardner-Johnson and Cole Bishop has not panned out overall, and now the Bills are going to be without Gardner-Johnson for a game, which will force Damar Hamlin and Jalon Kilgore into bigger roles. We know Hamlin's limits and the rookie remains unproven.
At cornerback, Maxwell Hairston has not taken the step forward the Bills were expecting, and rookie Davison Igbinosun is still raw and in need of more work.
All of this adds up to Beane needing to do something at the trade deadline to help his defensive coordinator out. The Bills general manager will have more than two weeks to get that done.

title: CJ Gardner-Johnson Debacle Exposes Bills' Free Agency Failures Under Brandon Beane
full_text:
It's seems safe to say that safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson is another swing-and-miss in free agency by Buffalo Bills ' general manager Brandon Beane.
In addition to subpar performance, Gardner-Johnson's circus act has already produced multiple distractions dating back to training camp . His one-game suspension for spitting at an opponent last time out in Week 6 should re-open the conversation about Buffalo's multiple free agency failures in recent years under Beane's watch.
Granted salary cap space has been far from plentiful, it's more than fair to question the Bills' use of limited resources over the past few free agency cycles.
With Gardner-Johnson continuing the trend into 2026, Buffalo has suffered from at least one costly free agent bust three years in a row.
The 2025 free agent class looks highly troubling with two of the four key members already off the roster but still accounting for significant portions of this year's salary cap space.
Here's a quick look at the Bills' last three underwhelming free agent classes and the dead salary cap money that remains. All figures are provided by Spotrac .
Edge rusher Bradley Chubb and slot cornerback Dee Alford have been nothing better than average thus far.
Chubb represents the biggest investment of the class, signing for three years and $43.5 million. He has only 1.5 sacks, but he's been solid against the run. Buffalo realistically must keep him through at least the 2027 season. Cutting him would cost $16.8 million in dead money on next year's cap.
Alford, who inked a three-year deal for $15.75 million, is also likely to stick around for at least two seasons, unless Buffalo is willing to eat $5.07 million in dead money on the 2027 spending limit.
While Gardner-Johnson is only under contract for one season, his deal contains void years in 2027 and 2028. He'll cost $1 million against the cap next year and $500K the following season. If the Bills release him now , they face a $3.08 million dead cap charge.
Joey Bosa and Larry Ogunjobi were both one-year propositions that failed , and in the latter's case failed miserably.
After opening the season with a six-game suspension due to a substance policy violation, Ogunjobi totaled 19 tackles and no quarterback hits over 215 defensive snaps. In the playoff loss to the Denver Broncos, he committed an awful offsides penalty that negated a Bills' fumble recovery.
Meanwhile, Bosa made a few noteworthy plays , but failed to consistently affect the opposing passer. He made 5.0 sacks over 15 games, and he was practically invisible against the run all year.
Unfortunately, the Bills are still paying the price for both players. Bosa is on the book for $7.2 million in dead cap space this year while Ogunjobi costs $2.35 million.
That's before mentioning Josh Palmer's disappointing 2025 season , and the fact that it doesn't look like the wide receiver will live up to his contract value this year, either. Palmer, who is on a three-year deal worth $30 million, has only 26 receptions in 17 appearances as a Bill.
Palmer is occupying $11.75 million of cap room this season, and he carries a $4.8 million dead money charge in 2027 if cut. Furthermore, Buffalo is on the hook for void years in 2028 ($3.2m) and 2029 ($1.6m).
Wide receivers Curtis Samuel and Mack Hollins were the two most significant free agent additions in 2024 with the latter only on a one-year contract.
The Samuel signing is the one that is truly mind blowing on multiple levels. He mysteriously failed to come close to the production level he enjoyed under offensive coordinator Joe Brady in 2020, and he wound up being a healthy scratch on multiple occasions in 2025 when he caught seven passes for 81 yards over six games.
Samuel, who initially signed on for three years and $24 million, counts $3.45 million against Buffalo's cap this year after being released during the offseason.

title: Bills Safety Sam Franklin Has Suspension Reduced After Spitting Incident
full_text:
Sam Franklin Jr. was suspended for one game after the league determined the Buffalo Bills safety spit at an opponent during the fourth quarter. Franklin appealed that ruling and according to Adam Schefter, his punishment has been reduced.
Franklin will no longer be suspended for a game and will not lose a game check. Hearing officer James Thrash apparently still felt Franklin's actions during the game deserved a punishment as he will receive a $14,926 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct.
Buffalo is on a bye this week , and will host the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8 on November 1. Franklin will be eligible to play in that game, making this ruling a win, even though he is still going to be hit with the fine.
The Bills defeated the Raiders in Week 6, but had a couple of unfortunate incidents from that game lead to punishments, and both were related to spitting.
During the second quarter, safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected, and later suspended , when he spit at Las Vegas tight end Brock Bowers. He initially refused to take full ownership of his actions, and never admitted to spitting . Still, the league had enough evidence to not only suspend Gardner-Johnson for one game, but they upheld his punishment on appeal .
Unlike Gardner-Johnson, Franklin was not penalized or ejected during the game. That made his suspension far more shocking, and Franklin was also surprised when the news broke. Shortly after the suspension was announced, Sal Capaccio of WGR 550 reported that Franklin would appeal.
"I'm told Franklin vehemently denies this ever happening and will be appealing," Capaccio reported .
Capaccio also shared a slow-motion video that Franklin shared on his social media, which showed that he was kicked during the alleged incident. Franklin also said he still wouldn't spit on anyone despite the contact.
As for the fine, this is the second time this season Franklin will be hit with one by the NFL. He was fined $9,425 for a blindside block in Week 1 . That penalty qualifies for the new "Three-Strike Suspension Rule."
Under that rule a player would be suspended if they receive three penalties for one of the following penalites: " hip drop tackle, horse collar tackle , launching, hit on a defenseless player and blindside block."

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit: Jalen Coker, Chuba Hubbard & Darren Waller
full_text:
It's been five games, so it's a big enough sample to say that the Carolina Panthers are an elite fantasy football offense. Every week, they have multiple players worth starting. This would've seemed impossible in the preseason, especially with Jonathon Brooks hurt.
Jalen Coker, Chuba Hubbard, and Darren Waller are among those players. This week, against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, should you start or sit these players?
Jalen Coker is in a difficult spot. He's the WR2 on this roster even though he does kind of match Tetairoa McMillan in production when both are healthy. That gives him a boost in defensive coverage, as he won't often draw the best cornerback.
It also means he's not going to get as much love from Bryce Young, although there will be plenty of weeks in which he does. But ultimately, Coker has produced when he's been healthy, and he is healthy.
The Buccaneers' secondary is not great against wide receivers this year, so Coker is not a bad play unless your wide receiver room is just incredibly deep.
Chuba Hubbard has been one of the best fantasy football running backs this year. He's getting a good amount of yardage and scoring at a ridiculous pace. That might slow, but there's no reason to expect a complete dropoff this week.
The Tampa Bay defense is ridiculously stout against the run. However, they're weak against the pass, and the Panthers have been passing to open up the second-half run game against tired defenses. That should happen here.
Plus, unless you somehow have two top-10 running backs also on your roster, you can't afford to bench Hubbard for a less-than-ideal matchup.
The Panthers have too many tight ends to worry about, making starting Darren Waller on a given week a tough sell. He is the premier passing target among the three, but the Panthers use the other two so much for blocking.
Waller is essentially touchdown-dependent at this point. He is likely to get a few catches, but unless he scores, then six or seven points isn't going to cut it. However, the Buccaneers are a good matchup for tight ends, and the tight end position is notoriously hard to manage in fantasy.
Verdict: Sit unless you're in desperate need of a Hail Mary attempt

title: Will the Panthers Beat the Buccaneers? Here Are Our Staff Predictions
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers will return home after a tough win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Awaiting them is their second divisional matchup, this time hosting the 1-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Baker Mayfield is on track to return, and based on his never-ending and pointless crusade against the Panthers, that is no surprise.
Will he be able to turn the tables on the NFC South leaders, or will the Panthers continue their solid start to the season? Here's what the Panthers on SI staff thinks will happen this afternoon.
I'm starting to trust this Panthers team, and I don't think I would've said that a few weeks ago. The defense has looked much better, Bryce Young finally has Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan together, and Carolina keeps finding ways to win. Tampa Bay will probably hang around because these NFC South games are rarely easy, but I think the Panthers are the better team right now. Give me Carolina at home.
The Bucs let one get away last week after squandering a 16-3 fourth-quarter lead to the Steelers. The Panthers did exactly what they needed to in knocking off the short-handed Eagles. Bryce Young's 11 TD tosses have gone to six different players and should be able to have success against the league's 20th-ranked pass defense. It's a divisional game, and Dave Canales's club should hold serve at home via a comfortable victory.
Maybe Baker Mayfield returns, maybe he doesn't. That doesn't make much of a material difference to me. He was playing horribly before he got hurt, and he's magically going to be good while nursing a throwing-hand injury? And potentially without Emeka Egbuka? I don't buy it. The Buccaneers won't be bringing much firepower against the improving Panthers' defense.
On the other side, Tampa Bay's defense is quietly legitimate, but they haven't exactly faced a murderer's row of offenses in the first six weeks. They also blitz a lot (43.8%, third-most in NFL), and that doesn't really impact Bryce Young (NFL-best 0.36 EPA/dropback against the blitz).
Not to mention, Tampa doesn't get home with the blitzes, as they have the second-worst pressure rate in the NFL. With Taylor Moton back, Carolina's offensive line is in better shape, so Tampa Bay's strength isn't going to translate. The rivalry nature will prevent a blowout, but Carolina should control this one.
This just feels like a slugfest type of game. Tampa Bay is coming in desperate, starting the season 1-5, and Baker Mayfield returns and is an ultra-competitor.
The Buccaneers' defense is exceptional against the run, which could lead to an inefficient day for Bryce Young throwing the ball. Both teams will have moments, but Carolina’s offense has been too good not to make just a few more plays to edge out a division win.

title: 5 Key Things to Know About Buccaneers vs. Panthers in Week 7
full_text:
We will certainly find out how things stand in the NFC South by late afternoon Sunday. Not only in terms of all four teams win loss record, but if the first-place Carolina Panthers remain the only team in the division to win at least one home game.
The New Orleans Saints are the designated home team in France against the Pittsburgh Steelers, while the Atlanta Falcons host the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. As for Dave Canales’s club, they look to win a third consecutive game and raise their record to 4-2. The Panthers would be two games above .500 for the first time since they started 3-1 back in 2001.
This afternoon, the reigning division champions host the 1-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Todd Bowles’s club comes off a tough 26-19 overtime home loss to the Steelers in which the Bucs squandered a 16-3 fourth-quarter. But there’s some positive news as quarterback Baker Mayfield makes his return after a three-game absence.
The teams have been NFC South rivals since the creation of the division in 2002, but the clubs first met during the Panthers’ debut campaign in 1995. All told, Carolina owns a one-game lead (26-25) in the all-time series standings.
A year ago, the clubs met twice during the final three weeks of the regular season. In Week 16 at Charlotte, the Panthers snapped a five-game losing streak in this rivalry courtesy of a 23-20 win. Two weeks later on a Saturday in Tampa, the Buccaneers came away with a 16-14 victory.
Bucky Irving breaks loose 😤 CLEvsTB on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/54tbo77wXW
Tampa’s Bucky Irving ranks ninth in the NFL with 452 rushing yards. Carolina’s run defense has improved on a game-by game basis since the Week 1 debacle (291 yards) vs. the Bears. In their last two wins, Devin Lloyd and company limited the Lions (46) and Eagles (35) to a combined 81 yards on the ground.
Five games into their season, the Panthers are averaging 29.2 points per game and scored 16 offensive touchdowns. That’s a far cry from last season’s 2-3 start, when Canales’s squad managed only 20.4 points per contest and 11 offensive TDs. Offensive coordinator Brad Idzik’s has certainly made a difference.
No. 2 on the day for Tommy Tremble! CARvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k2atMk31qb
After missing his rookie season in 2025 with a torn ACL, David Walker is making up for lost time. He leads the Bucs with four sacks and six QB hits. In six games vs. Tampa, Young has thrown seven TD passes and been picked just twice. But he’s been sacked 15 times, lost one-of-five fumbles and the Panthers are 1-5.
Panthers’ quarterback Bryce Young continues to be sharp and is spreading the ball around. Five players have totaled double-digit receptions and each of those—wideouts Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker, tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble , and running back Chuba Hubbard—have a pair of TD grabs.

title: Baker Mayfield's Panthers Revenge Could Backfire in Week 7
full_text:
The Panthers know what usually happens when Baker Mayfield gets another shot at his former team.
Mayfield is 5-1 against Carolina since joining Tampa Bay, and considering how his short stay with the Panthers ended, it's not hard to understand why these games seem to mean a little more to him. He's had plenty of chances to remind Carolina that things worked out just fine after the Panthers moved on from him.
For once, though, that might not be such a bad thing for Carolina.
Mayfield is coming back Sunday after missing three games with an injury to the thumb on his throwing hand. He's already the type of quarterback who isn't afraid to take chances, and I don't expect three weeks away to change that, especially against the Panthers.
If anything, Carolina should be hoping he tries to do a little too much.
The Panthers have played much better defensively over the last couple of weeks . Carolina held Philadelphia to 222 total yards and only 35 on the ground last Sunday, and the Panthers have now held back-to-back opponents under 50 rushing yards.
That's important against Mayfield because Carolina can't let Tampa Bay make his return easy. If the Panthers can slow down the run again and put the game on a quarterback who hasn't played in three weeks, they should get some chances to make plays.
Mayfield has never been afraid to trust his arm. He'll extend plays, try to squeeze the ball into tight windows and take shots when he thinks something is there. That's part of the reason he's been able to turn his career around in Tampa Bay, but it's also something Carolina has to be ready to take advantage of Sunday.
The Panthers haven't forced a bunch of turnovers this season, so I'm not going to suddenly predict three interceptions just because Mayfield is coming back. But if he's looking for the big play against his former team, Carolina can't let a tipped ball or bad decision hit the ground.
Those are the plays this defense needs to start making.
I wrote earlier about why Mayfield returning shouldn't change what Carolina expects from this game . He's better than the alternative Tampa Bay would've put on the field, but the Panthers are 3-2, they've won three of four and they're playing at home.
This shouldn't become a game where Carolina suddenly plays scared because Mayfield is back.
If anything, make him uncomfortable early and see how patient he's willing to be. Make Tampa Bay put together long drives. Don't give him the easy throws, and don't let him escape the pocket and turn a broken play into 25 yards.
Then see if that old Panthers history starts creeping into things.
Mayfield went 1-5 as Carolina's starter in 2022 and was released before the season was even over. Since then, he's rebuilt his career while making a habit of beating the team that moved on from him. If he still gets a little extra satisfaction out of beating the Panthers, I can't really blame him.
But Carolina doesn't have to make it easy for him anymore.
For years, Mayfield getting a little extra fired up to play the Panthers has usually ended with him getting the last laugh.
Maybe this time Carolina can finally use some of that against him
