title: Baker Mayfield Is Back — And the Panthers Shouldn't Care
full_text:
For most of the week, we didn't know whether the Panthers would face Baker Mayfield or rookie Jalon Daniels on Sunday. It looks like it's going to be Mayfield.
Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said Friday that Mayfield looks ready to go after missing the last three games with a thumb injury. He's still officially listed as questionable, but after practicing all week, it would be a surprise if he's not out there Sunday.
Does that make the game a little tougher for Carolina? Sure. Does it change how I feel about the Panthers' chances of winning? Not really.
Obviously, I'd rather face Daniels. He's a rookie with three NFL starts, while Mayfield has been around long enough that Carolina probably isn't going to show him much he hasn't seen before.
There's also plenty of familiarity here. Dave Canales spent a season with Mayfield in Tampa Bay, and the Panthers know exactly what kind of quarterback they're getting. He's tough, he'll move around when a play breaks down and he's not going to be bothered by coming into Charlotte for a division game.
But I'm not going to spend much time worrying about Mayfield playing. The Panthers are 3-2, they've won three of their last four and they're at home against a 1-5 Tampa Bay team. If we're going to start talking about Carolina as a possible playoff team , this is the kind of game it needs to win no matter who's playing quarterback for the other team.
I'm not expecting Carolina to roll Tampa Bay. These division games have a funny way of getting weird, and we've watched enough Panthers football over the years to know how quickly a game that looks good on paper can turn into a four-quarter headache.
I just don't think Mayfield being out there changes what we should expect from Carolina.
Mayfield may be back, but Tampa Bay isn't suddenly getting everybody else back with him. He hasn't played since Week 3, the injury is to the thumb on his throwing hand and he'll be wearing a protective glove Sunday.
Maybe he comes out and looks completely normal. I wouldn't be surprised if he does. But three weeks without playing is three weeks without playing, and now his first game back comes on the road against a Panthers defense that's been playing much better.
He'll also be without Emeka Egbuka and starting tackle Luke Goedeke. Antoine Winfield Jr. is out on the other side of the ball, which doesn't hurt Carolina's chances considering what Bryce Young and this offense have been doing lately.
Carolina held Philadelphia to 222 total yards and only 35 on the ground last week. That's two straight games holding an opponent under 50 rushing yards after the run defense looked like one of the biggest problems on the team earlier in the season. Even with 149 penalty yards, the Panthers found a way to win the kind of game they've usually found a way to lose .
Mayfield is a better test for this defense than Daniels would've been. That's fine. If the improvement we've watched the last couple of weeks is real, this is another chance to show it.
We've seen Carolina play down to teams it should beat plenty of times. That's part of the reason I'm still not completely ready to buy everything we've seen over the last month.
I'm getting closer, though.
The Panthers have won three of four, Young is playing some of the best football of his career, Coker is back and the defense has looked much better the last couple of weeks. At some point, you have to stop going into every game wondering what might go wrong and see if this team can handle being the one that's supposed to win.
That's really what I want to see from Carolina against Tampa Bay besides just getting another win . Would I have rather seen Daniels? Absolutely. I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Mayfield gives Tampa Bay a better chance to win, and I'd imagine Panthers fans would've been perfectly happy watching the rookie make another start.
But Mayfield playing doesn't give Carolina an excuse if things don't go well. The Panthers are at home, they're playing better football and they're facing a 1-5 team that's missing some important pieces.
If Carolina really is the better team right now, this is another chance to prove it.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Panthers Fantasy Predictions: Where I Disagree With the Experts in Week 7
full_text:
It wasn't that long ago that starting multiple Panthers in fantasy football would've felt like a pretty big gamble. Five games into the season, that's starting to change.
Bryce Young is averaging 309.8 passing yards per game, Chuba Hubbard has rushed for 242 yards over the last two weeks and Jalen Coker came back against Philadelphia and immediately saw 13 targets. Tetairoa McMillan still finished with 86 receiving yards of his own, so Coker's return didn't exactly slow him down.
That's what makes Sunday's game against Tampa Bay interesting from a fantasy standpoint. Carolina suddenly has several guys you can feel pretty good about putting in your lineup.
I took a look at what the fantasy experts are projecting for some of Carolina's top players and compared those numbers with what I think we'll actually see Sunday. I'm pretty close on a couple of them, but there are a few spots where I'm going higher.
FantasyPros projection: 245.5 passing yards, 1.7 TDs, 0.7 INTs, 18.5 fantasy points
My projection: 275 passing yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT, 10 rushing yards
My fantasy projection: 18 points
FantasyPros and I end up in almost the exact same place on fantasy points. It's the passing yards where I have a hard time agreeing with them.
Young hasn't thrown for fewer than 281 yards in a game this season and is averaging 309.8 through five starts. I'm not saying he's going to throw for 300 every Sunday, but I'm also not ready to knock him all the way down into the 240s when we haven't seen anything close to that yet.
He completed only 20 of 39 passes against Philadelphia, and there were stretches where the offense couldn't get much going. Still, I thought Young played better against the Eagles than that completion percentage suggested , and he finished with 281 yards and two touchdowns.
Coker being back also gives me another reason to go higher on the yardage. He and McMillan combined for 22 targets and 183 yards against Philadelphia, and if Tampa Bay makes things difficult for Hubbard on the ground, Young may have to throw it quite a bit again. I'll take 275 yards and two touchdowns.
Expert projection: Around 6 catches for 73 yards
My projection: 6 catches, 85 yards, 1 TD
My fantasy projection: 14.5 standard | 20.5 PPR
Coker might be my favorite Panthers fantasy play this week. He hadn't played since Week 2, came back against Philadelphia and Young threw his way 13 times. He caught six of them for 97 yards, including a 32-yard catch on third-and-9 that helped keep Carolina's 94-yard touchdown drive alive.
That's why I'm willing to go a little higher than the experts. Carolina didn't spend much time easing Coker back into things, and Young clearly had no problem going right back to him.
The touchdown is where I'm taking a chance. He didn't get one against Philadelphia, but if the targets are anywhere close to what we saw last week, I like his chances of getting one Sunday. Six catches for 85 yards isn't that far from what the experts are expecting, but the touchdown would turn it into a pretty big fantasy day.
Expert projection: Around 6 catches for 72 yards and a TD
My projection: 7 catches, 90 yards
My fantasy projection: 9 standard | 16 PPR
I was curious to see what Coker's return would do to McMillan's numbers. McMillan had become Young's clear No. 1 receiver while Coker was out, so it made sense to wonder if some of those targets would disappear.
At least against Philadelphia, they didn't. McMillan still saw nine targets and caught six passes for 86 yards, while Coker had 13 targets and 97 yards. There was plenty to go around for both of them.
That's why I'm going a little higher on McMillan's yardage. He already has 471 yards through five games, so putting him around 90 against Tampa Bay doesn't feel like much of a stretch.
Where I'm going the other way is the touchdown. The expert projection gives him one and mine doesn't, which is a pretty big difference in a standard league. In PPR, I feel better about McMillan because I think the catches will be there, and if he does get into the end zone, I'll gladly be too low.
Expert projection: Around 14-15 PPR points
My projection: 19 carries, 78 yards; 3 catches, 22 yards
My fantasy projection: 10 standard | 13 PPR
If I were only looking at what Hubbard has done the last two weeks, I'd probably put another 100-yard rushing game next to his name and move on. He ran for 122 yards against New Orleans and followed it with 120 against Philadelphia, where Carolina gave him 28 carries.
Tampa Bay is what makes me back off a little. It's a tougher matchup on the ground, and I think there's a good chance Carolina has more success getting the ball to Young, Coker and McMillan than trying to run Hubbard into a tough front all afternoon.
That doesn't mean Hubbard won't get his touches. Carolina has shown it'll stick with him, and his work in the passing game gives him a little more value in PPR. I'm putting him right around 100 total yards and leaving off the touchdown, which puts me a little below the expert projections.
Of course, if Carolina gets down around the goal line and Hubbard punches one in, that changes things in a hurry.
If I'm picking one based strictly on fantasy value this week, give me Coker. Young might be the safer play, McMillan has been the more consistent receiver and Hubbard has spent the last two weeks running through people, but those 13 targets in Coker's first game back are hard for me to ignore.
What I really liked was that McMillan still got nine targets of his own. Maybe instead of Coker taking opportunities away from McMillan, we're starting to see what Young can do when he finally has both of them on the field.
That's probably the bigger fantasy story with this offense. Young is averaging more than 300 yards passing, Carolina just had two receivers go over 85 yards in the same game and Hubbard has back-to-back 100-yard rushing games.
Panthers players aren't just desperation fantasy starts anymore. I'm going a little higher than the experts on Coker and McMillan this week, and we'll see Sunday if they make me look smart.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Rejuvenated Panthers' RB Chuba Hubbard Has Recaptured His 2024 Form
full_text:
He was a fourth-round pick in 2021 from Oklahoma State University. Running back Chuba Hubbard was the 126th overall pick in that draft by the Carolina Panthers. In three of his first four NFL seasons, he was the team’s top ground gainer.
That fourth year saw him total career highs in attempts (250), rushing yards (1,195), receptions (43), yards from scrimmage (1,366), and total touchdowns (11), despite missing the final two games of the season. Furthermore, the team inked him to a four-year, $33.2 million contract extension in the midst of what would be his best season to date.
Then came 2025, and Panthers’ general manager Dan Morgan wanted to add a little experienced depth to the backfield. Carolina inked running back Rico Dowdle, a 1,079-yard rusher with the Dallas Cowboys in 2024, to a one-year deal. Hubbard would start the team’s first six games but a calf injury opened the door for Dowdle, who finished the season with 1,076 on the ground and six scores.
Once healthy, Hubbard became a bigger factor later in the season. In the 34-31 playoff loss to the Los Angeles Rams, he totaled 13 carries for 46 yards and a pair of touchdowns.
This offseason, Dowdle took the free-agent highway to Pittsburgh. The Panthers still had oft-injured Jonathon Brooks and 2025 fourth-round pick Trevor Etienne, while Morgan added AJ Dillon in free agency. And they still had Hubbard, who has really come on strong in the team’s last two outings.
Panthers RB Chubba Hubbard Week 6 🏈 28 CAR 🏈 120 YDS 🏈 1 TD Panthers defeat the Eagles 25-14 pic.twitter.com/laajx6putG
The 27-year-old pro has started all five contests this season, and his carries have increased on a game-by-game basis. He began 2026 with 10 carries for 49 yards and one TD in the Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
His breakout game this season came on Sunday night against the Detroit Lions, totaling 20 attempts for 122 yards and two touchdowns in a 32-26 win. The Panthers returned to the field last Sunday and Hubbard racked up 28 carries for 120 yards and one score in the 24-15 victory at Philadelphia.
Per @NextGenStats : Chuba Hubbard was hit behind the line of scrimmage on 17 of his carries but gained 56 yards on those runs. Bully. pic.twitter.com/C1qEGQaHgd
The six-year pro suddenly ranks 10th in the NFL with 426 rushing yards. Meanwhile, Hubbard leads Carolina in total yards from scrimmage (511) and total touchdowns (6). And it’s also worth a mention that the 6’1”, 210-pound performer now ranks fourth in Panthers’ history in rushing yards (4,112) behind only Jonathan Stewart (7,318), DeAngelo Williams (6,846), and Cam Newton (5,036).
Head coach Dave Canales's and play-caller Brad Idzik’s offense is looking very balanced these days, and Hubbard’s bounce back season is becoming a huge factor as 2026 unfolds.
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: A Win Isn't Enough: 4 Things Panthers Need to Show Against Buccaneers
full_text:
Obviously, the first thing I want to see Sunday is a Panthers win. Carolina is 3-2, has won three of its last four and has a chance to move to 4-2 against Tampa Bay.
But we're past the point where that's the only thing I'm watching.
The Panthers have looked like a different team over the last month, and now I want to see if some of this stuff is going to stick. Was the run defense the last two weeks for real? Can the offense keep rolling now that Jalen Coker is back? And please, can we get through a game without 149 yards in penalties?
Here are four things I'll be watching Sunday besides the final score.
I'm not ready to say it is, but I'm definitely more interested in this conversation than I was a couple of weeks ago.
Carolina held Philadelphia to 35 rushing yards Sunday and has now held back-to-back opponents under 50 yards on the ground. That's a pretty big turnaround for a defense that is still allowing 5.12 yards per carry on the season.
Now let's see them do it again.
Bucky Irving is exactly the kind of back who can tell us whether we're looking at real improvement or just a couple of good weeks. He ran for 165 yards against Dallas earlier this season and has already gone over 100 yards twice against Carolina in his career.
I'm not asking the Panthers to hold him to 35 yards. Keep him from controlling the game, don't start giving up five or six yards every time Tampa Bay hands him the ball and make the Buccaneers beat you some other way. Do that again Sunday and I'll feel a whole lot better about where this run defense is headed.
I don't need to see Bryce Young throw for 300 yards every week. I do want Carolina to keep trusting the version of Young we've watched through the first five games.
He's averaging 309.8 passing yards per game and threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns against Philadelphia. The completion percentage wasn't pretty, but I thought Young played better against the Eagles than his 20-of-39 line suggested .
We also finally got Coker and Tetairoa McMillan on the field together, and I want to see more of that. Coker had 97 yards in his return, McMillan had 86 and suddenly Young has a couple of guys on the outside who can make things happen.
Tampa Bay is good against the run, so there may be stretches Sunday where Young has to carry the offense. Fine by me. If it's working, don't get cute.
Thirteen penalties for 149 yards. I still don't know how Carolina won that game.
The Panthers had eight penalties for 105 yards in the first half alone against Philadelphia. They had returns wiped out, kept putting themselves in bad situations and spent a good chunk of the afternoon making things much harder than they needed to be.
I wrote after the game that Carolina finally won the kind of game it usually finds a way to lose , and that's one of the reasons I came away encouraged. But let's not make winning that way a habit.
There are going to be penalties Sunday, and I'm not expecting perfection. Just don't make me watch another game where I'm checking for a flag every time somebody makes a big play.
Tampa Bay is 1-5. Carolina is 3-2, has won three of its last four and gets this game at home. That doesn't guarantee anything, especially against a division opponent, but I think we're past the point where we should be looking at a game like this and wondering if the Panthers are good enough to win it.
The Buccaneers have been competitive despite their record, and I'm certainly not treating this like some automatic win. Baker Mayfield practiced in full Wednesday and Thursday as he works his way back from a thumb injury, so Tampa Bay could have him back under center Sunday. Even if rookie Jalon Daniels gets another start, this is still a division game against a team that has given Carolina plenty of problems over the years.
If we're going to talk about the Panthers as a possible playoff team and a contender in the NFC South, games like this come with that conversation. They don't have to beat Tampa Bay by three touchdowns, and I'm not expecting them to play perfect football. Just take care of the ball, stop beating yourselves and don't spend the afternoon giving a 1-5 team chance after chance to stay in the game.
We've spent enough years watching the Panthers play down to teams they should beat. Carolina has spent the last month giving us reasons to believe this team might actually be different, and Sunday is another chance to show it.
Go play like the better team.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: NFL Analyst Makes Bold Dave Canales Claim Panthers Fans Have Waited Years to Hear
full_text:
For most of Dave Canales' time in Carolina, the conversation has been about what the Panthers might eventually become. There have been good stretches, some bad ones and plenty of weeks where we were left wondering whether this thing was actually headed in the right direction.
We're finally getting an answer.
NFL.com's Nick Shook has the Panthers at No. 13 in his latest power rankings, but what he said about Canales and the Panthers stood out more to me than the ranking itself. Shook called Carolina more consistent than it has ever been under Canales and said the Panthers look like a playoff team. He also said he's very optimistic about Carolina's chances of winning the NFC South.
That's not something we've heard much around here lately, but I'm starting to understand why he's saying it.
Carolina is 3-2 and has won three of its last four games. Bryce Young is playing the best football of his career, Chuba Hubbard just ran for 120 yards in Philadelphia, and the Panthers finally have Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan healthy and on the field together.
The defense is doing its part, too. Carolina held Philadelphia to 222 total yards in Sunday's 25-14 win and has now held back-to-back opponents under 50 rushing yards. There are still things that need to be cleaned up, but we're seeing this team play well in more than one area at the same time.
That hasn't always been the case under Canales. There have been games when the offense looked good and the defense couldn't get a stop, or the defense kept Carolina in it while the offense couldn't do much with the opportunity. We're seeing a more complete team now.
I'm not saying Canales suddenly has everything figured out. I gave him a B for the win in Philadelphia , and I still think that's about right. Carolina committed 13 penalties for a franchise-record 149 yards, and letting the clock run out at the end of the first half with three timeouts is still a decision I don't understand.
But there's a difference between questioning some of the decisions Canales makes on Sundays and questioning whether the Panthers are actually getting better under him. I'm having a much harder time questioning the second one.
The Panthers have given us good stretches before, only to turn around and look like a completely different team the next week. That's probably why I'm still a little hesitant to go as far as Shook and call Carolina a playoff team after five games.
Sunday in Philadelphia moved me a little closer, though. The Panthers made a mess of things and still found a way to win , which is something we haven't seen nearly enough around here. They overcame 149 penalty yards, got the running game going when they needed it and finished the game instead of giving Philadelphia another chance to steal it.
Tampa Bay comes to Charlotte on Sunday with first place in the NFC South on the line. If Carolina wins again and moves to 4-2, we're probably going to have to look at this team a little differently.
That's why I think Shook's comments are worth paying attention to. Calling Carolina consistent and talking about the Panthers as a playoff team would've sounded pretty wild not that long ago.
It doesn't sound nearly as wild anymore.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: 3 Bold Predictions for Panthers' Important Matchup with Buccaneers
full_text:
Coming off an impressive road win against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6, the Carolina Panthers are back at home, at Bank of America Stadium, welcoming the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Tampa Bay's season is already on life support, 1-5 to start, with little to no room for error. Injuries have also plagued the Buccaneers, as starting QB Baker Mayfield has been out with a thumb injury.
However, Mayfield is trending towards returning against Carolina, as the Panthers' defense deals with injuries all over the field.
With Mayfield back and the Buccaneers coming into Charlotte in last place in the NFC South , they're going to play desperate. Carolina won't have it easy regardless of what Tampa Bay's record is coming in.
Here are three bold predictions for Buccaneers at Panthers on Sunday.
Will Lee III has been up and down since taking on an elevated role, with both Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn out due to injury. Last week, with the Devonta Smith assignment, Lee had some really good reps, not allowing Smith to make a catch, but he also got mossed on a 19-yard touchdown.
Against the Cleveland Browns in Week 3, Lee should've had a pick six, but couldn't secure the ball. There's clearly talent in Carolina's fourth-round rookie; it just has to show more consistently.
Playing against Mayfield, who hasn't played since Week 3, Lee will make multiple big plays in this game. Mayfield wasn't balling out before the injury either, so it's not absurd to say turnovers are still on the board even with his return.
Bryce Young isn't a Lamar Jackson or Josh Allen threat with his legs, but he can be effective in scramble situations. That scenario could very well play out here. While Tampa Bay's defensive line is very good against the run, the pass rush has been awful.
That said, the Buccaneers haven't allowed a single rushing touchdown by a QB this season. That changes on Sunday. In the red zone, Young can find room to scramble to the outside and dive toward the pylon for a touchdown.
While Tampa Bay has lost all but one game this season, it has turned multiple games into ugly rock fights. Even with Carolina's offense being as good as it has been, the Panthers have already had an ugly offensive game against the Browns, so theres evidence that the offense can be limited.
Both teams will turn the ball over. The Buccaneers' run defense is great, and Carolina's is improving from the embarrassing Week 1 showing. It's also just a division game; these games can get weird. Carolina should be able to limit Tampa's pass game, even with Mayfield back.
While it may be a frustrating game to watch, Carolina should still have all the tools to come out with a victory.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: NFL Hits Caleb Williams and Jahdae Walker with Fines for Falcons Game
full_text:
Jahdae Walker's special teams plays were costly for the Bears against Atlanta in terms of yards lost due to penalties for a Week 6 victory, and they were also costly for him personally.
What quarterback Caleb Williams wore in the game was also costly.
The NFL fined Walker, a second-year Bears receiver, $5,620 for roughing the kicker and also fined him $5,620 more for unnecessary roughness stemming from the use of his helmet when the Bears beat Atlanta 31-23 on Oct. 18.
These were the second and third fines of the season for Walker. In the season opener, the NFL had fined him $5,620 for taunting against the Carolina Panthers.
Walker hit the plant leg of Atlanta punter Jake Bailey with 12:48 left in the third quarter after a punt, and the Bears were penalized on the play, resulting in a first down for the Falcons.
Jahdae Walker screwed up with this headbutt. But he shouldn’t have been ejected. Seems a bit extreme. #DaBears pic.twitter.com/DkA0ubkEqr
The other play involving Walker against Atlanta was a bit more costly. On the first play of the fourth quarter, Walker was involved in kickoff coverage and head-butted Atlanta receiver Chris Blair after the play, directly in front of the officials. He was flagged for unnecessary rougheness/using his helmet. Also, it resulted in Walker being ejected from the game.
If there was any satisfaction at all for Walker in this it was that Blair was also fined by the league, but it was for an earlier play in the game with 8:15 left in the first quarter when he threw a blindside block. The fine for this was $5,972.
Jahdae Walker runs into the punter Ben Johnson is pissed pic.twitter.com/zJGvpyLSLE
The Bears have been relatively free of fines this season but this wasn't their first fine from this game.  The NFL fined Williams $11,941 for wearing Caddix cleats, an NFL dress code violation.  The Caddix cleats have been relatively popular around the league this year and it has been reported about 40 players have been wearing them.
The NFL has contractual agreements  for players to wear adidas, NIKE and Under Armour cleats but not Caddix. Williams, receiver Cooper Kupp, and quarterback Joe Flacco are among the players who have been wearing the Caddix cleats.
It wasn't their first fine for uniform violation of this season. Cornerback Jaylon Johnson was fined $5,971 against the Philadelphia Eagles for wearing an unapproved streamer towel.
Walker's fine was the first for an on-field Bears incident since Tyrique Stevenson was fined $22,342 in Week 2 against the Vikings for using his helmet in a tackle.
Caleb Williams was fined by the NFL over $11K for his Caddix cleats he wore against the Atlanta Falcons for being in violation of the NFL Uniform and Equipment Rules. 📸: Getty pic.twitter.com/wf2F5VeRRu
Gene Chamberlain has covered the Chicago Bears full time as a beat writer since 1994 and prior to this on a part-time basis for 10 years. He covered the Bears as a beat writer for Suburban Chicago Newspapers, the Daily Southtown, Copley News Service and has been a contributor for the Daily Herald, the Associated Press, Bear Report, CBS Sports.com and The Sporting News. He also has worked a prep sports writer for Tribune Newspapers and Sun-Times newspapers.

title: Who Should Bears Fans Root for in Week 7 After Beating the Patriots on Thursday Night?
full_text:
For the first time in the 2026 NFL season, Chicago Bears fans can rest easy going into Sunday. The Bears pulled of a sensational primetime win over the New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football and are now getting some well-deserved rest before their next game, a Monday Night Football showdown with the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.
Sunday football is always a more carefree viewing experience for fans when their team already has a win in the books. However, there are still some matchups that Bears fans should have a rooting interest in, and that includes more than just division rivalries. With that in mind, here's a Week 7 rooting guide for Bears fans to follow once the action starts on Sunday.
At this point in the season, Bears fans should be rooting against the Green Bay Packers every week, and not just for rivalry reasons. They currently own the tiebreaker over the Bears after Chicago's disastrous Week 5 loss to the Packers , and that could come back to haunt them in what is expected to be a tight NFC Wild Card race. They still have one more game to play against each other, but the Packers could very well win that matchup, too.
The Lions could end up being a greater threat to the Bears' playoffs hopes than the Packers, but for now, Bears fans should root for Detroit.
Despite featuring one of the worst offenses in the NFL, the Vikings keep finding ways to win and at 5-0 they stand atop the NFC North. The rooting interest for Bears fans here is obvious. There's a lot of they need to make up if they're going to make a serious push for a second NFC North division title , and seeing the Vikings fall to 5-1 this week would be a good start.
Unfortunately for Bears fans, that's not likely to happen. The Colts are in complete disarray after an embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Tennessee Titans , and star defensive tackle DeForest Buckner's postgame comments suggested a team that had already given up on the season. Go ahead and root for the Colts, but Colts fans would probably tell you to keep your expectations low.
If the Bears can't win the NFC North this year, they'll be battling for a Wild Card spot in January, and that's where they'll need help from other teams. The Seahawks are currently in a precarious position at just 3-3 on the season and in second place in the NFC West. But it's far too early to count out the defending champs.
Expect Seattle to eventually figure things out and string some wins together. It's crucial for the Bears' playoffs hopes then that they first rack up a few avoidable losses like this one. Plus, the Bears face Seattle next week. Getting the Seahawks when they're in the middle of a slump would only help the Bears' chances.
A former Marine and Purdue Boilermaker, Pete has been covering the Chicago Bears since 2022 as a senior contributor on BearsTalk. He lives with his wife, two kids and loyal dog.

title: Do Bears Play Today? Remaining Schedule, Predictions for Rest of Chicago's 2026 Season
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are sitting at 5-2 after seven games and, going into Sunday, are in second place in the NFC North.

title: Montez Sweat Returns to Defense Getting Its Sacks From Kyler Gordon
full_text:
On Friday as the Bears bid farewell to tight end Cole Kmet for the season, they welcomed the return of the player with the biggest contract on their roster.
Oh yeah, Montez Sweat. Remember him? He was reinstated by the commissioner after his suspension for a performance enhancing drug policy violation.
Their pass rush hasn't exactly collapsed without the player regarded as their leading pass rusher. If anything can be said for Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen, it's that he knows how to make lemonade out of lemons, and he did it once again by using subs and with blitzes.
Allen went to more blitzing and switched up the fronts repeatedly over the last two weeks without Sweat available, and also with Dayo Odeyingbo on injured reserve with a quad injury. The pressure actually amped up. Largely, it's the result of getting Kyler Gordon back and blitzing their slot cornerback, along with other DBs or linebackers.
I want the record to show that while both QBs played exceptional tonight, Caleb was doing it against a borderline top 5 defense whereas Maye was doing it against Kyler Gordon and The Backyardigans https://t.co/Nz4SwVKFbR
Gordon has four sacks in two games, or as The Athletic's Dan Wiederer pointed out in the locker room after Thursday's win, the Bears DB has four sacks in five days.
It makes you wonder what Gordon can do with 10 games and numerous days still to go. And with Sweat now rejoining the rush to often line up on the same side of the field as Gordon, double-teaming   the edge rusher might not be possible if a team wants to block a blitzing DB.
In case you're counting or thinking of it, the NFL record for sacks by a defensive back in a season is 9 1/2 by Jamal Adams with Seattle in 2020.
Kyler Gordon isn’t just a pass blitzer. He can hold up against tight ends in the run  game. Uncommon blend of strength speed athleticism and quicks. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/ub2NiPxoKP
"That's only four," Gordon said after Thursday's game. "That's not enough."
It's twice as many as Sweat had in five games, in case anyone is counting. Gordon has tied teammate Austin Booker for the team lead, and it's Allen he has to thank for it.
"I appreciate it man," Gordon said. "I couldn't wait to do this together. I appreciate him putting me in a position to do that and that's just the beginning, so. ..."
Dennis Allen kept the Falcons off balance by using varying his pressure patterns. Here, the Bears run a simple double B-gap blitz with the Mike Hug Rushing the RB. Chicago assumes the TE will stay in the protection because of the pressure and "steal" his defender in the post.… pic.twitter.com/vEwsSXlJ3n
The blitzing Bears are going to be a thing even with Sweat returning. This was apparent in the playoffs last year as Allen finally had Gordon available after only three games played in the 17-game regular season due to injuries.  He turned Gordon loose on the Rams and it worked to a large extent.
While Gordon missed games with a calf injury this year, Allen didn't really say much about his slot cornerback returning before he was ready. Allen just made do with what he had, the same way he has done it without Sweat for two weeks and the way he did it without numerous players in the past.
The Allen defense with more speed now should be aggressive regardless of who they have on the field. They currently rank eighth in sacks per game at 2.7. That's probably a better stat to look at than sack total because some teams have played two less games than the Bears at this point. The positive is their pass rush win rate, which was near or at the bottom of the league most of last year, has risen dramatically. They rank sixth in this ESPN analytic, at 57%.
First 4th down of the game. 8 guys showing blitz, only 4 come. Jackson, Bush, Hicks & Booker drop out. Hardy crashes all the way to the center confusing the RT. Thieneman occupies the confused RT & TE w/ Kyler untouched off the edge. Another patented DA simulated pressure. #Bears pic.twitter.com/z8ei2hppsR
Allen has blitzed the eighth highest percentage at 34.2% through seven games, per Pro Football Reference. Unlike in some other seasons when they supplemented no rush with blitzing, the Bears are getting pressure. They are fifth in pressure percentage at 28%.
"I think these guys, they're really coming in there," coach Ben Johnson said. "I think they're building their confidence, too. I think they know that they can be pretty good.
"When you have these guys running free, I think they believe in the scheme. They see that, ‘Holy cow, DA's doing a great job scheming this stuff up, and we're coming in free for some sacks here.' I think we're heading in the right direction.”
It shows in overall defensive statistics heading into Sunday's games. The Bears are 11th in yards allowed, but it's actually less because they have a game or even two on some teams. They're eighth in points allowed and eighth in scoring on offense. They've allowed the second fewest first downs (107) even though they have played more games than all teams except New England.
The pressure can eventually lead to more takeaways.
D'Marco Jackson PICKS OFF Maye in the end zone. BEARS BALL. NEvsCHI on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wq8LKTC3lX
Everything hinges on what has been an effective run defense so far. They're sixth against the run a year after they were 27th. Of course, they're not not leading in takeaways like last year, as they're 13th with 10, but Johnson sees that coming if the pressure and the run defense on first and second downs continues at this pace.
"I do think there's an element of the more off schedule we can get offenses on first down, the better off we're going to be in terms of ending their drive," Johnson said. "I hate to look back at last year, but we're a better defense than we were a year ago.
"The biggest difference is we're not taking the ball away quite as much at this point of the season. If we can continue to harp on that ball production and getting those takeaways, I think you're going to see some really good defensive play, some more consistent defensive play."
And it can't hurt getting back their No. 1 pass rusher, even if he is only No. 4 now on the team in sacks with two.
Perhaps now they can used Gordon a little more at what he's there to do, and that's cover slot receivers. But not too much. They don't want to let QBs get too comfortable.
Callers are riled up after Bears defensive end Montez Sweat got hit with a 2-game suspension. "I work for a job, if I get drug tested and I fail, I lose my job," a caller says. "He's a millionaire. It's a wrap. You're a bust. You did nothing for us. Just beat it. Go home." pic.twitter.com/sYQBaxd7Oj

title: Ben Johnson Likes His Ball Hog Bears But Points Are the Real Goal
full_text:
The Bears are the NFL's accidental ball-control leaders.
At least this is what coach Ben Johnson contends .
It's not something Johnson necessarily sought and he's not even a big proponent of the possession game. This is the coach who loves big plays and got plenty of them on Thursday night in the 30-24 win over New England . But he also got the same thing he's been getting all season long, and that's ball control with time of possession.
“I do think that's played a part in some of these games so far," Johnson said. "I've never been one for the time of possession stat. I don't know that that really equates to winning and losing necessarily and yet, when you look up, we are possessing the ball more than our opponent more often than not."
. @Patriots @bears let the chess match begin...Lots of adjustments in real time by both sides #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/u6mx7iJe3c
They did it in every game except the loss to Green Bay. Even in that blowout loss using quarterbacks Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum for injured Caleb Williams, and with five turnovers, they still finished only minus-24 seconds in TOP.
"I do think it takes something off the defense," Johnson said. "I'm certainly conscious of how much it adds to the offense, as well, because they feel it. There's some lingering effects to that when that play count gets up."
Just because the offense has the ball doesn't mean it's the other team being worn out. The Bears offensive linemen can get worn down from being on the field for so long. Wide receivers can, as well. They normally rotate running backs anyway but in cases like the Jets game, a week before they played Green Bay, they monitoring snaps becomes necessary.
"We need to maintain an equal share of the load with all of our skilled players certainly but be conscious of it with our offensive line as well over the course of the week because it's a long season as we all know," Johnson added.
Bears are the best team in the NFL when Caleb Williams plays the entire game: 1st in points (45 PPG) 1st in total yards (460/Game) 1st in rushing 1st on 3rd down (61%) 1st in takeaways (3/game) 2nd in sacks And the Bears are #1 in the NFL in time of possession. pic.twitter.com/f3EXcxMy9Q
Whether this is necessarily the right path is debatable, even if it is a byproduct of taking what defenses give instead of the actual game plan. Also, it must be pointed out the Bears are leading in TOP despite operating without injured running back Kyle Monangai for three games. He is their ball-possession back, while D'Andre Swift is the breakaway threat.
Seven of the top 10 teams in TOP made the playoffs the last three seasons. The Bears last year were eighth at 30:53 per game. They were third in 2023 and didn't make it with a 7-10 record because, in addition to having possession time, they didn't score enough and allowed too many points.
It doesn't mean a Super Bowl for teams. The Eagles did lead in 2024 when they won the Lombardi Trophy, but that was with an asterisk. It didn't include overtime games. If you included OT, they didn't lead. The last time a Super Bowl champion led in time of possession overall it was also the Eagles, in 2017.
Ben Johnson is now 17-9 as Bears Head Coach, including postseason. pic.twitter.com/yUseba9Ooh
"I would rather have a one play drive for a touchdown than a 10-play drive for a touchdown," Johnson said. "The ability to stay efficient, stay on schedule, I do think that's something that good offenses show that they can do. I'm proud of the fact that right now we're not playing very clean football, very disciplined football from a penalty standpoint there's too many pre-snap penalties and there's too many holding penalties right now for us, but despite those, our guys still find a way to get back on track and overcome.
"I've been a part of teams where you get one penalty and that just derails the whole drive and that's it. That's not what's happening to us right now. I look forward to the day that we clean those up and see what that looks like.”
Although Johnson strives for big plays, the possession time follows him mainly because of his emphasis on the running game. His Lions offenses were third in 2024 and fifth in 2023 in TOP. They were 13th in his first season, 2022. They didn't make the playoffs in 2022 but did in 2023 and 2024.
Fourth-quarter time of possession: #Bears 12:21 #Patriots 2:39
What Johnson would rather have is like what they had on Thursday night. They had eight pass plays of 21 yards or longer to two by New England, and still owned the possession time edge 32:24 to 27:36.
The Bears lead the NFL in time of possession, but Ben Johnson isn't impressed: "I've never been one for the time of possession stat," Johnson said. "I would rather have a one-play drive for a touchdown." https://t.co/e5vlOAXFdd

title: Could Daniel Hardy's Emergence Eat Into Montez Sweat's Playing Time?
full_text:
Chicago Bears edge rusher Daniel Hardy has been far more valuable to the special teams unit than to the defensive side of the ball throughout his career.
Prior to this season, he had 853 career snaps on special teams and only 126 on defense. He was still waiting to break out the Jeff Hardy celebration for his first career sack, and only got close to one (via a QB hit) once in his career.
Hardy's at it again 🕺 pic.twitter.com/3MEZ8tW8w1
He was, however, a third-phase ace for Chicago. Hardy led the team with 12 special teams tackles in 2024 and a whopping 19 tackles last season. His prowess in that department led Chicago to re-sign him to a two-year, $5 million contract this offseason.
Many were worried when Montez Sweat got suspended for two games for violating the league's substance abuse policy prior to the team's Week 6 matchup against Atlanta. With Dayo Odeyingbo also on the mend with a quad injury, the Bears were in a precarious position at edge rusher .
I, myself, was guilty of counting Hardy out before he got an opportunity to prove himself. I said the Bears could experiment with deploying James Lynch or Neville Gallimore at defensive end over Hardy ahead of their Week 6 clash in Atlanta.
In my defense, Lynch has seen some action along the edge, but that still proved to be a moronic take. Hardy has been impressive, and I couldn't be happier that he made me look dumb.
Again, since entering the league as a seventh-round pick with the Rams in 2022 (he joined the Bears practice squad the following year), all but three of his 38 career tackles have come via special teams. Nevertheless, he's made a massive impact on Chicago's defense over the past two weeks.
Hardy took down Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. for his first career sack in the team's 31-23 win over Atlanta on Sunday. He then got another half-sack against New England on Thursday night.
Breaking down @Dhardy44 's first career sack with the man himself pic.twitter.com/snshfyObVe
Hardy is now up to 1.5 sacks on the season despite playing only 63 defensive snaps. Meanwhile, Sweat has only 2 sacks despite seeing nearly three times as much playing time (182 snaps).
Even more notably, Hardy has been charted with eight pressures ( according to Pro Football Focus ). Even when not getting home, he's consistently gotten close to opposing QBs. While some of his pressures can be attributed to defensive coordinator Dennis Allen's hyper-aggressive scheme, Hardy has still needed to win one-on-ones. He's not getting unblocked looks at defensive end.
Last year, cornerback Nahshon Wright came out of nowhere to become a key contributor ( and takeaway machine ) for the Bears. While two games may be a small sample size, Hardy has at least shown some signs that he can follow a similar trajectory this season.
The unheralded edge rusher has earned an opportunity to show whether he can keep the hot streak going. Sweat will obviously have a role, but they can't completely disregard what Hardy has put on tape over the past two games. He deserves a role in the rotation until proven otherwise.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Caleb Williams' Historic Stats Put Bears QB in Same Company as Mahomes, Brady & Rodgers
full_text:
There is no doubt Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is playing at an elite level, and he has the numbers to back that up.
Williams put together his latest impressive performance in Week 7, when he led the Bears to a 30-24 victory over the New England Patriots on the strength of 22-of-33 passing for 308 yards and a pair of touchdowns.
Over his first four starts this season, Williams has been operating at a different level, especially with a clean pocket.
According to ESPN (H/T Clay Harbor ), Williams' completion rate when not under pressure is a robust 88%, which is the highest completion rate for any quarterback through four starts since 2009.
The two guys behind him are Kansas City Chiefs superstar Patrick Mahomes, who tallied 87% in 2021, and Hall of Famer Tom Brady, who posted 86% in 2016 with the Patriots.
Adding to that, Williams has an active streak of 35 straight games with at least 20 attempts and one or fewer picks, and that is tied with Aaron Rodgers for the longest streak in NFL history, according to Pro Football Reference (H/T Larry Mayer ).
When it comes to Bears franchise history, Jim Miller topped out at 13 games with 20 attempts and one or fewer interceptions from 2001-02, which was the previous longest streak for the team.
Williams is also the first Bears signal-caller since 2018 to throw for 300 yards in back-to-back games (H/T Clay Harbor ).
With Mahomes, Brady and Rodgers being three of the greatest at their position in NFL history, Williams is in some pretty good company.
Prior to the start of the season, general manager Ryan Poles said he wanted Williams to give the team the "green light" to sign him to an extension by showing he has taken a step forward.
"It's good to almost feel like you've got it," Poles said. "If you go with a traffic light, it went red as a rookie to yello. You can creep foward a little bit and start having some of these conversations to anticipate (a contract extension). But we need him to give us the green light. I think we'll find out this year about his progress."
Williams has no doubt done that thus far, with the Bears quarterback showing clear improvement.
Two points of emphasis the Bears had for Williams during the offseason was improving his accuracy and decision-making, especially when it comes to when to hang in the pocket.
We have seen significant improvement in both areas. Williams has been laser accurate, even when on the run, and he isn't taking off as much and is instead keeping his eyes downfield in order to locate open receivers and make plays with his arm.
Now that he's putting it all together, Williams is starting to look like the elite quarterback the Bears thought they were getting with the No. 1 overall pick in 2024 and that makes Chicago a true Super Bowl contender in 2026.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Bears Trade Proposal Would Add 3-Time Pro Bowl Defensive Lineman to Fix Need
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are rolling along with a 5-2 record over seven contests, but that doesn't mean improvement isn't needed. One area that needs an addition is the interior of the defensive line.
The Bears' decision to trade Gervon Dexter has not panned out, as his subtraction has left Chicago with a weak interior pass-rush that has mustered up just one sack in 2026.
Chicago could use more help against the run, also, because the Bears are giving up the ninth-most rushing yards per attempt and rank 28th in run-stop win rate , according to ESPN.
The Jordan van den Berg experiment has not worked out after the rookie has struggled en route to a diminished role, and nobody outside of Grady Jarrett has stepped up to fill the void left by trading Dexter to the Atlanta Falcons.
One player the Bears should have an eye on ahead of the trade deadline is Indianapolis Colts three-time Pro Bowler DeForest Buckner.
NFL Trade Rumors' Logan Ulrich proposes a trade between the Bears and Colts that would send Buckner to Chicago for a 2027 third-round pick.
"A timeless way to improve on defense is upgrading the pass rush, and even though the Bears have been getting strong production so far to start the season, there's definitely room for improvement on teh defensive line," Ulrich said. "That might help the Bears be more judicious with their blitzing, as they currently bring extra defenders at the seventh-highest clip."
"Buckner is having a terrific season, with four sacks through the first six games," Ulrich adds. "If the Colts do decide to auction off pieces for draft picks to jump-start their rebuild next year, Bucker will be near the top of the list of players other teams will be interested in."
The firing of general manager Chris Ballard signals change is coming for Indianapolis and a fire sale could commence.
Buckner is one of the team's most attractive trade chips and he can garner a strong return to assist in the upcoming rebuild in Indianapolis.
It also makes sense to unload Buckner because he's 32 years old and in the final year of his deal . It makes no sense for Indy to keep him, as a rebuild means it's going to be at least a few years until the Colts are competitive again and by that time Bucker will probably be on the decline.
Even if the Colts are interested in keeping Bucker around, he might not feel the same and could be looking to move on to a contender in free agency next year as he approaches the twilight of his career.
Ulrich already touched on the fact that Buckner has four sacks this season, which would rank tied for second on the Bears and first among their interior lineman.
In fact, Bucker has three more sacks by himself than all Bears interior linemen combined.
Buckner has struggled against the run this season, as evidenced by his 45.3 Pro Football Focus grade , but he has traditionally been better than that, with Buckner posting grades north of 70 in six of 11 seasons.
The bottom line is that Buckner can offer a massive upgrade for the Bears, both as a pass-rusher and run defender, and trading for him amounts to a no-brainer move for Chicago if the opportunity presents itself ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

title: Cole Kmet's Injury Could Create an Opportunity For Forgotten Rookie
full_text:
Cole Kmet's season-ending knee injury will be a massive blow to Chicago's offense. He's played 62% of the offensive snaps and has been a huge part of their success in the running game.
The injury will probably give rookie Sam Roush a massive uptick in opportunities . However, they've run 13 personnel (featuring three tight ends) roughly 8% of the time. Unless they scrap that formation entirely, it feels safe to assume that they'll be making an addition, whether it be via free agency or the practice squad, to address his absence.
Adding Stephen Carlson to the active roster makes sense. He's been a fixture on the team's practice squad since 2023 and has been called up for three games since then, including two last season.
However, Ben Johnson also hinted at another name who might help fill the Kmet-sized void. He said the team will see where undrafted rookie Hayden Large, who actually made the team's initial 53-man roster before landing on Injured Reserve on September 1, is in his recovery from a core injury.
The Bears liked Hayden Large enough not to risk losing him on roster cut-down day. If they had cut him on August 30, he would've been subjected to waivers. Even if an injury might've thrown a wrench into those plans for another squad, they saw enough to invest a spot in him.
He was then placed on IR on September 1, which allowed the team to retain his rights for the season. If you remember Johnson's comments surrounding Large from rookie minicamp , that decision might not have been a massive surprise.
"He was one of the guys that we identified well before the draft that he's a player that we really liked," Johnson said. "I actually called him before the draft and let him know that we had a vision for him.
"When you take a tight end in the third round, that's kind of like, 'Ah shoot, that might take us away from Hayden coming here', and yet, he didn't bat an eye. This is where he wanted to be, and that speaks volumes about how he's wired. He was a walk-on at Iowa and had to earn playing time and going through a long, hard, road. I really think we got a good one there."
Hayden Large is Hawkeye Football. pic.twitter.com/hfNBTI6A8I
Why is Johnson so high on the undrafted rookie? The long, hard road he mentioned probably played a major role in his confidence. From a medical standpoint, few players endured a more difficult path than the University of Iowa product.
He missed his entire senior season of high school after part of his pelvic bone broke in a severe hamstring tear. Large's recovery included 35 days of bed rest, and doctors were unsure if he'd be able to continue playing football.
Large was considered damaged goods, and the recruiting interest died down significantly. He was forced to play three years at small-school Dordt University before landing at the University of Iowa ahead of the 2023 season.
While he'll probably never be a weapon in the receiving game (he had only 14 catches for 89 yards at the collegiate level), he showed strong run-blocking chops with the Hawkeyes. Some of that promise also showed up in the preseason.
Bears TE Hayden Large on an island with the Bengals' DE. pic.twitter.com/UzQMa4DjHB
Ben Johnson and Co. probably expected Large to have a redshirt rookie season, regardless of his health status. However, Kmet's injury might see him playing a key role far earlier than expected.
Large getting his foot in the door of the NFL is already a major accomplishment. His next battle will be to prove he belongs.

title: Caleb Williams, Kyler Gordon, Colston Loveland Troll Dave Portnoy After Bears Beat Patriots
full_text:
There are few bigger trolls on the internet than Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy, so it was funny to see him get a taste of his own medicine from Caleb Williams, Colston Loveland and Kyler Gordon.
Portnoy had a lot to say about Williams after he went down with a hamstring injury in Week 2 before it was later discovered that the Bears quarterback had a more serious issue than initially thought.
Rest assured, Williams saw Portnoy mocking him, so he took the opportunity to troll Portnoy after the Bears beat his favorite team , the New England Patriots, in Week 7.
On Instagram, Williams reposted a social media post of Portnoy's that included a photo of a handful of Barstool analysts picking the Bears to beat the Patriots. Portnoy had also included several eye emojis.
"On to the next," Williams wrote in the caption of the post.
FETISH ALERT 🚨     See you in Feb @CALEBcsw pic.twitter.com/lRIzAFfT9n
It's pretty comical that Portnoy would accuse Williams of having a fetish considering he takes every chance he gets to knock Williams, but I digress
Of course, this isn't the first time Portnoy and Williams have had a back-and-forth.
As we mentioned, Portnoy mocked Williams after his hamstring injury, as did the rest of the internet , and Williams later fired back at him with a repost on social media that basically accused Portnoy of being soft.
Portnoy then knocked Williams for not divulging more about his injury when Williams first addressed the media during the week the Bears quarterback returned to the field.
Bears players weren't done there.
Gordon and Loveland did a pizza review after the game, which was a clear troll of Portnoy and the countless pizza reviews he has done over the years.
It was pretty well done, except they forgot the score.
Bears players Kyler Gordon and Colston Loveland dropped a pizza review after last night’s win We cannot confirm or deny if they were trolling any Patriots fans that do pizza reviews pic.twitter.com/6Og9saWd8Q
The Bears have struggled mightily to beat the Patriots over the years, and that was the case for a lot of teams during the Tom Brady era.
Before their win on Thursday night, the Bears had lost six of their last seven against New England, with the last win coming in 2022.
However, with that win and the one in Week 7, the Bears are starting to flip the script and have now won two of three.
Barring a meeting in the Super Bowl, this will be the last time these two teams square off until at least 2028, as New England is not on Chicago's schedule next season .
In 2028, the Bears are slated to face one AFC East opponent, but who that is will depend upon where the Bears finish in the division.

title: Lamar Jackson Injury Status Revealed Ahead of Bengals-Ravens Showdown
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are on the eve of what will be one of their biggest games of the season. On Sunday, the Bengals are on the road as they look to keep pace in the AFC North in a battle against the Baltimore Ravens.
Coming off of a bye week, the Bengals are looking up at every other team in the division. A win on Sunday puts the Bengals in a place where they could control their own destiny.
Winning in Baltimore is a tall task. It's even taller when Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is in the lineup. However, the latest injury report from the Ravens may just change the Bengals' game plan.
The Ravens have announced that Jackson will be out in Sunday's contest against the Bengals. The former league MVP is dealing with an ankle injury that has sidelined him for the last two games.
In four games this season, Jackson has posted a 3-1 starting record and has thrown for 967 yards, six touchdown passes, and just one interception.
Obviously, the Ravens not having Jackson is a brutal blow for them. However, backup quarterback Tyler Huntley has been very serviceable since hearing his name called.
In two starts since becoming the starter for the Ravens, Huntley is 1-1, with a win over the Atlanta Falcons and a loss last week to the Cleveland Browns.
Huntley has done an outstanding job protecting the football in his two starts, throwing zero interceptions. However, he could be facing one of the most dynamic defensive lines he has seen in his short time under center.
Putting pressure in Huntley may be the key to winning the game for the Bengals. Interior defensive linemen Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen may very well be the biggest offseason acquisitions the Bengals have made in quite some time.
It's not just the interior of the defensive line that has impressed this season for the Bengals. Another offseason acquisition, Boye Mafe, has been a shining star on the edge. The Bengals are tied for the sixth most sacks in the NFL this season at 17, and aside from the Detroit Lions, who lead the league in sacks, every team ahead of Cincinnati on the list has played more games this season.
There's a lot on the line Sunday, and the Ravens are going to have to go to war without their best soldier against a Bengals team that is starving to get back on the field.

title: Tee Higgins Poised to Make Biggest Impact for Bengals Against Ravens
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase will look to unleash more chaos on the Ravens secondary in Baltimore on Sunday. He won't be alone, as Tee Higgins is set to make his fourth career start on the road against the Ravens.
As strange as it may sound, Higgins has only appeared in three road games to eight total contests against the Ravens in his career up to this point. Of those three games, two came in 2020 and 2021, with the other coming in 2022 where he only played ten snaps.
Through his career to this point, he has a total of 41 catches, 497 yards, and six touchdowns against the Ravens in all the games he has played against them.
After the success that Chase has gained against the Ravens over his career, they could have a plan in place to effectively neutralize him. That should equal more looks for Higgins, and could result in the type of stat line for him that we have seen for Chase from this matchup in the past.
Higgins has enjoyed the best start of his career to this point with 27 receptions for 423 yards and a touchdown. He's on pace for a career-high 92 catches and 1,438 yards. After suffering a groin injury in the teams Week 4 loss to the Jaguars, he recovered quickly enough to play against the Dolphins a week later.
When it comes to facing off against Ravens coach Jesse Minter's defense, Higgins has a history of success. In 2024 when Minter was with the Chargers, Higgins had nine catches for 148 yards and a touchdown.
Both Higgins and Chase should have big performances on Sunday. Though, if Minter and the Ravens defense focus on slowing Chase down, the crowd in Baltimore could witness Higgins carve them up in ways they have not seen up to this point.
Chase said in his Thursday press conference that the key for the offense is winning downfield catches. Higgins excels exceptionally in downfield contested catch situations, so it is possible that the Bengals game plan is to give Higgins enough chances to make big catches when necessary.
Sunday could decide who ultimately wins the AFC North, and regardless of whether it is Lamar Jackson or Tyler Huntley, the Bengals offense will have to play it's best football of the season. Higgins is a large piece of that, and he should finally have the chance to perform at a high level in Baltimore for the first time in four years.

title: Bengals vs. Ravens: Everything to Know Ahead of Week 7 Showdown
full_text:
The Bengals face several individual matchups against the Ravens on Sunday. The most prominent is Trey Hendrickson facing off against his former team. However, other matchups could also be key, and ESPN's Mina Kimes previewed some of them on The Mina Kimes Show Featuring Lenny.
Kimes noted that Ravens receiver Zay Flowers' success against opposing linebackers this season is an area Baltimore offensive coordinator Declan Doyle could exploit against the Bengals. Flowers currently leads the league in yards against linebackers among wide receivers.
"The other thing I wrote down was how many times can Declan Doyle get Zay Flowers on the Bengals linebackers, Flowers has 177 receiving yards versus linebackers this year which is 51 more than any other wide receiver," Kimes said on Flowers efficiency against linebackers.
Kimes stated that regardless of who plays at quarterback for the Ravens on Sunday, that linebacker remains the most glaring weakness of the Bengals' defense, and they must mitigate that weakness.
"I think from the Bengals perspective, regardless of who's playing quarterback, that's [linebacker] so obviously the glaring weakness of this defense, and if you can avoid that in any way you want to do so," Kimes said.
Domonique Foxworth noted that the Ravens' corner Marlon Humphrey has performed as expected for an older cornerback. He noted that the defense is still in a position where they ask a lot of Humphrey, and explained that it is not a position the Ravens should want.
While Foxworth expressed happiness with Nate Wiggins, Kimes said she expected a bigger leap from Wiggins in his third year and noted his inconsistency this season.
"I've been really happy with Wiggins honestly, and Humphrey I think has been what you expect, like he's been better than last year, but I mean he's an older corner, and they're still in a position where they're asking a lot from him which I think is not a place where you want to be," Foxworth said of Baltimore's cornerback duo.
"I thought this would be like another leap year and he's been a little bit up and down," Kimes responded.
Both Wiggins and Humphrey have shown a solid level of play this season, however, this remains a matchup that the Bengals offense and Joe Burrow can exploit.
Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have a combined 116 catches, 1,701 yards, and 14 touchdowns against the Ravens in their careers. Meanwhile, Burrow has completed 65% of his passes for 3,185 yards, 23 touchdowns and seven interceptions against Baltimore. With both Ravens corners having an inconsistent season so far, the Bengals stars should feast once more.
Burrow has faced Jesse Minter earlier in his career. Kimes pointed to Burrow's 356-yard, three-touchdown performance against the Chargers in 2024 and highlighted his efficiency against Minter's single-high approach. She said she is curious to see if Minter takes a different approach this time and said that she thinks the Bengals offense will have success on Sunday.
"Jesse Minter's defense with LA against Joe Burrow a couple years ago, Joe Burrow went 28 for 50, for 356 yards, and three touchdowns, particularly when they played single high he ripped them apart," Kimes said. "I am curious to see if Minter's learned from that experience, and what he does from a schematic perspective, I think the Bengals offense will have success in this game."

title: Ravens Defender Hopes to Avoid Ja'Marr Chase as Bengals Star Reveals Key to Beating Baltimore
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase has left a permanent scar on the Ravens' secondary throughout his career, and one of Baltimore's starting corners, Marlon Humphrey , is already dreading the challenge ahead.
Humphrey gave an honest answer about facing Chase.
“It would be cool if I didn’t match up with him so much,” Humphrey said. "He's obviously one of the best in the game, Tee is right up there with him in the top ten I think of this league."
Over Chase's career, he has caught 61 passes for 1,036 yards and seven touchdowns against the Ravens. Humphrey has been on the field for most of those performances. This could force Ravens coach Kevin Minter to pit third-year corner Nate Wiggins against Chase more often.
Wiggins has certainly improved since entering the league, but neither player has been able to stop Chase.
Another possible matchup against Chase, instead of Humphrey, is former teammate Chidobe Awuzie. He has had success covering Chase in the past largely due to their familiarity with each other. Awuzie has not played much for the Ravens this season so far with 82 total snaps.
During his weekly press conference, Chase said the key to beating the Ravens' secondary is winning downfield catches. He added that while the Ravens' defense is solid, it faces a bigger challenge against the Bengals' offense .
"Winning downfield catches, that's the key," Chase said. "They're a well-rounded defense at the end of the day, but they gotta play us."
Chase has consistently torched the Ravens, and he has had success against a Jesse Minter defense before. In 2024, Chase had seven catches for 75 yards and two touchdowns against the Chargers and Minter's defense.
While the Bengals must build momentum in the run game against Baltimore, Chase should remain the focal point of the Bengals' offensive game plan on Sunday. One area they can dial up more looks for Chase should come from lining him up outside more than they have so far this season.
"They're not going to give up anything easy," Burrow said. "And we have guys that can make contested plays on the outside, and we can make plays outside the pocket, outside the structure. These guys make everything so hard.
"And if you don't make contested plays, you're going to have a long day because they're going to stop the run and they're going to make you throw it deep. They're going to play everything down from shallow to deep. And if you don't make those contested plays down the field, it's going to be a long day."

title: Ja’Marr Chase Owns the Ravens as Bengals Hold Several Key Advantages
full_text:
The 3-2 Cincinnati Bengals travel to Baltimore to take on the 4-2 Ravens in their first daytime clash in B’More since 2021.
The biggest story leading into the game is the health of Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson. The former MVP missed the last two games including a loss to the Cleveland Browns last weekend.
This rivalry has already been robbed too many times when it comes to these two quarterbacks facing off, so let's hope Jackson plays.
I don't want to hear any excuses afterwards.
The real star in this AFC North rivalry has been Ja'Marr Chase. His average of 120 yards per game vs Baltimore is the most receiving yards per game by any player vs a single opponent in NFL history.
I never thought we'd have ANOTHER “Ravens Killer” after A.J. Green left, but of course Chase found a way to surpass Green.
Per Next Gen Stats, Chase and Marlon Humphrey have matched up on 83 snaps since he entered the league. Nobody has covered Chase more since 2021 and he's seen 21 targets, catching 14 balls for 318 yards against Humphrey.
For the non-mathematicians, that's 15.1 yards per reception for Chase, the most that any receiver averages against ANY defender during that span.
It sounds like Humphrey would like to cover Chase a little less in this one and he's been lining up almost exclusively on the boundary this season (95.7% of snaps) where he has allowed 69% of the passes targeted in his direction to be caught.
Joe Burrow is tasked with feeding his receivers in an effort to outduel Jackson on Sunday.
Burrow is still getting the ball out as quickly as anyone. This season, he's releasing the ball under 2.5 seconds on a league-high 57.1% of his throws.
That doesn't mean he's throwing short. Burrow has thrown downfield on 18.5% of his quick-throws and has completed 15 of 20 of these passes for 265 yards and 5 touchdowns.
Baltimore's defense has allowed an 81.8% completion percentage on quick-throws that go downfield this season.
And we're not just talking about deep passes. The Bengals and Joe Burrow are peppering the intermediate area (10-19 yards) with precision. Burrow is completing a league-high 73.2% of his passes and has averaged 12.0 yards per attempt, the third-most. The Bengals average a league-leading +0.95 EPA per pass into the intermediate part of the field.
The Ravens defense has allowed 69.8% of passes into the intermediate area to be completed, the second-highest rate in the NFL and those passes have gone for the third-most 617 yards. Their +0.62 EPA allowed per throw into the intermediate area ranks 24th in the league.
Baltimore is a heavy 2-high defense with 81.9% of all of their defensive plays featuring two safeties in deep coverage. That's the second-highest rate in the league and the Bengals have averaged +0.27 EPA per play against that coverage, third-best in the NFL.
If the Bengals offense can keep pace, it'll be up to the Cincinnati defense to answer the call and make a few plays like they did in that Thanksgiving Day win in Baltimore last season.
It starts with slowing down Derrick Henry and he might just be slowing down on his own already.
The guy is a machine, no doubt, but eventually time comes for us all.
Henry is averaging 2.4 yards AFTER contact per carry this season. His lowest average since 2018.
He's also being stopped for zero or negative yardage on 54% of his carries this season. That's his highest rate since 2018.
Henry has run outside zone on 44.2% of his runs this season. That's 57 carries for 302 yards and four touchdowns.
The Bengals have the highest Run Stuff Rate on outside runs in the league at 34.5%.
I bet that run stuff rate surprised you, too.
The biggest weapon for Baltimore's offense is receiver Zay Flowers. He's dicing up defenses from the slot this season and leading the league in separation as they keep finding creative ways to get Flowers open.
Last season, DJ Turner shadowed Flowers and did a great job.
Turner matched up with Flowers 21 times across two games last season and allowed one catch for 14 yards on four targets.
Baltimore has had some issues on their offensive line and traded for Cam Jurgens from the Eagles. He's healthy now after recovering from a concussion and should assume the starting center job for the Ravens.
I'm sure they're happy to get some stability inside, but Jurgens hasn't been good this season. Out of 85 interior offensive linemen, Cam Jurgens ranks 85th in PFF’s Pass blocking grade and that's largely because his 95.4% Pass Block Efficiency also ranks 85th and his 13.0 grade in True Pass Sets is 10 points lower than the 84th ranked interior offensive lineman.
Sounds like Dexter Lawrence gets another game to leave his mark and make the Bengals decision to trade for him look even better.
Speaking of offseason decisions, can we take a second to appreciate the decision the Bengals made when they had to replace Trey Hendrickson and landed Boye Mafe as the guy to do the job?
To this point, Mafe has been EVERYTHING the Bengals could've hoped for and it's just the cherry on top that he's outperforming Trey Hendrickson in every statistical category.
Now seems like a good time for this comparison pic.twitter.com/3EoZWIci7T
Trey Hendrickson says he forgives the Bengals and that this game isn't about him.
I say run the ball right at him. I just want to see something.

title: Lamar Jackson's Game Status Gets Clearer Ahead of Matchup With Bengals
full_text:
The Bengals and Ravens have finalized game statuses for Sunday's action in the AFC North. Cincinnati is healthy, with veteran safety Kyle Dugger set to return after suffering a quad injury last month.
On the other hand, the Ravens are hoping to have Lamar Jackson on the field for the first time since Week 4. He has been limited all week with an ankle injury and is questionable entering the game.
"Right now I'm heading in the right direction," Jackson said on Friday. "We'll see. Hopefully. But I feel like I'm heading in the right direction."
Jackson suffered the injury on October 4. He sounded unsure about playing on Sunday against the Bengals.
“Just trying to move how I move,” he said. “If I can’t do that, I can’t help my team.”
“Lamar [Jackson] was actually able to get a little bit of limited work in today in preparation. So, that’s where that’s at. Again, it’s a day-by-day thing, but he was able to get a little bit of work in and be involved in the preparation," Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said about Jackson on Wednesday before commenting on Jackson's workload. "[I am] not really [going] to get into the specifics of anything with that. I know this, when it’s ready for [Lamar Jackson] to be able to play, from both sides, and we feel like that’s the best thing to do; that’s what we’ll do.”
Cincinnati had a rare early bye week in 2026, but it helped them get much healthier over the past 10 days, and now they can attack the most important game of the season so far from the strongest health position possible.
It's basically a coin-flip game, with Cincinnati projected to win 54% of the time on ESPN's Matchup Predictor. Whoever can create a timely turnover or two will have a big advantage.
"It's critical," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said about the turnover battle on Wednesday. "Just winning the turnovers in general in a division game like this. I can think of many times we played the Ravens, and you feel like you leave the game with like three possessions, and so if you lose or gain one, that's always critical. Now the game's going to end up being an 18-possession game, of course, because I say that. But just any time it's like that, it turns out to be a big part of the game."
The action kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.
