title: Broncos' Riley Moss Is Ready to Cut Loose Against Cardinals
full_text:
Getting healthier can only help the 4-2 Denver Broncos keep rolling.
Sunday's trip to the desert to face the 2-4 Arizona Cardinals might end up being a week too early for cornerback Patrick Surtain II — who returned to practice this week and has been listed as questionable for Week 7 —  the Broncos' young secondary can be relied upon to carry the load, based on what we've seen of late.
Surtain's long-time partner in crime, Riley Moss, has been cleared to return to the starting lineup, and he's relishing the challenge the Cardinals will present on Sunday.
"Yeah, it'll be lit," Moss said this week via Denver Sports ' Andrew Mason . "I'm excited."
Moss sounded relieved to be past the rib injury that sidelined him for a game and a few quarters. Such an injury can make playing cornerback a bit tricky because of how the pain restricts movement.
"The biggest thing is a lot of twisting, a lot of movements like that kind of irritate it and that's kind of my job, and it's tough," Moss said via Mason.
Moss returned to action against the Seattle Seahawks, but his playing time was limited to just 20 snaps . A rib injury can take some time to heal.
"When you're rehabbing, you kind of just have to let it heal. And then you can get into your ramp-up and get rolling," Moss said via Mason. "The good thing is, I wasn't out for too long to lose too much conditioning and stuff, but yeah, we approached it good."
Even without the Surtain in the lineup, Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine have really stepped up and made some big plays for defensive coordinator Vance Joseph.
Barron, the Broncos' 2025 first-round pick, is proving he has the coverage chops to hang on the boundary. The Broncos' cornerback depth has shown up at the most opportune times in each of the past two seasons, but it really saved the day over the past three weeks.
Meanwhile, slot corner Ja'Quan McMillian has also continued to excel, so when Surtain returns to man the perimeter opposite Moss, this unit will be off and running again.
Perhaps seeing the young bucks making a name for themselves made Moss a bit more anxious to get back in the lineup — even if it was only in a limited capacity last week against the Seattle Seahawks.
"I was only in for certain personnel and stuff just to kind of get ramped back up," Moss said. "It was tough because it was a short week, so we didn't really practice."
Either way you slice it, the Broncos have a talented cornerback group, and it’s a dynamic collective that’s possibly the deepest and most talented in the entire league. We'll find out on Sunday whether Surtain is back against the Cardinals.
It wouldn't be a shock to see the Broncos hold Surtain out one more week, to reinsert him at home against the Kansas City Chiefs.

title: Broncos Trade Deadline: 5 Realistic Targets to Move the Needle
full_text:
The Denver Broncos still have three games to go between now and the November 10 NFL trade deadline .
The Broncos have some apparent needs, including running back and offensive line, but the next three weeks could reshape the conversation. If the return of rookie running back Jonah Coleman sparks the Broncos' ground game and J.K. Dobbins snaps out of his funk, the team could be more than content to stand pat at the deadline.
This team did face a ridiculous initial six-game schedule, which could explain why the Broncos' offensive line has looked so lackluster, especially as run blockers. With the schedule easing up for the foreseeable future, it wouldn't be a surprise to see the starting five rubber-band back into the top-five status it had entering the 2026 season.
Some would point to tight end as a need, and while I certainly wouldn't disagree, it doesn't feel like the Broncos see it that way. Even if they did, Bo Nix's middle-of-the-field avoidance in the passing game would make the pursuit of a pass-catching tight end pointless, though the Broncos could still use an upgrade at the Y.
Looking around the league, there are five realistic trade options the Broncos could consider. This is an already well-built veteran roster, so any trade acquisition would have to represent a clear upgrade over what Denver already has at that position.
Let's break down these five players.
The Indianapolis Colts could be poised to hold a fire sale at the trade deadline, having just fired GM Chris Ballard amid the team's disappointing 2-4 start. For now, the Colts are retaining head coach Shane Steichen, but if he survives into next season, this team's next GM could be looking to orchestrate a reboot, which will require draft assets.
Indy's best personnel resources could be put on the trade block. Taylor is certainly one of them.
Although his yards-per-carry average is currently at a career low (4.0), Taylor already has 492 rushing yards and seven touchdowns. He just signed a two-year, $44 million deal before the season started, so the Broncos would have to ensure they could fit his contract under the salary cap.
If Taylor was suddenly traded to Denver, Sean Payton would have to consider putting Bo Nix under center more often, at least on first and second down, instead of in the shotgun. Taylor needs that head of steam that the under-center offense can offer a ball-carrier.
Taylor is one of the NFL's best and most prolific running backs, and while it wouldn't be cheap to acquire him, I doubt it would cost the Broncos anywhere near as much as the San Francisco 49ers once gave to the Carolina Panthers for Christian McCaffrey. Taylor will turn 28 in January and he has a  lot of mileage on his three-time Pro Bowl tires.
Imagine for a moment — if you will — a Broncos offensive line that features Nelson at left guard and Quinn Meinerz at right guard. That would be one heck of a way to spark a run game. Nelson is playing on an expiring contract, which makes him an even more realistic trade candidate for the Colts.
That also helps make Nelson realistic for the Broncos, but the team would have to rethink it's long-term strategy at left guard. Current starter, Ben Powers, is expected to depart in free agency next year, and the Broncos drafted Kage Casey in the fourth round this past spring with an eye on being the future at left guard.
Casey had a really good summer, but he's been a healthy scratch thus far. Would Denver want to give up draft capital and sign a proven All-Pro like Nelson to a lucrative multi-year contract rather than follow through on its plan to develop Casey?
That's the rub, but when it comes to this offensive line's failure to launch, Powers is the least to blame of Denver's trio of culprits. Center Luke Wattenberg and right tackle Mike McGlinchey have been far more problematic, both as run and pass blockers.
As for Nelson, giving up a second-round pick would likely get the job done, but if the market heats up for his services, it wouldn't be a shock to see the Colts ask for more. He's going to be 31 next year, but he's coming off his eighth straight Pro Bowl nod and was a second-team All-Pro last season (for the third time in his career). He's also a three-time first-team All-Pro.
Irving has one more year left on his contract, but the Bucs are headed in the wrong direction. He's rushed for 452 yards and two touchdowns this season, averaging a healthy 4.7 yards per carry.
Irving was Nix's teammate at Oregon for two years, and they entered the NFL draft together in 2024. Nix went to Denver in Round 1 while Irving landed in Tampa in Round 4. They made a lot of hay together in Oregon, so I'd imagine they could hit the ground running as pros.
Irving is only 24, and while he rushed for 1,122 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, injuries caused him to finish with half that production in Year 2. He's appeared in every game this season for Tampa, though.
Depending on Tampa's desparation, I would start with a third-round pick for Irving's services. If the Bucs wanted a second-rounder, it might be a bridge too far, given that Denver could find a good running back in the draft next spring. But that wouldn't help them in the present.
While we're talking potential fire sales, Vea has to be in the conversation of realistic targets. He asked for a trade this past summer, but instead of dealing him, the Bucs gave him a one-year, $30 million extension.
The Broncos' defensive line has been okay this season, but when it comes to stopping the run, they've struggled. Only one team has been worse against the run, and one of Denver's biggest issues is the lack of mass up front.
The 6-foot-4, 347-pound Vea would be an immediate solution. The problem? He's about to turn 32 in February, so any team interested in his services would have to be confident that he has plenty left in the tank.
If a third-round pick would get it done, I'd be on the phone right now with the Bucs. At least to check on the possibility.
Barkley has been banged up this year, but the Eagles could be poised to sell off some of their top assets, being in a similar situation as the Colts, minus the firing of their general manager. Barkley turns 30 in February, so any team acquiring him would have to verify his health and feel confident in his long-term viability.
Barkley is under contract for two more years, which could be advantageous for the Broncos. That would give them the chance to make use of his talents now, and give them time to determine whether he's worth re-signing beyond 2028 when his contract expires.
When Barkley is healthy and in the zone, there's no better running back in the NFL. But it would probably take a second-round pick plus perhaps a 2028 Day 3 selection to pry him off Philly's hands.

title: Broncos Week 7 Injury Report: Final Decisions on Surtain, Coleman & Hufanga
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are coming off a "mini-bye" — three extra days of rest and preparation between their Week 6 Thursday night game and Sunday's road trip to take on the Arizona Cardinals . Denver's actual bye isn't until Week 10.
Given the gauntlet of opponents the Broncos faced to get to 4-2, they earned those three days. The question is whether that chance to breathe gave Sean Payton enough time to tweak the Broncos' offense, dig Bo Nix out of his slump, and get the run game firing on all cylinders.
This matchup with the Cardinals could answer that question and more, given that they rank bottom 10 in net yards and points allowed. It's a road game, and the Cardinals are coming off a big win over the Los Angeles Rams, but if Nix and Payton's offense can't get right against the NFL's second-worst scoring defense, it will only deepen doubts that the Broncos will ever turn the ship around this season.
On Friday, the Broncos and Cardinals dropped their final Week 7 injury reports. Let's break them down.
The Broncos are starting to get healthier. That may be a relative term, given that three players have been ruled out, but it's more about the caliber of players returning.
Surtain is questionable after returning to practice on Wednesday . He was limited all three days this week, so if he's fully healthy, he'll play. If not, the Broncos will be wise and wait until Week 8 to insert him back into the lineup.
Coleman is also listed as questionable, but only because Sean Payton wants Arizona to wonder for as long as possible whether the Broncos will actually activate their rookie running back. The Broncos started Coleman's clock to return from injured reserve earlier this week.
It's great to see Moss back to full participation. And Waddle has been fully cleared, though he was limited the first two days of the week.
Badie, Elliss, and Hufanga are out this week. It wouldn't be a surprise to see Badie and Elliss placed on IR to make room for Coleman and the return of veteran rush linebacker Jonathon Cooper, who's expected to come back from the commissioner's exempt list this week.
Friday's #DENvsAZ injury report: 📰 » https://t.co/mxd0ceioJ8 pic.twitter.com/yYI47WTUFp
Broncos fans won't get to see Love in action. Instead, it'll be Tyler Allgeier pounding the rock.
We'll be closely monitoring Baker's status on gameday. He did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday, and was limited on Friday, but it'll be a surprise if he doesn't suit up.
The Cardinals are pretty banged up on both sides of the ball, but Seumalo, Duvernay, and Sweat are fully cleared to play.

title: Davis Webb Hints at What Jonah Coleman's Return Could Mean for Broncos
full_text:
The Denver Bronco's rushing offense ranks 26th in the NFL, averaging a paltry 84.2 yard per game. Granted, the Broncos have faced some top-tier defensive fronts in each of their six games thus far, but their rushing production has been nowhere near good enough.
With the schedule opening up now, there's a chance that the combined efforts of J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, which, again, have been lackluster thus far, could suddenly kick into high gear. But Dobbins doesn't seem to have the same burst he did last year, and the Broncos are reluctant to lean on Harvey much as a between-the-tackles runner.
Thankfully, Jonah Coleman is about to rejoin the Broncos' backfield, and his return from injured reserve could be the spark this run game needs to get up off the mat. The rookie hit injured reserve with an ankle injury after his Week 2 debut at Mile High — a victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars that Coleman helped seal with a touchdown and some tough running to close out the game.
The Broncos started Coleman's clock to return from IR this week, and he's been a full participant in practice each day. On Friday, offensive coordinator Davis Webb talked about Coleman's return and what the rookie brings to the table.
"First of all, he's very smart. He's handled the playbook very quickly from day one, rookie minicamp on," Webb said.
We've heard a lot about Coleman's football IQ and makeup since the Broncos drafted him in the fourth round. Head coach Sean Payton often says , "You don't feel a rookie," when asked about Coleman.
This carry at the end of the Jaguars game showcases Coleman's football smarts and presence of mind, avoiding the sideline to keep the clock ticking.
Jonah Coleman with a heads up play to stay in bounds and go down after picking up the first. pic.twitter.com/b3rjBgmChq
He's only touched the ball in one game as a pro, but Coleman was impressive in that Week 2 game , and we know he was playing hurt late when he busted off a pair of 12-yard runs to move the chains, kill the clock, and ice the victory for Denver.
"Every time he's gotten an opportunity, whether that be in a regular-season game, obviously the Jacksonville Jaguars game sticks out, the Atlanta Falcons game in the preseason sticks out," Webb said of Coleman. "So we're excited to get him back into the fold. I think the last couple weeks, our whole running back room is kind of slowly going up, turning in the right direction."
I believe Webb that the Broncos' ground game is trending upward, if for no other reason than Coleman's return. There are other signs of life, including Dobbins's running in the first half last week against the Seattle Seahawks and his late-game performance the week prior against the Los Angeles Chargers.
As in all things offense for the Broncos, though, the consistency just hasn't been there. We would be remiss to pin this run game's hopes solely on the return of a still-untested rookie, but including Coleman in the mix with Dobbins, sprinkled here and there with the odd Harvey carry, is the most substantial reason for hope this rushing offense has had in weeks.
When the Broncos officially activate Coleman, they'll have to make a corresponding roster cut. It's looking like that player could be fellow running back Tyler Badie, who suffered a thumb injury early in Week 6's game and never returned.
Badie has not practiced all week, and if the Broncos expect him to miss more than one or two games, they might opt to just bite the bullet and put him on IR. That would open up a spot for Coleman, and give Badie plenty of time to heal up. Either that, or the Broncos will have to cut a player at another position.
The rookie Jonah Coleman gives the Broncos a fourth quarter lead 🐴 JAXvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wpnL52qLn8
The Broncos will travel to take on the Arizona Cardinals this week, whose rushing defense ranks 20th in the NFL. Arizona is allowing 120.8 yards per game on the ground, giving the Broncos a great opportunity to establish the run and keep the chains moving .
When it comes to things Payton likes to say, let's also not forget his comment about the quarterback position being the hardest to play without a running game. The Broncos had three extra days of preparation over their "mini-bye," and for the first time this season, they're not playing a battle-tested, playoff-caliber front seven.
The Broncos believe they have the horses in the running back room to field a competitive run game. We haven't seen much of one yet, but that initial six-game gauntlet of opponents was brutal and unprecedented in modern Broncos canon.
“We think it’s a deep room and a talented room," Payton said on Wednesday of the running backs. "So all those things are a positive.”
This is the week for a Bo Nix breakout . And that starts with a productive run game on the road at State Farm Stadium.

title: Bo Nix Breakout? Mile High Roundtable Picks Broncos vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are coming off a "mini-bye," looking to send a message this week that this offense shouldn't be written off.
Meanwhile, the Arizona Cardinals may be 2-4, but they're coming off a huge divisional victory over the Los Angeles Rams. The Cardinals are feeling it right now, and they're at home — but we know how Broncos Country travels, especially in the desert.
At 4-2, the Broncos can't afford a slip-up — not if they want to keep pace with the Kansas City Chiefs in the division, and make their Week 8 rematch at Mile High a potential chance to get back to the top of the division, depending on what happens this Sunday with the Seattle Seahawks.
That's me looking past the Cardinals a little bit. The Broncos won't be doing that. Sean Payton knows how to keep a team's focus on whichever game and opponent is up next, and that's the Cardinals.
How will this one shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff see Sunday's action unfolding in Glendale, AZ.
Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 4-2 : Getting Bo Nix back in the flow of things has become like a quest for the Holy Grail. All the internal tinkering on Nix might not be as important as facing a Cardinals team the Broncos should beat. While most eyes will be focused on how Nix performs, it's returning rookie running back Jonah Coleman who steals the limelight with two scores.
Pick : Broncos 31, Cardinals 21
Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 4-2 : The Broncos' coaches and players are buzzing about a Nix breakout game. Looking at the Cardinals' 31st-ranked scoring defense — a unit allowing 350.5 yards per game — this is about as golden a get-right opportunity Nix could hope for. Courtland Sutton said , "At some point, the tide's going to turn" for Nix and this offense, and it happens at State Farm Stadium on Sunday. Nix passes for three touchdowns and 280 yards, while the Broncos romp in the desert.
Pick : Broncos 27, Cardinals 17
Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 4-2 : Only speaking for myself, the Broncos haven’t yet earned the benefit of the doubt. Not yet. But if there’s any way to earn that — and any day to have a get-right game — it’s Sunday against the Cardinals. This goes for the offense more so than the defense, which has been fantastic of late. If not now for Nix, then when? Go out there and dominate, and those “confidence issues” will miraculously disappear. I foresee a better showing, though maybe not quite the 2018 Kick Your A** blowout. This is an inferior opponent who, quite frankly, the Broncos should handily dispatch. “Should.”
Pick : Broncos 30, Cardinals 16
Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 4-2 : The Broncos' offense has been the source of much consternation. Is Nix hurt? Has the game passed Sean Payton by? Luckily, the Cardinals appear to be a get-right game. It's the NFL; there is no such thing as a guaranteed victory, but I expect the Broncos' defense and special teams, as well as continuity across the organization, to be felt in Arizona. I don't think the offense looks great... and even if it does, it's just one game, and the broader sample size should hold more weight in the total evaluation. Still, it will be nice to provide the fan base some hope.
Pick : Broncos 20, Cardinals16
Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 4-2 : It's easy to think the Broncos will have their way with the Cardinals. But the Cardinals have shown they can challenge other teams , so it will be important for the Broncos' offense to come out strong. If the Broncos can do that and build a comfortable lead, the defense should be able to finish it from there, even with the Cardinals putting up a fight.
Pick : Broncos 23, Cardinals 16
Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 3-3 : 10 days between games feels like forever, but reality is the Broncos have really hit their stride after their Thursday night game in each of the past two seasons. This won't be a dominant display, but it will be the first time this season both the Broncos' offense and defense play good complementary football, and Nix finds consistent success. Nix throws for a couple of touchdowns and rushes for another, giving fans some hope that he's close to being back.
Pick : Broncos 24, Cardinals 13
Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 3-3 : If there was any opportunity to try to get the offense on track, it's this week against Arizona. Denver got the mini-bye, and Arizona's defense has allowed the most points in the league this season. Criticism of Nix is getting more intense by the minute, so it would be great to see him try to push the ball down the field and take chances against one of the worst defenses the league has to offer. I think he's gonna do it this week.
Pick : Broncos 31, Cardinals 17
James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 2-4 : The Broncos are coming off a mini-bye, which frankly has come at a good time for a sputtering offense. Another week with Payton calling the plays again should be beneficial for Nix, but ultimately, the Broncos will have to play well to beat a tricky and plucky Cardinals team. The defense keys the win with a few takeaways off Jacoby Brissett, while the offense — just about — does enough to show some signs of life.
Pick : Broncos 24, Cardinals 14
Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 2-4 : The Cardinals aren't pushovers and shouldn't be overlooked, but against their defense, the Broncos can get things jump-started. The Cardinals allow the second-highest explosive pass rate, which, despite ranking 18th in generating explosive offensive passing plays, is something the Broncos struggle with, as their 4.6% rate is 3% higher than Arizona's at 32nd. The Broncos' defense should be able to carry it enough to allow the offense to work things out, and this is the best opportunity for Nix and company to do that, similarly to the Dallas Cowboys game a season ago. The Broncos show progress in Arizona, and while they don't fix everything in a week, they do walk out with the win.
Pick : Broncos 18, Cardinals 10
Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 2-4 : Nix and the Broncos have a chance to put up some major points against the Cardinals and their weak defense. The Cardinals have one of the worst defenses against the pass, teeing up Nix and the Broncos' receivers to breathe life into what has been a disappointing offensive start to the season. Defensively, if the Broncos can limit Trey McBride's impact, this should be their easiest win this season.
Pick : Broncos 30, Cardinals 6

title: 5 Overlooked Broncos Who Could Swing the Cardinals Game
full_text:
Many are writing off the Arizona Cardinals as the Denver Broncos prepare to face them this Sunday, but they're a feisty team that shouldn't be overlooked.
The Cardinals' struggle areas mirror the Broncos', especially on defense and in the passing game. Today, we're looking at a handful of Broncos flying under the radar going into the desert.
The Broncos will want to get these players involved to improve the likelihood of walking out with a win .
Look, everyone is frustrated with the checkdowns and the designed throws to running backs, but the Cardinals struggle to run down the ball out of the backfield, especially in space. They're one of the worst teams at handling it, but Arizona's opponents have yet to fully exploit those issues.
Denver has a great matchup against the Cardinals' linebackers, and Harvey should be heavily used as both a receiver and a rusher.
The Cardinals are even worse at covering tight ends because of their linebacker issues. Evan Engram could be used here, but he would be more likely to draw Budda Baker (if he plays). Adam Trautman has struggled on a weekly basis, while Adkins has looked like a capable starter.
Denver should use some three-tight-end sets and get favorable passing matchups with Adkins against Arizona's linebackers.
The Cardinals' offensive line has struggled to block interior defensive linemen and edge defenders like Jones. While the Cardinals haven’t allowed a lot of pressure ( 12th-fewest pressures , with the seventh-ranked pass-blocking efficiency), they're weak against these types of defenders.
Jones has really come on over the last two weeks, so ride the hot hand to help generate some pressure and put the heat on Jacoby Brissett.
With Talanoa Hufanga and Patrick Surtain II out vs. the Seahawks, Rapp got called up off the practice squad and played 65 of 85 defensive snaps. There is a good chance Denver does that again against the Cardinals.
It would give Rapp the tough task of helping to cover Cardinals tight end Trey McBride and their quietly good receiver corps. Rapp played well against the Seahawks, and if the Broncos turn to him again, they'll need another strong performance.
With a few weeks to go until the NFL trade deadline (November 10), Mims is trending in the wrong direction. He isn't being used as a kick returner often; his play as a punt returner has been mediocre at best, and his effort on offense has been terrible.
As things stand, Mims is playing his way to be traded, and it's on him to flip the script. Maybe he makes something happen in this game; he certainly needs a big day.

title: Broncos Week 7 Injury Report: Who’s Trending For the Field—or IR
full_text:
The Denver Broncos continued full-scale preparation for Sunday's road game against the Arizona Cardinals, releasing their second injury report ahead of the Week 7 matchup.
On it, running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) and cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) were listed as full practice participants for another day, while defensive end Zach Allen was upgraded to full after getting his usual rest day on Wednesday.
Coleman was designated to return from injured reserve on Wednesday after missing the last four games. He still must be formally activated to the 53-man roster but is fully expected to play against the Cardinals.
Coleman's return is especially helpful this week considering third-string RB Tyler Badie missed practice for a second straight day due to a thumb injury. His status for Sunday's game is in jeopardy; he needs a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up.
Outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) both also were DNPs this week. Hufanga will be ruled out on Friday, and the Broncos anticipate Elliss landing on short-term injured reserve, back at some point later this year.
“He’s going to be someone that it’s not season-ending, and so we’re fortunate. So that’ll come out later in the week, but it was better news," head coach Sean Payton said of Elliss on Wednesday.
Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) and cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) were limited participants; Surtain could be a game-time decision, though Waddle is expected to go.
Unfortunately for the home team, the Cardinals are trending toward being at much less than full strength -- at least, according to their Thursday injury report .
Arizona listed starting safety Budda Baker and running back Jeremiyah Love as DNP for a second consecutive day, as well as safety Andrew Wingard. Cornerback Garrett Williams and defensive lineman Darius Robinson were upgraded to limited.
Baker's absence in particular would be a fortuitous break for a Broncos offense desperately seekin its first true breakout game in 2026. However, Payton knows well enough not to overlook the other 10 players on the Cardinals' defensive side.
“They give you a couple different looks," Payton noted Wednesday. "They’re in their base defense. They have a penny package. You have to I.D. if they’re in that. Then their pressure package from nickel. They affect the quarterback.
"I think the other thing that stands out is they’re causing more fumbles in their wins. Their takeaway numbers have been really good, and that’s something you see.”

title: Detroit Lions Updated 2026 Week 7 Depth Chart
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have a big opportunity for a statement win on Sunday.
Coming off their bye week, the Lions are set to take on the Green Bay Packers with a chance to make some headway in the NFC North division. All four teams in the division currently have a winning record, and with Sunday being Detroit's first divisional game of the year, it's an opportunity to position themselves to compete for their third crown in four years.
Detroit could be getting a boost on both sides of the ball, with center Cade Mays and safety Brian Branch both getting activated off of injury lists for Sunday's game. The expectation currently is that both players will start.
Here is an updated look at the Lions' depth chart heading into their showdown with the Packers .
Starter: Jared Goff. Backup: Josh Dobbs
Goff has the opportunity to continue what has been one of the cleanest stretches of his career, as he remains without a turnover through the team's first five games of the year. He is 7-4 career against the Packers, throwing 19 touchdowns against five interceptions in those games.
Starter: Jahmyr Gibbs. Backup: Sione Vaki. Reserve: Jacob Saylors. Inactive: Isiah Pacheco (Injured reserve).
The Lions will look to get Gibbs going after he was held in check in two games against Green Bay last year. Green Bay will be without two starting linebackers in Zaire Franklin and Edgerrin Cooper, and the Lions could look to utilize Gibbs to exploit this.
Behind him, Vaki is established as the second running back. He continues to improve in the pass-protection element of the game, which is an important part of his role.
Starters: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa. Backups: DeAndre Carter, Tay Martin. Injured: Tom Kennedy (Injured reserve), Kendrick Law (Injured reserve).
The Lions will continue to have their top receivers available, but they are still light on depth heading into Sunday's game. Carter is added to the mix after the season-ending injury to Tom Kennedy, while Martin remains a contributor exclusively on special teams.
Starter: Sam LaPorta. Backup: Brock Wright. Reserves: Tyler Conklin, Jackson Meeks.
The contract situation surrounding Sam LaPorta has caused something of a firestorm over the last couple of weeks, but he continues to produce at a high level for the offense. Coming out of the bye week, LaPorta could be another option to exploit the Packers' inexperience at linebacker.
Detroit has alternated between Conklin and Meeks as the third tight end, and as a result it's uncertain which of the two they will take active into Sunday's game.
Starters: Penei Sewell (left), Blake Miller (right). Backup: Larry Borom. Inactive: Gio Manu (Non-Football injury).
The Lions will lean on Sewell and Miller to handle business up front heading into their first divisional contest of the season. In four starts, the rookie Miller has earned a Pro Football Focus offensive grade of 67.1 and allowed nine total pressure and no sacks.
Starters: Christian Mahogany (left), Tate Ratledge (right). Backups: Juice Scruggs, Miles Frazier. Inactive: Ben Bartch (Injured reserve)
The guard position is one of the most intriguing spots on Detroit's depth chart this week. With Cade Mays returning, the Lions are making a change at center and as a result Scruggs could see some time at guard.
Scruggs is one of the top-performing centers through Detroit's first five games, and because of that the Lions could look to get him involved on the interior. However, Mahogany and Ratledge are both playing well and as a result neither need to be replaced.
Starter: Cade Mays. Backup: Juice Scruggs. Reserve: Seth McLaughlin
The Lions' offensive line has performed well in Mays' absence, and now he will join them as the starter at center after being activated off of injured reserve. It will be his debut with the team after signing a three-year deal in free agency this year.
Scruggs will be the backup, and likely the first option off the bench if any of the three interior linemen were to go down.
Starters: Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams. Backups: Skyler Gill-Howard, Levi Onwuzurike. Reserve: Mekhi Wingo.
The Lions have developed a nice rotation amidst its interior defensive line. Williams and Gill-Howard have complimented each other nicely, giving the Lions an answer for both the run and the pass. McNeill has been exceptional, recording 23 pressures which ranks second on the team.
Starters: Aidan Hutchinson, D.J. Wonnum. Backups: Tyler Lacy, Derrick Moore. Reserves: Eric O'Neill, Ahmed Hassanein. Inactive: Payton Turner (Injured reserve).
The Lions have been able to get plenty of pass-rush production this year, as they lead the league in sacks. Against a Packers' offense that has been reliant on the big play through the air, getting heat on Jordan Love could be a difference-making factor in whether or not they earn a win.
Starters: Jack Campbell, Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez. Backups: Trevor Nowaske, Jimmy Rolder, Amen Ogbongbemiga. Inactive: Devin White (Injured reserve), Damone Clark (Injured reserve).
The Lions lost White to a forearm injury that has resulted in an IR stint, which will lead to more opportunities for Malcolm Rodriguez. It could also create more snaps for Rolder, who has logged defensive snaps in just one of the first five regular season games.
Starters: D.J. Reed, Roger McCreary. Backups: Ennis Rakestraw, Rock Ya-Sin. Reserves: Keith Abney II, Khalil Dorsey
The Lions rolled with McCreary as the boundary corner against the Cardinals, and even with Ya-Sin expected to play on Sunday they should stick with McCreary. He had six passes defensed, which was the most by a Lions defender in one game this season.
Rakestraw should see some time. Meanwhile, Abney is an interesting spot. He started at safety against Arizona, but with Brian Branch returning could be in the mix to play some at cornerback.
Starters: Brian Branch, Chuck Clark. Backups: Keith Abney II, Christian Izien. Reserve: Bishop Fitzgerald. Inactive: Kerby Joseph (Physically Unable to Perform), Thomas Harper (Injured reserve), Avonte Maddox (Injured reserve).
Branch was officially activated and taken off of the injury report on Sunday, so his highly anticipated return will be on Sunday. Even if he's not the same game-breaking player he was prior to the injury right away, his presence alone will give them some stability.
Clark is the front-runner to play beside him, though Abney did show some intriguing ability in his audition at safety against the Cardinals. Fitzgerald has yet to be active since being claimed off Pittsburgh's practice squad nearly a month ago, and with Branch returning that may not change.
Kicker: Jake Bates. Punter: Jack Fox. Long-snapper: Hogan Hatten. Kick returners: Jacob Saylors, DeAndre Carter. Punt returner: DeAndre Carter.
The addition of Carter is an intriguing one. He's currently the NFL's active leader in returns, and is on his 12th team in 12 years. He should have an extended leash to handle the return duties, and could bring a spark to the return game after Kennedy had some success in Week 5 prior to his injury.
Interestingly enough, Carter made his official debut in 2018 for the Philadelphia Eagles where current Lions special teams coordinator Dave Fipp was in that role at the time. Now, the two will reunite with hopes of sparking Detroit's return game.

title: Expert Predictions For Detroit Lions Matchup With Green Bay Packers
full_text:
On Sunday afternoon, the Detroit Lions will take on a Green Bay Packers team playing its best football of the 2026 season.
The Packers, winners of three in a row, are coming off a 23-13 defeat of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. Meanwhile, Detroit, which spent Week 6 on its bye, defeated the Arizona Cardinals in Week 5, 45-21.
Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 7 matchup with Green Bay.
The Lions have their first chance to prove themselves in the NFC North Sunday, taking on a Green Bay Packers team that appears to be built to exploit Detroit's biggest weakness.
Quarterback Jordan Love has been unafraid to test defenses down the field with wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. As a result, I think the Lions will try to dial up the pass-rush and try to get to Love before he has a chance to cut it loose.
Offensively, the Lions need to get Jahmyr Gibbs going as the Packers did a good job of keeping him in check in their two meetings last year. Quarterback Jared Goff has been turnover-free through five games, and will need to keep that going to give his team the best chance to win.
While the Lions have the ability to keep up in the event this game becomes a shootout, the Packers are uniquely equipped to attack the Lions' issues in coverage, both in the secondary and at linebacker.
Green Bay makes one more play than Detroit, and hands Dan Campbell's team a crushing loss to start a crucial two-game stretch.
The Detroit Lions have a big time test ahead of themselves on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers.
The Packers not only are red hot and winners of three in a row. But they're also due to receive a big boost to their run game with the return of Pro Bowl back Josh Jacobs.
In addition, Green Bay receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are playing some of the best football of their NFL careers.
Consequently, Kelvin Sheppard's defense won't have it easy in this Week 7 divisional affair.
Yet, the Lions' defense will be in the best shape it's been all season due to the return of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch. He should provide a major boost to the team's secondary and put it in a stronger position to limit the productivity of Watson and Golden.
I think Detroit's pass defense holds up just enough and Jared Goff and the offense come through in the fourth quarter, leading Dan Campbell's squad to its fourth victory of the season.
The Lions return to action after a much needed week off. The Packers are visiting Ford Field missing a few key players, but will have running back Josh Jacobs in the lineup.
If the defensive line can have another strong performance, Jordan Love will not have ample time to find his key targets.
Tight end Tucker Kraft could be in line for a big game, but Detroit’s offense should keep the momentum from the first quarter of the season rolling. Sam LaPorta might just also have himself a productive afternoon, given the noise he created and wanting to prove he deserves a lucrative new contract.
The Lions start divisional play with the Green Bay Packers this week, and it sees the return of Brian Branch and Josh Jacobs for their respective teams. That makes this week even more intriguing.
It will be interesting to see how, or if, the bye week has given Detroit time to somewhat fix its porous secondary. The return of Branch will give fans a glimpse as to how this secondary should operate, but the boundary corner issues could make this discussion irrelevant.
Green Bay is a hard team to gauge, even before factoring in the wild card element that it is a divisional game in the NFC North. The Lions, on fresh legs and with momentum, alongside a rowdy Ford Field crowd, take the win to open the second half of the season.

title: Detroit Lions Activate Safety From PUP, OL From IR
full_text:
The Detroit Lions announced a pair of Week 7 roster moves, just a little less than 24 hours ahead of their Week 7 contest against the Green Bay Packers.
Safety Brian Branch was activated off of the Physically Unable to Perform List, while center Cade Mays was activated off of the injured reserve list. They were both removed from the game status after being listed as questionable, which signals that both will make their season debut.
Detroit's coaching staff has a good idea of how much both will play in their 2026 season debuts. Branch is returning from a torn Achilles, while Mays will play his first game in a Lions uniform after rehabbing an injured wrist.
With both activations, the Lions' roster now is full with 53-players. Detroit did not elevate anyone from the practice squad for this week's game, and does not have anyone with an injury designations after removing Branch and Mays from the list.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Green Bay Packers Will Be Without Veteran Linebacker in Week 7
Veteran Packers running back Josh Jacobs has now been officially activated off of the Commissioners exempt list and is expected to play against Detroit at Ford Field.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard was asked earlier this week about the challenges of going against an offense getting Jacobs back and if he thinks they will run a similar offense to what they have been the first quarter of the season.
“They're probably over there just like we are about (Safety Brian Branch) BB, to be honest with you. You know what I mean? It's kind of the same for them," said Sheppard. "Everybody's asking, 'How much is he going?' Listen, whenever you could gain an All-Pro player back, obviously that's going to boost everything. Everybody's just looking at the run game . It's going to open up everything. It's going to boost everything. So, it's just a matter for them just like us, like how much will he do? But we're prepared to play the player.
"We've played them previously, not only Green Bay when he was in Vegas. Have the utmost respect for that player, Josh Jacobs. I think he's one of the top-end guys in this League. And like I said, I believe we'll be prepared for the challenge.”

title: Why Waiting on Sam LaPorta Deal Could Be Disaster For Detroit Lions
full_text:
The cloud surrounding the Detroit Lions and their contract situation with tight end Sam LaPorta continues to swell.
Ahead of their pivotal Week 7 showdown with the Green Bay Packers, some tension has grown between the two parties in their efforts to get a new deal done before LaPorta is eligible for free agency in the offseason.
Reports of the two sides being at odds first surfaced in early October, when it was noted that the two sides had paused negotiations for a new deal before the Lions took on the Carolina Panthers in Week 4.
Earlier this week, LaPorta voiced his frustrations during an interview on the Barstool Sports' 'Pardon My Take' podcast. Now, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones has added some additional context to the situation and why it could be important for the Lions to get a deal done rather quickly.
"Things don’t appear to be great between the Detroit Lions and tight end Sam LaPorta, but it is more likely than not that the two sides eventually reach an agreement on an extension before free agency," Jones wrote.
Jones noted that the Lions under general manager Brad Holmes have been keen on retaining their drafted talent, with LaPorta being a second-round pick who has produced at a high level since being drafted in 2023.
Detroit has not been opposed to get deals done during the season, with notable examples being defensive lineman Alim McNeill during the 2024 season and star EDGE Aidan Hutchinson last year.
However, the longer the Lions wait, the more expensive LaPorta could become.
The franchise tag is an option the Lions could utilize to keep LaPorta for an additional season, but Jones noted that it wouldn't be a cheap one. According to OverTheCap , the current projection for the franchise tag at the tight end position is approximately $17.5 million.
Additionally, Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is extension eligible following the conclusion of this season. Bowers broke the rookie reception record for tight ends one year after LaPorta set it, and is on track to reset the market.
Via a league source, Jones reported that Bowers could indeed get that record money, which will put even more pressure on the Lions to pay a massive sum in order to retain LaPorta.
"George Kittle sits at the top of the market at $19.1 million per year," Jones wrote. "A league source estimated Bowers could get into the mid-20s, in large part because the Raiders paid a center $27 million per year who a) had never played a down for the team and b) never made an All-Pro team. With Bowers eligible for his extension in a few months, waiting would not behoove the Lions."
The Lions have watched as multiple members of the 2023 NFL draft tight end group have received extensions from their respective teams. Kyle Pitts (three years, $54 million), Tucker Kraft (four years, $75 million) and Michael Mayer (three years, $45 million) all have received new deals and established a market for what LaPorta's contract could look like.
However, with the ongoing speculation and Detroit's desire to keep their drafted talent , an extension that exceeds all three of those deals to keep LaPorta could be on the horizon.
According to OverTheCap, the Lions currently have just over $36 million in effective cap space for the 2027 season. In addition to LaPorta, the Lions are also expected to explore a contract extension with fellow 2023 second-round pick, safety Brian Branch.
The Lions have been without Branch for the first five games of the season, but Branch is expected to make his season debut Sunday after rehabbing a torn Achilles barring anything unforseen.

title: 'Everybody's Ass Was Tight': Detroit Lions' Defense Loosened Up
full_text:
Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson called a players-only meeting for defensive players prior to the game against the Arizona Cardinals.
To start the season, Kelvin Sheppard's defense was giving up far too many explosive plays and looked out of sorts against the Bills and the Panthers. Even in victories, opponents like the Saints and Jets were able to mount comebacks in the second half.
Detroit's roster felt the pressure, with some players succumbing to the growing need to succeed by making up for the mistakes of others and not sticking to their primary defensive responsibilities.
“I feel like everybody’s ass was tight. Players, everybody. Coaches," said Barnes, via the Detroit Free Press . "I just feel like it was one of those things that we just had to remind ourselves as a defense, as players, like, ‘Man, we have to play loose, we got to have fun.’ The most important thing about that meeting was we had to just remind ourselves, at the end of the day, this is a kid’s sport that we get to play and that we love.”
The meeting was intended to get everyone on the same page and to remind the group to still go out and have fun, while sticking to their assignments and responsibilities.
Second-year defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard agreed regarding how important it was for players to remain loose out on the field.
"It's ultra important, man. This game's hard enough. I tell the guys, 'This job and what we do is hard enough. You should get to Sunday and go out and cut it loose and have fun.' And that's when I say guys, that kind of encompasses when I talk about it's the players," said Sheppard. "This is a player's league. The coaches do the work during the week. We present them things. We show them things that we've seen. We present the plan to prepare them and try to make Monday through Saturday as stressful as possible so Sunday it's easy, so to say."
Sheppard explained there is still room to grow, but he is starting to see the growing confidence of the defense, especially after their best performance against the Cardinals.
"Nothing's easy in this league, but you kind of get what I'm saying. Sunday should feel free. You should go out and have fun with your brothers doing something that a small percent of this world gets blessed and fortunate enough to do," said Sheppard. "So absolutely. And I saw that and that kind of trickles into the swagger, especially on the defensive side, man. When you take the field, you want to have a bounce in your step. You want guys to feel your presence out there, but all that's built off confidence.
"I think that's what you're starting to see with these guys. And I'm just excited for them, man, because this is what I've always believed. Like I said, this is what we always believe we could be. And there's still so much growth and things we need to improve on moving forward off of that.”

title: 5 Players Detroit Lions Must Scout in College Football Week 8
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions begin divisional play, taking on the Green Bay Packers after getting a week off to heal up, most notably with safety Brian Branch.
However, in recent days, the Lions have not seen Branch as one of their homegrown players taking center stage and being the main storyline. Instead, a contract dispute, or lack of urgency towards a deal, with tight end Sam LaPorta has owned the news cycle.
The tight end position , which was thought to be a set position upon a presumed re-signing, now sits in flux. With Saturday’s slate of college football coming up, extra attention was paid to the tight end spot.
Here are five players the Lions should look at during Saturday’s slate.
Johnson is a player the Lions might not be able to afford missing out on after Kenyon Sadiq flew off the board this spring. Sadiq, a freakishly athletic tight end from Oregon, has Johnson following in his footsteps.
Johnson has great size for a tight end, at 6-foot-5, 257 pounds. He has yet to post a drop this year while also being a star run and pass blocker. Separation and versatility are also strong calling cards, and the few times he cannot create separation, it is no problem with his ability to pull the ball down in traffic.
Last season, there was less looks at the tight end tape for Oregon’s Sadiq considering Motown’s situation. This year, Johnson might find himself as a Detroit draft darling. His Ducks take on Illinois at 3 p.m. EST.
Reynolds, a junior, has the option to return to the Hokies after the year is done. However, as his play stands currently, with over 400 receiving yards at the midpoint of the season, it is very probable the Massachusetts native goes pro.
While he has a drop on the season, he can read zones well to plant. He has less athleticism, size, and versatility than Johnson, but makes plays and is an instant upgrade on the Lions’ tight end room sans Sam LaPorta.
The Hokies travel to Clemson and Death Valley at 7 p.m. EST.
Roberts is a player that has dragged himself into the draft conversation. In what has been a down year for Michigan State football , the defensive tackle has put together a strong campaign.
That campaign came to a head last Saturday against Northwestern, with the Washington native recording eight tackles, three tackles for loss and two sacks, all of which were career-best marks.
Roberts has burst off the line that has seen him go unblocked in each of the last two games, and excels in forklifting players to create havoc. He is a run-stuffer with some pass-rush potential being tapped his senior year.
The Spartans take on UCLA in the Rose Bowl at 3:30 p.m. EST.
West is a tweener defensive lineman, taking some reps on the inside as well as the outside. In 158 pass rush snaps, West has 11 pressures and taken part of a trio of sacks.
His run-stop ability will keep teams watching the tape, with his rate ranking among the top quadrant of the class alongside his pass rush ability. West followed head coach Bob Chesney to the Bruins from James Madison, and has seen a dip in production that could be expected.
West has similarities with Eric O’Neill, another former JMU transfer that made the Lions roster out of camp after an underwhelming season with Rutgers.
The Bruins, as mentioned above, host the Spartans at 3:30 p.m. EST.
The Group of Six spot belongs to Finley, who elected to remain a Bulldog despite offers to improve his competition this season. He is a blocking heavy tight end with soft hands, ranking just outside the top quarter of tight ends in receiving grade on PFF.
Finley joins Temple’s Peter Clarke as the top Group of Six tight ends highlighted. However, Finley has a pass upgrade, although his drop rate is not among the lowest currently.
The Bulldog’s four touchdowns have doubled his combined scores in the last two seasons as a senior.
The Bulldogs take on Old Dominion at 5 p.m. EST.

title: Behind Enemy Lines: Can Lions Slow Down Packers Passing Attack?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are looking to come out of the bye week with a win in Week 7.
On Sunday, the Lions will host the divisional rival Green Bay Packers, which have won three consecutive games.
Reporter Bill Huber covers the Packers for Packers OnSI . He recently answered five questions from Lions OnSI to preview Sunday's divisional affair.
Bill Huber: Josh Jacobs is going to play, I was told on Thursday. I suppose Friday’s practice might not go well, but this is different than a player coming off a significant injury who needs some ramp-up to get ready for the games. Jacobs has been around the team throughout his six-game stay on the exempt list and he’s been able to go through workouts with the training staff. So, physically and mentally, he should be ready to go.
There will be some rust, obviously, after being out since the end of training camp. But, shoot, a rusty Jacobs should still be a shot in the arm for a running game that’s not just the worst in the league but on pace to be the worst in the NFL.
The Packers don’t need a great running game to score points. They just need to stay out of second-and-10. The blocking hasn’t been good enough, to be sure, but Jacobs’ vision and strength will be an asset in grinding out hard yards
Huber : It's the biggest statistical matchup on the field. Green Bay’s passing game has been excellent and Detroit’s pass defense is on pace to at least threaten the NFL record for most passing yards allowed per game.
Christian Watson was drafted as a size-speed threat but has blossomed into an all-around receiver. Until being somewhat limited by the Cowboys last week, he was on pace for 1,600 receiving yards and 20 touchdowns. That’s unprecedented in NFL history. Meanwhile, Matthew Golden has been a breakout star after a quiet rookie season. He averaged 25.8 yards per game last year but is averaging 83.5 yards this season.
Together, they’re on pace for close to 3,000 yards.
Two things stand out for this game. First, the Packers have to establish the run to maximize their play-action game. Jordan Love was 1-of-7 in play-action last week because the Cowboys weren’t buying what the Packers were selling. Two, Love has had 19 passes dropped. That’s the most in the league and more than all the NFC North quarterbacks combined.
Huber : They’ve got to get the offensive line and running game squared away. The pass protection has been leaky for most of the season, with Jordan Love paying the price. The second thing is finding a running game. They’re averaging less than 60 rushing yards per game and 3.0 rushing yards per attempt.
They are playing an unsustainable brand of football. You can’t put your quarterback in harm’s way without him getting knocked out of the game, and you can’t play winning football without the ability to run the football to run out the clock or control the game in one of those classic cold-weather games.
Defensively, they’ve just got to survive until Micah Parsons returns. So far, so good, but the pass rush hasn’t been good enough unless it’s been schemed up by coordinator Jonathan Gannon.
Huber : Offensively, it’s the tackles. Left tackle Rasheed Walker left in free agency and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 2. In their place, Jordan Morgan has been OK at left tackle and Anthony Belton has been in survival mode at times at right tackle.
Aidan Hutchinson has to be licking his chops about the potential of a big day fueled by the fans and coming against two young tackles.
Defensively, nobody considers Javon Bullard a premier player in the slot. A second-round pick in 2024, he has zero career interceptions or forced fumbles. He’s an excellent player, though. His six passes defensed are more than he had his first two seasons combined. He’ll face a huge matchup against Amon-Ra St. Brown. This matchup will be worth the price of admission.
Huber : As we barrel through the Upper Peninsula to visit family while I’m at the game, I’m leaning toward Detroit.
The Lions, as usual, are really good. Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs – you know the names. They have elite players all over the offense. It’s odd to see them toward the bottom of the league in some key categories on offense. They’re scoring 32 points per game with the upside to get close to 40.
The Packers should score a lot of points, too, but it strikes me that they’ll have to play a nearly perfect game while the Lions have some margin for error. The ability of the Lions’ front to get after Love will make the difference in getting the key stop or two needed to win.

title: Detroit Lions Had Former Vikings Nose Tackle Visit For Tryout
full_text:
The Detroit Lions welcomed former Minnesota Vikings nose tackle Taki Taimani to the teams Allen Park Performance Center for a visit on Friday, according to the NFL's official transaction wire.
After playing collegiately at Oregon and Washington, the 6-foot-1, 325-pound defender went undrafted in 2024.
He was subsequently signed by the Minnesota Vikings. He was able to secure a spot on their 53-man roster coming out of his first training camp.
In 2025, he was not able to make the team, but was brought back on the practice squad.
Prior to the official roster cuts this season, Taimani was waived with an injury designation and reverted to injured reserve list the following day.
Earlier this week, the front office signed safety Myles Bryant to the practice squad . Defensive lineman Aidan Keanaaina was also added recently to the practice squad.
According to a league scouting report , Taimani is a "A two-gapping wide-body capable of standing firm when manning his gaps, Taimani has some pop and anchor to battle along the interior but is a non-factor as a rusher. He has shown the ability to play at a variety of weights, but he’s lacking initial snap quickness and rarely captures lateral positioning or the neutral zone off the snap. Taimani might not have the traits or versatility to be drafted, but players with power who can challenge run games will always have a chance to make a roster."
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard still has the tough task of managing a defense that could use some more help in the secondary.
Getting Brian Branch to assist the back end will certainly be a benefit, but the Packers game will be his first game action in 10 months.
Sheppard was asked this week if he team can replicate the success the defense had against the Cardinals.
“I mean each week is different to be honest, as you know. I'm not telling you nothing you don't know. And week-to-week, you try to do what's best for the defense and for the team's success week-to-week. And every week's different," said Sheppard. "Every week's going to call for certain things to change. Every week's going to call for different guys needed to step up depending on where the ball is focused on and so on and so forth. So, I don't want to say we're going to replicate anything. What I want to say is I definitely want to build on a lot of the positives that came from that game. And I just want to credit the players, man.
"That's the thing that gets lost in all that. People start to, 'Oh, what did you change? What did you do?' The players went out and executed and played at a high level and played at a high level like they expect to do every week. It just showed up in Arizona on a more consistent basis than it had the previous four weeks.”

title: Detroit Lions 2026 Week 7 Friday Injury Report: Two Questionable
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have released their official Week 7 injury designation report, ahead of their Week 7 contest against the Green Bay Packers.
According to the team, safety Brian Branch and offensive lineman Cade Mays were both ruled questionable.
Veteran Rock Ya-Sin, who was limited at practice on both Wednesday and Thursday, was a full participant on Friday and should be cleared to play against a division rival at Ford Field.
Ya-Sin does not have any injury designation this week and has been rehabbing from a hamstring injury that kept him out of action for the past few weeks.
Head coach Dan Campbell indicated they have a decent idea at this point of how much the team is going to play Branch and Mays in their first appearance of the the 2026 NFL season.
Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing was asked this week how the offense could settle in earlier and start a little faster, including the offensive line.
Additional NFL Insider Analysis: Odds Detroit Lions Defeat Green Bay Packers in Week 7
While Detroit's offense has been among the top scoring units in the NFL, there have been issues with three-and-outs, penalties and scoring early in games.
"Yeah, I think again, it's emphasized, it's stressed," said Petzing. "And at the end of the day, sometimes it's play calls. Sometimes it's execution. It's always a combination of both. And honestly, and I've said it here before, anytime we don't score, I'm a little irked whether it's the first drive of the game or the last drive of the game. title: Packers-Lions Prediction: Will Green Bay Beat Odds So It Can Beat Rivals?
full_text:
DETROIT – One of the biggest games of the season for the Green Bay Packers comes with one of the biggest scheduling mismatches imaginable.
The Packers are coming off a Sunday night home game. The Lions are coming off a Sunday at their homes with their bye week. So, Detroit – in a huge NFC North game, mind you, that could have playoff ramifications – has been given by the league a home game and a week of rest.
Will it matter? Here are our predictions.
Since the start of the 2020 season, teams with a home game after their bye are 63-41, according to Stathead. That’s an enormous advantage.
Will that alone decide the game? Probably not. But in a game between two quality teams – the Lions are 3.5-point favorites – it might not take much to be the tipping point. Eight consecutive games at Ford Field between the teams ended with a one-score differential; the last exception was in 2017, when Brett Hundley was the Packers’ quarterback.
Both teams are going to score points. A lot of points. The over/under of 55.5 points is the highest on the board at FanDuel.
The Lions on offense have been a well-oiled machine. It tallied 30 points in five of six games this season and is second in the league in scoring. Quarterback Jared Goff hasn’t thrown an interception all season. He is surrounded by probably the best quartet in the league with receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, running back Jahmyr Gibbs and tight end Sam LaPorta.
Green Bay’s defense was great last week against the Dak Prescott-led Cowboys passing attack, but it didn’t have to contend with a back like Gibbs, who is arguably the best in the league – especially at home.
The Packers have been hit and miss on offense – which is about what you’d expect for a team with a big-time quarterback and two big-play receivers but with an inconsistent offensive line and an unimaginably bad running game.
The matchup is favorable, though, because the Lions’ defense has been terrible. It ranks 30th in points allowed and 32nd in total defense. At its current clip, it will threaten the 2011 Packers as the worst pass defense in NFL history.
For the Lions, the best defense has been a good offense. They are 3-2 despite allowing 20 touchdowns. According to Stats Perform’s Opta data, they are the first team in NFL history to allow 20 offensive touchdowns and have a winning record through five games.
Ultimately, three big issues stand the Packers’ way.
One, they have struggled to protect Love. Well, the Lions lead the NFL in sacks even while playing one fewer game than most teams. Can Green Bay’s tackles overcome the noise to keep Aidan Hutchinson away from Love?
Two, they have struggled to pressure the quarterback at times. Goff is an elite quarterback when given time. As coach Matt LaFleur said this week, “It’s hard for a quarterback to throw when he’s on his back.” Can the Packers put Goff on his back enough?
And, finally, there’s this festering problem: The Packers have fatal flaws they haven’t solved. Love has been stymied by 19 drops; no other quarterback has more than 11. They lead the league in penalties and penalty yards. Love has faced the third-most pressures.
“The simple stuff, whether from scheme-wise or the understanding of what we’re trying to get done, when you have some mistakes that can lead to negative plays, that’s the stuff we got to clean up and be better at,” Love said.
It’s those things that will put the Packers at a disadvantage in every big game – no matter the location or scheduling quirk – until they get them fixed.
Ultimately, the team that makes the fewest mistakes will win. Based on the first five games, it’s hard to believe that will be the Packers.
Bill Huber’s Prediction: Lions 31, Packers 27.
The Packers have lost too many games like these in recent years, which have caused them to travel the long road in the postseason.
In 2024, they lost all but one division game, which played a significant factor in them being the seventh seed in the NFC playoffs. Last year’s late-season debacle in Chicago essentially sealed their fate that the wild-card meeting rematch would be at Soldier Field instead of the friendly confines of Lambeau Field.
Simply put, the Packers need to knock off the Lions on the road on Sunday to keep pace with those in front of them and remain in position to be a legitimate NFC North contender.
In a game where points should be scored in bunches, one mistake could be the difference. Who do you trust more to play clean and disciplined?
Dan Campbell's Lions or Matt LaFleur's Packers?
That, combined with the Lions being at home off a bye, gives them the nod.
Jacob’s Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 31

title: Ultimate Mismatch Is Among Three Reasons Why Packers Will Beat Lions
full_text:
DETROIT – The Green Bay Packers have won three consecutive games. Jordan Love and his receivers are humming, the defense has allowed 14 points or less in each game and confidence is high.
Can they keep it going on Sunday against the Detroit Lions? Yes, and here are three reasons why.
The Lions’ pass defense is almost impossibly bad. They are last in the NFL with 297.4 passing yards allowed per game. They are on pace to be the first team to ever allow 5,000 passing yards in a season.
The 2011 Packers allowed the most passing yards in NFL history with 299.8 per game. That team went 15-1 and had opponents in catch-up mode all season. There is some of that element involved with the Lions’ pass defense, too, with opponents knowing they must keep up with their high-powered offense.
But Rock-Ya Sin and D.J. Reed are vulnerable at cornerback. Not even a high-powered pass rush has helped; the Lions are 29th in opponent passer rating. The Lions will regain the services of premier safety Brian Branch following last year’s torn Achilles but are still without fellow safety Kerby Joseph, who led the league with nine interceptions in 2024.
On paper, Jordan Love and the Packers’ explosive passing attack could have a big day.
“They’re No. 1 in the league when it comes to that category, as far as big plays, the deep balls,” Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said. “It's why Jordan Love is special. He has one of the best deep balls I've seen. He flicks it 50 yards off his fingertips. It's very impressive. They have two of the most explosive vertical receivers in the game. It's a tremendous challenge for us and we understand what we're going into.”
Great year-over-year stat from @StatsPerform about Packers WR Matthew Golden is the jumping-off point on this feature on the team's breakout star. ⬇️ https://t.co/EsADb0e8gG
The “vertical receivers” are Christian Watson, who is fifth in the NFL with 538 receiving yards, third with 18.6 yards per catch and second with six touchdowns, and Matthew Golden, who is sixth with 501 yards, fifth with 16.7 yards per catch and tied for 13th with three touchdowns.
Combined, they are on pace for 2,943 yards and 25 touchdowns.
Entering Week 7, the Packers were third in the league with 24 completions of 20-plus yards, just one behind the league leaders. Watson entered the week tied for the lead with 10 with Golden next with nine. The Lions, on the other hand, were third in the league with 23 completions of 20-plus yards allowed.
The Lions will challenge the Packers in terms of their pass rush – they lead the NFL in sacks despite playing only five games – and the environment at Ford Field. But Love has shredded the Aidan Hutchinson-led Lions defense in his three road starts. He’s had passer ratings of greater than 111 in each game with eight touchdowns and zero interceptions with the Packers scoring 31, 31 and 29 points.
“It’s a good environment over there,” Love said. “They definitely got a loud crowd and it’s a tough place to play, but we’ve had the right mindset in the past. These NFC North games, you got to go out there and win, and we’ve done some good things, and I think it just comes down to us going out there and winning the matchups.
“We know them well. Their scheme has changed a little bit but, for the most part, a lot of the personnel, a lot of the calls are similar. So, yeah, it just comes down to figuring out what their plan is going to be on Sunday, what they want to do and go from there. But we’ve found ways to make plays and I feel like we’ve had good games. I don’t think there’s any rhyme or reason, but we got to do that again Sunday.”
The Packers have the worst rushing attack in the NFL and one of the worst in the history of mankind.
Finally, help has arrived with Josh Jacobs off the exempt list and ready to go for Sunday. His vision and toughness should make an immediate difference, even if it’s in a limited role.
“You can't defend all of it, so you better pick your poison and what you think means the most to you to stop,” Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters this week. “We can't let this run game get going and they're going to try to establish the run. He's done that every week and nothing's going to change. I would anticipate Jacobs is going to be back. He brings another element to them.”
The Lions are 20th with 4.25 yards allowed per carry, so there should be opportunities – though it didn’t matter against the Cowboys’ worst-in-the-league run defense last week.
“They're probably over there just like we are about BB (Brian Branch), to be honest with you,” Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said this week. “It's kind of the same for them. Everybody's asking, 'How much is he going?' Listen, whenever you could gain an All-Pro player back, obviously, that's going to boost everything.”
The run game will be huge to open up the play-action attack, where the Packers can get the chunk gains the offense has depended on this season. The Cowboys weren’t buying what the Packers were trying to sell last week, so Love was just 1-of-7 in that phase last week after he threw for more than 240 yards vs. Chicago.
From that perspective, Jacobs could change everything in providing a running threat the Lions can’t just ignore.
“If they're able to get that thing really lit up and going now, it's problematic,” Campbell said.
Detroit’s defense is all-around horrendous, though the return of Brian Branch will help and the pass rush ranks among the best in the league in terms of sacks (first) and pass-rush win rate (third).
The situational stats are green lights for the Packers. Here is the tale of the tape for Detroit’s defense:
On third down, the Lions are 30th. They’re also 30th in fourth down. In the red zone, Detroit ranks 31st with an opponent touchdown rate of 81 percent. It hasn’t had a single stop in goal-to-go situations.
Green Bay’s offense isn’t very good in any of those categories – 24th on third down, 12th on fourth down, 23rd in the red zone and 24th in goal-to-go – but an improved running game and the perimeter mismatches should swing this in the Packers’ favor.
“I still think they got some good players over there, good DBs, and we’ll see what their scheme is going to be for the game,” Love said. “You look at the film, they’ve mixed it up in a couple of their games, whether they want to play zone, whether they want to play man, whether they want to bring pressure.
“We’ll see. No matter who we’re playing, I always like our guys and our matchups, and we create some mismatches just with our speed and who we got on the outside.”

title: Packers Make Big Roster Move, And It’s Not Just Activating Josh Jacobs
full_text:
DETROIT – The Green Bay Packers got by with four defensive linemen for last week’s win against the Dallas Cowboys. They’ll have five available for Sunday’s game against the Detroit Lions.
The Packers activated defensive tackle Jordon Riley from injured reserve on Saturday.
The Packers, as expected, added running back Josh Jacobs to the active roster and signed receiver Coleman Owen to the active roster from the practice squad. Those moves, as reported on Saturday morning by Packers On  SI, are detailed here . Plus, they made one practice-squad elevation; more on that in a moment.
The Packers have only 50 players on the roster, so they can add three today. Here's the start. https://t.co/Mc3bXTpmS7
Here is our weekly look at the roster moves.
Riley, who is coming off a torn Achilles, will provide depth where depth had evaporated with Warren Brinson, Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Ford on injured reserve.
“I knew just sticking to the process this day was going to come,” Riley said this week. “I know those days where it’s like, ‘Ah, man, we doing the same thing over and over’ and the days that I got over that hump, and each day I would get better and better.
“Those are the days I look at and I was proud. I don’t know how I handled it. Those are the days I think about where if it wasn’t me sticking to it every day, I wouldn’t be here at this point. So, that’s how I feel about it.”
Riley, who is listed at 6-foot-5 and 338 pounds but tips the scales at a bit less than that following his rehab, was signed late last season to add a stouter presence against the run. He delivered four quality performances before sustaining a torn Achilles in the second-to-last game of the season against Baltimore.
“Big, stout, physical D-lineman. Exactly what we need,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Friday. “He brings great size. I love his energy, his attitude – it’s very contagious. The work he puts in does not go unnoticed by anybody. Excited for when he gets the opp to go out there and play.”
The 28-year-old was a seventh-round pick by the Giants in 2023 and played in 21 games with five starts during his first two seasons. He was on their practice squad when the Packers signed him last year.
When Riley was injured last season, the Packers brought back Ford. Now that Ford is injured, Riley will fill the void.
It’s a key role. Green Bay’s defense was 0.39 yards per carry better when Ford was on the field compared to when he was on the sideline.
Riley will join a defensive front that includes Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks, Chris McClellan and Anthony Campbell.
“It’s just been good, man,” Riley said of the last two weeks. “I’ve just been taking it one day at a time and just soaking it all in really. Being coached and messing up, and finally getting to mess up, get coached up. So, it’s been good.”
Riley was limited participation at all six practices the past two weeks.
“Body’s feeling great, man,” Riley said. “The body’s feeling surprisingly where I thought it was going to be. It’s just every day getting better and better. As close as you get, it’s feeling better and better. I’m in a good spot.”
Riley hasn’t played in a game since Dec. 27, so Sunday’s game will mark his return after almost a 10-month layoff. He said the technique has been “like riding a bike.” In fact, he said he’s in a “better spot” than he thought he would be at this point.
“It’s really just technical for me,” he said. “I think mentally I was already locked in in the playbook. There’s walkthroughs, OTAs, you got training camp, so a lot of times when I couldn’t be at those, in those walkthroughs, I was mentally in the back taking those reps.
“We got good coaching. So, getting that too on the side, stuff like that, that really helped out. So, when I came in, I wasn’t really worried about the play, it was how can I play this block? How can I set ourself in this call? As far as like schematic, technical execution, those reps was already banked mentally.”
Riley will have a key role against the Lions. While they are a modest 13th in rushing yards per game and 11th in rushing yards per carry, Jahmyr Gibbs is fifth in the NFL with 504 rushing yards even though the Lions have played only four games.
“I want to come in and help these guys stop the run,” Riley said. “Obviously, we’re doing a good job as of now and continue to help in any way I can, whether it’s blocking a field goal or anything. Anything. But the main thing is stopping the run so these guys can go rush.”
With linebackers Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin out with injuries, meaning Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper will start on defense rather than being stalwarts on defense, the Packers for a second consecutive week elevated Arron Mosby from the practice squad.
He had an assisted tackle in his season debut last week against Dallas.
“I think that’s what’s great about the practice squad is it’s not a 53-man roster anymore. It’s a 70-man roster” special teams coordinator Cam Achord said this week of the experience provided by Mosby, among others.
“Those guys understand that each week you’re a sickness or an injury away from playing. Obviously, it’s an injury that’s long term, you’re on the active roster. It makes those guys at practice, they got to know the game plan. They got to know what’s going on.”
