title: Forget the NFC West, Can the Rams Even Make the Playoffs?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are 2-4 entering Week 7 and it can be argued that Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders is a must-win situation. A win against the Arizona Cardinals last week would have put the Rams in second place in the NFC West, right behind the San Francisco 49ers. Losing that game put them at 0-2 in the NFC West and in last place. At this point, it’s highly unlikely the Rams win the division, especially with the 49ers at 6-0.
Entering Week 7, the Rams have a four percent chance to win the NFC West. However, the playoffs are still within reach. Cue Jim Mora’s “Playoffs?! Playoffs?! You want to talk about playoffs?! I just hope we can win a game!” rant from November of 2000.
Happy 19th anniversary to the Jim Mora 'Playoffs' rant.  You shall be in our lives forever🙏 pic.twitter.com/iKk41mlvog
That’s where the Rams are at right now. It seems ridiculous to talk about the playoffs because they really need to just focus on winning a game. After losing 18-16 to the Cardinals and suffering the amount of injuries they have, the Rams simply need to focus on taking things one week at a time.
Still, that doesn’t mean that we can’t look ahead a little bit. Back in 2023, the Rams came back from a 3-6 start to make the playoffs. In 2024, they came back from a 1-4 start to make the postseason. Making the playoffs isn't completely out of the realm of possibility. The Rams just need to start stringing some wins together.
As it stands, the Rams have a 39 percent chance to make the playoffs via The Athletic . ESPN’s model has them slightly lower at 33 percent. While the Rams are playing an AFC opponent on Sunday, a win is critical to their playoff chances simply because they can’t afford many more losses.
A loss to the Raiders would put the Rams at a 27 percent chance to make the playoffs. Winning on Sunday makes it a near coin-flip at 45 percent. It’s very possible that we are looking at this game as the one that saved or ruined the Rams’ season.
To make the postseason, the Rams may need to finish 11-6 or 10-7. That means they can afford just two or three more losses over their final 11 games. They still have to play the Kansas City Chiefs, Seattle Seahawks twice, the San Francisco 49ers, and the Green Bay Packers. It’s likely the Rams will lose two of those games at minimum.
Looking at ESPN’s model , the biggest threats to the Rams’ playoff chances right now are the second- through fourth-place teams in the NFC North and the Seattle Seahawks. The good news is that the Rams will play the Packers after the bye week and then play the Seahawks twice in the final three weeks of the season.
Unfortunately, the timing may not work in the Rams’ favor, as the Packers have bounced back from their early-season struggles. While the Seahawks are in a rut, they may snap out of it by Week 16.
The Packers, Bears, Lions, Vikings, and Seahawks will all be teams that the Rams will be watching closely. There will likely only be one team to come out of the NFC South and NFC East divisions. However, the NFC North and NFC West could provide multiple playoff teams.
As it stands, the Rams’ most likely record is between 8-9 and 10-7. Since the NFL expanded to a 17-game format in 2021, only the Seattle Seahawks in 2024 missed the playoffs at 10-7. That’s what the Rams are looking at right now with the overall strength of the NFC. An 8-9 team has never made the playoffs as a wild card, and if the Rams were to go 9-8, they would certainly need help. They may need help at 10-7.
Realistically, the Rams are hoping they can finish ahead of the Seahawks in the NFC West and that either the Vikings collapse after starting 5-0 or the Packers lose their form again. There’s very little confidence right now that the Rams can string wins together, but the schedule has set up for it. If the Rams can win each of their next five games, that alone would increase their playoff chances to 77 percent. That would allow the Rams to lose to the Chiefs, the 49ers, and the Seahawks once and still finish 10-7. If that’s the way things play out, the Rams would have an 89 percent chance at the postseason.
They would obviously need certain things to go their way as well. Given the Rams’ poor record in the division, they would not be able to tie with the Seahawks. They would need the Seahawks to finish worse than 10-7 or take the season series and win both games in Week 16 and 18.
It seems likely with their schedules that the Bears and Lions finish with 11 wins. That leaves the Vikings and Packers as teams to monitor.
With the Vikings, they could lose four of their next five games. They play the Lions, Packers, and 49ers on the road and then also play the Bills. The Patriots on the road will be tough and the Panthers have looked good as well. It’s possible the Rams could use some help in later weeks. However, if the Vikings finish 10-7, the Rams would be seeded ahead of them.
Finally, the Rams’ game against the Packers after the bye is a must-win. If the Rams lose that game, it would be very difficult to come back from that. Assuming they win that game, it's possible the Packers could finish 10-7 and behind the Rams in the standings.
When all is said and done, we could be looking at: 1. 49ers 2. Bears 3. Panthers 4. NFC East Winner 5. Lions 6. Rams 7. Packers/Vikings
That would put the Rams in the playoffs and a trip to Carolina in the Wild Card round for a second consecutive season. Given the Rams’ current situation, they would very likely need to win three road playoff games to make the Super Bowl, but if they get healthy and find their stride, they would be a rare team with a good chance of doing that.
The Rams have come back from early-season deficits in the past. That’s certainly not the path they wanted to take this year, but it’s where they find themselves. Still, they need to show they can consistently win games. The Rams may be better than their record says they are, but they are 2-4.
🚨 NFL FRAUD METER - Week 6 🏈 The 6-0 49ers aren't frauds The 5-0 Vikings are... pic.twitter.com/f2gjARxzCJ
In 2024, it was a win against the Raiders in Week 7 that sparked a 9-3 finish. The Rams will hope a win against the Raiders in Week 7 this year does the same. The year before, the Rams lost three straight before a win against the Seahawks sparked them to a 7-1 finish.
However, the difference in both cases was that the Rams were getting healthy and coming off their bye week. At this point in the season, the Rams couldn’t be more hurt at key positions, and they don’t have their bye until Week 11.
Still, Sunday’s game against the Raiders is important. If the Rams are going to turn it around, it starts on Sunday. We can talk about playoff scenarios all we want, but none of it matters if the Rams can’t start winning games. The margins are already small and they get narrower with every loss. If they can get to the bye week with some momentum, the season could look very different. At 2-4, however, they can no longer afford to keep waiting for things to turn around.

title: Rams Week 7 Injury Report: Puka Nacua, Trent McDuffie Questionable vs. Raiders
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams could be without wide receiver Puka Nacua on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders. Nacua was officially listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report after injuring his calf on Thursday . Also listed as questionable was cornerback Trent McDuffie, who did not practice on Friday. Additionally, linebacker Nate Landman has officially been ruled out.
Nacua was a surprise addition to the injury report on Thursday after he left practice with an apparent calf injury. He did not practice on Friday and will be a game-time decision. According to NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport , Nacua’s calf injury is only minor, but his status is up in the air for Sunday’s game. Rams head coach Sean McVay talked about Nacua’s injury in more detail in his media availability.
“I don't think he knows exactly when it occurred,” said McVay. “You look at it and there's a little minor thing in there. Felt it where he wasn't able to have some of the power and full explosion. Just noticed it, but I don't think he was aware of any sort of specific play that led to it.”
If the Rams are without Nacua, they will rely on depth players such as Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and Jordan Whittington. The Rams would also likely lean heavily on their tight ends and running backs. Earlier this season without Nacua, Williams had six receptions against the Denver Broncos and became a big part of the passing game.
Landman being ruled out would imply that he didn’t pass through the concussion protocol this week. With Landman unable to go, McVay noted on Friday that the team would bring up linebacker Eric Kendricks from the practice squad, who they signed two weeks ago.
“He's got a veteran presence, real good concept understanding, can play a variety of schemes,” McVay said. “Has had success in a variety of schemes, understands football from a big-picture perspective, has a good vibe about himself.”
McDuffie missing his fourth consecutive practice with a groin injury certainly isn’t a good sign. McVay didn’t provide much of an update on McDuffie, only that he was questionable. McDuffie did work off to the side to an extent during the media portion of practice.
Rams CB Trent McDuffie working with training staff. He is questionable for game against Raiders. pic.twitter.com/993xUzHHPT
The Raiders will be relatively healthy heading into Sunday’s game against the Rams. After being limited on Wednesday with hamstring and calf injuries, tight end Brock Bowers was a full participant on Thursday and Friday and was not given an injury designation. Tonka Hemingway was also cleared.
With that said, the Raiders will be without wide receiver Dont’e Thornton and tight end Carter Runyon. Running back Mike Washington’s status is also up in the air for Sunday. Washington has been used alongside Ashton Jeanty this season and has averaged 4.9 yards per carry. He did not participate in practice the last two days and is listed as questionable.
The Rams were already going to be shorthanded heading into Week 7, but the uncertainty surrounding Nacua and McDuffie only adds to their challenges. With several starters already sidelined, the Rams will need their depth to step up in a significant way if they're going to get back in the win column.

title: Rams vs. Raiders Prediction: Week 7 Preview, Key Matchups, and Players to Watch
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 7 desperately needing a win. After losing to the Arizona Cardinals last week, the Rams are at risk of dropping to 2-5 and are set to take on a Las Vegas Raiders team that is much better than in past years.
It’s fair to call Sunday a must-win game for the Rams. A loss to the Raiders would drop their already slim playoff chances even lower. Given where the Rams are, they can’t afford many more losses. At some point, they need to find some consistency and string together some wins, which won’t be easy with all of their injuries.
The Raiders are 3-3 and have lost three games in a row. With that said, two of their three losses are by three points, including last week’s 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Much like the Cardinals, the Raiders have been feisty this season and quarterback Kirk Cousins has played well. This isn’t a Raiders team that the Rams can afford to overlook.
Through six weeks, the Raiders’ defense ranks 26th in defensive EPA per play, success rate, and points per game allowed. Despite the injury to Davante Adams , the Rams should be able to move the ball. However, the same could’ve been said last week against the Cardinals, and the Rams managed just 16 points. The Raiders are better defending the run than the pass. This season, they are allowing the second-highest average depth of target and 13 passing touchdowns. Matthew Stafford should be able to find success.
With Puka Nacua as the Rams’ only legitimate threat at wide receiver, how the Raiders cover him will be something to watch. That becomes even more important if Nacua is unable to play and the Rams have to rely on Konata Mumpfield.
However, the Rams need to protect Matthew Stafford and keep him clean in the pocket. While McClendon has allowed a 6.8 percent pressure rate this season, Crosby has generated 25 pressures when facing right tackles, the second-most in the NFL. The Raiders also like to drop Crosby into coverage from that spot, which will also be something for the Rams to look out for.
The Raiders and head coach Klint Kubiak will be plenty familiar with Chris Shula and the Rams’ defense. Kubiak comes over from the Seattle Seahawks and was previously with the San Francisco 49ers in 2023. The Raiders have generated the 14th-most yards after the catch, while the Rams have allowed the most. Kubiak is going to dare the Rams’ defensive backs and linebackers to come up and tackle.
The Rams have done well covering tight ends this season. Last week, they held Trey McBride to seven receptions for only 53 yards. It wasn’t his lowest output of the season, but the Rams still managed to keep him in check. Brock Bowers will be another challenge. Bowers adds an explosive element to the Raiders’ offense. If Lake and the Rams can keep Bowers in check, they’ll force the Raiders to win with Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor at wide receiver.
Despite the Rams losing to the Cardinals in Week 6, playing on the road, and sitting at 2-4, they are favored to beat the Raiders. Still, it’s hard to have any confidence in that happening on Sunday. Even without Adams, the Rams should be able to move the ball on offense, but they have to be able to finish drives. Given the injuries on defense, the Rams may need to score 30 points to win. This is a winnable game despite the injuries, but the Rams haven’t shown enough consistency. Prediction: Raiders 27, Rams 21

title: Rams Get Encouraging Puka Nacua Injury Update, But Week 7 Status Remains Uncertain
full_text:
The injuries just continue to pile up for the Los Angeles Rams. During Thursday’s practice, wide receiver Puka Nacua left early and was listed as limited with a calf injury . While details weren’t immediately available, NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported on Friday morning that the injury is believed to be minor.
“My understanding is, after tests, it was more minor than anything else. I wouldn’t say precautionary, because it’s not nothing, but at least not a significant injury,” said Rapoport. What that doesn’t tell us is whether or not Puka Nacua would be able to play.”
From @GMFB : #Rams WR Puka Nacua suffered what is believed to be a minor calf injury, while the #Colts will have a decision to make on RB Jonathan Taylor. pic.twitter.com/lF6yuIEo9I
Rapoport mentioned that it’s safe to say that Nacua’s status is up in the air for Sunday. After placing a handful of players such as wide receiver Davante Adams and defensive lineman Kobie Turner on injured reserve this week , the Rams were hoping to go into Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders as healthy as possible.
The Rams took significant hits on defense this week as Turner was placed on injured reserve along with Poona Ford. Additionally, cornerback Trent McDuffie has not practiced at all this week after injuring his groin last Thursday.
Remaining as healthy as they can on the offensive side of the ball as Adams and Terrance Ferguson recover from injuries will be essential to keeping the offense competitive over the next several weeks.
Nacua has already missed two games this season with a groin/hip injury. When Nacua was out, it was Adams who stepped up in his place. With Adams set to miss the next six weeks, the Rams will be relying heavily on Nacua.
If Nacua were to miss Sunday’s game, it would put the Rams’ offense in a very difficult spot. The offense would likely rely on Tutu Atwell, who previously stepped up in place of Nacua in 2024. Players like Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington would be asked to step up as well, and the Rams could look at rookie CJ Daniels. Even with Nacua out, it wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams bring up Brennan Presley from the practice squad.
The Rams will get information on Nacua later on Friday when the team reports to practice. Nacua will unlikely be a full participant, but head coach Sean McVay should at least be able to provide some more details.
Given the Rams' injury luck over the last few weeks, they can certainly be relieved that Nacua’s calf injury doesn't appear to be serious. However, while the news surrounding Nacua is encouraging, his availability for Sunday remains uncertain. Given the inconsistencies on offense and Adams' absence, the Rams need Nacua available as they look to avoid dropping to 2-5.

title: Rams Midweek Report: Sean McVay Faces His Toughest Test, Myles Garrett Uncertainty, Wide Receiver Trade Targets
full_text:
Throughout the Sean McVay era, there have been some difficult seasons and slow starts for the Los Angeles Rams. Despite all of the adversity in past seasons, what the Rams are going through now may be his toughest challenge yet.
In 2020, the Rams started 4-1 and had the No. 1 defense in the NFL. However, the relationship between McVay and quarterback Jared Goff hit a breaking point. After McVay broke out in a “run it back” chant at the Super Bowl parade, the Rams went 5-12 and the head coach almost walked away. The Rams started 3-6 in a “re-tool” year, and McVay clawed that team back to make the playoffs. When the Rams started 1-4 in 2024, McVay got that team out of its funk and won the NFC West.
There have been a lot of trials, tribulations, and moments of adversity for McVay. However, what the Rams have gone through in 2026 through six weeks has been mentally exhausting. This is a team that entered the season as Super Bowl favorites. They traded for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie to help get them over the top.
However, with each passing week, the Rams seem to hit a new low. The issues that have plagued this roster over the last two years continue to haunt them. Against the Buffalo Bills, they were a blocked field goal away from their most impressive win of the season. This is a roster that should be 4-2 instead of 2-4. But that’s not where this team is.
Over the last two years, this is a team that continues to find new ways to lose. The heartbreaking losses continued to mount following Sunday’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals. After the game, running back Kyren Williams seemed to throw shade at his role when asked why the offense lacked energy, saying, “I can't tell you, bro. Probably because I'm not out there.”
This isn’t to say that McVay is on the verge of losing the locker room or anything to that extreme. With that said, he needs to find a way to bring this locker room together. Williams’ comments, for as much as the Rams may want to brush them aside, are a sign of the team imploding from within. How the Rams have lost in combination with the pressure they faced coming into the season would be mentally draining on any team.
Entering Week 7, the Rams have hit the injury bug hard. They lost wide receiver Davante Adams for 6-10 weeks and defensive lineman Kobie Turner also ended up on injured reserve . Puka Nacua hurt his calf and was limited in Thursday’s practice.
Whatever timeline the Rams entered in which it’s as if they walked under a ladder once a day for an entire year, it’s with certainty that they want out. McVay has proven throughout the last decade that he’s one of the best leaders in the NFL. His leadership will be put to the test if he’s going to reel this team back in for another comeback.
Following the game against the Denver Broncos, the Rams placed tight end Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve. The next week on the Coach McVay show, McVay told J.B. Long that Ferguson would be ready to go after the four weeks. “Bummer for Ferg, man. But he’ll be back, he’ll be ready to go after those four weeks,” said McVay at the time.
That four-week period would have placed Ferguson’s return in Week 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers. While McVay didn’t specify an exact timeline, It didn’t sound as if Ferguson would be out past the four-week injured reserve period.
For an offense that has lacked speed and explosiveness out of 13 personnel, Ferguson’s return would certainly be welcomed. McVay answered questions on Ferguson on Monday.
“No updates on Terrance, he's just continuing to rehab,” McVay said. “I don't have any sort of imminent return for him quite yet.”
On Tuesday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter noted that Ferguson is not expected to be ready next week. According to Schefter, Ferguson’s recovery will take time. That doesn’t sound as if Ferguson's return is imminent. It wouldn’t be surprising if the Rams’ tight end was out until the bye week in Week 11.
The Myles Garrett injury saga continues to linger . After Garrett underwent arthroscopic knee surgery, he was given a six-week timeline. However, at the time, it was said that Garrett was determined to beat that. Later, it was reported that the Rams were hopeful that Garrett could return last week against the Cardinals, but a return in Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders was more realistic. The six-week timeline was a worst-case scenario.
Earlier this week, ESPN’s Dan Graziano slipped in a nugget on Garrett’s potential return in his weekly notebook. While reporting that the Rams would explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver, Graziano also noted that Garrett could likely be out for “another two or three weeks at least.”
If Garrett is out another two or three weeks, that would make the six week timeline a seven or eight week timeline. Much like Ferguson, it would not be surprising if Garrett remained sidelined until after the bye week.
On the final drive against the Cardinals in Week 6, Davante Adams pulled up with a hamstring injury. After the game, it was revealed that Adams had ruptured his hamstring and would be out 6-10 weeks.
According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, Adams is set to undergo a procedure to repair his hamstring by Neal ElAttrache in Los Angeles. Fowler reported that the hope is for Adams to return on the front-end of that 6-10 week timeframe and as close to the post-Week 11 bye as possible.
Rams WR Davante Adams will undergo a procedure to repair his ruptured hamstring via renowned Dr Neal ElAttrache, per source. Adams hopes to return on the front end of the 6-10 week timeframe, as close to the post-Week-11 bye as possible, the source said. pic.twitter.com/6V6v0xglhS
McVay said on Wednesday that Adams hadn’t had surgery yet and they were still figuring out details.
“I think they’re going to give it a couple of days and figure out exactly when is the best time. It’s more of a cleanup type of procedure,” said McVay. “There is a surgery, but it's a cleanup. I'm not a doctor so I don't want to speak out of turn, but it will be something that'll get cleaned up.”
Rams Hall of Fame running back Marshall Faulk has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease, according to CBS Sports . Faulk has been dealing with the disease for 18 months. Faulk mentioned in an interview that he’s in a good place.
"The little tremors that I get, you know, they are what they are. I just pay attention to my gait, you know, while I walk, when I'm working out, my ability to balance. It's still where it is,” said Faulk. “I'm functioning. I'm good. You know, I just, I think I caught it early. I'm in a good place."
Faulk is third on the Rams’ all-time rushing list and is tied with Todd Gurley for the most rushing touchdowns in franchise history. The Rams traded for Faulk prior to the 1999 season and he played a key role in the Greatest Show on Turf. Faulk retired with the Rams in 2005 and was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2011.
While the Rams didn’t lose because of the unnecessary roughness call, it almost guaranteed that they would lose. The Rams had already jumped offsides on the play and the 21-yard completion put the Cardinals just outside of field goal range. The following night, Fred Warner was initially flagged for unnecessary roughness for a more egregious hit and it was picked up.
According to Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer , the NFL believes the officials did get the call right on Wallace. However, it also thought that the Warner flag should have stayed. The issue remains the league's lack of consistency in officiating and its use of replay assist.
There’s no doubt that Matthew Stafford hasn’t played well. He played well against the Buffalo Bills, but in the week before against the Philadelphia Eagles and most of the game last week, he did not. It’s true that Stafford gave the Rams the lead at the end of the game against the Cardinals. The offense was also stagnant and didn’t start moving the ball until under three minutes to play in the game.

title: Rams Trading for Wide Receiver Brian Thomas Jr. Would Be a Mistake They Can't Afford
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams may be 2-4, but that doesn’t mean that general manager Les Snead is simply going to sit back and wave the white flag. On Wednesday, it was reported by ESPN’s Dan Graziano that the Rams will at least e xplore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver in the wake of Davante Adams being placed on injured reserve.
It shouldn’t be a total surprise that the Rams aren’t just going to call it a season. Back in 2019, with the team at 3-3, the Rams made moves for Austin Corbett and Jalen Ramsey. Both players were key pieces in the team’s Super Bowl run in 2021.
When the Rams were 3-3 in 2022, they were close to trading for Christian McCaffrey and Brian Burns. However, they were outbid for McCaffrey, and the Panthers weren’t ready to part ways with Burns at that time.
Very few would be surprised if the Rams made a move. However, if they do make a trade, it needs to be the right one . A popular name that has surfaced is Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.
Thomas Jr. would be a perfect replacement for Adams as the team’s “X” receiver and was originally drafted in the first round. He also plays for the Jaguars, whose general manager, James Gladstone, has a relationship with Snead. While an exciting name, trading for Thomas would also only dig the Rams into a deeper hole.
Sometimes, the best moves are the ones that aren’t made. That was likely the case when the Rams didn’t acquire McCaffrey and the Panthers said no on Burns. The Rams went 5-12 in 2022 and the 2023 NFL Draft played a large role in the team’s quick turnaround.
There’s nothing to confirm that the Rams have interest in Thomas. In fact, McVay said on Wednesday that the team isn’t even looking at wide receiver replacements.
“That's not something that we've talked about right now,” said McVay. “We have some depth on our roster. Maybe we talked about the practice squad, but not anything externally.”
Whether McVay was honest in what he told the media can certainly be argued. However, there has been speculation about wide receiver options the Rams could be interested in, with Thomas being near the top of the list.
There’s no doubt that Thomas would fit the type of player the Rams typically target in trades. The moves for Sammy Watkins, Austin Corbett, Dante Fowler Jr., Jalen Ramsey, and Kevin Dotson were all players who had fallen out of favor with their previous teams.
Per Brian Thomas Jr.'s profile via @RecepPerception 🟣 72% success rate on "go" routes 👀 🟡Down on 1st contact on 48% of “in space” attempts 🟡72.7% contested catch rate and 2 dropped passes Would not be shocked if Rams took BTJ at 19 as an Atwell replacement. pic.twitter.com/fLcIbbZb4T
Thomas played just 21.1 percent of the Jaguars’ offensive snaps in Week 6 and doesn’t have a reception on five targets in the last two games. After a promising rookie season in which he had 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns on 87 receptions, he has just 57 receptions for 812 yards and three touchdowns since.
Ever since the Jaguars moved on from Doug Pederson and hired Liam Coen, he simply hasn’t been the same player. Given that evidence, it’s worth questioning his fit since Coen and McVay come from the same offensive coaching tree. The schemes are very similar.
Over the last two years, Thomas Jr. has ranked last in adjusted catch percentage via FTN Fantasy. Adjusted catch percentage is the rate of catchable targets converted into a catch. Among players with at least 15 targets this season, his 22.2 percent drop-rate is the highest in the NFL. Last season, he also ranked inside the top-5 in drop-rate at 9.1 percent. Thomas’ targeted success rate of 47.3 percent over the last two years ranks 78th out of 116 qualifying receivers. Much like Konata Mumpfield, Thomas struggles at the catchpoint.
Matt Harmon of Yahoo Sports and founder of Reception Perception, which focuses on charting wide receivers, gave Thomas a pass for 2025 in his offseason profile .
“Brian Thomas Jr.’s second season was a frustrating one. It included both dips in his play across the board in isolation and a role that continued to get scaled back as the season went on until his final profile looked merely that of a low-volume X-receiver,” wrote Harmon. “He’s a good press and man-beater who wins both on the vertical routes and helps clear space for his teammates. If he simply maintains this level of deployment and success as a route runner, while cleaning up his drops and contested-catch rate, he’d be a good and useful starting X.”
However, we’re now one-third of the way into 2026, and it’s been much of the same. It’s possible that Thomas’ rookie year was the exception and what we’ve seen the last 1.5 years is the norm. This isn’t to say that the Rams couldn’t get the most out of Thomas or that a change of scenery couldn’t be beneficial. However, it’s also a massive risk, and arguably too much of a risk that the Rams can’t afford.
After just one 1,000-yard season, the Rams traded for Sammy Watkins in 2017. The Rams traded a second-round pick and EJ Gaines for Watkins and a sixth-round pick. Watkins had 593 yards for the Rams and was not brought back the following year.
Earlier this season, the Houston Texans traded a second and seventh-round pick for Marvin Harrison Jr. and a sixth-round pick. Harrison Jr. has never had more than 900 receiving yards in a season.
Unlike Watkins and Harrison Jr., Thomas wasn’t taken inside the top five of his draft class. Still, he’s a former first-round pick and has more production than Harrison and Watkins had. His price point likely starts with a second-round pick unless the Jaguars are desperate to get rid of him, which doesn’t appear to be the case.
Looking at the 2027 NFL Draft, the Rams already don’t have a first or third-round pick. If they were to move off of the second-round pick, they wouldn’t draft until the fourth round. Given the state of the roster and pending free agents, the Rams may need their second-round pick to add young, cheap talent to replenish the roster.
While the Baltimore Ravens gave up a 2028 second-round pick for Cam Jurgens, the Rams don’t have a 2028 second-round pick to give up. Considering their current roster situation, they also aren’t in a position to trade away a 2028 first-round pick.
The Rams may believe that adding a wide receiver can help turn their season around. At the same time, it needs to be one that fits their price point. The Rams got Kevin Dotson for a late-round pick swap and Austin Corbett for a fifth-round pick. A fourth-round pick may not get a flashy name like Thomas, but it could still get them what they need.
This is a front office that has already invested significant resources into building this roster, and the results have been disappointing. Doubling down by sacrificing another valuable draft pick for a receiver who has struggled for the better part of two seasons would only compound the problem.

title: Myles Garrett's Uncertain Status Raises Bigger Questions About the Rams' Blockbuster Trade
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams traded for edge rusher Myles Garrett this offseason , it was thought that he would be the missing piece and help lead the team to the Super Bowl. Garrett was coming off a 2025 season in which he won NFL Defensive Player of the Year and broke the single-season sack record.
Over the past few seasons, the Rams have been rebuilding the defense. After moving on from Leonard Floyd, Bobby Wagner, and Jalen Ramsey, along with Aaron Donald's retirement, the Rams essentially tore the kitchen down to the studs and rebuilt it.
They added some pieces that simply allowed them to get by, such as Ahkello Witherspoon and Darious Williams at cornerback, but they also found strong foundational pieces in players like Kobie Turner and Byron Young. Braden Fiske had proven some value on the defensive line as well. While the Rams still cut some corners, going cheap at linebacker, they had their star centerpiece in Jared Verse.
This past offseason, the Rams looked to complete the rebuild project on defense. They traded for cornerback Trent McDuffie and signed Jaylen Watson to finish the kitchen cupboards. Everything seemed complete until they arguably got greedy.
They had a perfectly good working fridge in Verse. It had plenty of space to work with and had an ice maker. While it may not have been perfect, it was still a high-quality fridge.
In June, Les Snead took a walk through the fridge section at Home Depot when a salesperson on the floor, let's call him Andrew Berry, caught his attention. Snead didn’t need a new fridge, but if he traded in his old one, he could get the Myles Garrett model with all the bells and whistles for a great price. It was a high-end model with commercial-grade engineering and precision climate control. You could control everything from your phone. This was the piece that would bring the entire kitchen together.
While everybody was excited for the new fridge, they were also disappointed to see the old one go. Earlier this offseason, Trent McDuffie went on Bussin’ With The Boys and described the vibe in the locker room after the team acquired Garrett.
“Guys weren't even excited excited, knowing you have Myles Garrett coming,” McDuffie said. “I heard the news, I started smiling. I looked around and I was like, ‘Oh, we’re not like, yeah!’ Everyone was like 'Whoa, hold on. J-Verse? You're going to let him go?'”
Back in August, Byron Young was asked about the trade. “That was unfortunate. It's part of business and it's something that definitely did hit me pretty hard,” said Young. “Building that relationship and friendship with him. That was a brother to me. Still a brother.”
Young wasn’t the only player to voice some disappointment. Braden Fiske also said at the time that his initial reaction was disappointment. That hit pretty hard pretty quick,” said Fiske. “My first instinct isn’t, ‘Oh, s---. We got Myles Garrett.’ My first instinct is like, ‘Oh, s---. We lost Jared. That really sucks.’”
Verse was the heart of the defense. He certainly had his deficiencies, but his presence and impact on the defense and locker room as a whole couldn’t be measured. The NFL isn’t a Madden video game or fantasy football where trading big-time players doesn’t reverberate through a team. There are real human relationships and connections to consider.
This isn’t the first time that general manager Les Snead has traded a player. Back in 2021, the Rams traded Jared Goff for Matthew Stafford. With that said, that trade felt different. Most of the team likely understood that they had reached a ceiling with Goff. That doesn’t mean there wasn’t disappointment, but there was at least some understanding that they had hit a ceiling.
That doesn’t appear to have been the same vibe when the Rams moved on from Verse. Trading away Verse accelerated his development timeline to closer match the Rams' championship window . However, where the argument could be made the Goff was holding the offense back in 2020, that couldn't be said about Verse and the defense.
The core of the defense had been through a lot together.In 2024, they experienced the divisional-round loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. Last season, they all came up short together in the NFC Championship game. The Rams built that unit through the draft and it was a tight-knit group.
When the Rams first acquired Garrett, everything appeared to be working great. Everyone seemed pleased with the new fridge in the kitchen. Rams reporter Stu Jackson noted that Garrett looked as fast and explosive as advertised.
“When he's out there, you can just feel his aura,” said McDuffie in training camp.“Everybody likes to say this aura that the guy has. He's gigantic. He's a monster.”
As can be the case with many appliances, that’s when the electronics began to malfunction. Back in early August, Garrett missed consecutive practices with what the team described as lower-body soreness that was expanded to swelling in his knee. While the Rams erred on the side of caution, something still wasn’t right. Garrett didn’t practice for much of August and then was estimated as a full participant in the days leading up to Week 1.
The Rams tested their new fridge for a neighborhood get-together in Week 1with the San Francisco 49ers visiting. Garrett didn’t perform well. For the first time since 2018, he was held without recording a single stat.
When Sean McVay was asked after the game whether Garrett was feeling 100 percent , he responded, “To my knowledge, ya.” Minutes later, Garrett walked in and said, “No. This was the worst version of myself.”
The Rams did what they should have done weeks prior and sent their new fridge back to the factory to get fixed, placing Garrett on injured reserve. Garrett would be out at least four weeks.
While Garrett recovered from arthroscopic knee surgery, reports flooded in on his potential return timeline. To be fair, the Rams never put a timeline on Garrett. However, according to NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport on September 27, Garrett was given a six-week timeline . Rapoport reported then that Garrett was determined to beat that timeline.
On October 4, The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones added more information . Jones noted that the six-week timeline would be a worst-case scenario. The team remained hopeful that Garrett could return in Week 6 against the Arizona Cardinals, but people inside the building believed that Garrett could return against the Las Vegas Raiders.
As we know now, Garrett didn’t play against the Cardinals, and McVay already stated on Monday that he would not return to practice this week ahead of the Raiders. ESPN’s Dan Graziano added in a report on Wednesday that Garrett could be out another two or three weeks at least.
We’ve gone from being hopeful about four weeks and realistic about five, with six weeks being a worst-case scenario and Garrett being determined to beat that timeline, to Garrett potentially missing at least seven or eight games.
The Rams sent their malfunctioning fridge back to the factory, were given a timeline, and that timeline continues to get pushed back. Without Garrett, the Rams have been left with a minifridge that they could have gotten by with for four or five weeks, but half the season has put them in a difficult spot.
Over the last four weeks, Josaiah Stewart has just a 7.8 percent pressure rate. That ranks 72nd out of 81 qualifying edge rushers. That’s not a knock on Stewart. Coming into the season, he was expected to be the minifridge used to keep drinks cold. Now, he’s one of two edge rushers on the Rams with over 100 snaps and a full-time player.
After Garrett’s surgery, McVay was asked how it went. “He's like Wolverine, healing fast,” McVay said. However, Garrett is like Wolverine if Wolverine healed very slowly and nobody knew when he’d be good to go again.
hoping for more progress than this ... for medical people, is this a bad sign? https://t.co/Ih4ftvGmO2 pic.twitter.com/SfZNV1hNye

title: What To Expect From Raiders’ Top Offensive Players vs. Rams
full_text:
A couple of weeks ago, this matchup was labeled a daunting one for the Las Vegas Raiders, as the Los Angeles Rams were once viewed as the class of the NFL.
However, the Rams have been one of the most disappointing teams in the league, entering Sunday with a 2-4 record. Not to mention, Los Angeles is dealing with an onslaught of injuries, with Poona Ford, Kobie Turner, and Davante Adams all out for the foreseeable future. Meanwhile, Puka Nacua is a game-time decision, and Trent McDuffie is questionable.
Despite being viewed as underdogs at home, the Raiders have a legitimate chance of ending their three-game losing streak in Week 7. With the Rams ravaged by injuries, specifically on defense, here's how Las Vegas' top offensive players can perform on Sunday.
Although the Raiders are in the midst of a three-game skid, Cousins has been more than serviceable. Now, there have been times when his immobility has been exposed, but that won't be a problem on Sunday. Los Angeles' defense has recorded eight sacks this season and will be without Ford, Turner, and Myles Garrett.
Cousins will have all the time in the world to operate in a clean pocket, which is all he needs to dissect an opposing defense. The Rams' secondary could also be short-handed if McDuffie is ruled out. While Cousins isn't supported by a bona fide WR1, the 38-year-old quarterback has more than enough to expose Los Angeles’ defense. You should expect an impressive outing from the 15-year veteran.
Jeanty has been underwhelming this season, averaging 3.2 yards per carry and rushing for one touchdown in six games. However, the 22-year-old running back has been battling through injuries during that stretch. While those injuries may still be present, the Rams' defensive line isn't.
At this point, Los Angeles' front line is a makeshift unit, with Aaron Donald headlining the group. Jeanty has an opportunity for a breakout game, but Mike Washington Jr. should carve into his workload, which is why I project a modest carry count for the second-year running back.
Regardless, Jeanty should surpass his production from the last two weeks, in which he's compiled 49 yards and one touchdown on 20 attempts.
Despite not recording his first reception until the third quarter last week, Bowers finished the game with four receptions for 70 yards. It's safe to assume that the 23-year-old tight end will be involved much earlier on Sunday.
If Cousins and Bowers have a rapport early in the game, the superstar tight end will have a monster outing. He's eclipsed 100 yards in two of four games this season; achieving that feat for the third time in 2026 is definitely in play.

title: One Raiders Player Who Could Surprisingly Be Traded Before Deadline
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' front office spent the offseason making wholesale moves to improve its roster in its first season under head coach Klint Kubiak. John Spytek and the Raiders dished out big bucks to improve nearly every position group on the team.
The only two positions the Raiders didn't add talent to were the two positions where they have two of the league's best players: tight end and punter. Even though Las Vegas made plenty of progress this offseason, its roster rebuild will take years to finish. This matters for multiple reasons.
Las Vegas made enough progress on its roster in one offseason that it has little room to add more talent this season without it hurting them in one aspect or another. If the Raiders trade a player away, it could impact the foundation Kubiak and his staff are building.
After the roster changes the Raiders made and the work the team put in on the field this offseason, I don't believe the Raiders should trade away any player, even when the deadline arrives on Nov. 10. To do so would be hasty. After the season would be a different story.
Of course, if the Raiders get a big offer for a major draft haul or players in return, it goes without saying that they should consider it and probably make the trade. However, they should refuse anything except an offer they cannot refuse.
Still, the trade deadline is approaching, and teams will undoubtedly keep discussing offers. Spytek has said in the past that he is open to hearing trade offers, both big and small. Even during his first season at the helm, Las Vegas struck a deal for a contributor in exchange for an often-injured player.
Spytek was also close to pulling off the trade of the offseason, ahead of having the best free-agency signing period and one of the best draft hauls in the league. I do not believe they should make a trade, but it is unquestionably on the table, as the Raiders sit at 3-3 on the season.
Las Vegas has lost three straight games . Two of those three losses came against the Kansas City Chiefs and the Buffalo Bills by six points combined. The Raiders' two losses to the Chiefs and Bills showed how close they are to regularly competing against, and eventually beating. the league's elite.
Their loss to the New England Patriots showed how far they are from doing so. All three losses make it fair for the front office to consider a trade. However, Kubiak knows the Raiders do not take the field on Sundays to almost win . A trade could help Las Vegas take an even bigger step this season.
“It's such a competitive game, and if you're just hoping to keep it close in the fourth quarter, that's not a winning mindset. So, just having the mindset when you have an opportunity to make a play, when you're playing complementary football on one side of the ball, special teams gives you good field position, you got to go score on that drive,” Kubiak said earlier this week.
“Defense gets a turnover; you got to go score on that drive. If there's a sudden change defensively, then we got to get a stop. So, just having the ultimate competitor's mindset of not being okay with having the game be close in the fourth quarter. That's not what we're here to do.”
Technically, one player who could be traded - and it would be a significant surprise - is offensive tackle Kolton Miller. Yet the way his contract is structured for both this season and next season eliminates him from the conversation.
The bigger surprise would be to see offensive lineman Jackson Powers-Johnson traded. Offseason rumblings and Caleb Rogers starting over Powers-Johnson in Week 6 may make this seem like less of a surprise. He is a very tradeable piece, but it would still be a surprise because of the timing.
Yet if those reasons make him potentially being traded not a surprise, Las Vegas trading him before the trade deadline, with the depth they have at the offensive guard position without Powers-Johnson, should outweigh those offseason rumblings and Rogers starting last week by a large margin.
He has plenty to improve upon, but teams in the league have a backup offensive guard as good as Powers-Johnson. Maybe adding a high-end veteran guard and another serviceable guard after the season, while continuing to develop Powers-Johnson, is the answer.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders’ Kirk Cousins Outlines Roadmap to Success for Silver and Black
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) have a tremendous opportunity on Sunday versus the team anointed in the preseason by the pundits as the unequivocal Super Bowl favorites, the Los Angeles Rams (2-4), to send the visitor’s season spiraling, and their season on a projectile that could end in the NFL Playoffs.
It's an incredible journey, and we aren’t even halfway through the regular season.
For the Raiders to get the big win, it is no secret that 15-year NFL veteran QB Kirk Cousins will lead the way.
Still young in life (38), the sage veteran of football experience is old in NFL years, and wise beyond them.
Matthew Stafford, the Rams QB, is 38 as well, but in his 18th season.
Sunday’s game will be the most unique in the NFL, simply because of the wisdom and experience of the two opposing QBs.
I covered Cousins in high school and every game of his college career, and Stafford as a Lion. I know, respect, and admire them both, and I am excited to have a front-row seat for this epic QB duel at Allegiant Stadium on Sunday.
Quarterback Kirk Cousins knows the Rams are loaded with great coaching and players, and the record doesn't reflect what they are bringing to the desert.
“I know the Rams are 2-4, but when you watch the tape and see the statistics behind the record, you see a really, really good football team that could easily have one of the best records in the league. So, we understand the challenge we have, the great players they have and great coaches, and we’ve got to be at our best.”
Klint Kubiak has made it clear that the Raiders need to improve their third-quarter production, and he put enormous emphasis on it this week in practice. Cousins elaborated on that.
“We’ll emphasize it in our practice routine, create a stoppage in practice to simulate that. We did that a couple weeks ago as well, so we’ll practice it the best we can, and then it’s an absolute point of emphasis. It’s got to be better.”
When Michael Mayer entered the NFL in 2023, he was considered the best TE in that draft. Shockingly, he slipped to the 35th pick (second round), and the Raiders' war room erupted with applause (according to a source in the room) when they picked him.
Cousins wasn’t here in 2023, but today he is as excited about his Notre Dame Fighting Irish teammate as anyone.
“He’s a good football player. I think Klint [Kubiak] is using him well, but he’s catching the football and making things happen, breaking tackles. He’s where he needs to be when he needs to be there, he’s got great hands, he’s accountable, and you can depend on him. I think there’s a reason our organization extended him, and he’s showing why, game in and game out.”
Cousins elaborated on how he started to identify Mayer as a go-to target.
“Maybe the first practice in OTAs. Natural hands, good feel for the position, could create space. Even when he’s covered, he can create space to get open. He had a great spring. In fact, we gave out, I don’t know if ‘award’ is the word, but Klint [Kubiak] gave out an award at the end of OTAs, and Michael [Mayer] was the top guy on offense. He had a great spring, and he’s carried it over to camp and into the regular season.”
Cousins and Kubiak have both talked about players earning trust. Especially young players, so I asked him to take the fans inside that process and how players do that, not just with him, but with the team.
“Similar to what I said about Michael [Mayer] be where you’re supposed to be when you’re supposed to be there, make plays with the ball in your hands when it comes your way, and do your job. The old Patriots line, ‘Do your job.’ We all have a job on each play, 11 of us, we've all got to do our job and each job is different. When you are consistently doing your job, you build trust.”
The Raiders went from concern to encouragement this week on the health of rookie RB Mike Washington Jr., who, if healthy enough to play, Kubiak told me has earned more reps this weekend than against the Rams. Cousins elaborated on what Washington Jr. has done to earn that.
“When you see the 30-plus-yard run for a touchdown against the Saints, you see the ability to break away. In practice, it’s hard because you’re not being brought to the ground often. So, until you get to the real thing, it’s difficult to evaluate. I think he’s run hard, and he’s continuing to get comfortable in the offense."
"I think every week as a rookie, no matter what position you're playing, you’re gaining confidence and earning trust. It’s a building process, and coming up on Week 7, the sample size is getting large enough to build that up.”
I heard another NFL executive this week call Brock Bowers "Superman" because he can do just about anything on the field. Cousins has seen a lot over his career, but the Georgia Bulldog still won his respect.
“He’s done a great job. We do ask him to run a pretty wide route tree, and I think it’s important that we give him variety so he’s less predictable to cover. He’s done a great job catching the football in traffic. Any time a player can be versatile, and you can ask a lot of them, they're harder to defend, and I think that’s true of Brock [Bowers].”
When Bowers comes up for his new deal (his rookie contract runs through 2028), Bowers is expected to transform the TE market. According to one league executive, “He is being used as a WR1 and contributing as a WR1, and if he actually hit the free agent market he would get paid like a WR1.”
So with him doing so much more than just being a TE, does Cousins still see him in that role?
“Yeah, I’d call him a tight end. It’s more about can you help in the run game, can you help in pass protection, can you at any moment wear a different hat? Brock [Bowers] can absolutely do that, so as a defense, you need to honor that.”
As teams stack the box to stop Klint Kubiak’s commitment to the run game, Cousins and WR Tre Tucker’s chemistry is taking off downfield. Cousins said they use the deep attack to open running lanes.
“Any time you go back and look, there are always plays where you say maybe we could have taken that one, or vice versa, maybe in moments you were too aggressive and should have checked it down. I think that’s what happened on the second-to-last drive, where we had three straight incompletions. It really needed to be a check-down deal more than trying to take it down the field the way I did. So, it’s both.”
Cousins went even deeper: “The key is, when you take the shots, you want to hit them. Otherwise, it’s a gain of zero, and it doesn’t matter if you almost hit it or how close it was. If it’s incomplete, you’re back to second-and-long or third-and-long, and you don’t want that. If you’re going to take the shots, you want to hit them and give yourself a chance to be in favorable downs and distances.”
I have known Kirk for decades, and in all that time (22 years), I have never known him to engage in or practice hyperbole. It isn’t part of his character. So when asked to talk about Tucker’s speed (which GM John Spytek may have painted himself into a corner over), Cousins’ genuine enthusiasm tells the true story.
"He's fast. I mean, he can roll. Everybody's fast in this league, and I used to joke that there's certain guys, like in high school when you play in high school, you hear about these guys that are unbelievable. And you go see them, you're like, oh yeah, they jump out. That starts to dwindle in college, and it dwindles even more in the NFL because everybody's good."
"But over my career, there have been like a couple guys where you're like, it feels like I'm back in high school where they're just different. It was Adrian Peterson, Percy Harvin, like certain guys where you're just watching and you're like, whoa.”
Cousins wasn’t done praising Tucker: “But Tre [Tucker] has speed where throwing to him, it's like I've thrown to a fair number of guys over my career, and he can roll. There's only a handful of them at the very top. You know Brandon Banks, Deshawn Jackson, Aldrich Robinson, where…

title: 3 Raiders Who Must Take Advantage on Sunday Against Rams
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are trying to get back on track after losing three straight games, and they'll try to get back in the win column vs. the Los Angeles Rams.
The Rams have not been the unstoppable force everyone expected them to be, sitting at 2-4 and dealing with significant injuries on both sides of the ball. This could be an opportunity for the Raiders to win their fourth game of the season.
Considering the injuries the Rams are dealing with, a few Raiders could have big games against the NFC powerhouse. Who might stand out for the Silver and Black in this game?
Let's break down three names who could shine against the Rams.
Playing better football since returning to the lineup, it could be a big day for the Raiders' second-year cornerback.
The Rams are dealing with injuries to two of their top wide receivers, so Porter will not see Davante Adams in this game. Puka Nacua has a minor calf injury, so he may not be at his best if he suits up for this game.
The Raiders need to force more turnovers, and Porter can help if he's lined up against receivers who won't give him as many problems. Look for Porter to have his name called a few times in this game.
Playing as the team's best downfield threat, Tucker will look to keep his hot streak going against a depleted Rams secondary.
Tucker, who has 24 receptions for 371 yards and three touchdowns, may not face Trent McDuffie, who has been dealing with a groin injury. If he avoids the All-Pro corner, he has a chance to win downfield.
The Raiders need explosive plays to beat the Rams, and Tucker will be the recipient of them. If he doesn't face some of the Rams' best corners, he may explode like he did last week.
Looking to bounce back after a rough go against the Buffalo Bills last week, Linderbaum won't face some of the Rams' most nightmarish defensive linemen.
Poona Ford is out for the season, and Kobie Turner is out for multiple weeks. The Rams may not be as effective up the middle, allowing Linderbaum to clear running lanes and prevent interior pressure.
The Raiders paid Linderbaum to be one of the best centers in the NFL, and he has a chance to be that against a depleted Rams team. This could be a chance for him to cash in.
Carter Landis studied journalism at Michigan State University where I graduated in May of 2022. He currently is a sports reporter for a local television station, and is a writer covering the Las Vegas Raiders

title: 3 Glaring Reasons Raiders Can Pull Off Rams Upset
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are reeling, as they are in the midst of a three-game losing streak.
However, they're in a great spot to end their winless drought in Week 7 against the once Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams. Despite trading for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie, while bringing back Aaron Donald out of retirement, the Rams enter this contest with a 2-4 record. With that in mind, Los Angeles is still expected to win this game on the road at Allegiant Stadium. Here are a few reasons why the Raiders can pull off the upset and regain their footing in the AFC playoff picture.
Not only did Los Angeles suffer an unforeseen defeat to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6, but it also departed that game with multiple players suffering significant injuries. The Rams lost both defensive tackles Kobie Turner (placed on injured reserve with a groin injury) and Poona Ford (out for the season with a ruptured triceps). Additionally, Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring and is expected to miss 6-10 weeks. So, obviously, all three of those players will miss Sunday.
Unfortunately for Los Angeles, that was only the beginning of the injury bug. Earlier this week, wide receiver Puka Nacua suffered a calf injury during practice and is now listed as a game-time decision. Meanwhile, McDuffie is questionable due to a groin injury after not practicing on Friday. It goes without saying that the Rams will be a downgraded version of themselves in Week 7.
Not only is Los Angeles short-handed on the defensive line, but Las Vegas' backfield is expected to be fully intact for this game. Ashton Jeanty's injuries have been well-documented, but Mike Washington Jr. popped up on the injury report after missing practice on Thursday. At one point on Friday, the rookie running back was listed as questionable. However, head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters yesterday that Washington Jr. is expected to play against the Rams.
The aforementioned injuries to the Rams' defensive line, including Myles Garrett not being ready to return, are why Las Vegas is in a favorable spot to unlock the rushing attack. If that happens, Kirk Cousins should be put in comfortable situations to succeed throughout the game.
At this point, the Rams are expected to win based on pedigree alone. They have lost three of four games, with the most alarming defeat coming last week against the Cardinals. Matthew Stafford has thrown six interceptions already this season, and that's been with his full allotment of pass-catchers.
Defensively, the Rams have eight sacks this season, ranking 31st in the league. Meanwhile, special teams derailed their Super Bowl aspirations last season, and those glaring issues remain. Considering the preseason hype that everyone preemptively anointed Los Angeles as Super Bowl champions, they are on track to be the biggest flop in NFL history.
Logan Lazarczyk is a graduate of the University of Missouri-Kansas City, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts in Communication Studies with an emphasis in Journalism. Logan joined our team with extensive experience, having previously written and worked for media entities such as USA Today and Union Broadcasting.

title: Why Raiders Catching Rams at Opportunistic Time
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are preparing for a showdown with the Los Angeles Rams, looking to rebound after losing three straight.
The Raiders may be sliding, but the Rams are in a worse spot. Everyone expected them to be a powerhouse that would mow down every team in their way, but they sit at 2-4 and have lost their last two games, including a loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
For a Raiders team that needs to get back on track, the Rams come to town at the right time. Not only are they significantly injured, but they're not playing with much confidence.
The Raiders have lost three straight, but their confidence does not appear to have wavered. They put a scare into the hearts of the Buffalo Bills, who may be the best team in the AFC and possibly the entire NFL.
It would be a major confidence boost to beat a Rams team that has floundered in the last two weeks. Granted, one of those losses was to the Bills, but they had no business losing to the Cardinals in that fashion.
Klint Kubiak is still learning the ropes as a head coach, and facing off against Sean McVay on the other sideline won't be easy. However, McVay has made some poor coaching decisions this season, which have set the Rams up for failure.
Kubiak should go into this game with a simple plan that doesn't need to be overly complicated. If he thinks too much about how to approach this game, McVay will make him pay and leave Allegiant Stadium with a road victory.
There is a laundry list of players who won't appear in this game for the Raiders' opponent.
Among them: Davante Adams , Myles Garrett, Poona Ford, Nate Landman, and Kobie Turner. Oh, and Puka Nacua is questionable for this game.
All the star power the Rams entered the season with has somewhat faltered, so they may not be bringing their A-game to Las Vegas. The Raiders will face a Rams team that is somewhat comparable in terms of talent level.
For a Raiders team that needs a win, this game presents that opportunity. The Rams are struggling, and they may not be able to rebound and dominate the NFL like we all expected.
That said, this would still be a tremendous win for Kubiak's team if they can pull it off. They would move to 4-3, and with the NFL looking as wide open as it is, that would give the team enough reason not to pull the plug on the season just yet.
Carter Landis studied journalism at Michigan State University where I graduated in May of 2022. He currently is a sports reporter for a local television station, and is a writer covering the Las Vegas Raiders

title: Raiders vs. Rams: 5 Key Players To Watch
full_text:
Week 7 is here, and this game could determine the fate of both franchises for the rest of the season. The Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Rams go toe-to-toe on Sunday afternoon in a game many saw as a gimme for the supposed "superteam" that is the Rams.
Las Vegas has lost three straight games while Los Angeles is battling injuries to key starters and special teams miscues. Both teams are in a must-win situation as their regular-season futures hang in the balance. The Raiders will need some help to secure a big win over the Rams in what could be an exciting game at Allegiant Stadium.
Here are five players on the Raiders roster to watch in this weekend's crucial matchup.
Even if he has just come out of retirement, Aaron Donald is still a handful for opposing offensive linemen. He is consistently doubled and tripled teamed, which is why the production isn't as high as many were expecting. Yet the Raiders could be the team that leaves their guards on an island, and Caleb Rogers must be ready for the challenge.
Making his second start of the season, Rogers had an impressive day against the Buffalo Bills' defensive front last week. He hasn't shown anything that would warrant a move back to the bench anytime soon, but the former Texas Tech standout could earn a lot of trust from head coach Klint Kubiak if he slows down Donald.
I think if there is a game where the Raiders need Quay Walker to look like a star, it's this one. The former Green Bay Packer has been playing his best football as a versatile WILL linebacker who can rush the passer, set the edge, fit the run off the ball, and run the flag pole in the middle of the field.
Against an offense with the third-best run success rate (48.6%), according to Next Gen Stats , Walker has a chance to be a disruptor in the backfield while closing off the middle of the field in coverage against the Rams' heavy usage of 13 personnel (three tight ends).
After missing last week's game with a concussion, Tonka Hemingway returns to the lineup with no injury designation for this weekend. The Raiders are in desperate need of his explosiveness and penetration skills at the line of scrimmage, as he has emerged as arguably their best defensive tackle. Hemingway faces a tough matchup against a great Rams interior offensive line and will be entrusted to be the difference-maker in the middle of the defensive front.
The Rams' special teams have been the Achilles' heel of their season, and nothing seems to be getting any better. They lack discipline on punt and kickoff coverage and have allowed some serious returns. This is an opportunity for the Raiders to have a great day on special teams and utilize the speed and quickness of both Laube and Benson, so look for this duo to create some big plays.
Jared Feinberg, a native of western North Carolina, has written about NFL football for nearly a decade. He has contributed to several national outlets and is now part of our On SI team as an NFL team reporter.
