title: One Trade Deadline Move Raiders Must Prioritize ASAP
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders spent the offseason revamping their roster from the top down. Las Vegas' front office did an admirable job of quickly revamping what was the league's worst roster last season. Still, too many holes remained to fill them all in one offseason.
Las Vegas' season and future will largely depend on the moves the front office makes during this year's free agency and the NFL Draft. A productive offseason saw the Raiders eliminate multiple needs, most notably at center and at quarterback.
The start of the regular season allowed the Raiders to better gauge the strengths and weaknesses of their revamped roster. Just as the new additions have shone, so have their remaining deficiencies at times. Thus, perfectly explaining Las Vegas' 3-3 record.
Arguably the biggest issue the Raiders have right now is their offensive line. Although it is not nearly as bad as last season, improving the unit would eliminate most of the issues that are plaguing the offense overall. The unit is still gelling together after several new pieces joined this offseason.
Raiders offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko explained how detail-oriented the staff is with the unit and how it tracks the unit's progress over time.
“I think it's really every meeting, every snap, every play that we go every series and just building those things together," Janocko said earlier this week.
"Can we get 1% better with our techniques, our hand placement, how we come off the ball, what's our eyes look like? What's our pad level? What's our finish? All those things that we can quantify. Can we get 1% better than that? And that's how we're going to grow as not just an offensive line, but as an offense and as an organization."
Las Vegas could easily decide not to make any move at all at the deadline. However, if the Raiders should look to make a move, it would be a trade for an offensive guard. If Las Vegas trades away draft picks or a player, it should be for a dependable offensive lineman.
After adding veteran Tyler Linderbaum during the offseason, the Raiders are now figuring out which offensive line positions still need work. After the season's first six games, it is clear the team will need more from that position group for the rest of this season and likely beyond.
The Raiders are 3-3, but their offense has struggled for long stretches. It has been a major reason Las Vegas has lost three straight games. At times, Las Vegas' offense has struggled to move the ball through the air. The unit has also struggled to run the ball for most of this season.
“It’s just something we’re going to look to improve every week. Whether we have a game that we rush for 150, 200 yards, we’re still going to go back and say, 'Okay, how can we get better?' So, I don’t know that we’re looking at it in terms of it’s close. We’re looking for incremental improvement every week in everything we do,” Kubiak said.
Las Vegas' offensive line could use help and more time together. However, on one level or another, the Raiders' line collectively has room for improvement. The Raiders' offensive line, like the team as a whole, has improved significantly from last season, but still needs more.
The trade deadline would be the quickest and most efficient way to add a quality offensive lineman, but after this offseason's moves, Las Vegas may have to work with what it has. Janocko gave insight into the thought process he and the Raiders' coaching staff use to approach situations.
"I think everything you look at, you got to look at the big picture, and it's not the same thing all the time," Janocko said.
"But what is our efficiency on first down? Are we in are we in second and long? And then, do we have specific tendencies? So, we dig into all of that. Whether it be first down, second down, third down. Wherever we're studying, we look at when we have success, what's the why, and then when we don't, what's the why?"
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Announcers, Referees & Jersey Combination for Raiders' Week 7 Matchup
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders hope this Sunday will go better than the previous three, as they host the Los Angeles Rams. Both teams enter Week 7 with issues that will likely impact Sunday's game. The rebuilding Raiders have a chance to get back on track this Sunday.
Las Vegas continues to work through one of the toughest schedules in the league. Despite their record, Sunday's game against the Rams will be another challenging matchup for Klint Kubiak's Raiders.
The Raiders will continue to lean on quarterback Kirk Cousins, who is playing some of the best football of any quarterback in the league entering Week 7. Still, the 15-year veteran knows he has plenty to work on to play at his best each week.
Even after all this time, and the Raiders' early success compared to last season, Cousins knows that learning the game and improving as a player is a constant process.
"Footwork, progressions, decision-making, your leadership, your presence, your communication skills, your toughness. You're always being tested, mentally, physically, emotionally, and every day you're asking yourself, am I meeting the standard to win a championship? And I think when you go back and look at a game like Sunday, and it's happened a couple times, several times this year, 90% is good,” Cousins said when asked what he can get better at.
“And it's not the 90% that I get worried about. It's the 10% where you say that's not up to the standard of what it takes to win a championship. And so, how do we get that 10% to shrink to 3% to 2% And you're always going to do that. You're always going to have plays you want back, but that's what you're trying to trim to make sure that you meet the standard to go win a championship."
Raiders offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko spent multiple seasons with Cousins while both were a part of the Minnesota Vikings' organization. Janocko recently shared his thoughts on Cousins' growth from the last time they worked together to now.
"I think, like you said, experience. So, even more experience than he was then. He's seen good things. He's had success in different systems since we've been apart. So, he has a different base of knowledge that we can bounce ideas off of each other. Being around different ideas, different players,” Janocko said earlier this week.
“Much like I've been around different ideas with different coaches, so you see that, and then you just see a guy that you know he just he wants to do what it takes to win and wants to – he's a guy that thrives on accountability."
“So, he wants to be pushed, he wants to be coached, and when other guys see a guy that's been in this league that long, want to be coached, and is the first one to say, ‘I got to do this, I can make this throw, or I got to step up’. And then when it's successful, it's we, it's us, it's together. That's type of stuff that young guys should mimic."
Jonathan Vilma will serve as an analyst, Chris Meyers will serve as the play-by-play, and  Megan Olivi will be the sideline reporter on Sunday. The Raiders will wear their black home jerseys, silver pants, and silver helmets. Ron Torbert is the head referee designated for the Raiders' Week 7 outing.
The Raiders have a tall task on their hands, as they will face a Rams team desperate to stop their own losing streak. Matthew Stafford poses several problems for the Las Vegas' defensive backfield. However, he also has the potential to score points, no matter who his receivers are.
This means Stafford poses issues for the Raiders' defense and Las Vegas' offense, as the unit will again be forced to face an elite coach-and-quarterback duo. Stafford is yet another strong-armed quarterback Las Vegas will face in consecutive weeks.
Las Vegas has the talent to compete with any team they face this season. This is especially true with the Rams, as they enter Week 7 minus several key contributors. To break its three-game losing streak , it must capitalize on opportunities to pull ahead when they present themselves.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: What Raiders Can Realistically Afford at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders roster is nearly set as the trade deadline approaches, but it is still far from complete. A team can only do so much to fix its roster before the trade deadline, but with room for improvement, Las Vegas could be in the market.
John Spytek noted during the offseason that he is "always listening" to trade offers. During his brief time in Las Vegas, Spytek has not been a man of hyperbole. Still, the Raiders front office made sweeping changes this offseason to revamp what was the league's worst roster last season.
So, as much as Spytek is always listening, he and the Raiders' front office have every right to sit on their remaining resources ahead of the deadline if they choose. The Raiders handed out over $300 million in contracts during free agency. Then, added 10 rookies via the draft.
That is significantly more than most front offices do in one offseason. That is more than some front offices do in years. It would be understandable if Las Vegas did not make a move at the deadline. Their 3-3 start confirms they are on the right track. It may be best to leave things as is.
Still, the Raiders have several talented players who could entice other teams to try to strike a deal. Then there are the numbers. The money Las Vegas spent in free agency left little cap space to work with on the back end. This forced multiple contract restructurings.
Las Vegas has around $11 million in available cap space ahead of the trade deadline. That should be enough to make a solid move, as a potential player-for-player trade could improve the Raiders' numbers. That would undoubtedly change if the Raiders traded a player for draft picks.
As the Raiders know all too well, many things must go right for two teams to complete a trade. Beyond making the numbers work, teams must answer other questions before deciding whether a deal is realistic or reasonable, considering how well they have played overall this season.
For Las Vegas to complete a trade, they would likely have to trade one of their best players with a sizeable contract. That would mean trading the likes of Maxx Crosby or Kolton Miller, which would be unthinkable at this point in the season. However, Las Vegas has three games before the deadline.
The Raiders will face the Los Angeles Rams at home this Sunday, the New York Jets on the road next Sunday, and the San Francisco 49ers on the road the following week. If the Raiders lose two of the next three games, they will be 4-5. A trade could seem more plausible then.
Even at 4-5, Las Vegas trading one of their best players for anything less than a top-tier offer, such as two first-round draft picks for Crosby, would not make much sense because of what it would do to what Klint Kubiak and his coaching staff have started to build.
For the Raiders to trade one of their best players and risk hurting the clear progress they've made would have to mean they received an offer they couldn't refuse. They must consider this as the deadline approaches. Las Vegas is not obligated to consider a trade.
The Raiders could also trade picks in return for a player at a position of need, but trading away picks also seems counterproductive. Las Vegas has made significant progress by inserting several rookies and second-year players into significant roles this season.
Las Vegas trading away draft picks now would go against that. Spytek also values having more picks. The Raiders have drafted at least 10 players in both of their drafts under Spytek. Las Vegas has a higher chance of success drafting players under Spytek than a retread from another team.
The Raiders are ahead of schedule. If they were to make a trade, it should be a very low-key move- nothing big; no need to overdo it.
Las Vegas needs to fine-tune its existing operation unless it can strike a trade for a player they believe can elevate it immediately.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Dolphins Saturday Mailbag: Why Fans Should Want to See Victories
full_text:
Part 1 of the pre-Jets game Miami Dolphins On SI mailbag:
So me and my sons are flying up for the game. Even though we want a top draft pick next year, can you give us a reason to root for a win?
Hey Mark, because the biggest thing you should want to see this season is progress from the young players, namely all the recent draft picks, as well as from Malik Willis. And the Dolphins starting to win some games certainly would be a sign of progress, which might provide more optimism than winding up with a higher draft pick in 2027 than with more and more losses.
Hello Alain, which of the Dolphins and Jets has the better future outlook with their current QB situation? Or is the present irrelevant, and both are likely to find themselves in a future competition to acquire the best prospect that might provide hope in challenging the top of the division?
Hey Ricky, this is a very good question and the answer will come down to whether Malik Willis can take that step and establish himself as a bona fide long-term answer so the Dolphins can use their resources in other areas. If we’re looking at the totality of the roster, I think the Jets actually might be a bit ahead at this time, though it’s pretty close, but Geno Smith clearly is a stopgap for them. Also remember that the Jets have three first-round picks again next year and if they can nail the quarterback, that could set them up for a pretty drastic turnaround sooner rather than later.
I don’t see everything that you say, but I’ve yet to hear you proclaim what you would do, only what you would not do, with the first overall pick. So that being said, as things stand right now and we’ll pretend like the Dolphins have the No. 1 pick and not the Chargers. Who would you select at this very moment with the No. 1 overall pick for the Miami Dolphins?
Hey Dana, you haven’t missed anything because my take always has been that I don’t like the idea of Jeremiah Smith first overall because of positional value (or lack thereof) and I’ve also said that I need the season to play out in college football before I decide which prospect I would prefer. To answer your question, my first preference at No. 1 would be trading down, hopefully not too far down, and picking up additional draft picks. If that’s off the table, based on what I know right now and subject to change, I’d be inclined to go with either Texas edge defender Colin Simmons and might even consider Leonard Moore, the cornerback from Notre Dame. I still don’t have a QB prospect that screams “must take” right now.
Hey Davis, if you’re asking why the Dolphins waived him in terms of this being a big surprise, my answer to you would be that it shouldn’t have been a big surprise. While Duck did show potential at times for the Dolphins in 2024 and in training camp last year, it’s not like he was an established player. And that Miami decided he didn’t rank higher than any of the three newcomers they have — Jaylin Simpson, Marcellas Dial Jr. and Reece Taylor, all of them claimed off waivers, mind you — and that should tell you all you need to know.
Greetings Alain! Had to take an emergency trip to Central Florida last week & on way back was caught in one of the infamous traffic jams around Miami area, so I listened to the Collective.  I then noticed I was in the stadium area & I was creeping along & y'all were talking about the season; the irony wasn't lost on me. This season is meant to creep along, but it gets lost on us fans sometimes. Not sure if he's been asked, but do you think Hafley regrets no 7 on 7's to build some chemistry between QB/receivers? Also to get receivers better familiar with proper routes? Final question: Is Chris Bell's lack of separation due to still recovering from knee injury? Not knowing the assignments? Something else? As always, look forward to both All Dolphins and Dolphins Collective podcasts (best out there) and all the great written content on Miami Dolphins on SI.Com.
Thanks as always, Dave. I don’t think there’s any question that Bell’s knee injury still factors in his ability to separate at the time, but it’s also fair to ask what his ceiling is in that department once the injury is a thing of the past because I don’t think that ever was considered his forte. Hafley explained his disdain for 7-on-7 work in training camp as not being representative of what players will do in games, and I’m thinking he wouldn’t be about to second-guess himself there. And if that 7-on-7 that wasn’t done was replaced by 11-on-11 sessions, then the Dolphins didn’t miss out on that kind of work.
Do you think the Dolphins' staff will be less likely to activate or play injured players due to the history of injuries at that crap field?
Hey Lloyd, it’s a very interesting point you raise because MetLife Stadium historically has been rough on players, for sure. That said, no, I don’t think decisions will be made specifically because of that surface. If the Dolphins decide, for example, that Caleb Douglas is ready to go, I don’t think Jeff Hafley wants to go down the road of being afraid of something bad happening because the game is at MetLife Stadium.
I need your honest opinion here. Do the Miami Dolphins have the smallest shoulders for a coach and general manager duo in the NFL?
First off, I always give my honest opinion. Never a need to preface a question with that. Second … huh? Smallest shoulders? You mean, Jon-Eric Sullivan and Jeff Hafley are not physically imposing? So? And I haven’t studied or examined other coach/GM combos to see where they stand among their peers.
What weapon not named Ollie Gordon steps up on offense on Sunday?
I think Malik Willis comes back from the bye with his best performance of the season. If you’re asking for somebody other than the QB, then maybe I go with Greg Dulcich, who’s due to have a big performance in the passing game.

title: Breaking Down the Louis News and the other Week 7 Dolphins Saturday Moves
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins will get a second rookie back when they face the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on Sunday.
Safety Kyle Louis was activated off injured reserve Saturday, meaning he'll be ready to return to action for the first time since sustaining a knee injury in the season opener against the Las Vegas Raiders. Louis' availability had been trending positively all week, culminated by his full participation in practice Friday, though he remained listed as questionable on the final injury report of the week.
Along with activating Louis, the Dolphins also made their two weekly practice squad elevations, this time with edge defender Max Llewellyn and kicker Zane Gonzalez.
The move with Gonzalez basically was a given since the Dolphins don't have a kicker on the 53-man roster after releasing Riley Patterson on Tuesday, while the move with Llewellyn suggests that Rob Beal Jr. will miss a fourth consecutive game because of the hamstring injury he sustained in the Week 2 loss against the San Francisco 49ers. He was listed as doubtful on the Dolphins' final injury report of the week.
Llewellyn, the rookie seventh-round pick out of Iowa, will be making his second appearance. He played five snaps in the 35-13 loss at Levi's Stadium.
Louis will become the fifth safety on the active roster, joining Dante Trader Jr., rookie Michael Taaffe, Zayne Anderson and Julius Wood.
A linebacker at the University of Pittsburgh, Louis was switched to safety at some in training camp and in an ideal world he could become a good nickel defender because of his coverage ability. Before he was injured, Louis also had become a gunner on the punt team.
Given that he hasn't played since the opener, it's probably fair to expect Louis to play mostly, if not exclusively, on special teams against the Jets.
But regardless it's great to have him back.
He is the third player the Dolphins have designated to return from IR so far this season after DT Kenneth Grant and LB Trey Moore. Grant also has returned to the active roster, while Moore remains on IR and was designated to return on the day of the cuts to 53 to preserve a roster spot for somebody else.

title: Three Bold Predictions for the Miami Dolphins Against New York Jets
full_text:
The 0-5 Miami Dolphins take on the 2-4 New York Jets in Miami’s first divisional game of the 2026 season. Both teams are looking to keep their seasons from going completely off the rails, so let’s make some predictions for this Week 7 matchup.
Sunday will mark the return of rookie receiver Caleb Douglas, who has missed the past three games with an ankle injury. Adding his size to the top of the depth chart should bump everyone else to a more natural position, and there may be no bigger benefactor than Malik Washington.
Washington has quietly put together an impressive third season, tallying 50 or more scrimmage yards in four of his first five games. He has also established himself as a favorite target of quarterback Malik Willis, who has thrown his way 36 times this year (more than double the second-place mark).
As Miami looks for sustainability, targeting Washington underneath seems like a potential solution, and he has the agility to make defenders miss in space. His ascension, Douglas’ return, and Willis likely needing quick answers against a Jets defense that ranks eighth in blitz percentage is a recipe for a big day for Miami’s most experienced receiver.
This matchup features two passers who have done a poor job mitigating pressure this season. Both rank top 12 in time to throw, top three in pressure rate allowed, and top five in sack percentage.
The Jets are well equipped to take advantage of Malik Willis’ indecision. Their defense ranks in the top eight in pressure rate, and is tied for sixth in total sacks through six weeks.
The Dolphins, on the other hand, have been inept up front. Their four sacks are half the next-lowest team in the NFL, and all four came against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4.
With two weeks to prepare, a quarterback who is willing to hang in the pocket, and the potentially dumb luck that Miami’s sacks have come in a bunch, this feels like a perfect opportunity for the Dolphins’ defensive front to make its mark, even if Malik Willis’ play leads to a similar outcome on the opposite side of the ball.
Ollie Gordon's development in year two has been a revelation. His footwork looks substantially better than it did in 2025, and he’s made the most of his elevated opportunity. Gordon’s rushing yards over expected per attempt is ninth among qualified rushers, per NextGenStats.
The Jets have a very sound defense on a per-run basis. Their EPA per rush allowed is tied for third best in football, and they’re right around the middle of the pack in terms of yards-per-attempt. They have, however, struggled to stop runs in the backfield. Their stuffed run rate is seventh-lowest, and they’re allowing over a yard and a half before contact per carry, which ranks ninth-worst.
Miami’s massive offensive line has opened up big lanes for Gordon in recent weeks. He has a 20+ yard carry in each of the last two games. Now, against a defense that particularly struggles to generate displacement, it wouldn’t be shocking to see the left-side duo of Paul and Proctor give Gordon a runway that he can use to get downhill and put his massive frame to work against New York’s defensive backs.
Tyler DeSena is currently a journalism student at the University of Central Florida. Prior to joining Dolphins On SI in 2026, DeSena worked with dolphinstalk.com, and created independent social media content on X, YouTube and TikTok.

title: Great Douglas News Highlights Positive Final Week 7 Dolphins Injury Report
full_text:
After some extensive time off in the form of a bye week, the Miami Dolphins won't be completely healthy when they take on the New York Jets, but they're getting there.
But they will get back a big piece of their offense for the Week 7 matchup against the New York Jets, with wide receiver Caleb Douglas off the injury report after being a full participant in practice Friday.
Douglas missed the past three games because of an ankle injury he sustained in the Week 2 loss against the San Francisco 49ers and the Dolphins clearly missed him.
It's not ridiculous to say the outlook of this game changes with the return of Douglas. The Dolphins passing offense was one-dimensional without him, with only Malik Washington and Greg Dulcich being consistent targets for Malik Willis, but even that's pushing it.
Despite missing three games, Douglas STILL has the third-most receiving yards of any target on the Dolphins with 113.
Miami is lacking a wide receiver that has as much upside as Douglas has shown so far, even with limited snaps due to the injury. His ability to separate from defenders is unmatched on the roster right now, combined with his speed and agility to get open in a hurry. His return brings size back to the position, with his 6-4 frame being taller than any other wide receiver.
The Dolphins currently average 153.6 passing yards per game, the second-fewest in the NFL, just 0.1 yards ahead of the Tennessee Titans. The group could use a splash of youth to energize it against a Jets secondary that allows only 185 yards per game, the fourth-fewest in the NFL.
Douglas isn't the only Dolphins rookie who could make his return against the Jets.
Safety Kyle Louis was listed as questionable for Sunday even though he's currently on the IR, but the encouraging sign here is that he was a full participant in practice Friday after being limited the previous two days. This could be a sign he's ready to return in his first week of eligibility after missing the required four games.
Normally, activating someone from the IR would require a corresponding roster move to stay within the 53-player limit, but the Dolphins are currently at 52.
Running back Jaylen Wright, who's been dealing with a nagging foot injury, also was cleared to play. With that said, Wright has struggled to make an impact as Ollie Gordon's backup, but the Jets' defense hasn't had the best success against rushing offenses - 123 yards per game given up. This could be his best chance yet to contribute.
Rookie tight end Will Kacmarek, who has been dealing with a hamstring injury, specifically noted on Thursday that he'll be ready to play Sunday, and he was cleared on Friday. As mentioned earlier with Wright, attacking the ground might be key for Miami's offense, and Kacmarek has impressed as a run blocker for Gordon thus far.
However, there are a few players on defense who might not play this game. That includes edge rusher Rob Beal Jr., who is listed as doubtful. He had to exit the San Francisco game with a hamstring injury. Before that, he recorded a single tackle against Las Vegas in the season opener.
It's also confirmed that cornerback Reese Taylor will not play Sunday because of a quad injury; he was ruled out.
Linebacker Willie Gay Jr. was back at practice Friday after being out one day with an illness, and he was listed as questionable after being a limited participant.
On the other side, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn is dealing with a significantly larger number of questions in terms of who's playing in this game. The most significant player on the list is running back Breece Hall, who was listed as questionable. He's been dealing with a quad injury suffered against Detroit in Week 3.
Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said that he'd be surprised if Hall didn't play in this game, but the Jets might not want to rush things with Hall, especially because his replacement, Braelon Allen, has done such a great job in his wake with 314 yards and two touchdowns.
A big boost to the Jets' receiver corps will be the return of wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, who is expected to play while dealing with a broken finger. It'll be the first time that Mitchell, Garrett Wilson and rookie first-round pick Omar Cooper Jr. will all be ready to go in the same game since their season opener.
Nose tackle T'Vondre Sweat is dealing with a knee injury but is expected to play Sunday. He's been reliable when healthy, with 15 tackles in six games played. It's a solid contribution for a player who was acquired from Tennessee in a trade that sent Jermaine Johnson to the Titans.
There are a few players officially ruled out: linebacker Kiko Mauigoa (quad), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle), and offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion).
Left guard Dylan Parham is questionable to play in this game with a knee injury that has sidelined him for three games. His backup, Jordan Meredith, has played well in his absence, but it would mean a lot for the Jets to get one of their top linemen healthy once again.
Kene Nwangwu is also listed as questionable, which is a big blow for the special teams. He's been a decent kick returner with 251 yards on 11 attempts but hasn't had an opportunity to break a long run yet this season. If he can't go, Isaiah Williams will likely have to shoulder returning once again for the Jets. It should be noted that Williams had a 78-yard punt return for a touchdown for the Jets' only score in the Dolphins' 34-10 victory at MetLife Stadium last December.

full_text:
The Miami Dolphins again will be looking for their first victory of the Jon-Eric Sullivan/Jeff Hafley era when they return from their bye to face the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on Sunday.
Here's all the pertinent info for this Week 7 Dolphins-Jets matchup:

The Jets, much like the Dolphins, still are in rebuilding mode two years removed from ending the failed Aaron Rodgers experiment. This is a relatively young team under second-year head coach Aaron Glenn, though the Jets appear on the right track with the promising early returns on their three rookie first-round picks — edge David Bailey, tight end Kenyon Sadiq, and wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. The Jets have another three first-round picks next year and it's widely expected that's how they hope to land their quarterback of the future. In the meantime, it's 36-year-old veteran Geno Smith running the offense in his second stint with the team after first arriving as a second-round pick in 2013.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The best place to start here is that the Dolphins have owned the Jets lately, winning 14 of the past 17 matchups, including a season sweep last year. The Jets might be a better team than they were in 2025 when they struggled offensively with Justin Fields at quarterback, but they still rank in the bottom third of every significant offensive statistical category. While Smith has an impressive passer rating, he's also taken an awful lot of sacks. The Dolphins are coming off two good performances with their running game and the Jets have been very inconsistent with their run defense.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
When a team is 0-5, the reasons a team could lose should be obvious. While the bye may have helped the Dolphins in many ways, this remains a very young team lacking in talent across the roster. The Jets defense doesn't have the big names anymore after the trades of Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams, but they can play good football at times, evidenced by the fact New York held three of first six opponents to under 200 total yards.
This game was highlighted from the start as one of those best opportunities for the Dolphins during this full-blown rebuilding season, and nothing has changed that outlook. The Jets — to borrow an expression — pretty much are who we thought they were, a young team that's not good enough to compete for a playoff spot, good enough to be a tough out but also never an overwhelming opponent. The Dolphins haven't played since that disappointing Week 5 loss against Cincinnati when they took a step back after competitive games against Kansas City and Minnesota, so it's difficult to gauge what kind of performance they'll offer. The Dolphins will defeat the Jets this season, but we're thinking it'll happen in the rematch in five weeks. Final Prediction: Jets 19, Dolphins 17

title: Dolphins Opponent Intel: Jets Insider Dishes on Minkah, Mason Taylor, Geno Smith and More
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins’ Week 7 matchup against the New York Jets will feature a matchup of AFC East in rebuilding situations.
While the Dolphins will head into the game with an 0-5 record, the Jets will come with a 2-4 mark that isn’t exciting, but clearly better than last year when New York started off 0-7 on their way to “earning” the second overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft.
The Dolphins swept the Jets last season, winning a close game at Hard Rock Stadium in the Week 4 Monday night matchup and blowing out the Jets at MetLife Stadium in December.
While it’s clear the Dolphins aren’t as talented as they were last season, the Jets are a bit more of a mystery.
On an episode of the All Dolphins Podcast earlier this week, New York Daily News reporter Antwan Staley helped provide some inside info on the Jets.
Here were some of the highlights of our conversation with Staley:
On an overall outlook for the season:
"What I would say is the good news is they're not 0-7 like they were last year. The Jets still aren't a good team, but I feel like they've gone from a really bad team to now a mediocre team, one that you know it's gonna be in games there, and it's gonna pressure opposing teams and all that stuff. We saw it against the Patriots there. I felt like they had some grit, had some fight. They just did. They’re just not talented enough to be able to overcome the mistakes that they have. Whether you talk about you know clock management or you know drops or penalties and things of that nature. So I think we're just seeing a team that was really young last year, they're the third-youngest team in football. Now they added some veterans there, Minkah Fitzpatrick, Demario Davis, among others, and now they're just trying to get from a mediocre team to a playoff team. And it might be another year before that happens too. But you know, they're a team that's probably going to be in every single game this year for the most part. But lack of talent is still evident in a few spots."
On Geno Smith’s performance this season and how legit is his 101.8 passer rating:
"Yeah, he's held the ball too long at times. Obviously, him being 36 years old now, like he doesn't have the same athleticism that he once had. Doesn't have necessarily the quick release like he once had. So I think he gets in trouble where you know he can hold on to the ball a little bit longer, waiting for his receivers to get open, and thenI think teams now — kind of what you found in the Patriots game — speed him up, like get him processing a little bit faster. That way he can possibly make mistakes. We've seen him fumble the ball a few times. He's only had one interception, but he's had a few fumble losses as well. So it's been up and down. It's been better than what it was last year with Justin Fields, which is a very low bar. But you know, I think Geno has given them opportunities to win games. He just hasn't always played well, so I think the quarterback rating is a bit of a mirage too.”
On whether head coach Aaron Glenn is on his way to solidifying his spot as Jets head coach for the future after a shaky first season, or is that still way up in the air:
"Yeah, that's still to be determined. The positive again is the Jets are fighting; they're in these games. They're showing grit. They're not just laying down and letting teams beat them by 30 points, like you saw sometimes last year. So it looks a lot different. However, they're just not closing games the way that they should be, and it seems like it's the same mistakes that are happening all over again. It seems like it's some kind of boneheaded penalty. It seems like it's some kind of mistake as far as play calling as well. … And I think ultimately the biggest thing, the damning stat on Aaron Glenn is this: opponents have outscored the Jets right before halftime within the last two minutes 90-6 throughout his tenure. And then him being 0-7 in the AFC East. Those are the two damning stats on Aaron Glenn. So until those change, then yeah, it's gonna be up in the air whether he comes back for 2027 or not. It starts there. You have to be able to take care of the division. Forget about New England and Buffalo for a minute, but you cannot get swept by the Dolphins and expect to keep your job this year. So this is a critical game for him. I'm sure it's a critical game for Jeff Hafley and the Dolphins organization too. The loser is going to be in really bad shape, especially if it's the Jets, because people were already calling for Aaron Glenn to be fired even before the season started. If you lose to the Dolphins, then it's hard to kind of overcome that."
On the play so far of two-time Dolphins safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, who they traded to the Jets this offseason for a seventh-round pick:
"I mean, he's been solid. He actually recorded their first interception. They broke the drought, so he'scome in and done the things that they expected him to do: be a quarterback for the defense, be a ball hog. Really helped young safety Dane Belton, who I think has been one of the biggest surprises of the Jets too this year. So I think Minkah is doing a really good job, especially since coming back (from a hamstring injury). He's not the same player that he once was when he was younger, but I think the Jets still benefit from his intelligence and just be able to see just diagnose what the offense is trying to do on a down-to-down basis."
On how Mason Taylor, the son of Dolphins Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, is doing in his second season as a Jets tight end after the team drafted fellow tight end Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of the 2026 draft:
“Well, he had a thumb injury, which kind of kept him out for a little bit, and then since coming back, think he's become more of a safety valve for Geno Smith, especially with Breece Hall being out the lineup too. If you're getting opponents pressuring you and blitzing you regularly, then you need somebody that can kind of get you out of those situations. That's something Mason Taylor can do, kind of find those soft spots in the zone, get some 4- or 5-yard catches and just kind of move the chains down the fiel. He has a different kind of athleticism than Kenyon Sadiq. I think Sadiq is more of a genetic freak, running 4.3, where I think Mason Taylor is more that guy that can move the chains, is just going to be a possession guy, and there's nothing wrong with that. "
On this idea that Malik Willis is very similar to former Jets starter Justin Fields:
“Here's the thing. Like, at least Malik is not afraid to throw the ball down the field. Now, hethere's times where he shouldn't, but he's not afraid to take those chances down the field. I feel like Justin Fields was very scared and hesitant to throw the ball past 10 yards. I don't see the comparison whatsoever. Justin was very cautious, like overly cautious of taking the football, protecting the football. Malik, I don't think it's that at all. He should be sometimes, but I don't think he is. So, no, I don't think that's a good comparison at all.”

title: Division Clincher, "Fail Mary" Highlight List of Best Dolphins Road Victories vs. the Jets in the 2000s
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins' first road game against the New York Jets in the 2000s produced one of the wildest fourth-quarter comebacks in NFL history — or worst fourth-quarter collapses, depending on your viewpoint.
It was part of a very rough start for Miami in those away games against their AFC opponents from the New York/New Jersey area in the new millennium, though the Dolphins have evened things out at 13 wins apiece heading into their 27th matchup of the 2000s in the Northeast this Sunday at MetLife Stadium.
Here is our countdown of the Dolphins' top five of those 13 victories at Giants Stadium, Meadowlands Stadium or MetLife Stadium against the Jets in the 2000s.
We start our countdown with one of those rare games — the only one we can remember, actually — where the punter was the difference-maker. In this game under cloudy skies, the Dolphins offense was brutal to the tune of 131 total yards and two turnovers, not to mention going 3-for-15 on third downs. The defense did hold New York to 280 yards, but the difference was Brandon Fields averaging 56.4 yards with an absurd net of 49.6 yards. A big example of Fields' brilliance that day came with Miami leading 10-3 on the second play of the fourth quarter and having to punt from its 7-yard line. Fields unleashed a 69-yard punt and even after an 11-yard run, that produced a 58-yard net that had the Jets starting at their own 35.
The term "Hail Mary" had been used before to describe the fiasco produced by an apparent (or obvious) officiating mistake that changed the outcome of a Green Bay-Seattle game on a, you guessed it, Hail Mary. But it was more appropriate here because this was a bad player fail, with the culprit being future Dolphins QB Tim Boyle and the hero/beneficiary being former Dolphins safety Jevon Holland. For those who don't remember, the Dolphins were in full control leading 10-0 against the Jets heading toward halftime until a pick-six gave New York some life. Holland's touchdown off a brilliant return basically ended all suspense.
Talk about coming up big as a backup quarterback. With the Dolphins in the midst of a playoff run, Matt Moore had to start this Saturday night game after Ryan Tannehill went out the previous week with a knee injury, and he lit up the Jets for four touchdown passes. Those came after a pair of future Dolphins — QB Bryce Petty and WR Robbie Chosen — connected on a 40-yard touchdown pass to give the Jets an early 7-0. The Dolphins' other touchdown came on a blocked punt return by Walt Aikens, which we bring up because ...
Yep, more special teams fireworks, this time courtesy of Ted Ginn Jr. The Dolphins' controversial 2007 first-round pick — who absolutely was overdrafted, but still had a productive NFL career — made NFL history with not one but two kickoff returns for touchdowns in the third quarter alone. Oh, and that third quarter also featured a 48-yard fumble return for another Miami touchdown by Jason Taylor. Those big plays allowed the Dolphins to score 30 points and steal a victory despite the offense being held to a meager 104 total yards.
As the Dolphins going through this rebuilding 2026 season, it's always nice to look back on those days when the team was able to win the AFC East title. It hasn't happened in 18 years, but it was an oh-so-satisfying capper to an improbable run just one year after the Dolphins were 1-15 — and certainly a measure of hope for fans going through the pain of 2026. That seven-point win against the Jets in 2008 was highlighted by defensive end Phillip Merling's pick-six in the second quarter, but don't forget about QB Chad Pennington — maybe the most important player in the amazing turnaround after the Jets discarded him for Brett Favre and the Dolphins gladly scooped him up in August of that year — converting a massive fourth-and-1 with a run that basically clinched the victory and the division title.

title: Would the Dolphins Really Consider Trading Jordyn Brooks?
full_text:
It seems everybody, or just about everybody is fair game when it comes to the NFL trade deadline and the Miami Dolphins.
It was expected that we would see the names of Zach Sieler and Austin Jackson mentioned among trade candidates given their contract status and age, plus the obvious situation in which the franchise finds itself.
That one, we have to say, surprised us when we saw him included in a list of top 50 trade candidates put together by The Athletic.
Yet there was Brooks at number 21, between Jets edge defender Will McDonald IV and Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley.
"The Dolphins are executing their tank effectively," writer Daniel Popper began. "They have remained moderately competitive while still losing five straight games to begin the season. Their rookie class looks promising. The next step would be accruing some more draft capital for 2027. One issue, though, is they do not have many tradable players. Brooks, a reliable veteran off-ball linebacker, is one of the few. He signed a three-year extension in July and has close to $13 million in guaranteed salary in 2027, so any acquiring team would be making a multiyear commitment. The Dolphins would take on $15.6 million in dead money in 2027 if they traded Brooks. This regime, with coach Jeff Hafley and GM Jon-Eric Sullivan, has not been afraid of dead money thus far."
Brooks' name came in trade speculation in the offseason, with the Dallas Cowboys and Cincinnati Bengals mentioned as logical suitors, and Popper mentioned the Cowboys, Bills and Steelers are potential trade partners now.
But the big question here is simple: Why would the Dolphins trade Brooks only a few months after giving him a contract extension that included a $20 million signing bonus?
If they were to trade Brooks, the Dolphins would be on the hook for Brooks' bonus when it comes to the cap space on top of already having signed that check.
After the Dolphins signed Brooks to his extension after doing the same with De'Von Achane and Aaron Brewer, GM Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley both spoke of making sure to hang on to franchise "pillars," good players who do things the way the Dolphins want them done.
Hafley also talked about showing players that the franchise will reward those who produce and do things the right way.
What kind of message would it send to sign Brooks to an extension and then trade him in the middle of a season that's gone not too far from where the organization figured it would or could go after they dumped high-profile veterans and saddled themselves with $180 million of dead space to clear the books for future years.
Sure, Sullivan has shown a willingness to take dead cap money if it accomplishes a goal, but what goal would be accomplished by dumping Brooks if the Dolphins can't get a premium pick in return.
And that's what it boils down, as always, because there's no player for whom the Dolphins shouldn't entertain an offer too good to be true.
But what could the Dolphins realistically expect to get for Brooks?
In terms of his appeal and market value, he probably was more valuable in the offseason coming off his All-Pro season than he is right now after dealing with an injury in training camp and then leaving the Week 5 game against the Cincinnati Bengals with a foot injury.
Would a third- or fourth-round pick in 2027 be more valuable to the Dolphins than having Brooks next season and the one after, both in terms of talent but also in terms of intangibles — Brooks' leadership plus keeping the player you just extended?
The bottom line is stranger things have happened, which is why we'll never say never, but a Brooks trade seemed a lot more likely then than it does now because making a deal months after giving a player an extension and giving him $20 million in signing bonus just doesn't compute.

title: Examining the Pending Dolphins UFAs Who Could Be Playing Their Way to an Extension
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins roster has a lot of new faces this year, and it figures to be the same thing next season as they continue the rebuilding project that began with the regime change.
The Dolphins have 22 players currently on their roster who are scheduled to become free agents in 2026 and the questions is how many of them will be back for another go-around.
The breakdown of free agents includes 12 UFAs free to sign with any other team barring the Dolphins using the franchise tag, which we already can tell you is highly unlikely given the financial commitment to a single player; five RFAs, who require a qualifying tender for the right to match an offer they might receive from another team; and and five ERFAs, who the Dolphins basically will keep if they want because any qualifying tender gives them exclusive rights to those players.
The 13 pending UFAs are T Austin Jackson, TE Greg Dulcich, CB JuJu Brents, P Bradley Pinion, CB Darrell Baker Jr., WR Jalen Tolbert, EDGE Joshua Uche, LB Willie Gay Jr., S Zayne Anderson, LB Ronnie Harrison Jr., EDGE Malik Herring and EDGE Robert Beal Jr.
The five pending RFAs are OL Jarrett Kingston, LB Shaka Heyward, TE Cole Turner (who's on IR), WR Jared Wayne and C Andrew Meyer.
The five pending ERFAs are LS Tucker Addington, LB Jackson Woodard, T Chukwuebuka Godrick, CB Reese Taylor and QB Kyle McCord.
As we evaluate the outlook for those players and their status with the team, we should not it's entirely possible — if not downright probable — that some of them will be gone before the end of this season.
But, for now, here are our best projections as to which players will be back in 2027, understanding that for UFAs it's a two-way street that requires both the team and the player to want to continue working together.
CB JuJu Brents — This is a player the Dolphins should prioritize because he still continues to perform at a high level and plays a premium position. The ability to stay healthy has been the issue so far in Brents' career, but he hasn't missed a game yet (knock on wood) so far in 2026.
TE Greg Dulcich — The Dolphins showed they valued him by giving him considerably more than most of their other free agents when they re-signed him in the offseason, though they did make it a one-year deal. But he's still pretty young, has good upside, and it's not like the Dolphins are swimming in high-end tight ends.
EDGE Joshua Uche — While he's been around a bit, Uche still is only 29 years old and he's been easily the second-best edge defender on the team, if not the best. The biggest question with him is whether the Dolphins will resist the temptation to move him before the trade deadline if a team offers a draft pick in a trade.
P Bradley Pinion — Yes, this might sound weird, particularly since Pinion is 33, but the fact is he's punted well all season — we can forgive him that blip when he dropped the ball proceeding to get into his punting motion — he's not expensive and punters can work in the NFL into their late 30s with no issues.
T Austin Jackson — Despite his poor Pro Football Focus standing (he's dead last among all NFL tackles), Jackson is a solid veteran tackle who's simply off to a bad start. The issue with Jackson is how it would cost to bring him back in what probably wouldn't be a starting role and whether he even would be interested in that idea after being asked to take a pay cut this year.
WR Jalen Tolbert — It's hard to imagine the veteran wide receiver wanting to come back to Miami after he found himself behind not only Malik Washington but the team's three draft picks at the position — Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr.
S Zayne Anderson — The special teams specialist got his big chance when he was in the starting lineup at safety in the opener, but he's now gone back to his previous role of working mostly in the kicking game. He's also 30 years old, which won't make him a priority to bring back.
LB Ronnie Harrison Jr. — Harrison was one of the latest free agent acquisitions in the offseason and he made the 53-man roster after a strong training camp showing. But he's been out since Week 1 because of a hamstring injury and he's also 30 years old.
The lowest qualifying tender for restricted free agents in 2026, which simply gave teams to right to match an outside offer with no compensation if declined, was $3.5 million. None of the pending RFAs signed for more than $1.1 million this year, so it's highly unlikely — if not an outright foregone conclusion — the Dolphins will not be extending any qualifying offers.
That means the Dolphins then would have to decide which to try to bring back, and we've got three we've got pegged as most likely to return.
OL Jarrett Kingston — Kingston, claimed off waivers from the Houston Texans, had a solid outing in relief of Jonah Savaiinaea in the Week 5 game against Cincinnati.
OL Andrew Meyer — The Dolphins have been developing Meyer for three years now and offensive linemen always are a valuable commodity.
TE Cole Turner — That the Dolphins placed Turner on injured reserve in training camp and didn't simply waive him injury suggests they think he's got potential worth investigating.

title: Vikings vs. Colts: Who Wins and Why in Week 7
full_text:
Just a year ago, the Indianapolis Colts pushed all their chips in, giving quarterback Daniel Jones a monster extension, and doling out two-first round picks for cornerback Sauce Gardner. Life comes at you fast, though, and the 2-4 Colts have now fired the man responsible for those decisions in long-time general manager Chris Ballard after the team lost to the previously winless Titans in Week 6.
But despite hitting rock bottom, Indy still has some nice pieces on both sides of the ball, and Minnesota would be foolish to overlook them on their quest for 6-0. It's the Vikings and Colts in Week 7, so let's get into who wins and why in this Midwest battle.
Outside of guard Donovan Jackson, who is out for the season with a knee injury, the Vikings enter this matchup at near full strength, something that hasn't been the case since Week 1.
Justin Jefferson and the now healthy Jordan Addison have played just 18 snaps together this season, while Jordan Mason is finally back after spending four weeks on injured reserve. The stage is set for what could be the best offensive performance of the year.
The Colts defense will also be without their best player, as Gardner couldn't get his calf right in time to suit up. That's good news for the Vikings pass-catchers, who need to find some momentum soon, and bad news for a Colts team that has allowed 30 or more points four times this season. Mason and Aaron Jones should be in line for big days too, as the Colts have already allowed three 100-yard rushers this season despite an impressive interior defensive line.
Cam Bynum, the former Viking, and ironically, the one player this defense could really use right now, has five interceptions since joining Indianapolis last season and could be the X-factor on defense.
Ultimately, the Vikings are an ascending unit on offense, and the Colts haven't shown the ability to stop anyone besides a third-string Commanders quarterback so far this season.
Vikings legend Daniel Jones hasn't lived up to his expensive contract this season, and ranks near the bottom in most major quarterback metrics. Over the past three weeks, he's completed just 54% of his passes and thrown one touchdown to three interceptions. His nine total turnovers and 15 sacks on the year certainly don't stack up well to a Viking defense elite at creating both.
Star rusher Jonathan Taylor has seven rushing touchdowns, but still has yet to notch a 100-yard game this season with his pedestrian four yards per carry. Meanwhile, the Vikings defense has allowed more than 50 yards to a rusher just once all season. Taylor has been linked to the Vikings as a potential trade candidate, and Minnesota will get an up-close-and-personal look this Sunday.
The Vikings league best +6 turnover margin and the Colts' league worst -8 will likely tell the story of this game, and Indy will have to play clean game to find a win in Minneapolis. That, or hope Spencer Shrader can continue his perfect season with a multiple 50+ yard field goals.

title: Ivan Pace Jr.'s Time With the Vikings Could End Sooner Rather Than Later
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings' defense is thriving under coordinator Brian Flores, and a significant reason for that success is the linebacker play. Starting interior linebackers Blake Cashman and Eric Wilson are playing so well that it is hard to take them off the field, which has led to a drastic decrease in snaps for Ivan Pace Jr.
Pace has played in all five games for the Vikings this season, but he has only participated in 45 of 295 possible defensive snaps. Even scarier is that he has played a total of seven defensive snaps in the last two games, getting only two against the New Orleans Saints in Week 5.
Eventually, rookie linebacker Jake Golday will start cutting into those snaps as well. The 23-year-old second-round draft pick has been getting a lot of experience by playing 95 special teams snaps in his first five games, but has been limited on defense, getting only seven defensive snaps.
Pace is only 25 years old but is in his fourth season in the NFL. His snap count on defense has decreased with every passing season since being signed as an undrafted free agent in 2023, but it can't get much lower than the 16 percent that he is playing this season.
It was a little surprising when the Vikings signed Pace to a one-year extensio n this offseason worth $3.52 million to stay in Minnesota for the 2026 NFL season, since the team was going to move forward with Cashman and Wilson as starters and drafted Golday with an early selection.
For now, Pace is essentially earning $3.52 million for his work on special teams. However, even his work in that phase of the game is shrinking, and he had his lowest special teams snap count of the season (17) in Week 5 against the Saints.
With Pace on a one-year deal and his role on defense and special teams shrinking, it is difficult not to feel like the clock is ticking on his future with the Vikings.
If a team with a need for an interior linebacker called with a mid-to-late-round draft pick as a trade offer for him, Minnesota general manager Nolan Teasley would be foolish not to listen to the pitch and consider the offer.
Otherwise, he may continue to be phased out of Minnesota's plans until he is eventually inactive on game day.

title: Vikings Week 7: Potential Trade Targets Among Most Important Things to Watch for vs. Colts
full_text:
Fans will once again fill the stands at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday as the Vikings return from a much-needed bye week break to host a Colts team desperate to turn their season around .
While everything suggests this should be a straightforward matchup for Minnesota, longtime fans know they can never write off an opponent . Let’s break down three key things to watch as the Vikings look to achieve their first 6-0 start since 2009.
The NFL trade deadline is rapidly approaching, and the Vikings are possible buyers. The Colts, meanwhile, fired their general manager six weeks into the season, signaling that anything short of a rapid change of fortune on the field could lead to a fire sale .
The Colts have several players who could be targets for a contender like the Vikings. Names floated over blogs, podcasts and social media include defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, left guard Quenton Nelson and even a possible reunion with former Vikings safety Cam Bynum.
The hottest name, though, is three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor.
While Minnesota may have no interest in acquiring any of the players listed, Sunday’s game gives general manager Nolan Teasley a chance to evaluate whether he wants to take a swing or two. If Teasley likes what he sees, a decisive Vikings win may be the nudge the Colts need to start answering phone calls.
Minnesota’s offense finally showed some life before the bye week, and the return of some familiar faces may take it to the next level. Thursday’s injury report listed every player on the 53-man roster as a full participant, providing a massive sigh of relief for Vikings fans everywhere (h/t: Vikings).
Barring setbacks, the team should see the return of Christian Darrisaw, Jordan Addison, Jordan Mason, and T.J. Hockenson.
Thursday's #Vikings injury report pic.twitter.com/EVmLOt2D49
While Minnesota is still dealing with the season-long losses of Donovan Jackson and Josh Oliver, Sunday will be the closest the offense has been to “full strength” since Week 1. The opportunity for the offense to gel against a spotty defense could not come at a better time as they prepare to face a gauntlet of top-end teams over November.
If the offense looks sluggish with a full slate of weapons, it may be time to worry about how sustainable that side of the ball could be.
Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier. Magic Johnson and Larry Bird. Tom Brady and Peyton Manning. These are just some of the greatest matchups in sports history, and Sunday’s Colts-Vikings game will feature the next great battle of titans, as kickers Spencer Shrader and Will Reichard battle for supremacy.
In all seriousness, this game could very likely turn into a special teams shootout. Shrader and Reichard are both at the top of their craft, with Shrader’s 66 points scored through six games currently leading the NFL. His 11 points per game put him just above Reichard’s average of 10.6 over five games played (h/t: NFL Films ).
Don't mess with Will the Thrill 😮‍💨 @Vikings | @InsideTheNFL pic.twitter.com/n1CmRxSRje
Reichard’s 34-made-field-goal streak dating back to last season puts him just two kicks away from breaking Gary Anderson’s franchise record of 35. Hall of Fame kicker Adam Vinatieri holds the NFL record with 44.

title: Vikings Have No Excuse to Keep Sidelining Forgotten Rookie Amid Safety Concerns
full_text:
The Vikings have a real problem at safety . Veterans Harrison Smith and Josh Metellus are ranked among the ten worst safeties in the NFL this season, ranking dead last and sixth-worst, respectively, on Pro Football Focus . Despite the success of defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit, a change is needed.
That said, the answer to Minnesota's safety issues might already be on the team's roster—a 2026 NFL Draft pick has yet to make an impact this season.
The Vikings selected Jakobe Thomas with the 98th overall pick in April, yet he hasn't played a single snap this season. The 6'1", 211-lb defensive back was inactive for each of Minnesota's five games before the bye, which doesn't bode well for his chances against the Colts in Week 7 .
Thomas played in one preseason game after working hard to recover from a back injury sustained during training camp. In that exhibition game against the Broncos, he had five tackles, three of which were solo efforts. His 79.4 tackling grade ranked second-best among Vikings defenders that game, according to PFF , while his 66.0 run defense grade was seventh-best.
Now that he's healthy and the safety room needs all the help it can get, Thomas needs to be active on game day.
Even if he only gets started on special teams, getting the former Miami (FL) and Tennessee defensive back some on-field experience could go a long way in preparing him for the future.
On Friday, Andrew Krammer of the Minnesota Star Tribune shared an article about Thomas that included a quote from Vikings special teams coordinator Matt Daniels. Apparently, the rookie safety has been asking when he will finally get on the field in a regular-season game.
The 23-year-old safety is chomping at the bit to get some reps this season. Considering how Smith and Metellus have struggled this season , it is imperative that the Vikings find a way to take pressure off Theo Jackson.
Jackson has played 191 defensive snaps for Minnesota this season and has the highest PFF grade among Vikings safeties this year, at 63.7. That's still not great, since it ranks him 41st out of 98 qualifying safeties across the NFL.
It is time to see Thomas finally play some snaps for the Vikings, and that should start in Week 7. He needs to be active on game day to prepare for a future where he steps into a defensive role for the Purple and Gold and helps keep Flores's defense among the NFL's most feared units.

title: Jordan Mason's Return Brings Much-Needed Changes to Vikings' RB Room in Week 7
full_text:
After spending the last four weeks on injured reserve with a thumb issue, Vikings running back Jordan Mason is now healthy and ready to suit up against the Colts on Sunday.
Mason enters the game with a questionable injury designation (h/t Vikings), but that's mostly just semantics, as he still technically needs to be activated off of injured reserve. So, assuming he kept his thumb wrestling to a minimum over the last month, Mason should have essentially no restrictions for Sunday.
With Aaron Jones still battling through a sprained MCL , how should the Vikings handle their freshly reformed backfield and the potential changes Mason's return could bring?
During Week 1—and the only game so far this season that the duo has played together—the Jones-Mason tandem notched a near 50/50 split, with Mason getting 15 carries to Jones's 12. That's been the plan along for Minnesota, and something similar could be in store for Sunday, but how well conditioned Mason is after the break, and how well Jones's knee is holding up could boost or drag these numbers in either direction.
Presumably, though, the answer to both of those questions is: good enough.
That means it's doubtful Mason gets put on a snap count, and equally doubtful that the Vikings completely put Jones on ice either despite running him ragged the past month. Mason averaged a pedestrian 3.9 yards per carry against Green Bay in the season opener, but the Colts' run defense ranks a hum-drum 22nd in the NFL this year, so he may find some more opportunity to get back on track after a month away.
And without reliable production coming from either DeeJay Dallas or Demond Claiborne, both starters should once again see double-digit touches. Look for Mason to get work on early downs, while Jones takes on more of a third-down back role, thanks in part to his pass-catching ability.
Speaking of Dallas and Claiborne, the return of Mason now means that the Vikings are rostering four running backs. That doesn't feel like something general manager Nolan Teasley wants to last, especially since the Vikings may look to bolster their depth elsewhere with the NFL trade deadline approaching on Tuesday, Nov. 10 .
With a possible deal to bring in more talent along the offensive line, secondary or even at running back, one of these reserves could be getting the boot.
Dallas has some special teams appeal, so rookie sixth-round pick Claiborne could be the one on the outside looking in sooner rather than later. He's logged just six carries for 13 yards on the season, and it likely wouldn't be too difficult to pass a late-round pick with no production down through waivers to the practice squad. It'll be something to monitor moving forward.
How the backs fare against Indianapolis will likely determine some of those plans, and if Mason looks sluggish, or Jones's condition deteriorates, anything could be on the table over the course of the next three weeks.

title: 5 Pending Vikings Free Agents Already Deserve Contract Extensions
full_text:
The Vikings are surprising everyone with their hot start to the season. The team's 5-0 record has fans dreaming about an NFC North title and a deep playoff run, which makes the future look bright for the Purple and Gold.
Several key contributors on the Vikings' roster have contracts expiring at the end of the 2026 NFL season. Those players will need an extension to stay in Minnesota; otherwise, they will seek a role with another franchise.
There are five players for Minnesota who will become unrestricted free agents if they aren't re-signed. The problem is that the Vikings are estimated to have approximately $37.5 million in salary cap space , according to Spotrac , but still need to re-sign players and add talent to replace any players who are lost.
The offseason is a ways away, but here's a look at the players who have earned contract extensions to stay with the Vikings past the 2026 NFL season.
Pairing Andrew Van Ginkel with Dallas Turner as the Vikings' edge rushers has been a recipe for success this year. To stay with Minnesota, Van Ginkel signed a one-year, $23 million deal and has rewarded the Purple and Gold by racking up 14 combined tackles, eight quarterback hits, four sacks, a forced fumble, and an interception in five games.
The 31-year-old edge rusher has played 249 defensive snaps this season and has a Pro Football Focus grade of 74 . His 78.4 pass-rush grade is highlighted by 18 pressures that have kept opposing quarterbacks on their toes.
T.J. Hockenson will be 30 years old next season, but he has been one of the few players to step up offensively this season for the Vikings. In five games, he has caught 23 of 27 targets for 202 yards and a touchdown, earning a 77.5 PFF grade that ranks him fifth among all qualifying tight ends.
Hockenson is playing the 2026 season on a one-year deal worth $10.25 million, and the two-time Pro Bowl pass-catcher will likely get a similar deal at the conclusion of this season. He hasn't dropped a single pass and has accumulated 80 yards after the catch so far this season, so he shows no signs of slowing down.
The combination of Eric Wilson and Blake Cashman as Minnesota's interior linebackers has been stout. Cashman is in the final year of his three-year, $22.5 million contract, and the 30-year-old Minnesota native will likely be one of the team's top priorities to re-sign this offseason.
Cashman has played 281 defensive snaps this year on his way to a 73 PFF grade. His solid grade was earned by being a statistical monster this season. He leads the team with 42 combined tackles while having seven hits on opposing quarterbacks, four tackles for a loss, 2.5 sacks, a pass defense and a fumble recovery.
Minnesota trusted Isaiah Rodgers to be a breakout player when the team signed him as a free agent, and he has delivered. He is likely going to get a significant raise from the two-year, $11.045 million contract he signed, based on his playing over 90% of the defensive snaps.
This season, Rodgers has played in all five games so far, getting 15 combined tackles, four pass defenses, an interception, and a fumble recovery. His stellar 87.9 PFF grade shouldn't be a surprise to any fan who has watched him play this season.
The Vikings are probably moving on from Aaron Jones Sr. at running back after this season, which makes bringing Jordan Mason back even more important. Minnesota's RB2 has missed time recovering from surgery on an injured thumb.
Mason hasn't played enough snaps to qualify for a PFF grade this season, but he had 15 carries for 59 yards and a touchdown in Week 1 against the Packers. The 27-year-old rusher will get a raise from his previous two-year, $10.5 million contract when general manager Nolan Teasley re-signs him during the offseason.

title: 3 Vikings Lineup Decisions I'd Make If I Were Kevin O'Connell vs. the Colts in Week 7
full_text:
The bye week provided a perfect opportunity for the Vikings to get healthy and regroup.
Now, in Week 7, the Vikings have plenty of things to figure out ahead of the upcoming NFL trade deadline , and this matchup against the Colts may be the ideal platform to determine the best path forward .
So with a 6-0 start and potential future deals on the line, here are three changes I would make if I were in head coach Kevin O'Connell's shoes against the Colts this weekend.
Jordan Mason has logged multiple full practices this week, and looks like a full go for Sunday after spending the last four weeks on injured reserve with a fractured thumb. With the recent news that Aaron Jones's banged-up knee is actually a sprained MCL , there's really no reason not to lean on Mason heavily against Indianapolis.
Giving Mason a good look on Sunday is more than just letting Jones get a breather; it's also a chance to see if the Vikings duo can perform well enough to hold off on a trade deadline deal . If Mason returns with some energy, Minnesota potentially strides past the Nov. 10 deadline without adding another back.
Either way, getting Mason involved again will be a huge boost to the work-in-progress offense.
Beckham has been coming along just fine since joining the Vikings two weeks ago, according to O'Connell, but he should take another back seat in Week 7 for one very good reason.
Despite the temptation to see what Beckham can do, the Vikings still need to find out whether Jauan Jennings will be part of this team going forward. Trying to work Beckham in while also implementing some looks for Jennings is just too convoluted.
Ideally, Jennings shows some juice and leaves Beckham as some valuable veteran insurance down the road. But if the disappointing free agent drops another dud, the Vikings may look to fire up the trade machine .
Beckham, meanwhile, has no trade value, and the Vikings shouldn't be in a rush to put him on the field. He can sit and learn the playbook for another week while O'Connell and general manager Nolan Teasley figure out Jennings' situation.
The second-rounder has played just seven defensive snaps this season, but after some strong special teams play, it might be time to give rookie linebacker Jake Golday some run on defense.
Golday forced a fumble on a kickoff return against the Saints, and may parlay that into a bigger role. Typically, Ivan Pace Jr. has been the first linebacker off the bench, but after logging just five and then two snaps over the last two contests, he may be falling out of favor. Enter Golday, who has seen action at both edge and off-ball linebacker and should now be in line for possibly double-digit snaps on defense.
The Vikings' rookie class hasn't been incredibly impactful in 2026 , but maybe Golday can change that trend, starting this week against the Colts.

title: Analyzing What a Jonathan Taylor Trade Could Look Like for the Vikings
full_text:
The Nov. 10  NFL trade deadline is fast approaching, and Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley will face some incredibly difficult decisions. With minimal input on the current roster after being hired in June, the coming weeks will be his first chance to shape the organization's present and future. While there are a few paths to choose from, one potential home run swing has become a dream scenario for many Vikings fans.
Colts running back Jonathan Taylor has quickly become a name to watch as a possible trade candidate after the firing of general manager Chris Ballard signaled a possible fire sale in Indianapolis. Luckily for Teasley and the Vikings, they’ll get a close look when Taylor and the Colts come to town this weekend.
But could the Vikings even pull off a move this big? Heck, is there even a need for it? Let’s break down what a deal could look like and if it’s worth pursuing.
Taylor is fresh off signing a two-year, $44 million extension in August that carried him through the 2028 season. Now, the Colts must decide on their long-term future.
As it stands, trading Taylor before June 1 would hit the Colts with over $7.5 million in dead money in 2026 , per Spotrac . That dead money rises to $10 million in 2027 before dropping to $5 million in 2028. Simply put, trading Taylor wouldn’t remove him entirely from Indy’s books, but it would free up over $8.6 million in cap space this season that the Colts wouldn't have.
Now, Minnesota’s side of the equation comes into play.
According to Spotrac , the Vikings have $4.1 million in cap space available for 2026 , far less than Taylor's current cap hit of approximately $16.19 million before any offsets. Teasley and executive vice president Rob Brzezinski would need to find creative ways to create more cap space through restructures, extensions, or trading away other players. Their projected $37.5 million in cap space for 2027 will likely increase once the NFL announces the final cap number for the year, but several impending roster holes will make things tricky.
Let’s say the financials can be worked out—now it’s time to talk trade compensation.
Acquiring a player of Taylor’s pedigree will not come cheap, and other suitors will likely only drive the price up further. Minnesota will likely need to offer its 2027 second-round pick to close the deal. There are clearly numerous hoops to jump through for any of this to work, but the question is: is it worth it?
With Aaron Jones off to the best start of his career and Jordan Mason returning from injury, a running back acquisition does not exactly seem like a top priority. But with Jones and Mason both in the final years of their current deals, finding a talented long-term upgrade now could prove to be the best decision. The announcement that Jones has been playing through a sprained MCL adds even more urgency to find stability at the position.
With Teasley fresh off a Super Bowl win in Seattle led by Kenneth Walker, I have a hard time thinking he doesn't at least make a call or two about Taylor. The ultimate decision will come down to his assessment of the 2026 Vikings. If he believes this roster can truly win it all, he may take the swing and go all in.
If his priorities are long-term roster construction, Teasley will likely retain his draft picks and see where the current roster can go.
