title: ‘Guys Gotta Step Up:’ Saquon Barkley Sends Message to Eagles Ahead of MNF Return
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Top-tier athletes are often hardest on themselves, a common trait among high achievers. There is a fine line, though, between productive self-scouting and slipping into a negative mindset.
Eagles star running back Saquon Barkley, expected to return Monday night against the Cowboys after missing two games with a hamstring injury, has worked to manage that balance as his NFL career has progressed.
Barkley, who recently took up golf, used that sport as an example.
“Some of you guys are golfers. When you think about the next shot after a bad one, you’re just like, ‘Oh, no. No.’ You stand no chance,” Barkley explained. “Someone was playing with Tiger Woods, and even he was hard on himself. It was never in a negative way. He always had a mindset that the next putt’s gonna go in or the next shot’s gonna be great. … You gotta take that to the field, right? And that’s just like the game.
As poorly as the Eagles played offensively against the Panthers in Week 6, Barkley noted they were one drive away from flipping the script in what ended as a 25-14 loss.
“We did not put together our best game on offense, and before you know it, we were one drive away,” Barkley said. “After we just scored a touchdown, the defense made a stop. We had a great special teams play, and we got the ball back in our hands.
“Then on that drive we had a missed snap, and just like that it was second-and-21. We keep doing stuff like that to put us behind the sticks.”
Barkley’s point was that the game was still there if the offense had executed better.
“Going into that drive, that game was right there for the taking, ready for us to win,” the Eagles' RB1 said. “We can’t lose sight of that, and that’s just how the NFL works. At any moment it can change, and we got the guys for it. I’m excited. I love the install that we have in for Dallas. I think Tanner [McKee’s] a great leader of men also.”
While acknowledging the adversity of losing players like starting tackle Lane Johnson to retirement and franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts to blood clots , Barkley said it’s time for others to step up.
“It’s time," Barkley said. "Guys gotta grow up. Guys gotta step up. That’s why this is a big-boy league, and we have the guys, and I’m excited for it.”

title: One Eagles Rookie Could Be the Next Late-Round Pick to Break Out
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Rookie Keyshawn James-Newby doesn’t have to look very far to see the success a seventh-round draft pick can make. All the Eagles' outside linebacker needs to do is walk a few stalls deeper into the locker room where Moro Ojomo stows his gear.
Further toward the back of the locker room is another former seventh-rounder—left tackle Jordan Mailata from 2018, who is already on his third contract with the Eagles. Ojomo was a seventh-round pick in 2023 and is playing himself into a second contract that should pay him handsomely, either back in Philly or in another city.
The Eagles have had some recent success mining talent in the final round of the draft, and James-Newby could be the latest to emerge. There could also be some success stories in waiting, considering the Eagles drafted two others in the seventh round last spring – defensive tackle Uar Bernard and safety Cole Wisniewski, both of whom were taken earlier in the round ahead of James-Newby.
“Whether you're first or seventh or a free agent, everyone has odds to beat,” James-Newby said at his locker earlier this week. “It doesn't really matter where you're at, you know? Everyone has odds to beat. … I can't look in the future, I can't look in the past, and I just gotta continue forward and take it day by day.”
The Eagles didn’t have seventh-round picks in 2022, 2024 or 2025. In 2021, they selected Patrick Johnson, who played 58 games with two starts in five years in Philly. He is still in the league, playing a big special teams role for the Raiders.
James-Newby—who is 6'1", 240 lbs—burst onto the scene last week against the Panthers after being elevated from the practice squad for the first time this year. He played 48 snaps (61%) on defense and 24 more (83%) on special teams, earning praise from both the defensive and special teams coordinators.
It was a huge jump for James-Newby, as it was after he was released at the end of training camp. General manager Howie Roseman said he was concerned that his seventh-round pick would be claimed, but James-Newby wasn’t and was added back to the practice squad.
“It's kind of a credit to him being a rookie, first time really playing in a big game, and I thought he did a solid job, and he's going to keep getting better and better the more times he's able to go out there and do it,” said ST coordinator Michael Clay. “I thought he did a fairly good job for us being that first time, and there's always things to improve on.”
Added defensive coordinator Vic Fangio: “He’s a pretty good athlete. He's got some speed to him. I think he'll even do better now that he's got his feet wet more than he expected, or we expected. I do like him, and I think hopefully we'll see steady progress from him the more he gets to play.”
James-Newby made only one tackle but showed enough in other areas to earn another elevation, or even a roster spot, as the Eagles prepare to host the Cowboys on Monday Night Football.
James-Newby played more than he probably expected after Nolan Smith left last week’s game with a concussion . The outside linebacker was in concussion protocol to start the week.
“Keyshawn has never once, no matter the circumstance, gotten down on himself,” outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt said. “You can tell some things frustrate him, but it doesn't change the fact that he's coming back out. He's gonna go 100 miles an hour whenever he can. He's gonna ask questions when he doesn't know something, and he's gonna work to be the best at what he can do.”
KJN spent time at three different colleges: Montana Tech, Idaho, and New Mexico, where he spent his final season before the draft. At New Mexico, he made 15 tackles for loss with nine sacks.
He understands that the NFL is a different level, and there are things he needs to do to become the next Ojomo or Mailata.
“I wouldn't say necessarily work on,” James-Newby said. “I would just say get better at some specific moves. I only have a couple of moves, and those moves are the moves I always like to use, and I always will continue to use. I just have to become more accurate with them, and it'll work out in my favor.”

title: Joe Milton Left Cowboys for Eagles With Starting Job in His Sights
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A.  — For the foreseeable future, Tanner McKee will have an opportunity to try to stabilize a struggling Eagles offense .
The next in line from there may be Joe Milton, the lengthy, cannon-armed Michigan Man turned Tennessee Volunteer who has been working behind the scenes with New England and Dallas over the past two-plus seasons as a developmental quarterback.
The call came from Philadelphia while Milton was still on the Cowboys' practice squad. His agent mentioned the Eagles were interested in adding him after it became clear Jalen Hurts would be headed to injured reserve . Milton went through a normal day of work, got in his car afterward and realized everything had changed.
“I was just like, ‘What am I gonna do? Am I gonna stay on practice squad or should I show up for my opportunity?’ I’m here, so,” Milton told Eagles On SI .
The 6-foot-5 Sunshine State native chose the clearer opportunity.
The Eagles officially signed Milton off Dallas’s practice squad and put him on their 53-man roster before the Week 6 game against Carolina after Hurts was sidelined indefinitely with pulmonary blood clots.
McKee is the starter for now, with Milton joining the room alongside rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton. The move puts Milton on a potential collision course with his former team when the Cowboys visit Lincoln Financial Field on Monday Night Football.
Milton was surprised it was a rival who called.
“Yeah. Just because it is a rival, and it was just like, you know, dang, like no way,” Milton said. “But my agent called me and mentioned it to me.”
At first Milton compartmentalized.
“I went to practice like it was a normal day and just tried to operate as a Dallas Cowboy at the time, and I went home.”
From there, Milton quickly understood the direction he should go.
The timing is imperfect for everyone involved. Milton offered prayers for Hurts, noting he had spoken with the Eagles quarterback a couple of times while still in college.
“Obviously, I talked to (Jalen) a couple times before I even got here, like when I was in college, so we don’t have a strong relationship, but I’d talked to him before, so all prayers out to him for sure,” Milton said.
Milton's development in Dallas had been going well, and he has leaned on that foundation while absorbing a new system.
“My development was going well in Dallas. I feel like I’ve learned a lot, especially coming here and talking with the coaches and hearing this offense now. … I definitely learned a lot over there,” Milton said. “So shout out to [the Cowboys] for that. But development-wise it’s going great. It’s amazing. I love to learn, so here taking notes again and learning a new offense, so it’s amazing.”
Milton described what’s been a whirlwind process: “Plug in and play.”
That means getting the concepts down, understanding how runs are called, how the offense operates, and how the coordinator calls plays.
“So it was great to hear that on game day [against the Panthers],” Milton said.
Being on the other side of the Cowboys-Eagles rivalry feels different for Milton.
“Obviously I’m in another color now. And that’s a rival, but hey, can’t wear blue this week. I’m totally fine on that,” he said.
Milton downplayed the idea that he is here to offer up intel on the Cowboys' dynamic offense led by QB1 Dak Prescott.
For fans who do not know his style, Milton offered up a straightforward self-scouting report.
“Let things come to me and operate efficiently. Run enough, run if I have to,” he said.
Early impressions of the staff have been positive for Milton, particularly quarterbacks coach Parks Frazier, who has made a strong first impression.
“Oh, I love Parks, man. I love [OC] Sean [Mannion] too, but I love Parks. Parks was the first person, first coach I met here, and it’s pretty much, he took me under his wing,” said Milton. “He did what a coach is supposed to do in the right way, and he’s still doing it to this day.”
Milton arrived in Philadelphia with limited regular-season experience—no starts, 37 completions on 53 attempts for 424 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions—plus some rushing production, along with a strong preseason in Dallas.
Whether the opportunity with the Eagles leads to snaps against the Cowboys , or beyond, depends on how quickly he absorbs the offense and how the depth chart shakes out behind McKee. For now, Milton is focused on showing up and proving he belongs.
“Going on my second week, so yeah, man, I love what they’re doing upstairs. It’s great,” Milton said. “They come with the right energy every day. And shoot, they got the right mindset, and that’s what you need as a quarterback. And just take it with a grain of salt, but at the same time, Parks and Sean, they do a great job coaching and explaining why a play is in and what’s the definition of those plays for sure.”

title: 5 Eagles Who Will Likely Be Inactive vs. Cowboys in Week 7
full_text:
The Eagles could be getting a major contributor back for their Week 7 showdown with the rival Cowboys on Monday Night Football.
After missing the past two games for Philly due to a hamstring injury, star running back Saquon Barkley returned to the practice field ahead of the game against Dallas, and he's expected to be good to go for the game, barring a setback. While Barkley might be available for the Eagles, several other players likely won't be.
Here's a look at five Eagles players who are likely to be inactive for the seventh game of the season.
Safety Michael Carter II suffered an abdominal injury in London in Week 5 against the Jaguars that sidelined him for the remainder of the game. He then missed Philadelphia's Week 6 loss to the Panthers due to the injury, and he also missed the first practice of the week ahead of the Dallas game.
Barring a quick turnaround, it seems like Carter is trending towards a second consecutive absence for Philadelphia.
Nolan Smith tallied his third sack of the season in the first half of Philadelphia's game against Carolina last weekend. Unfortunately, he exited the game with a concussion shortly thereafter and didn't return.
Smith was placed in the league's concussion protocol, and he'll have to pass through it before he's cleared to return to the field for Philadelphia. It remains to be seen whether that happens or not. He didn't participate in the first practice of the week.
Landon Dickerson has missed five straight games for Philadelphia after being placed on the IR list with a knee injury following the first game of the season. The Eagles opened up the practice window for Dickerson last week, paving a path for him to return, but he didn't play in Week 6, and it remains to be seen if he'll play in Week 7, as he's now dealing with two separate injuries.
In addition to the knee issue, Dickerson is now apparently dealing with a pectoral injury as well.
Joe Milton is still getting acclimated to Philadelphia's playbook after being signed by the team last week, but it's unlikely that he'll be active for the game against his former franchise. The Eagles aren't likely to have three QBs on the active roster, so Milton will probably be the odd man out.
With Tanner McKee as the starter and Cole Payton as the backup, Milton was likely to serve as the emergency third quarterback, as he did in Week 6.
The Hollywood Brown experiment hasn't really worked out well in Philadelphia .
The speedy receiver has only appeared in one game for the Eagles on the campaign, and he hasn't registered a single catch. He missed several games due to an ankle injury, but he was a healthy scratch in Week 6. He could be in for a similar fate in Week 7,

title: Wide-Open NFC East Adding Urgency to Saquon Barkley's Injury Return
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — During his two-game absence from the field, Eagles running back Saquon Barkley has been talking the talk. Now, it appears as if he’s ready again to walk the walk, and in a subpar NFC East, a walk may be all it takes to finish at the top.
“The NFC East is really asking for someone to take it over ,” Barkley said. “It's gonna be a team that figures out and starts playing at a high level, and we have the opportunity; we have that chance.
“I'm not from this area, but I live close enough. I was raised close enough from this area. That's what Philly's about, man. We kind of have to take that underdog mentality. No one kind of believes us anymore, but there's a reason why there's a statue of a fictional boxer, and his name is Rocky.”
Barkley might be the Eagles’ Rocky on Monday night when the Cowboys visit Lincoln Financial Field . He wouldn't say if he's playing, but he was on the practice field Thursday and was listed as a limited participant.
“Sometimes it takes one play, it takes one drive, it takes one game to get this thing where we're going,” he said. “When I say one person, I mean an individual performance. It's just being on the sidelines and being in the huddle and just trying to provide that energy, and the energy can come from leadership. The energy can come from making a play.
“Sometimes that's all it takes. Hopefully I'm able. I just know that I'm doing everything I can to try to play.”
It’s a big game in the sense that both teams are 2-4 and on losing streaks. The winner will gain confidence and perhaps put themselves in position to start taking over the division.
Barkley knows he has a responsibility when he returns.
“There's a reason why we were voted captains,” said Barkley. “There's a reason why the leaders on the teams are leaders, and you're gonna see what you're really about. It's easy to come in this building and put on a smile and come to work when the world's patting you on the back, and you're 13-4, and you're the new, hottest thing and everyone's scared of the Eagles. It's a little challenging when it's the opposite way.”
Barkley has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury. He pushed to play last week, but doctors told him it was best to put another week behind him to make sure the injury is good to go.
Quarterback Tanner McKee was asked to throw the ball 45 times last week in his first start of the season. The Eagles ran just 12 times against a porous Panthers defense.  The QB talked on Thursday about how it took him a while to settle in and his feet weren’t as quiet as they should be. Yet the game plan dialed up 10 passes to start the game.
Having Barkley should help.
“Saquon is one of the best players in the NFL,” McKee said, “so I think having him back is gonna be great; super excited for him. Obviously, we've all seen what he can do. Just having another weapon out there is obviously great and exciting for a quarterback.”

title: 3 Realistic Riq Woolen Trade Destinations That Would Net Eagles Biggest Return
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is under three weeks away. In recent seasons, this is when general manager Howie Roseman would start searching for veterans to boost Philadelphia's roster in hopes of winning a Super Bowl. However, a disastrous first six weeks means he could be the one dealing talent away .
A four-game losing streak fueled by injuries has the Eagles facing an uphill battle to make the playoffs. Most notably, quarterback Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the rest of the season due to blood clots. That said, players across the roster could be floated in trade talks , especially those on expiring contracts.
Cornerback Riq Woolen, one of those expiring deals, was inked to a one-year, $12 million deal in March. The former Seahawk has been solid in coverage, surrendering 15 receptions for 187 yards (two touchdowns) in six games. He has allowed a 51.7% completion rate when targeted and racked up four pass breakups.
Here are three teams that would benefit from acquiring Woolen and have the ammunition to pull it off.
The Jaguars' need for help in the secondary became clear during their Week 6 loss to the Texans. Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud zeroed in on cornerback Jarrian Jones, who conceded six catches for 100 yards. He has been a liability all year, ranking 100th out of 102 cornerbacks in PFF's coverage grade.
Jones has been on the field for nearly every defensive snap over the last three weeks due to Montaric Brown's hamstring injury. Solely banking on Brown returning to full health and stepping up in pass coverage alongside Travis Hunter would be unwise when an AFC South title is within reach.
Adding Woolen to the mix would give Jacksonville a veteran with the necessary closing speed to eliminate throwing lanes and swat away jump balls. The Jaguars are projected to have three fifth-round picks in 2027, which could be used to sweeten the pot on Woolen's expected trade value of a fourth-round pick.
Carolina's secondary has been bitten by the injury bug. Starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn (quad) and Mike Jackson (groin) have both landed on injured reserve. It's a duo that guided the Panthers' defense in 2025. Horn registered five interceptions, and Jackson led the NFL with a stellar 19 pass breakups.
However, it leaves the Panthers in desperate need of a cornerback. The group of Akayleb Evans, Will Lee III, and Chau-Smith Wade is inexperienced. Carolina defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero runs a similar scheme to that of Philadelphia's Vic Fangio. It utilizes zone coverage to keep the action in front of defenders.
It's a scheme that plays to Woolen's strengths. The former UTSA standout can use his 6'4" frame to disrupt route timing, while also reading the quarterback's eyes. Carolina has intriguing trade chips like wide receiver Xavier Legette and tight end Ja'Tavion Sanders that it can add to a late-round pick.
The Bills enter their bye week looking like a true AFC contender with a 5-1 record. A glaring weakness remains, though. Buffalo is allowing the second-most passing yards per game (285.8) and the eighth-most yards per completion (10.9). Opposing pass-catchers are constantly finding open space.
Cornerback Christian Benford has done his job. He lacks a reliable partner. Second-year pro Maxwell Hairston has posted a dismal 21.4% missed-tackle rate. Rookie Davison Igbinosun has tallied five pass breakups, but two early penalties in Buffalo's Week 6 game show he still has a way to go.
Woolen's covering skills on deep routes would come in handy when the Bills battle elite offenses. Buffalo general manager Brandon Beane has displayed aggressive trade techniques before, most recently trading out of the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft in three separate moves. He could offer a deal to Roseman that would be hard to refuse.

title: McMullen: Eagles' Are Playing Risky Game With Unsustainable Defensive Workload
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles’ defense was on the field for 79 snaps in Sunday’s 25-14 loss to the Panthers , marking the fifth time in six games this season that the unit has played 70 or more defensive snaps.⁠
That volume is consistently rising into Vic Fangio's third season as Philadelphia's defensive coordinator. In 2025, the Eagles reached 70-plus defensive snaps in six of 17 games. During the 2024 Super Bowl-winning campaign, that number was hit only three times all year.⁠
Through six games in 2026, the defense is averaging 71.7 reps per contest —the highest mark of the Nick Sirianni era and well above the 61.6 average from the Super Bowl season. Over the last four games, the figure has climbed even higher as the offense has struggled to sustain drives.⁠
The disparity was a little better against the Panthers: the Eagles’ offense managed  64 snaps while the defense faced 79. The time of possession was tilted heavily toward Carolina (34:48 to 25:12), consistent with a season-long pattern in which the Eagles’ offense has produced a league-high number of three-and-outs and often failed to manage the clock well.
In a complementary game, those short possessions leave Fangio’s group with little rest between series.⁠
Key defenders absorbed the bulk of the work against the Panthers. Linebacker Zack Baun and cornerback Quinyon Mitchell played all 79 snaps, while safety Drew Mukuba matched them. Cooper DeJean logged 78 snaps and Riq Woolen 77. Up front, Jalen Carter played 74 snaps (94 percent), and edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie played 72—both heavy loads given the rotation and injuries that limited others, including Jonathan Greenard and Nolan Smith, who exited early with a concussion after just 14 snaps.⁠
On Wednesday, Fangio addressed the cumulative toll of the repeated high snap counts when asked by Eagles On SI whether the volume could wear a defense down week after week. He rejected the idea of letting it become an emotional burden.
“No, you can’t let it emotionally,” Fangio said. “We tell [the players] very early in training camp, we have no control how we get on the field. We control how we get off the field, and that’s where our mindset is.”
The comment reflects a consistent message from Fangio and his staff.
The control what you can control mindset. Players are expected to focus solely on the snaps they can influence—getting stops and forcing the offense back onto the field—rather than dwelling on the circumstances created by the other side of the ball.
Earlier in the season, after a high-snap outing against the Rams that included a late collapse, Fangio acknowledged that extreme volume “has an effect” while still insisting the unit must find ways to finish games.
The current pattern raises practical questions about sustainability moving forward, especially with the unproven Tanner McKee subbing in for Jalen Hurts , who is likely done for the season with blood clots in both lungs.
While Fangio’s group has shown resilience in stretches, the combination of frequent three-and-outs on offense and late-game defensive lapses has contributed to a four-game losing streak . Fourth-quarter points allowed have been a recurring problem, with a sizable share of the season’s total points surrendered coming after intermission.
Complementary football remains the stated ideal. When the offense cannot stay on the field, the defense inherits longer periods of work and fewer opportunities for rest or rotation.
Fangio’s emphasis on mindset and controllable factors is admirable and obviously designed to keep the unit from fracturing under those conditions, but the sheer volume of snaps through the first six weeks is not the formula for winning football.

title: Steelers RB Good to Go vs. Saints Despite Knee Injury
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are in Paris, France, set to take on the New Orleans Saints in Week 7. Their second international game in two years is a battle of two offensive-minded head coaches, and for Mike McCarthy, he'll have one of his top pieces available.
The Steelers announced their Week 7 inactives, which did not include running back Rico Dowdle. Dowdle came into the weekend listed as questionable with a knee injury after being limited in practice throughout the week.
It was his second lower-body injury of the season after missing three games with a dislocated toe earlier in the year.
The rest of their inactives include:
WR Ben Skowronek QB Drew Allar QB Will Howard CB Brandin Echols RB Eli Heidenreich CB Terell Smith
Howard will serve as the emergency third quarterback, allowing him to dress for the game but not be allowed to be used unless Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph are injured.
Echols (hamstring) and Skowronek (calf) were ruled out prior to the team's trip to Paris. They are the only injured players on the inactive list.
Dowdle is coming off his first game since Week 2, when the toe injury happened. He rushed seven times for 40 yards against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6, holding a 5.7 yards per carry average as he helped Pittsburgh earn their fourth victory of the season.
Dowdle will continue to work as the 1B option behind Jaylen Warren in the backfield. Travis Homer and Lew Nichols round out the group in Week 7 with Heidenreich being inactive.
The Steelers have also cleared safety DeShon Elliott to play against the Saints. This will be Elliott's first game of the 2026 season after being activated off of Injured Reserve just yesterday.
Elliott missed the end of the 2025 season with a lower-body injury. He returned during training camp and played in a preseason game but was placed back on IR to start the year because the team didn't feel he was fully ready to return.
After returning to practice nearly three weeks ago, Elliott is back in the lineup for his first game of the season. He'll join Jaquan Brisker and Roberts Spears-Jennings in the safety room, and will likely take back the starting role alongside Brisker.
Last year, when the Steelers played internationally in Dublin, Ireland, Elliott recorded six tackles, a sack, a forced fumble and an interception.
Pittsburgh will hope that magic returns againt the Saints.
Noah Strackbein is a Publisher for On SI, covering the Pittsburgh Steelers since 2019. A Jessup, PA native, Noah attended Point Park University, where he fell in love with the Steel City and everything it has to offer. You can find Noah's work at Steelers On SI and weekdays as the hosts of All Steelers Talk.

title: 3 Reasons Steelers Will Beat Saints in Paris
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers will defeat the New Orleans Saints in their international Week 7 meeting. The Steelers meet the Saints in Paris, France, looking for their fifth victory of the season.
To secure that win, the Steelers have to play a much better game than they did in Week 6. For three quarters, the Steelers gave the Tampa Bay Buccaneers every chance possible to win. Finally, they found their footing in the fourth quarter and pulled out the win.
That can't happen again in front of the French crowd against an easy to underestimate Saints team. Thankfully, the Steelers are in a much better position entering Week 7. Due to these three reasons, Pittsburgh will exit Stade de France with their fifth victory of the season.
Running back Jaylen Warren is coming off a disappointing outing compared to his previous three monstrous performances, but he's set for a rebound against the Saints. The biggest reason for this is because New Orleans has not produced a good run defense in 2026.
Through their first six contests, the Saints are allowing 138 rushing yards per game. That figure ranks as the third-worst in the NFL so far. The Saints are one of the worst-performing defenses so far in 2026, but they are especially vulnerable against the run. That's a perfect scenario for Warren to return to his 100-yard rushing form and possibly even more.
Another factor is the health of Rico Dowdle. He enters Week 7 questionable with a knee injury. If he can't go at 100%, the Steelers will be heavily reliant on Warren.
After outside linebacker Nick Herbig exploded in Week 6, recording two sacks in the win, the Steelers are expecting a game-wrecker to appear once again in Paris.
Herbig lived up to his big contract extension against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but the Steelers are counting on him to bring that production against the Saints as well. Not only because he has momentum, but because both T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith are dealing with minor injuries ahead of the matchup.
Herbig is healthy and raring to go. That's trouble for Saints quarterback Tyler Shough.
DeShon Elliott is back on the Steelers' active roster after nearly a year due to a major knee injury. The star defender has been sorely missed by the Steelers' defense, and his possible return comes at the perfect time.
The Steelers have been a solid, but imperfect defense in 2026. They started red-hot, but after a couple of tough weeks, they have issues that can be exploited.
One of those blemishes is the safety position. The team released veteran Rayshawn Jenkins after two weeks of playing nearly zero snaps, leaving Jaquan Brisker, Robert Spears-Jennings and Jalen Ramsey as the only safeties on the active roster.
With Elliott back in the mix, the safety position suddenly shifts from worrisome to the position that sets the tone on defense. The Saints will find that out first-hand.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Elevated Two WRs for Saints Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are bringing up multiple wide receiver from their practice squad.
Before their Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris at the Stade de France, the Steelers added Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson to their game day roster.
Smith had previously been brought up from the practice squad in Weeks 5 and 6, meaning he is now out of elevations for the year while Johnson has one remaining.
With Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) on the reserve/injured list, with the former having missed two games thus far while the latter has been out for one, Pittsburgh has been in clear need of receiver depth.
Add in the fact that Ben Skowronek (calf) will miss a second-straight contest as well , and Smith in particular has become somewhat of a key piece for the Steelers' offense after a strong summer.
Smith turned some heads during training camp and even earned some first-team reps during the Steelers' stay at Saint Vincent College in Latrobe.
He didn't get much of an opportunity to prove himself during the preseason, though, as he suffered a lower-body injury in the opener against the Green Bay Packers and remained out for Pittsburgh's final two exhibition games.
Smith was later released at the roster cutdown deadline on August 30 before re-signing to the Steelers' practice squad.
He was first elevated for the team's Week 5 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts after Pittman Jr. was placed on IR. Smith ended up playing 16 offensive snaps in that contest after Wilson and Skowronek went down in the first half, and while he didn't record a catch, he did help out as a blocker on Jaylen Warren's 50-yard touchdown run in a 34-22 win for Pittsburgh.
Smith came up from the practice squad once again , this time alongside Johnson, for the Steelers' Week 6 bout with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Once again, Smith did not log a reception. He did, however, record 41 snaps on offense as the team's third receiver behind DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard in addition to garnering 18 special teams reps (per Pro Football Focus ).
There's a lot up in the air for Pittsburgh in regards to its receiver room.
It's unknown when, or if, Pittman Jr. will be activated off IR, as there seems to be some concern that he could miss the rest of the season.
At the very least, though, it feels incredibly unlikely that he'll return at the earliest possible date, which would be in Week 10 after he misses the required minimum of four games while on IR.
Wilson appears to be in better shape when it comes to making a swifter recovery for the Steelers, though he still won't be eligible to play until Week 11.
With questions about when Skowronek will be ready to take the field again as well, Pittsburgh's receiver depth is being pushed to the limit. Smith is a solid short-term answer if he were to end up signing to the 53-man roster now that he can no longer be elevated beyond this week, though general manager Omar Khan may also have to get aggressive in finding another solution from outside the organization.
Perhaps Marquez Valdes-Scantling will scratch that itch in his return to the Steelers via the practice squad given his connection with Aaron Rodgers , but he didn't show much in his five games with the team last season and is now 32-years-old.
It's possible Smith's spot will be taken by Valdes-Scantling since he has elevations left, and he may also lose out on some opportunities once Skowronek is back as well.
It also becomes even tougher to envision Smith sticking around (if he were to sign to the 53-man roster) once Wilson and/or Pittman Jr. come back, and the possibility of a trade for a receiver ahead of the November 10 deadline may still be alive.
As such, Smith likely has to take advantage of his current role in order to convince Pittsburgh to keep him around and play him again this season, which would require adding him to the 53-man roster after this week.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Get Starting Safety Back From IR
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers defense just got one of their best players back for the first time in 2026.
The Steelers announced that they activated safety DeShon Elliott off injured reserve.
"He's pretty juiced up about this," linebacker Patrick Queen said about Elliott returning.
Elliott coming off injured reserve means that he can play in the Steelers' Week 7 matchup against the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France, another big-time matchup.
With 11 games remaining in the season, the Steelers have bolstered their postseason chances with Elliott back on the field.
The Steelers haven't had Elliott on the field for them in almost a year, last playing vs. the Green Bay Packers in a 35-25 Week 8 loss at Acrisure Stadium, before suffering a lower-body injury .
Pittsburgh hoped to get Elliott back for the playoffs , but he wasn't ready, and then he only appeared in one preseason game before they placed him on the IR.
Elliott's been a difference maker for the Steelers when healthy, with 146 tackles (92 solo), five tackles for loss, one sack, two interceptions, eight passes defended, three forced fumbles and three fumble recoveries in 19 starts and 20 games in 2024 and 2025.
He has the ability to change a game with one play and can make the Steelers' defense much more versatile going forward.
The Steelers have won games this season with their defense, especially 20-13 over the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium in Week 1 and 26-19 over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium in Week 6.
Elliott's return could continue that trend going and help the offense get going as a result.
The Steelers cut safety Rashawn Jenkins on Oct. 21, meaning he won't be joining the team plane to Paris or be on the active roster either.
Jenkins, who struggled in his six games with the Steelers this season, lost his place to 2026 seventh-round draft pick Robert Spears-Jennings , a bad sign for the 32-year-old veteran.
Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy hinted that Elliott could return and that he was working hard during practice to come back for this game.
"It definitely would be huge for him to play again, especially Sunday against the Saints," McCarthy told reporters in Paris. "It’s been a long road back, but he’s a big part of what we’re about in Pittsburgh."
The Steelers have three safeties now with Elliott back, which includes Jaquan Brisker and Spears-Jennings.
Brisker has started all six games for the Steelers, with 41 tackles (20 solo), three passes defended and an interception in the win over the Falcons.

A Pittsburgh native, Dominic grew up watching Pittsburgh Sports and wrote for The Pitt News as an undergraduate at the University of Pittsburgh, covering Pitt Athletics. He would write for Pittsburgh Sports Now after college and has years of experience covering sports across Pittsburgh.

title: Steelers vs. Saints Bold Predictions: Offense Puts on a Show
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are officially in France and are ready to take on the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Paris.
Riding a two-game win streak heading into Week 7, the Steelers still have things to clean up as they look to keep pace in the race for both the AFC North and one of three Wild Card spots in the conference.
Regardless, Pittsburgh is 4-2 for a fourth-straight season and has what some may consider a must-win type of game vs. New Orleans given how tough its schedule gets immediately following its Week 9 bye.
With that, here are three bold predictions for the Steelers as they look to take down the Saints.
Pittsburgh's offense largely falls near the middle of the pack, averaging the 12th-fewest yards (320.5) and the 15th-fewest points (22.8) per game in the league.
Those numbers are dragged down quite a bit by the team's poor outing against the New England Patriots in Week 2, however, during which they scored just three points with 235 yards of offense.
Under Mike McCarthy, the Steelers have proven that they're at least capable of explosive offensive performances. For example, they scored 30 points with 411 yards in a Week 3 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals and put up 34 points in a Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
It's possible that Pittsburgh comes out a bit sluggish against the Saints in Paris after arriving later in the week, but the formula is there for the black and gold to have another huge performance.
New Orleans' defense is currently tied with the Arizona Cardinals for the most points allowed per game (29.7) while also giving up the fourth-most yards per contest (377.7).
The Saints have struggled to consistently get after the quarterback too, as their 33.2 percent pressure rate (per SumerSports ) is the fourth-worst in the NFL despite having 15 sacks.
The Steelers' offense already had their way with one of the worst defenses in the league in the Colts, and there's no reason they can't do the same vs. New Orleans by finishing with over 400 yards of total offense.
The Saints' offense cannot be taken lightly. Even though first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson has yet to play this season with a hamstring injury, while franchise left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. has been out since Week 3 after undergoing ankle surgery, they are still averaging the 11th-most points (25.3) in the league.
At the same time, quarterback Tyler Shough has thrown five interceptions and lost three fumbles while New Orleans as a whole has turned the ball over 12 times , which is tied for the third-most in the NFL.
Pittsburgh, meanwhile, has 10 takeaways on the year, which is tied with five other teams for the second-most behind the Green Bay Packers and Seattle Seahawks at 11.
The Steelers' defense is among the better units in the league, as they allow the sixth-lowest EPA per play (-0.1) and the seventh-fewest yards per game (307.5).
New Orleans is capable of doing a little bit of damage, but Pittsburgh's defense has stepped up and largely made the necessary plays when it's needed to.
Winning the turnover margin is always crucial, and considering how susceptible the Saints are to giving the ball away, the Steelers will end up with two takeaways in this one.
Pittsburgh is short-handed along the interior of its defensive line with Sebastian Joseph-Day (triceps) joining Derrick Harmon (foot) on the reserve/injured list.
The same can be said at wide receiver, as Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) are on IR as well while Ben Skowronek (calf) will miss his second-straight game .
Cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) will be sidelined too, and there are also some questions about Rico Dowdle's (knee) availability after he was deemed questionable to suit up on the Steelers' final injury report of the week.
Still, this is a game the Steelers should win. Again, maybe they aren't at tip-top shape playing overseas, but they're simply the better and more talented team.
The Saints are not a pushover by any means and have the potential to make things tough for Pittsburgh, as evidenced by their comeback win over the Baltimore Ravens on the road in Week 2.
That being said, New Orleans is 2-4 for a reason. Its defense is among the worst in the league, and while its offense is a formidable unit, it's going to have a tough time keeping up with the Steelers.
After notching their first two-score win of the season in Week 5 vs. Indianapolis, who profiles similarly to the Saints, Pittsburgh will do so once again in France and move to 5-2.

title: Pros and Cons of Steelers Trying to Land Quenton Nelson
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are positioned to buy at this year's NFL trade deadline.
Wide receiver, inside linebacker, cornerback and safety make up the Steelers' top needs as they sit at 4-2. One position that's flown a bit under the radar in that regard, though, is offensive guard.
Mason McCormick's transition from right to left guard has worked out thus far, and Brock Hoffman has been about as good as Pittsburgh could've ever hoped for after entering the starting lineup in place of Spencer Anderson in Week 3.
Again, there are several other areas of concern on the team's roster that should be addressed before seriously considering acquiring a potential upgrade at guard before the November 10 trade deadline passes.
With the Indianapolis Colts potentially selling off multiple high-impact players after moving to 2-4 on the year and firing general manager Chris Ballard, however, Quenton Nelson is a name that could pique the Steelers' interest .
If Nelson is made available, what are the pros and cons of Pittsburgh potentially exploring a trade for the superstar left guard?
Any time you have an opportunity to add a three-time first-team All-Pro, three-time second-team All-Pro and eight-time Pro Bowler to your roster, you have to consider it.
Hoffman has performed well for Pittsburgh, particularly in pass protection, where he's allowed just seven pressures and no sacks over 257 total snaps (per SumerSports ).
Nelson, as one of the best offensive linemen in the NFL, is on a whole other level, though. To go alongside his status as an elite run blocker, the 30-year-old has given up eight pressures and no sacks across 397 snaps for the Colts this season (per SumerSports).
It goes without saying that Nelson would be a massive upgrade over Hoffman and help transform the Steelers' offensive line even further, potentially making them one of the better units in the league.
Given that he's a rental and will reach free agency once the season concludes, the price tag won't be overly expensive to acquire him.
A 2027 third-round pick is nothing to scoff at, but for a player of Nelson's caliber, that's still somewhat of a bargain for Pittsburgh if that's what it ends up taking.
The Steelers won't negotiate any contracts in-season and don't seem willing to budge on that front, as we saw with Joey Porter Jr. before he was dealt to the Dallas Cowboys.
Regardless, bringing in Nelson and building that relationship over the back half of the year could help put the necessary pieces in place for a long-term deal once the offseason arrives.
Having Nelson help anchor the offensive line next to the likes of Troy Fautanu, Max Iheanachor, Zach Frazier and McCormick would add to an impressive infrastructure Pittsburgh is crafting for whoever starts at quarterback in 2027 as well.
Amassing that level of talent in the trenches would do wonders for the Steelers and make the entire operation on offense flow far more seamlessly, which is why the concept of adding Nelson could be so alluring for Omar Khan, Mike McCarthy and company.
Between the 2024 and 2025 seasons, McCormick played 1,929 snaps at right guard (per Pro Football Focus ) while Isaac Seumalo held down the fort at left guard.
McCormick has proven that he can be a good starter at right guard, though now that he's switched over to left guard and is in the midst of arguably his best season for Pittsburgh up to this point, it's fair to wonder if switching sides in the middle of the year could halt some of his momentum.
Nelson is strictly a left guard and has never logged a snap at right guard (per PFF), meaning McCormick would have to move. With Hoffman also being a relative bright spot, perhaps the Steelers feel as though they shouldn't rock the boat and give up a Day 2 pick for Nelson when their guard play has been pretty strong over the last handful of weeks.
Furthermore, finding the money to keep all of the key pieces along the offensive line in place for years to come would be tough.
Frazier and McCormick will be up for new deals next year in the final seasons of their rookie contracts. Pittsburgh can kick the can down the road a little by picking up Fautanu's fifth-year option and possibly delaying extension talks until 2028, though it will still have to figure out that situation at some point.
The Steelers also cannot acquire Nelson with the idea that he's just a rental. Sure, they could get a compensatory pick for him if he walks in free agency, but having a player of his caliber in the building and not retaining him would feel short-sighted and illogical.
While Pittsburgh is certainly a playoff contender, it's not quite a Super Bowl contender. As a result, bringing in Nelson, who's not the missing piece in the team's quest for a title, and keeping him for the back half of the season before moving on just wouldn't make much sense, regardless of the comp pick argument.
There are a lot of moving parts and some potential long-term uncertainty along the offensive line that would come with acquiring Nelson, which the Steelers may choose to avoid altogether by opting not to look into trading for him over the next couple of weeks.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers Gets Blunt About Jalen Hurts Situation
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers offered some thoughts about Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts' situation after being ruled out for the rest of the season due to deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in his lungs.
While speaking with reporters after the Steelers flew over to Paris for their Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints, Rodgers addressed Hurts and his health before taking a bit of a shot at Dr. Allen Sills, the NFL's Chief Medical Officer.
“I don’t have a close relationship with Jalen (Hurts). Obviously, we’re in the quarterback fraternity, so you don’t want to see anything like that happen to anybody, especially a guy who’s still in football,“ Rodgers said, per PennLive's Nick Farabaugh . ”Obviously, I don’t know all the details about what’s going on. All I’ve seen is what’s been printed. Allen Sills, he’s the guy in charge of all things medical at the NFL office. And he and I haven’t always seen eye-to-eye about things. So, I can’t say I’m real surprised."
During the COVID-19 pandemic, Rodgers drew headlines when he revealed that he did not receive a vaccination and instead turned to homeopathic treatment.
He appealed to the NFL that those treatments should qualify him as vaccinated (per ESPN ), though the league did not accept it.
Rodgers was fined alongside Allan Lazard for a violation of the league and NFLPA's COVID-19 protocols in November 2021 for attending a team-sanctioned Halloween party that took place outside of the Green Bay Packers' facility since they were unvaccinated (per NFL.com's Grant Gordon ).
He also stated on "The Pat McAfee Show" that "some of the rules to me are not based in science at all" regarding how the NFL approached COVID-19, which Sills pushed back on without directly naming Rodgers.
“We've been very consistent,” Sills said in a conference call in November 21, per USA Today's Jarrett Bell . “First of all, these are things that we decided collectively with the players association (NFLPA). They're always based on science. The science that at best we understand for public health, but also our own data. We are constantly looking at our own data in every way possible, to see where we might still be vulnerable and what parts of our protocols we think are particularly effective. So, we're very comfortable with what we've put in place being driven by our data and is working.”
The NFLPA has called for an investigation into Hurts' situation, as he was cleared to play in London against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5 after a superficial blood clot was found in his calf via an ultrasound.
Upon the team making its way back to Philadelphia ahead of Week 6, another ultrasound found that the blood clot had moved.
From there, he was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, which means that a blood clot traveled from his legs to his lungs.
"The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts," the NFLPA said, per ESPN's Tim McManus . "In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received," the statement read. "Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward."
Sills stated earlier this week that he was confident in how Philadelphia's medical staff handled the situation.
“I have complete confidence in the Eagles' medical staff and their handling of this situation, and I would characterize their work as very conservative, very patient-focused and appropriately guarded at every step,” Sills said, per NFL.com . “I don’t think you can take that outcome and say there was something flawed about the process. Sometimes in medicine, we do all the right things and diseases progress and other things develop.
“In this case, everyone was incredibly conservative and incredibly vigilant and was very quick to make diagnoses of these conditions that might not have been diagnosed in a nonathlete.”

title: Steelers' Nick Herbig Ready to Explode
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers paid big money to multiple members of their 2023 draft class this past offseason.
The trio of tight end Darnell Washington , defensive tackle Keeanu Benton and linebacker Nick Herbig all cashed in over the summer , securing a sizable raise and their place on the franchise moving forward.
To begin the 2026 campaign, the recently-paid Steelers got off to a sluggish start. Benton recorded just six tackles, four of which were assisted, over the opening three weeks. Herbig had half of a great game in Week 2 against the New England Patriots, but his lack of production outside of that turned him into an early candidate for the fanbase's criticism.
Then, Week 6 happened. Herbig recorded six tackles, all solo and 2.0 sacks. It was exactly the type of bounce-back performance the 24-year-old edge rusher needed.
Now, he heads to Paris, France, hoping that Week 6 outing was just the beginning.
All signs point to Herbig exploding over the next few weeks, continuing with the team's Week 7 international contest against the New Orleans Saints.
The biggest and most obvious reason to believe in Herbig right now is that the Steelers are likely going to rely on him more over the coming contest or two.
Starting outside linebacker Alex Highsmith popped up on the team's injury report recently with a groin injury. The severity of his injury is not yet known, but the Steelers don't have to wait to find out.
While Highsmith deals with whatever this ailment is, they have Herbig right there. He's another starter ready to be deployed by defensive coordinator Patrick Graham.
Through the first six games, Herbig has played in just 204 defensive snaps, according to Pro Football Reference . That figure accounts for 54% of the Steelers' total defensive snaps. With Highsmith limited, Herbig will be on the field way more.
And when he's on the field, Herbig produces. He's proven that time and time again. In Paris against the Saints, Herbig is about to get another huge chance to remind the NFL.
Another reason to buy the Herbig stock for this weekend is the fact that the Steelers linebacker has a bit of history on his side.
Last year, the Steelers also traveled across the Atlantic Ocean for a regular-season game. They met the Minnesota Vikings in Dublin, Ireland, and Herbig was one of the standout performers.
He finished that game with five total tackles and 1.5 sacks, giving Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz nightmares in the process.
Herbig doesn't need any extra incentive or motivation to go out there and try to dominate. It's in his professional nature. But it's a nice reminder that history is on the young edge rusher's side as he tries to get back on track.
And getting back on track is exactly what Herbig is doing. It began in Week 6 and will take the next step in Week 7, as Herbig returns to being the dynamic and productive defender the Steelers need.

title: Steelers RB Questionable vs. Saints With Knee Injury
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers shared a bit of good and bad news with their latest injury report.
The good news is that as the Steelers arrived in Paris, France, their top defensive player received a clean bill of health. Outside linebacker T.J. Watt popped up on the report with a calf injury. After being limited in practice, he returned in full the following day in the team's estimated report.
A bit of bad news continues to be a story to monitor, however. Running back Rico Dowdle returned to the lineup in Week 6, but he’s dealing with a new injury that might keep him out against the New Orleans Saints. Dowdle was listed as questionable for the Week 7 matchup due to a knee injury.
With Dowdle potentially being out or limited, this puts running back Jaylen Warren in line for another monster day in the Pittsburgh backfield.
This is the second lower-body injury Dowdle has battled this season, missing three games earlier this season with a toe injury. Brought in to be a key part of the Steelers’ backfield tandem, the franchise is still waiting for the back-to-back 1,000-yard rusher to get going.
This latest ailment certainly hurts. Not only is it a setback that Dowdle hoped to avoid after he missed a few games with a toe injury, but it’s also another missed opportunity for the offense as a whole to get going.
Entering Week 7, the Steelers are still searching for their offensive identity. At times, they appeared to find it, but consistency remains elusive.
Having Dowdle on the field gives the Steelers the personnel to achieve that consistency, however. He gives Warren a breather and changes the pace of the backfield. Without him, the running game is much more one-dimensional.
Without Dowdle, the Steelers will once again rely on Warren as their featured player. That’s not exactly a surprise, as head coach MIke McCarthy has continued to affirm that Warren is one of the most prominent pieces of their offense.
Even if Dowdle is active, but limited, Warren is in line for a big day. He’s looking at around 15 to 20 carries and at least five targets in the passing game. In three of the past four contests, he's taken those carries for at least 90 yards and added on at least 25 receiving yards in every game this season. On the season, he has 460 rushing yards and a touchdown on 84 carries and 29 receptions for 258 yards and another score, and he’s set to have a big day in Paris, France.

title: Steelers Give Positive T.J. Watt Update Before Saints Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers received some good news ahead of their Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris.
On their final injury report of the week, EDGE rusher T.J. Watt was listed as a full participant in practice and did not have a game designation.
The 32-year-old popped up on the previous injury report with a calf injury and was a limited participant in the Steelers' final practice before flying over to Paris.
Pittsburgh did not practice on October 23 due to weather , meaning that the final injury report was an estimation in terms of participation, but it still is a positive development for Watt.
Prior to the report coming out, head coach Mike McCarthy told reporters that there wasn't much concern about Watt not being able to suit up vs. New Orleans at the Stade de France, though Saturday's practice would be the deciding factor.
“I would say no, frankly, we just got off the flight and we’ll work the guys here and see how they respond. And tomorrow’s practice will answer all those questions,” McCarthy said, per PennLive's Nick Farabaugh .
With Watt over the injury report, though, that obviously bodes extremely well for his availability, and he stated that he feels "really good".
"I feel really good honestly," Watt said. "Just trying to hydrate as much as possible. Was able to sleep on the plane, just hit an espresso, so I should be good to go."
Watt has remained healthy all season outside of a brief instance against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5 in which he was checked out after appearing to be poked in the eye.
In six games, he has recorded 15 total tackles, 4.5 sacks, a pick-six and a forced fumble.
Watt wasn't the only Pittsburgh EDGE rusher to find himself on the injury report this week.
Alex Highsmith was also listed on all three installations of it due to a groin injury . He was limited on both October 21 and 22 as a result, though he was upgraded to a full participant in the team's estimation on October 23 and also doesn't have any game designation.
Groin injuries have become a bit of a recurring issue for Highsmith, as he missed a single game with one in 2021 while being sidelined for three in 2024.
He also suffered a groin injury during training camp in 2025, but he did not miss any regular season time as a result.
There doesn't seem to be any level of long-term concern with Watt and Highsmith, however, and both are now set up to play against the Saints.
Nick Herbig, who's coming off a two-sack outing against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and/or Jack Sawyer could've stepped up in a world where either or both of Watt and Highsmith were inactive this week.
Instead, all four of Pittsburgh's EDGE rushers look like they'll take the field in Paris.

title: Seahawks Are Not Showing Real Concerns After Charbonnet's News
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (3-3) have a must-win game in Week 7 as they host the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) on Sunday Night Football. This has to be the Seahawks' get -right game, or they will be under .500% past Week 3 for the first time since the 2024 season. One of the biggest things that the Seahawks must fix is their lack of impact from the running game, player utilization and turnovers.
​The Seahawks were preparing for veteran running back Zach Charbonnet to return on the field for the first time since tearing his ACL in last season’s Divisional Round over the San Francisco 49ers. He was a full participant in practices, but on Friday, he was ruled out. This comes at horrible timing as the Seahawks are now left with a depleted and talentless backfield before taking on an undefeated team.
​To go from a full participant in practices to now being out is highly questionable. The only two suggestions are that the Seahawks are putting Charbonnet on the trade block for another running back like the Indianapolis Colts’ Jonathan Taylor . The other theory is that they are taking one more week for him to fully get in shape and take a huge amount of carries.
This isn’t the time for a 3-3 Seahawks team going into Week 7 to be playing games. If the 2026 NFL Season ended now, the Seahawks would be left out of the playoffs and they still have to host the undefeated Chiefs and then go on the road to take on the Chicago Bears (5-2) for Monday Night Football. There is a real chance that the Seahawks could be 3-5 by the time they head into Week 9 .
​They’ve rarely taken opportunities to improve their run game. Outside of signing undrafted rookie Robert Henry Jr. off the Washington Commanders practice squad, the front office hasn’t added another valuable running back to the roster. The Seahawks worked out former two-time Pro-Bowler Joe Mixon, but they didn’t like his physical.
​In the first two games of the season, the Seahawks averaged 129.5 rushing yards. They accomplished this by mixing Price with a power back like Wilson and Holani. The Seahawks only averaged 96 yards through the last four games when the turnovers increased and Price was put on IR after Week 3. Seattle put their entire running game on Wilson and Holani, who are both short-yardage running backs with no power or explosiveness.
​As a result of the running game being less efficient, the Seahawks have put too much pressure on quarterback Sam Darnold, who has regressed in his turnovers and decision-making . Darnold had 51 passing attempts, escaped several times for runs and was sacked five times. The Seahawks need a reliable run game in some way on Sunday night for a chance at winning.
​The Seahawks’ coaching staff seemed scared to utilize new schemes or new players. Wide receiver Rashid Shaheed took a pitch handoff for a 28-yard touchdown in the Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers and he had only one rushing attempt in the losses to the San Francisco 49ers and the Denver Broncos. Veteran Velus Jones Jr. is a faster running back, but he only had four carries for 20 yards against the Broncos. Meanwhile, Henry has yet to play a game for the Seahawks.
​If the Seahawks want to create a more balanced offense, they need to have their offensive line create more push at the line of scrimmage. They also need to be smart about who gets the carries. This means fewer carries for Wilson and Holani and more for Jones and Henry. The more the Seahawks don’t take their running game issues seriously, the worse the team’s chances for the playoffs get.

title: Sam Darnold Is Running out of Time for the Seahawks
full_text:
A month ago, I was fairly confident I knew how the Sam Darnold story would go. He’d have another solid season, win a bunch of games, go deep into the postseason, and then sign a contract extension in the realm of $55 million a year . I didn’t think it was possible that things could change this fast. But such is life in the NFL. So where are we now?
This isn’t the first low moment in the Sam Darnold experience for the Seattle Seahawks. Last year’s week 10 game in Los Angeles, a four-interception affair that wasted a superhuman defensive performance, was in the conversation for the worst game a Seahawk quarterback had played in decades. But what happened after that game was over?
The Seahawks went to bat for Sam. They defended him and stood by him. Ernest Jones, famously, gave some colorful quotes sticking up for him . And Darnold rewarded that belief the rest of the season, with the Seahawks not losing another game the rest of the way, including some where Sam had to pick up the slack for the defense. But what about now?
Far be it from me to play armchair psychologist right now. But Byron Murphy and Derick Hall run a podcast where they get to express themselves on a level that most players don’t. And after last week’s loss to the Denver Broncos, it’s hard for me to not read into their comments. They sounded like a couple defensive players that knew their offense was failing them .
Murphy said that he felt like, as a defense, they did everything they were supposed to do, and that they played lights out. Hall echoed that, saying he felt like they played a hell of a game. They did concede some minor imperfections, but overall, it felt like a couple of players that were tired of playing elite football and still not getting the win.
I can’t help but think about a decade ago, when the Legion of Boom era in Seattle was winding down. You could tell things weren’t right, and once the star defenders departed the Seahawks for other teams or retirement, they publicly confirmed it. There was a rift between the defense and quarterback. The defense didn’t appreciate the double standard in treatment.
I don’t believe there’s any double standard in this situation, but I believe the resentment could creep in regardless. And once that resentment is there, it’s very hard to get rid of it. Fans rattling the cages for Drew Lock to start is one thing, but the moment the players in that locker room start echoing that , I think it’s a wrap. Does that happen with one more bad game?
The defense is not wrong if they feel like the offense is selling them out . The Seahawks currently rank third in Rush EPA and Success Rate, second in EPA, Dropback EPA, Success Rate, and Dropback Success Rate, and first (by a mile) in yards allowed per game and yards allowed per play. You can’t be much better than they are right now.
That final point is an especially big one. The Seahawks are allowing 4 yards per play. No defense since at least 2003 has done that, and only one (the 2008 Pittsburgh Steelers) has come close, at 4.1. It’s a defense that should be 6-0 right now. Blame Brian Fleury, George Holani, Abe Lucas, Rashid Shaheed, or whoever else, but Sam is the QB.
It’s possible Sam has a bit of a reprieve at the moment , as Drew Lock is battling a right elbow injury that may make him unavailable this weekend. I wouldn’t be surprised if the Seahawks also at least wait until Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price return before passing full judgement on Darnold. But the NFL season is only seventeen games long.
The Seahawks would be 5-1 at worst right now with a bad offense that avoids turnovers. They’re 3-3 because they have a very bad offense that turns it over constantly. I don’t believe this team can fix all of their offensive issues this season, but if they can fix some of them with a quarterback change, that might be enough for them to start winning games.

title: Seahawks Mailbag: 3 Questions Leading Into Chiefs Game
full_text:
It’s a two-game losing streak that could easily turn into three this weekend . Such poor results definitely gets a fanbase asking tough questions. I asked my discord server what their biggest questions about the team are right now. Let’s take a look at what’s on the mind of the fans. The wording of the questions has been lightly edited for this article.
“Will Zach Charbonnet fix the Seahawks’ backfield problems?”
I don’t think so. He definitely makes things better , but let’s keep perspective on what Zach Charbonnet can provide. He’s never had a thousand yard season, even if you use total scrimmage yards, and he’s only gone over 200 touches once (and did so barely). He’s not a bellcow, or even close to one. And what kind of Charbonnet are we getting?
It will be months before Zach is at full power. It may not happen this season. Expect a tight snap count limit for the foreseeable future. Furthermore, he doesn’t possess the speed to be an elite outside zone runner, so he’s not a great fit for the run plays that Brian Fleury wants to run. His ball security and blocking will help, but Jadarian Price is ultimately the key here.
“Why is Sam Darnold throwing so many interceptions?”
Maybe the only question that really matters right now. And also one that’s hard to really answer. There’s a lot going into this one, from the lack of threat from the run game to poor play sequencing to being forced into passing situations. But the thing I always come back to is Sam Darnold’s history as a player. He’s always been a turnover-prone player.
Even back to college for a very good USC team, Sam turned it over a lot. He’s consistently turned it over a lot his entire NFL career. Expecting him to cut that part of his game out was never realistic to me. The thing that surprises me is how everything else in his game is also deteriorating at the same time. He’s not really doing anything well right now .
“Will the return of Anthony Bradford fix the oline woes?”
There’s something to be said for restoring continuity and familiarity to the offensive line . Those aspects are often more important to the play of the group than individual talent level. The last month has taught us a surprising lesson as it pertains to Bradford’s value to this team. His strength and power matter on a line this finesse and movement-based.
I wonder if Abe Lucas’s recent struggles are related to not having Bradford to his left on some level. I wouldn’t be shocked if things immediately look much better with AB out there. I don’t know if it can fix everything wrong with this unit, but at the very least the run-blocking should get a lot better. Continuity matters a lot right now.

title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Seahawks’ Week 7 Clash vs. Chiefs
full_text:
It wasn’t all that long ago that the Seattle Seahawks were in the midst of a 12-game winning streak. Mike Macdonald’s club won its final 10 overall outings in 2025, including three playoff contests, and got off to a 2-0 start this season. Now the reigning Super Bowl champions have dropped two straight and three of their last four games.
The three setbacks, which equals last season’s total, have been by a total of eight points. Now the club takes on the lone undefeated team in the AFC in the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs.
Here’s a look at some key individual battles when the clubs collide at Lumen Field this Sunday.
It’s a clash between two of the best players at their respective positions. The Chiefs’ offensive line has had some ups and down. However, Gordon McGuinness of Pro Football Focus elevated this unit from 22nd to 19th following the club’s 22-6 victory in Week 6 over the Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium.
Center Creed Humphrey is a four-time Pro Bowler and a two-time First Team All-Pro. He’s currently PFF’s No. 12 pivot, but it’s very interesting to note that his 66.8 grade is easily the lowest of his six-year career.
Meanwhile, Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV is having another solid year, The two-time Super Bowl champion, who won a ring during his rookie season with the Los Angeles Rams, leads the club with 59 tackles. There’s also three sacks, one interception, and three passes defensed. The ‘Hawks entered Week 7 as the league’s top-ranked defense in terms of fewest total yards and fewer passing yards allowed per game.
Mansoor Delane’s first full game of his NFL career 10 tackles 1 TFL 5 receptions allowed (7 targets) 24 yards allowed (4.8 Y/REC) 1 PBU 75.9 passer rating allowed pic.twitter.com/kzS9RrNEYh

He leads the NFL with 717 receiving yards and seven touchdown grabs, and is tied for the league lead with Cardinals’ tight end Trey McBride with 49 receptions.

title: Zach Charbonnet Injury News Changes Seahawks RB Trade Discussions
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks and their fans need a little hope at running back in Week 7 against the Kansas City Chiefs, but they won't be getting that from Zach Charbonnet, who is out for the game.
Charbonnet has missed the NFC Championship, Super Bowl LX and the first six games of the 2026 season with a torn ACL that he suffered in the Divisional Round of the 2025-26 playoffs.
It's a remarkable recovery time of just over nine months, and the Seahawks desperately need him back. Seattle gambled on Charbonnet after letting Kenneth Walker III — who they will see on Sunday — leave in free agency.
In the meantime, the Seahawks' stable of running backs has not delivered. Potential trade targets have emerged , and Charbonnet now needs to silence when he returns to the field.
The major question is how much Charbonnet will play when he comes back. If he gets an RB1 workload and is healthy enough to handle it, there's reason to believe that Charbonnet could immediately return to his previous effectiveness.
A big performance from Charbonnet will not only boost the Seahawks by making the offense much more functional, but it'll also quiet the demands to make an addition to the running back room.
Seattle has to justify sticking with their current players, who are currently averaging a cumulative 3.9 yards per carry and have a combined five fumbles (four lost). Charbonnet has zero career fumbles and a career average of 4.1 yards per carry.
Charbonnet totaled 184 carries for 734 yards and 12 touchdowns in 16 regular season games last season. He can be the immediate difference to rejuvenate the offense, but he has to be healthy enough to do so. Avoid the big contract that will have to be paid or inherited by a trade.
The Seahawks need to see a decent amount from Charbonnet before the trade deadline on November 10 so they can make the best decision possible about whether they need to add reinforcements at the position. Knowing that he'll miss Week 7 against the Chiefs, the margin for error becomes that much tighter.

title: 5 Key Things to Know About Chiefs vs. Seahawks in Week 7
full_text:
During their Super Bowl championship season of 2025, the Seattle Seahawks played in a total of 20 games and lost just three times. Their three setbacks were by a total of nine points, and each were decided by four points or less. Mike Macdonald’s club opened with a 3-2 mark, then lost just once more, closing with 10 consecutive wins. And that includes the team’s impressive three-game postseason run that resulted in a Lombardi Trophy.
It’s suddenly been a different story in ’26. The ‘Hawks have dropped three of their last four games after a 2-0 start. Once again, those losses have been by narrow margins—each by three points or less. However, Macdonald’s club has dropped consecutive outings to the San Francisco 49ers (32-29) and Denver Broncos (17-14) —the latter in overtime.
Now the defending champions face an extremely big challenge i n the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs. And to make matters even trickier, Andy Reid’s team has the NFL’s current rushing leader at his disposal in Kenneth Walker III. The five-year pro was a huge part of the ‘Hawks title campaign, and his last game with the franchise saw him capture Super Bowl LX MVP honors.
For the third time in four weeks, Seattle faces a former division rival. The Seahawks and Chiefs were both members of the AFC West from 1977-2001, and the former was placed in a new-look NFC West in 2002. Since becoming interconference rivals, Kansas City owns a 4-2 lead in six meetings dating back to ’02.
The clubs last met in 2022 at Arrowhead Stadium, with the Chiefs coming away with a 24-10 triumph. As for the teams’ last battle at Seattle, the Seahawks survived a wild 38-31 Sunday night shootout in 2018.
The Chiefs are already FLYING! Kenneth Walker III with the touchdown and the Chiefs are 9-0 up against the Chargers. pic.twitter.com/Pa5zKxeE6q
In six games this season, nine Seattle Seahawks have combined to tote the ball 165 times. They’ve gained 643 yards and rushed for a total of five touchdowns. In five games with the Chiefs, Kenneth Walker III has totaled 106 attempts for 665 yards and six scores —rushing for 100-plus yards in four of those contests.
Speaking of a C-note, Jaxon Smith-Njigba has totaled at least 100 yards receiving in five of the Seattle’s six outings in 2025. He’s amassed 717 yards and caught seven touchdown passes—both league highs. The other 11 Seahawks with at least one catch have totaled 752 receiving yards and have four TD grabs.

The 10-year signal-caller has also escaped the pocket 17 times for 57 yards and one score. He’s been sacked just six times in five games—zero in two of the club’s last three outings.

title: Why Seahawks Cut CB Trevon Diggs Ahead of Chiefs Game
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are making moves to satisfy their roster ahead of Week 7 against the Kansas City Chiefs , which included moving cornerback Trevon Diggs off of the 53-man roster.
According to sources, Diggs has been released by the team, but the Seahawks plan to add him back to the practice squad as a vested veteran.
In a corresponding move, the Seahawks signed Irvin Charles to the active roster. The Seahawks really like what Charles brings to the table on special teams and they did not want to waste much time shuffling him back and forth from the practice squad. Now, he's officially on the 53-man roster and he's ready to go for Week 7.
As for Diggs, he signed with the active roster on Oct. 10 after he appeared in his first game with the Seahawks in Week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers. Diggs went on to participate in the team's Week 5 contest against the San Francisco 49ers and Week 6 against the Denver Broncos, but he has only seen 21 combined snaps on defense thus far.
Diggs was always viewed as a fringe member of the team, even when he signed in the middle of training camp. The days of him being one of the best cornerbacks in the league are over, but he still remains a valuable part of the team's depth at the position.
Seattle is fortunate to have enough depth at the cornerback spot to not have to utilize Diggs too much, but it's clear that the team values him in the locker room as he will continue to be part of the practice squad.
Diggs still has two elevations that he can use for the season as a member of the practice squad, but it's very possible that he makes a return to the 53-man roster later in the season if other cornerbacks suffer injuries.
Diggs is not expected to play in the team's Week 7 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs, but keep him on the back burner, as he may return to the field at some point during the season.
The Chiefs and Seahawks are set to kick off on Sunday at 5:20 pm PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on NBC or stream it on Peacock.
